We derive precise orbital solutions and discuss the stellar parameters, including metallicities, rotational velocities, and activity indices, to assess their impact on the radial-velocity measurements. The properties of these planets are placed in the broader context of known exoplanet populations, particularly regarding the correlation between stellar metallicity and the occurrence of giant planets. These results further demonstrate the efficiency of HARPS for detecting low-amplitude signals and contribute to refining statistical constraints on the formation and evolution of giant planets around nearby solar-type stars.
label: llm

text: Presenting theoretical arguments and numerical results we demonstratelong-range intrachain correlations in concentrated solutions and melts of longflexible polymers which cause a systematic swelling of short chain segments.They can be traced back to the incompressibility of the melt leading to aneffective repulsion $u(s) \approx s/\rho R^3(s) \approx ce/\sqrt{s}$ whenconnecting two segments together where $s$ denotes the curvilinear length of asegment, $R(s)$ its typical size, $ce \approx 1/\rho be^3$ the ``swellingcoefficient", $be$ the effective bond length and $\rho$ the monomer density.The relative deviation of the segmental size distribution from the idealGaussian chain behavior is found to be proportional to $u(s)$. The analysis ofdifferent moments of this distribution allows for a precise determination ofthe effective bond length $be$ and the swelling coefficient $ce$ ofasymptotically long chains. At striking variance to the short-range decaysuggested by Flory's ideality hypothesis the bond-bond correlation function oftwo bonds separated by $s$ monomers along the chain is found to decayalgebraically as $1/s^{3/2}$. Effects of finite chain length are consideredbriefly.
label: human

text: We theoretically investigate intramolecular long-range correlations in polymer melts by analyzing the segmental size distribution and its moments. Using scaling arguments and perturbation theory within the framework of polymer statistical mechanics, we derive analytical expressions for the segmental size distribution that go beyond ideal-chain approximations. The resulting deviations from Gaussian behavior are quantified through a systematic study of the low-order moments and cumulants, highlighting the role of melt incompressibility and chain connectivity. Our results provide a unified description of segmental statistics in dense polymer systems and offer benchmarks for simulations and experiments probing chain conformations at intermediate length scales.
label: llm

text: We study the effects produced by D-brane instantons on the holomorphicquantities of a D-brane gauge theory at an orbifold singularity. These effectsare not limited to reproducing the well known contributions of the gauge theoryinstantons but also generate extra terms in the superpotential or theprepotential. On these brane instantons there are some neutral fermioniczero-modes in addition to the ones expected from broken supertranslations. Theyare crucial in correctly reproducing effects which are dual to gauge theoryinstantons, but they may make some other interesting contributions vanish. Weanalyze how orientifold projections can remove these zero-modes and thus allowfor new superpotential terms. These terms contribute to the dynamics of theeffective gauge theory, for instance in the stabilization of runawaydirections.
label: human

text: We investigate non-perturbative effects arising from stringy instantons localized at orbifold singularities in type II string compactifications. Using the framework of D-branes at singularities, we systematically classify the instanton zero-mode structure and identify the conditions under which such instantons can generate superpotential and higher-derivative F-term corrections. We show that the interplay between orbifold projection, orientifold action, and world-volume fluxes can lift unwanted neutral fermionic zero modes, thereby rendering the instanton contributions phenomenologically relevant. Explicit quiver gauge theory examples are constructed to illustrate how stringy instantons can induce Yukawa couplings, Majorana masses, and other operators that are absent at the perturbative level. Furthermore, we analyze the dependence of these non-perturbative effects on closed-string moduli and discuss their role in moduli stabilization and supersymmetry breaking.
label: llm

text: We present new Faraday rotation measures (RMs) for 148 extragalactic radiosources behind the southern Galactic plane (253o < l < 356o, |b| < 1.5o), anduse these data in combination with published data to probe the large-scalestructure of the Milky Way's magnetic field. We show that the magnitudes ofthese RMs oscillate with longitude in a manner that correlates with thelocations of the Galactic spiral arms. The observed pattern in RMs requries thepresence of at least one large-scale magnetic reversal in the fourth Galacticquadrant, located between the Sagittarius- Carina and Scutum-Crux spiral arms.To quantitatively compare our measurements to other recent studies, we considerall available extragalactic and pulsar RMs in the region we have surveyed, andjointly fit these data to simple models in which the large-scale field followsthe spiral arms. In the best-fitting model, the magnetic field in the fourthGalactic quadrant is directed clockwise in the Sagittarius-Carina spiral arm(as viewed from the North Galactic pole), but is oriented counter- clockwise inthe Scutum-Crux arm. This contrasts with recent analyses of pulsar RMs alone,in which the fourth-quadrant field was presumed to be directedcounter-clockwise in the Sagittarius- Carina arm. Also in contrast to recentpulsar RM studies, our joint modeling of pulsar and extragalactic RMsdemonstrates that large numbers of large-scale magnetic field reversals are notrequired to account for observations.
label: human

text: We present new rotation measure (RM) observations of extragalactic radio sources located behind the southern Galactic plane to probe the large-scale magnetic field structure of the inner Milky Way. Using high-sensitivity, broadband polarimetric data from [instrument/survey placeholder], we derive reliable RMs for [N] sources spanning Galactic longitudes [l-range] and latitudes |b| ≲ [b-limit]. We combine these measurements with existing RM catalogs and electron density models to disentangle magnetic field and electron density contributions along the line of sight. The resulting RM distribution reveals coherent large-scale patterns, including clear signatures of magnetic field reversals associated with major spiral arms in the inner Galaxy. Our analysis finds that the dominant regular magnetic field component is predominantly aligned with the spiral structure, with typical strengths of a few microgauss and evidence for at least one additional field reversal inside the solar circle. These results provide new constraints on Galactic magnetic field models and highlight the importance of dense RM sampling in the southern plane for completing a global picture of the Milky Way’s magneto-ionic structure.
label: llm

text: A critique of the singularity theorems of Penrose, Hawking, and Geroch isgiven. It is pointed out that a gravitationally collapsing black hole acts asan ultrahigh energy particle accelerator that can accelerate particles toenergies inconceivable in any terrestrial particle accelerator, and that whenthe energy $E$ of the particles comprising matter in a black hole is $\sim10^{2} GeV$ or more, or equivalently, the temperature $T$ is $\sim 10^{15} K$or more, the entire matter in the black hole is converted into quark-gluonplasma permeated by leptons. As quarks and leptons are fermions, it isemphasized that the collapse of a black-hole to a space-time singularity isinhibited by Pauli's exclusion principle. It is also suggested that ultimatelya black hole may end up either as a stable quark star, or as a pulsating quarkstar which may be a source of gravitational radiation, or it may simply explodewith a mini bang of a sort.
label: human

text: We investigate whether classical gravitational collapse inevitably culminates in a space-time singularity or whether more subtle outcomes are possible. Building on the singularity theorems of Penrose and Hawking, we examine the assumptions—such as energy conditions, global hyperbolicity, and cosmic censorship—under which singularities are predicted to form. We then analyze how quantum gravity effects, semiclassical backreaction, and alternative theories of gravity might regulate curvature growth and potentially avoid singular end states. Our results suggest that while classical general relativity robustly predicts singularities under broad conditions, plausible quantum and semiclassical corrections could replace the singular core of black holes with a nonsingular, high-curvature region, leaving the ultimate fate of gravitational collapse an open question.
label: llm

text: In most theories of gravity involving torsion, the source for torsion is theintrinsic spin of matter. Since the spins of fermions are normally randomlyoriented in macroscopic bodies, the torsion generated is normally negligible.However, in a recent paper, Mao et al. point out that there is a class oftheories in which the angular momentum of macroscopic spinning bodies generatesa significant amount of torsion. They argue that by the principle of actionequals reaction, one would expect the angular momentum of test bodies to coupleto a background torsion field, and therefore the precession of the GPBgyroscopes should be affected in these theories by the torsion generated by theEarth. We show that in fact the principle of action equals reaction does notapply to these theories. We examine in detail a generalization of theHayashi-Shirafuji theory suggested by Mao et al. calledEinstein-Hayashi-Shirafuji theory. There are a variety of different versions ofthis theory, depending on the precise form of the coupling to matter chosen forthe torsion. We show that for any coupling to matter that is compatible withthe spin transport equation postulated by Mao et al., the theory has eitherghosts or an ill-posed initial value formulation. These theoretical problemscan be avoided by specializing the parameters of the theory and in additionchoosing the standard minimal coupling to matter of the torsion tensor. Thisyields a consistent theory, but one in which the action equals reactionprinciple is violated, and in which the angular momentum of the gyroscopes doesnot couple to the Earth's torsion field. Thus, the Einstein-Hayashi-Shirafujitheory does not predict a detectable torsion signal for Gravity Probe B. Theremay be other torsion theories which do.
label: human

text: Can Gravity Probe B usefully constrain torsion gravity theories? Gravity Probe B (GPB) was designed to test specific predictions of general relativity, particularly the geodetic effect and frame-dragging, with unprecedented precision. However, alternative theories of gravity with spacetime torsion can in principle modify gyroscope precession in ways that mimic or depart from the general relativistic predictions. In this work we systematically examine whether GPB data can usefully constrain torsion gravity theories beyond the standard Riemannian framework. We first classify a broad set of torsion theories according to their coupling to matter and their impact on spin and orbital motion. We then derive the modified precession equations for GPB’s gyroscopes in a general torsion background consistent with the weak-field, slow-motion regime of the Earth’s gravitational field. Particular attention is paid to the distinction between torsion effects on spin transport and those on the metric, and to how these effects project onto the GPB observables. Using the published GPB results and error budget, we place bounds on combinations of torsion parameters in representative theories, including Poincaré gauge theory and Einstein–Cartan–like models with dynamical torsion. We show that under minimal coupling assumptions for macroscopic bodies, GPB is primarily sensitive to a restricted subset of torsion components, leaving large degeneracies with metric parameters. In many torsion models, the dominant effects either vanish for unpolarized matter or can be reabsorbed into post-Newtonian parameters already tightly constrained by other experiments. Consequently, GPB provides only modest and highly model-dependent improvements over existing constraints on torsion, and it cannot serve as a generic probe of torsion gravity.
label: llm

text: We present optical spectroscopy of nine cataclysmic binary stars, mostlydwarf novae, obtained primarily to determine orbital periods Porb. The starsand their periods are LX And, 0.1509743(5) d; CZ Aql, 0.2005(6) d; LU Cam,0.1499686(4) d; GZ Cnc, 0.0881(4) d; V632 Cyg, 0.06377(8) d; V1006 Cyg,0.09903(9) d; BF Eri, 0.2708804(4) d; BI Ori, 0.1915(5) d; and FO Per, forwhich Porb is either 0.1467(4) or 0.1719(5) d.  Several of the stars proved to be especially interesting. In BF Eri, wedetect the absorption spectrum of a secondary star of spectral type K3 +- 1subclass, which leads to a distance estimate of approximately 1 kpc. However,BF Eri has a large proper motion (100 mas/yr), and we have a preliminaryparallax measurement that confirms the large proper motion and yields only anupper limit for the parallax. BF Eri's space velocity is evidently large, andit appears to belong to the halo population. In CZ Aql, the emission lines havestrong wings that move with large velocity amplitude, suggesting amagnetically-channeled accretion flow. The orbital period of V1006 Cyg placesit squarely within the 2- to 3-hour "gap" in the distribution of cataclysmicbinary orbital periods.
label: human

text: Spectroscopy of nine cataclysmic variable stars is presented, based on medium- and high-resolution optical observations obtained over multiple epochs. We report time-resolved radial-velocity measurements that enable refined orbital period determinations and constraints on the binary mass functions. The spectra reveal prominent Balmer and He I emission lines in all systems, with several objects also exhibiting He II λ4686 and Bowen blend features indicative of high excitation conditions and ongoing accretion. By modeling the emission-line profiles and Doppler tomograms, we identify accretion disk structures, bright spots, and, in some cases, evidence for magnetically channeled flows. We detect significant variability in line strengths and profiles on orbital and shorter timescales, suggesting changes in mass-transfer rates and disk geometry. For a subset of the sample, we place limits on the spectral type and contribution of the donor star, supporting their classification as short-period systems near or below the period gap. These results refine the system parameters of the nine cataclysmic variables and provide a basis for future multiwavelength studies of their accretion physics and evolutionary status.
label: llm

text: The existence of a connected 12-regular $\{K_4,K_{2,2,2}\}$-ultrahomogeneousgraph $G$ is established, (i.e. each isomorphism between two copies of $K_4$ or$K_{2,2,2}$ in $G$ extends to an automorphism of $G$), with the 42 orderedlines of the Fano plane taken as vertices. This graph $G$ can be expressed in aunique way both as the edge-disjoint union of 42 induced copies of $K_4$ and asthe edge-disjoint union of 21 induced copies of $K_{2,2,2}$, with no morecopies of $K_4$ or $K_{2,2,2}$ existing in $G$. Moreover, each edge of $G$ isshared by exactly one copy of $K_4$ and one of $K_{2,2,2}$. While the linegraphs of $d$-cubes, ($3\le d\in\ZZ$), are $\{K_d, K_{2,2}\}$-ultrahomogeneous,$G$ is not even line-graphical. In addition, the chordless 6-cycles of $G$ areseen to play an interesting role and some self-dual configurations associatedto $G$ with 2-arc-transitive, arc-transitive and semisymmetric Levi graphs areconsidered.
label: human

text: We construct and investigate a countable graph that is ultrahomogeneous with respect to the family of finite induced subgraphs isomorphic to either the complete graph \(K_4\) or the complete tripartite graph \(K_{2,2,2}\). In this context, \(\{K_4,K_{2,2,2}\}\)-ultrahomogeneity means that every isomorphism between finite induced subgraphs that are disjoint unions of copies of \(K_4\) and \(K_{2,2,2}\) extends to an automorphism of the entire graph. We provide a characterization of this graph via a suitable Fraïssé class and show that it is unique up to isomorphism. Structural properties of the graph, including its automorphism group, connectivity, and local configuration of cliques and tripartite subgraphs, are analyzed in detail. We further discuss necessary and sufficient conditions for the coexistence of \(K_4\) and \(K_{2,2,2}\) patterns in an ultrahomogeneous setting. Finally, we compare this example with other known ultrahomogeneous graphs and outline several open problems related to mixed-pattern ultrahomogeneity.
label: llm

text: The quadratic pion scalar radius, \la r^2\ra^\pi_s, plays an important rolefor present precise determinations of \pi\pi scattering. Recently, Yndur\'ain,using an Omn\`es representation of the null isospin(I) non-strange pion scalarform factor, obtains \la r^2\ra^\pi_s=0.75\pm 0.07 fm^2. This value is largerthan the one calculated by solving the corresponding Muskhelishvili-Omn\`esequations, \la r^2\ra^\pi_s=0.61\pm 0.04 fm^2. A large discrepancy between bothvalues, given the precision, then results. We reanalyze Yndur\'ain's method andshow that by imposing continuity of the resulting pion scalar form factor undertiny changes in the input \pi\pi phase shifts, a zero in the form factor forsome S-wave I=0 T-matrices is then required. Once this is accounted for, theresulting value is \la r^2\ra_s^\pi=0.65\pm 0.05 fm^2. The main source of errorin our determination is present experimental uncertainties in low energy S-waveI=0 \pi\pi phase shifts. Another important contribution to our error is the notyet settled asymptotic behaviour of the phase of the scalar form factor fromQCD.
label: human

text: We investigate the scalar radius of the pion in connection with the analytic structure of the scalar form factor, with particular emphasis on the role of zeros. Using dispersion relations and unitarity constraints, we derive model-independent relations that link the scalar radius to the low-energy behavior and possible zeros of the form factor in the complex plane. The formalism incorporates input from chiral perturbation theory and experimental ππ scattering data to constrain the phase and modulus of the scalar form factor. We show that the presence of zeros can significantly modify the dispersive representation and, consequently, the numerical value extracted for the scalar radius. In particular, we examine how different assumptions about the location and multiplicity of zeros impact the stability and convergence of the dispersive integrals. Our analysis highlights that neglecting zeros may lead to systematic biases in the determination of the scalar radius from phenomenological fits. We provide updated estimates for the scalar radius of the pion under various scenarios concerning zeros and discuss their consistency with existing lattice QCD and chiral predictions.
label: llm

text: We reanalyse leptogenesis via the out-of-equilibrium decay of the lightestright-handed neutrino in type II seesaw scenarios, taking into accountflavour-dependent effects. In the type II seesaw mechanism, in addition to thetype I seesaw contribution, an additional direct mass term for the lightneutrinos is present. We consider type II seesaw scenarios where thisadditional contribution arises from the vacuum expectation value of a Higgstriplet, and furthermore an effective model-independent approach. Weinvestigate bounds on the flavour-specific decay asymmetries, on the mass ofthe lightest right-handed neutrino and on the reheat temperature of the earlyuniverse, and compare them to the corresponding bounds in the type I seesawframework. We show that while flavour-dependent thermal type II leptogenesisbecomes more efficient for larger mass scale of the light neutrinos, and thebounds become relaxed, the type I seesaw scenario for leptogenesis becomes moreconstrained. We also argue that in general, flavour-dependent effects cannot beignored when dealing with leptogenesis in type II seesaw models.
label: human

text: Flavour-dependent effects can play a crucial role in determining the efficiency and viability of leptogenesis scenarios. In this work, we investigate type II leptogenesis in the presence of flavour-dependent interactions arising from the couplings of scalar triplets to the lepton sector. We formulate the Boltzmann equations governing the evolution of lepton asymmetries in a fully flavour-resolved framework and identify the conditions under which flavour effects significantly modify the generated baryon asymmetry. Our analysis incorporates thermal corrections, spectator processes, and flavour-dependent washout to provide a quantitatively reliable prediction of the final asymmetry. We show that flavour-dependent type II leptogenesis can substantially enlarge the region of parameter space consistent with the observed baryon asymmetry of the Universe compared to flavour-blind treatments. These results highlight the necessity of a flavour-sensitive treatment in models with scalar triplets and have important implications for the interpretation of low-energy neutrino data in the context of leptogenesis.
label: llm

text: We studied in detail the optical spectrum of the post-AGB star HD56126(IRAS07134+1005). We use high resolution spectra (R=25000 and 60000) obtainedwith the echelle spectrographs of the 6-m telescope. About one and a halfthousand absorptions of neutral atoms and ions, absorption bands of C_2, CN,and CH molecules, and interstellar bands (DIBs) are identified in the 4010 to8790 AA wavelength region, and the depths and radial velocities of thesespectral features are measured. Differences are revealed between the variationsof the radial velocities measured from spectral features of differentexcitation. In addition to the well-known variability of the Halpha profile, wefound variations in the profiles of a number of FeII, YII, and BaII lines. Wealso produce an atlas of the spectrum of HD56126 and its comparison staralphaPer. The full version of the atlas is available in electronic form fromWeb-address: http://www.sao.ru/hq/ssl/Atlas/Atlas.html
label: human

text: The high-resolution optical spectrum of the post-asymptotic giant branch (post-AGB) star HD 56126 has been investigated in the wavelength range 4010–8790 Å with the aim of characterizing its atmospheric and circumstellar properties. We identify and classify atomic and molecular features, including lines of s-process elements and molecular bands associated with carbon-rich chemistry, and measure their equivalent widths, radial velocities, and line profiles. The analysis reveals pronounced line asymmetries and differential shifts between weak and strong lines, indicative of complex velocity fields and stratification in the stellar atmosphere and envelope. From the metal lines we derive atmospheric parameters and chemical abundances, confirming HD 56126 as a metal-poor, carbon- and s-process–enhanced post-AGB object. The behavior of hydrogen Balmer lines and selected resonance lines suggests ongoing mass loss and the presence of an extended, partially ionized circumstellar shell.
label: llm

text: It has been shown that, for the two-qubit Heisenberg XY model, anisotropy andmagnetic field may together be used to produce entanglement for any finitetemperature by adjusting the external magnetic field beyond some finitecritical strength. This interesting result arises from an analysis employingthe Wootters concurrence, a computable measure of entanglement for two-qubitstates. Recently, Mintert {\em et al.} proposed generalizations of Woottersconcurrence for multipartite states. These MKB concurrences possess amathematical property that enables one to understand the origin of thischaracteristic behavior. Here, we first study the effect of anisotropy andmagnetic field on the multipartite thermal entanglement of a four-qubitHeisenberg XY chain using the MKB concurrences. We show that this modelexhibits characteristic behavior similar to that of the two-qubit model. Inaddition, we show that this can again be understood using the same mathematicalproperty. Next, we show that the six-qubit Heisenberg XY chain possessesproperties necessary for it to have the characteristic behavior too. Mostimportantly, it is possible to directly measure the multipartite MKBconcurrences of pure states. This may provide an experimental verification ofour conjecture that for a Heisenberg XY chain of any even number of qubits, itis always possible to obtain non-zero genuine multipartite entanglement at anyfinite temperature by applying a sufficiently large magnetic field.
label: human

text: We investigate the genuine multipartite entanglement properties of finite-size multi-qubit Heisenberg \(XY\) chains in the presence of anisotropy and an external transverse magnetic field. Using the framework of genuine multipartite concurrence and related entanglement witnesses, we quantify how anisotropic exchange interactions affect the structure and robustness of multipartite quantum correlations. We analyze both ground-state and thermal-state entanglement, thereby identifying temperature and field regimes where genuine multipartite entanglement persists. By varying the anisotropy parameter, we demonstrate qualitative changes in the entanglement scaling with system size and relate these to the underlying energy spectrum and correlation functions. The role of the transverse magnetic field is examined in detail, revealing field-induced suppression, enhancement, and reentrant behavior of genuine multipartite entanglement. In particular, we show that near critical points the entanglement displays characteristic nonanalytic features that can serve as indicators of quantum phase transitions. Our results highlight that anisotropy can either stabilize or destabilize genuine multipartite entanglement depending sensitively on the interplay between field strength and exchange couplings. We further compare the behavior of genuine multipartite entanglement with bipartite measures, showing that multipartite correlations can remain finite even when pairwise entanglement vanishes.
label: llm

text: We report observations of the dust cloud L1204 with the Onsala 25-m telescopein the 6 cm (1$_{11}-1_{10}$) transition of \htco. The observed region includesthe  S140 H${\alpha}$ arc. This spectral line is seen here in absorption againstthe cosmic microwave background, indicating the presence of widespread warmmolecular gas at intermediate densities. Overall, the distributions of H$_2$COand CO (taken from the literature) are fairly similar, though significantdifferences exist at small scales. Most notably, while the CO peak is nearlycoincident with the S140 H${\alpha}$ arc, the maximum H$_2$CO absorption isclearly separated from it by a full 10$'$ beam ($\sim$ 3 pc). We argue thatthese differences result from differing abundances and excitation requirements.The CO(1-0) line is more optically thick and more biased towards warm gas thanthe H$_2$CO 6 cm line. On the other hand, formaldehyde is more easilyphotodissociated and is, therefore, a poorer tracer of the molecular gaslocated immediately behind Photon Dominated Regions.
label: human

text: We present a detailed comparison between anomalous 6‑cm H$_2$CO absorption and CO(1–0) emission in the L1204/S140 star-forming complex. Using high-sensitivity radio observations, we map the spatial distributions of both tracers to investigate their correspondence across regions of varying density and radiation field strength. We find that the H$_2$CO absorption features often extend beyond the boundaries of bright CO(1–0) emission, indicating that H$_2$CO can probe lower-density or more diffuse molecular gas not well traced by CO. In contrast, the strongest CO(1–0) emission is generally associated with dense clumps and known sites of active star formation, where the H$_2$CO absorption may be weakened or confused by continuum effects. Quantitative analysis of line profiles reveals systematic differences in velocity centroids and line widths, suggesting that the two tracers sample overlapping but kinematically distinct components of the molecular cloud. Radiative transfer modeling implies that the anomalous H$_2$CO absorption arises under conditions of moderate density and subthermal excitation, sensitive to the local continuum and far-infrared radiation fields.
label: llm

text: For the first time we apply the methodologies of nonlinear analysis toinvestigate atomic matter. We use these methods in the analysis of AtomicWeights and of Mass Number of atomic nuclei. Using the AutoCorrelation Functionand Mutual Information we establish the presence of nonlinear effects in themechanism of increasing mass of atomic nuclei considered as a function of theatomic number. We find that increasing mass is divergent, possibly chaotic. Wealso investigate the possible existence of a Power Law for atomic nuclei and,using also the technique of the variogram, we conclude that a fractal regimecould superintend to the mechanism of increasing mass for nuclei. Finally,using the Hurst exponent, evidence is obtained that the mechanism of increasingmass in atomic nuclei is in the fractional Brownian regime. The mostinteresting results are obtained by using Recurrence Quantification Analysis(RQA). New recurrences, psudoperiodicities, self-resemblance and class ofself-similarities are identified with values of determinism showing oscillatingvalues indicating the presence of more or less stability during the process ofincreasing mass of atomic nuclei. In brief, new regimes of regularities areidentified for atomic nuclei that deserve to be studied by future researches.In particular an accurate analysis of binding energy values by nonlinearmethods is further required.
label: human

text: New nonlinear analysis tools are employed to investigate previously unexplored properties of atomic nuclei. In this study, we apply fractal analysis and recurrence quantification analysis (RQA) to nuclear observables, including energy spectra and transition probabilities, across a broad range of mass numbers and deformation regimes. The fractal approach is used to evaluate scaling behavior and determine generalized fractal dimensions, which are then interpreted as indicators of underlying complexity and self-similar structures in nuclear dynamics. Recurrence plots and RQA measures, such as recurrence rate, determinism, and entropy, serve to characterize the temporal-like patterns embedded in ordered sequences of nuclear data. Our results reveal distinct fractal signatures that correlate with known structural phenomena, such as shell closures, shape coexistence, and collective excitations. Moreover, the RQA parameters exhibit systematic variations that effectively discriminate between spherical, transitional, and deformed nuclear configurations. These findings suggest that nonlinear methods provide complementary information to conventional nuclear-structure models, highlighting subtle regularities and fluctuations that are not easily captured by standard approaches. We discuss the implications of these emergent scaling and recurrence properties for the description of nuclear collectivity, level clustering, and chaos-regularity interplay.
label: llm

text: Multifrequency VLBA observations of the final group of ten objects in asample of FIRST-based compact steep spectrum (CSS) sources are presented. Thesample was selected to investigate whether objects of this kind could be relicsof radio-loud AGNs switched off at very early stages of their evolution orpossibly to indicate intermittent activity. Initial observations were madeusing MERLIN at 5 GHz. The sources have now been observed with the VLBA at 1.7,5 and 8.4 GHz in a snapshot mode with phase-referencing. The resulting maps arepresented along with unpublished 8.4-GHz VLA images of five sources. Some ofthe sources discussed here show a complex radio morphology and therefore acomplicated past that, in some cases, might indicate intermittent activity. Oneof the sources studied - 1045+352 - is known as a powerful radio andinfrared-luminous broad absorption line (BAL) quasar. It is a young CSS objectwhose asymmetric two-sided morphology on a scale of several hundred parsecs,extending in two different directions, may suggest intermittent activity. Theyoung age and compact structure of 1045+352 is consistent with the evolutionscenario of BAL quasars. It has also been confirmed that the submillimetre fluxof 1045+352 can be seriously contaminated by synchrotron emission.
label: human

text: We present a Very Long Baseline Interferometry (VLBI) study of Compact Steep Spectrum (CSS) radio sources selected from the FIRST survey, focusing on their milliarcsecond-scale morphology. Our sample comprises N CSS objects identified through well-defined spectral and flux-density criteria to ensure homogeneity and minimize orientation bias. Observations were carried out at multiple frequencies to investigate the small-scale structure, spectral properties, and physical conditions in the central regions of these sources. We detect compact components in the majority of the targets, frequently resolving them into double or triple structures on linear scales of a few tens to a few hundreds of parsecs. A significant fraction of the sample exhibits symmetric morphologies consistent with Compact Symmetric Object (CSO) candidates, suggesting that many CSS sources are young radio galaxies rather than beamed core–jet systems. We find that the brightness temperatures and spectral indices of the compact components support synchrotron emission from confined jets interacting with a dense interstellar medium. Several objects show evidence of bent or distorted structures, indicative of strong jet–cloud interactions and environmental impact on source evolution. By comparing the VLBI morphology with arcsecond-scale images.
label: llm

text: The past two Decadal Surveys in Astronomy and Astrophysics recommended thecompletion of a space-based interferometry mission, known today as SIMPlanetQuest, for its unique ability to detect and characterize nearby rockyplanets (Bahcall 1991, McKee & Taylor 2001), as well as contributions to abroad range of problems in astrophysics. Numerous committees of the NationalResearch Council as well as NASA Roadmaps have similarly highlighted SIM as theone technology that offers detection and characterization of rocky planetsaround nearby stars and which is technically ready. To date, SIM remains theonly program with the capability of detecting and confirming rocky planets inthe habitable zones of nearby solar-type stars. Moreover, SIM measures massesand three-dimensional orbits of habitable planets around nearby stars (within25 pc); these are the only stars for which follow-up by other techniques isfeasible, such as space-based spectroscopy, ground-based interferometry, and ofcourse TPF.
label: human

text: SIM PlanetQuest represents the most promising near-term astrometric technique for the detection and characterization of Earth-mass planets in the habitable zones of nearby stars. By achieving sub-microarcsecond precision, SIM will measure the tiny stellar reflex motions induced by orbiting terrestrial planets, enabling robust determinations of planetary masses independent of inclination. The mission’s repeated, high-accuracy observations over several years will allow reconstruction of full three-dimensional orbits, including eccentricities and mutual inclinations in multi-planet systems. These capabilities will not only identify the most accessible nearby habitable planets for future direct imaging and spectroscopy, but also provide critical empirical constraints on planet formation, dynamical evolution, and the prevalence of potentially habitable worlds in the solar neighborhood.
label: llm

text: Star patterns, reminiscent of a wide range of diffusively controlled growthforms from snowflakes to Saffman-Taylor fingers, are ubiquitous features of icecovered lakes. Despite the commonality and beauty of these ``lake stars'' theunderlying physical processes that produce them have not been explained in acoherent theoretical framework. Here we describe a simple mathematical modelthat captures the principal features of lake-star formation; radial fingers of(relatively warm) water-rich regions grow from a central source and evolvethrough a competition between thermal and porous media flow effects in asaturated snow layer covering the lake. The number of star arms emerges from astability analysis of this competition and the qualitative features of thismeter-scale natural phenomena are captured in laboratory experiments.
label: human

text: The Formation of Lake Stars investigates the physical mechanisms responsible for the characteristic star-shaped melt patterns that appear on frozen lake surfaces. Using a combination of field observations, laboratory experiments, and numerical modeling, we examine the coupled roles of heat transfer, fluid flow in thin water films, and ice microstructure in generating radial symmetry. Our results demonstrate that small perturbations in ice thickness and surface roughness can, under specific thermal and hydrodynamic conditions, amplify into stable, star-like morphologies through a feedback between localized melting and water redistribution. These findings not only provide a unified theoretical framework for lake star formation but also contribute to a broader understanding of pattern formation in geophysical ice systems.
label: llm

text: The LHC will have unprecedented sensitivity to flavor-changing neutralcurrent (FCNC) top quark decays, whose observation would be a clear sign ofphysics beyond the standard model. Although many details of top flavorviolation are model dependent, the standard model gauge symmetries relate topFCNCs to other processes, which are strongly constrained by existing data. Westudy these constraints in a model independent way, using a low energyeffective theory from which the new physics is integrated out. We consider themost important operators which contribute to top FCNCs and analyze the currentconstraints on them. We find that the data rule out top FCNCs at a levelobservable at the LHC due to most of the operators comprising left-handed firstor second generation quark fields, while there remains a substantial window fortop decays mediated by operators with right-handed charm or up quarks. If FCNCtop decays are observed at the LHC, such an analysis may help decipher theunderlying physics.
label: human

text: We investigate the interplay between top-quark flavor-violating processes at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) and rare flavor observables measured at B factories. Using an effective field theory framework, we systematically parameterize flavor-changing neutral current interactions involving the top quark and relate them to operators constrained in the down-type quark sector. We perform a global analysis combining LHC searches for rare top decays and single top production with precision measurements from Belle, BaBar, and LHCb, including rare B decays and meson mixing. Our results demonstrate that current B-factory data significantly restrict the allowed parameter space for top flavor violation, in many cases exceeding the sensitivity of existing collider searches. We identify well-motivated benchmark scenarios in which LHC measurements can provide complementary or leading constraints, particularly in channels involving top–charm transitions. Finally, we outline strategies for future LHC runs and next-generation flavor factories to optimally probe the correlated signatures of top flavor violation and B-physics anomalies.
label: llm

text: During the last three decades, evidence has mounted that star and planetformation is not an isolated process, but is influenced by current and previousgenerations of stars. Although cool stars form in a range of environments, fromisolated globules to rich embedded clusters, the influences of other stars oncool star and planet formation may be most significant in embedded clusters,where hundreds to thousands of cool stars form in close proximity to OB stars.At the cool stars 14 meeting, a splinter session was convened to discuss therole of environment in the formation of cool stars and planetary systems; withan emphasis on the ``hot'' environment found in rich clusters. We review herethe basic results, ideas and questions presented at the session. We haveorganized this contribution into five basic questions: what is the typicalenvironment of cool star formation, what role do hot star play in cool starformation, what role does environment play in planet formation, what is therole of hot star winds and supernovae, and what was the formation environmentof the Sun? The intention is to review progress made in addressing eachquestion, and to underscore areas of agreement and contention.
label: human

text: Cool stars in hot environments provide a unique laboratory for studying stellar evolution under extreme external conditions. In this work, we investigate the physical properties, atmospheric structures, and activity levels of cool stars located in regions characterized by elevated radiation fields, strong tidal forces, or high ambient temperatures, such as galactic centers and dense stellar clusters. Using a combination of high-resolution spectroscopy, multiwavelength photometry, and numerical simulations, we quantify the impact of these harsh environments on mass loss, magnetic activity, and chemical abundances. Our results reveal systematic deviations in surface activity, rotation rates, and atmospheric escape when compared to analogous cool stars in more quiescent regions. These findings offer new constraints on stellar evolution models and have implications for planet formation and survival in dynamically and thermally extreme astrophysical settings.
label: llm

text: The question whether the dark matter halo density in the centers of galaxiescould be changed through interactions with a rotating bar in the baryonic diskis of considerable current interest. While N-body simulations have been used toaddress this question, it has also been claimed that results from suchsimulations cannot be trusted. Based on a perturbative treatment of resonantexchanges between orbits and a rotating perturbation, Weinberg & Katz contendthat N-body simulations of this process will not reveal the continuum resultunless many more than the usual numbers of particles are employed. Here Ireport a study designed to examine their contention, finding results that showno dependence on the number of particles over the range usually employed up tothat advocated by these authors. I show that my results are independent of allnumerical parameters, and that field methods perform equally with grid methodsin this respect. I also identify the reasons that the required particle numbersuggested by Weinberg & Katz is excessive.
label: human

text: Bar-halo friction, arising from the resonant exchange of angular momentum between rotating stellar bars and dark matter haloes, is a key process in the secular evolution of disc galaxies but remains numerically challenging to model accurately. We present a systematic study of the particle number requirements needed to obtain converged measurements of bar-halo friction in collisionless N-body simulations. Using a suite of controlled experiments with live haloes and self-consistent bars, we vary the number of halo particles over several orders of magnitude and quantify the impact on bar slowdown rates, resonance structure, and noise-driven diffusion in phase space. Our results show that resolving the dominant low-order resonances and suppressing spurious stochastic torques typically requires halo particle numbers of at least 10^7–10^8, depending on the bar strength and halo density profile. We demonstrate that simulations employing substantially fewer particles can significantly underestimate bar braking, misrepresent the redistribution of angular momentum, and lead to erroneous inferences about the compatibility of strong bars with cuspy dark matter profiles.
label: llm

text: A classical problem in elasticity theory involves an inhomogeneity embeddedin a material of given stress and shear moduli. The inhomogeneity is a regionof arbitrary shape whose stress and shear moduli differ from those of thesurrounding medium. In this paper we present a new, semi-analytic method forfinding the stress tensor for an infinite plate with such an inhomogeneity. Thesolution involves two conformal maps, one from the inside and the second fromthe outside of the unit circle to the inside, and respectively outside, of theinhomogeneity. The method provides a solution by matching the conformal maps onthe boundary between the inhomogeneity and the surrounding material. Thismatching converges well only for relatively mild distortions of the unit circledue to reasons which will be discussed in the article. We provide a comparisonof the present result to known previous results.
label: human

text: Elasticity problems in solids containing inhomogeneities of arbitrary shape arise in a wide range of engineering and materials-science applications. This article develops a general theoretical and computational framework for characterizing the elastic fields induced by a single inhomogeneity of completely arbitrary geometry embedded in an otherwise homogeneous host medium. The approach is based on a boundary-integral formulation of the governing elastostatic equations, enabling the reduction of the problem dimension and the treatment of complex interfaces without volumetric meshing of the entire domain. We derive explicit integral representations for displacement and traction fields that remain valid for inhomogeneities with strong material contrast, including nearly rigid or nearly void inclusions. Numerical implementation is carried out using high-order quadrature schemes and adaptive discretization of the inhomogeneity boundary to resolve geometric features such as sharp corners and high curvature regions.
label: llm

text: The assumption of the capture by the Solar System of the electrically chargedPlanckian DM objects (daemons) from the galactic disk is confirmed not only bythe St.Petersburg (SPb) experiments detecting particles with V<30 km/s. Herethe daemon approach is analyzed considering the positive model independentresult of the DAMA/NaI experiment. We explain the maximum in DAMA signalsobserved in the May-June period to be associated with the formation behind theSun of a trail of daemons that the Sun captures into elongated orbits as itmoves to the apex. The range of significant 2-6-keV DAMA signals fits well theiodine nuclei elastically knocked out of the NaI(Tl) scintillator by particlesfalling on the Earth with V=30-50 km/s from strongly elongated heliocentricorbits. The half-year periodicity of the slower daemons observed in SPboriginates from the transfer of particles that are deflected through ~90 deginto near-Earth orbits each time the particles cross the outer reaches of theSun which had captured them. Their multi-loop (cross-like) trajectoriestraverse many times the Earth's orbit in March and September, which increasesthe probability for the particles to enter near-Earth orbits during this time.Corroboration of celestial mechanics calculations with observations yields~1e-19 cm2 for the cross section of daemon interaction with the solar matter.
label: human

text: Daemons and DAMA: Their Celestial-Mechanics Interrelations We investigate a hypothetical population of dark electric matter objects (“daemons”) and their possible role in explaining annual modulation signals observed by the DAMA experiment. Building on celestial mechanics, we model the capture, orbital evolution, and spatial distribution of daemons in the Solar System, focusing on Earth-crossing trajectories. Our analysis explores how gravitational focusing by the Earth and Sun, combined with the kinematic properties of the galactic halo, can yield a seasonally varying flux at Earth. We derive the expected temporal and spectral signatures of daemon interactions in terrestrial detectors and compare them with the DAMA/LIBRA modulation pattern. The results indicate that, within certain parameter ranges for daemon mass, charge, and interaction cross section, the predicted modulation amplitude and phase can be made compatible with DAMA’s observations. We conclude by outlining the critical observational and experimental tests needed to distinguish the daemon-based explanation from more conventional WIMP and background-origin scenarios.
label: llm

text: We report results from a 30 ks observation of Cygnus X-1 with the High EnergyTransmission Grating Spectrometer (HETGS) on board the {\em Chandra X-rayObservatory}. Numerous absorption lines were detected in the HETGS spectrum.The lines are associated with highly ionized Ne, Na, Mg, Al, Si, S, and Fe,some of which have been seen in earlier HETGS observations. Surprisingly,however, we discovered dramatic variability of the lines over the duration ofthe present observation. For instance, the flux of the Ne X line at 12.14 \AA\was about $5 \times 10^{-3}$ photons cm$^{-2}$ s$^{-1}$ in the early part ofthe observation but became subsequently undetectable, with a 99% upper limit of$0.06 \times 10^{-3}$ photons cm$^{-2}$ s$^{-1}$ on the flux of the line. Thisimplies that the line weakened by nearly two orders of magnitude on a timescaleof hours. The overall X-ray flux of the source did also vary during theobservation but only by 20--30%. For Cyg X-1, the absorption lines aregenerally attributed to the absorption of X-rays by ionized stellar wind in thebinary system. Therefore, they may provide valuable diagnostics on the physicalcondition of the wind. We discuss the implications of the results.
label: human

text: We report on a systematic study of the temporal variability of X-ray absorption lines in the black hole candidate Cygnus X-1 using high-resolution spectroscopy. Our analysis combines multiple observations obtained with modern X-ray observatories to characterize changes in line strength, centroid energy, and profile shape on timescales ranging from minutes to days. We detect prominent absorption features from highly ionized species, including Fe XXV and Fe XXVI, whose properties exhibit dramatic variability correlated with the source’s spectral state and luminosity. The equivalent widths of these lines vary by factors of several, indicating substantial changes in the column density and ionization state of the absorbing material. In particular, we find that transitions between the hard and soft spectral states are accompanied by systematic shifts in ionization balance and line-of-sight velocity structure. Phase-resolved analysis around the binary orbit reveals that the variability is also modulated by the geometry of the focused stellar wind from the donor star. Modeling the line profiles suggests that a clumpy, anisotropic, and partially ionized wind, influenced by X-ray irradiation and possibly by the black hole’s accretion disk, is required to reproduce the observations.
label: llm

text: Within the internal shock scenario we consider different mechanisms of highenergy ($>1$ MeV) photon production inside a Gamma Ray Burst (GRB) fireball andderive the expected high energy photon spectra from individual GRBs during theprompt phase. The photon spectra of leptonic and hadronic origins are comparedwithin different sets of parameter regimes. Our results suggest that the highenergy emission is dominated by the leptonic component if fraction of shockenergy carried by electrons is not very small (e.g. $\epsilon_e > 10^{-3}$).For very small values of $\epsilon_e$ the hadronic emission component could becomparable to or even exceed the leptonic component in the GeV-TeV regime.However, in this case a much larger energy budget of the fireball is requiredto account for the same level of the observed sub-MeV spectrum. The fireballsare therefore extremely inefficient in radiation. For a canonical fireball bulkLorentz factor (e.g. $\Gamma=400$), emissions above $\sim 10$ GeV areattenuated by two-photon pair production processes. For a fireball with an evenhigher Lorentz factor, the cutoff energy is higher, and emissions of 10 TeV -PeV due to $\pi^0$-decay can also escape from the internal shocks. The fluxlevel is however too low to be detected by current TeV detectors, and thesephotons also suffer attenuation by external soft photons.
label: human

text: We investigate the prompt emission of high energy photons from gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) using a combination of recent observational data and theoretical modeling. Our study focuses on the temporal and spectral properties of photons with energies above several tens of MeV detected during the prompt phase. We analyze a sample of GRBs observed by space-based gamma-ray observatories, emphasizing events with robust high-energy detections and well-constrained redshifts. The data reveal extended high-energy emission relative to the lower-energy prompt component, as well as distinct spectral breaks and delays that challenge simple one-zone emission models. We interpret these features within the framework of internal shock, magnetic dissipation, and photospheric emission scenarios, assessing the viability of leptonic and hadronic radiative processes. Our modeling suggests that inverse Compton scattering in relativistic outflows can account for much of the observed high-energy component, but that hadronic processes may be required for the most extreme events. Constraints on bulk Lorentz factors, emission radii, and magnetic field strengths are derived from opacity arguments and spectral fitting. We further discuss the implications of high-energy prompt emission for the production of ultra-high-energy cosmic rays and high-energy neutrinos. These results provide a coherent physical picture of prompt high-energy photon production in GRBs and delineate key observational tests for future.
label: llm

text: Let $\Dh$ and $A$ be unital and separable $C^{*}$-algebras; let $\Dh$ bestrongly self-absorbing. It is known that any two unital $^*$-homomorphismsfrom $\Dh$ to $A \otimes \Dh$ are approximately unitarily equivalent. We showthat, if $\Dh$ is also $K_{1}$-injective, they are even asymptoticallyunitarily equivalent. This in particular implies that any unital endomorphismof $\Dh$ is asymptotically inner. Moreover, the space of automorphisms of $\Dh$is compactly-contractible (in the point-norm topology) in the sense that forany compact Hausdorff space $X$, the set of homotopy classes $[X,\Aut(\Dh)]$reduces to a point. The respective statement holds for the space of unitalendomorphisms of $\Dh$. As an application, we give a description of theKasparov group $KK(\Dh, A\ot \Dh)$ in terms of $^*$-homomorphisms andasymptotic unitary equivalence. Along the way, we show that the Kasparov group$KK(\Dh, A\ot \Dh)$ is isomorphic to $K_0(A\ot \Dh)$.
label: human

text: We study the Kasparov KK-theory of strongly self-absorbing C*-algebras and its interaction with their internal structural properties. Building on the defining absorption isomorphism \(D \cong D \otimes D\), we analyze the induced maps in bivariant K-theory and show that they exhibit a high degree of rigidity. In particular, we establish conditions under which the KK-groups \(KK(D, D)\) and \(KK(\mathbb{C}, D)\) are determined by the order structure and approximate innerness of the canonical embedding \(D \hookrightarrow D \otimes D\). We prove that for a large class of strongly self-absorbing C*-algebras, the unit in \(KK(D,D)\) is uniquely characterized by its behavior under these absorption maps. As an application, we derive classification results for separable, nuclear C*-algebras that absorb a given strongly self-absorbing C*-algebra tensorially, formulated purely in terms of KK-theoretic data. We show that in many cases the KK-equivalence class of such an algebra is rigid under small perturbations and approximately inner automorphisms.
label: llm

text: We have measured the flux, profile, color, and substructure in the diffuseintracluster light (ICL) in a sample of ten galaxy clusters with a range ofmass, morphology, redshift, and density. Deep, wide-field observations for thisproject were made in two bands at the one meter Swope and 2.5 meter du Ponttelescope at Las Campanas Observatory. Careful attention in reduction andanalysis was paid to the illumination correction, background subtraction, pointspread function determination, and galaxy subtraction. ICL flux is detected inboth bands in all ten clusters ranging from 7.6 x 10^{10} to 7.0 x 10^{11}h^{-1} solar luminosities in r and 1.4 x 10^{10} to 1.2 x 10^{11} h^{-1} solarluminosities in the B-band. These fluxes account for 6 to 22% of the totalcluster light within one quarter of the virial radius in r and 4 to 21% in theB-band. Average ICL B-r colors range from 1.5 to 2.8 mags when k and evolutioncorrected to the present epoch. In several clusters we also detect ICL in groupenvironments near the cluster center and up to ~1 h^{-1} Mpc distant from thecluster center. Our sample, having been selected from the Abell sample, isincomplete in that it does not include high redshift clusters with low density,low flux, or low mass, and it does not include low redshift clusters with highflux, mass, or density. This bias makes it difficult to interpret correlationsbetween ICL flux and cluster properties. Despite this selection bias, we dofind that the presence of a cD galaxy corresponds to both centrallyconcentrated galaxy profiles and centrally concentrated ICL profiles. This isconsistent with ICL either forming from galaxy interactions at the center, orforming at earlier times in groups and later combining in the center.
label: human

text: We investigate correlations between diffuse intracluster light (ICL) and global cluster properties in a statistically well-defined sample of galaxy clusters. Using deep, multi-band imaging from [survey/instrument placeholder], we derive spatially resolved maps of diffuse optical emission after carefully modeling and subtracting the contributions from cluster galaxies and foreground/background sources. The ICL is quantified through its surface brightness profiles, total luminosities, colors, and morphologies, and these measurements are compared to cluster mass, richness, dynamical state, and brightest cluster galaxy (BCG) properties. We find that the ICL fraction, defined as the ratio of diffuse light to total cluster optical luminosity, increases systematically with cluster mass and richness, albeit with substantial intrinsic scatter. Clusters exhibiting strong evidence of dynamical activity, such as substructure in the galaxy distribution or significant X-ray asymmetries, tend to host higher ICL fractions and more extended diffuse light profiles. The colors of the ICL are generally consistent with those of the red sequence population, but show mild radial gradients indicative of a mixture of disrupted satellites with different star-formation histories. We find a strong correlation between ICL luminosity and BCG stellar mass, suggesting that processes building up the BCG also contribute significantly to the diffuse component. At fixed mass, clusters with more centrally concentrated galaxy distributions display larger central ICL surface brightnesses, consistent with efficient tidal stripping in dense environments. Comparisons with state-of-the-art hydrodynamical simulations indicate that the observed ICL fractions and their trends with mass and dynamical state are broadly reproduced.
label: llm

text: We derive masses and radii for both components in the single-lined eclipsingbinary HAT-TR-205-013, which consists of a F7V primary and a late M-dwarfsecondary. The system's period is short, $P=2.230736 \pm 0.000010$ days, withan orbit indistinguishable from circular, $e=0.012 \pm 0.021$. We demonstrategenerally that the surface gravity of the secondary star in a single-linedbinary undergoing total eclipses can be derived from characteristics of thelight curve and spectroscopic orbit. This constrains the secondary to a uniqueline in the mass-radius diagram with $M/R^2$ = constant. For HAT-TR-205-013, weassume the orbit has been tidally circularized, and that the primary's rotationhas been synchronized and aligned with the orbital axis. Our observed linebroadening, $V_{\rm rot} \sin i_{\rm rot} = 28.9 \pm 1.0$ \kms, gives a primaryradius of $R_{\rm A} = 1.28 \pm 0.04$ \rsun. Our light curve analysis leads tothe radius of the secondary, $R_{\rm B} = 0.167 \pm 0.006$ \rsun, and thesemimajor axis of the orbit, $a = 7.54 \pm 0.30 \rsun = 0.0351 \pm 0.0014$ AU.Our single-lined spectroscopic orbit and the semimajor axis then yield theindividual masses, $M_{\rm B} = 0.124 \pm 0.010$ \msun and $M_{\rm A} = 1.04\pm 0.13$ \msun. Our result for HAT-TR-205-013 B lies above the theoreticalmass-radius models from the Lyon group, consistent with results fromdouble-lined eclipsing binaries. The method we describe offers the opportunityto study the very low end of the stellar mass-radius relation.
label: human

text: We present a comprehensive characterization of the unseen M-dwarf companion in the single-lined eclipsing binary system HAT-TR-205-013. Using high-precision time-series photometry of the primary eclipse from ground-based telescopes, we derive stringent constraints on the orbital geometry and inclination. High-resolution spectroscopy of the primary star yields radial velocity amplitudes that, combined with the photometric solution, allow us to infer the mass function of the system. Adopting spectroscopically determined stellar parameters and evolutionary models for the F-type primary, we determine the primary’s mass and radius and propagate these to obtain the companion’s absolute mass. The relative photometric radius ratio and the well-constrained orbital inclination provide an accurate measurement of the M-dwarf’s radius. We find that the companion has a mass of approximately [M value] M⊙ and a radius of approximately [R value] R⊙, placing it firmly within the mid M-dwarf regime. These measurements are compared against contemporary low-mass stellar evolutionary tracks, revealing [general agreement / a modest discrepancy] in the predicted mass–radius relation. We discuss the implications of our findings for the inflation of low-mass stellar radii and the role of metallicity, age, and magnetic activity in shaping the structure of M-dwarfs. HAT-TR-205-013 thus adds a valuable, precisely characterized data point to the empirical calibration of low-mass stellar models.
label: llm

text: We calculate the form factors for the semileptonic decays of heavy-lightpseudoscalar mesons in partially quenched staggered chiral perturbation theory(\schpt), working to leading order in $1/m_Q$, where $m_Q$ is the heavy quarkmass. We take the light meson in the final state to be a pseudoscalarcorresponding to the exact chiral symmetry of staggered quarks. The treatmentassumes the validity of the standard prescription for representing thestaggered ``fourth root trick'' within \schpt by insertions of factors of 1/4for each sea quark loop. Our calculation is based on an existing partiallyquenched continuum chiral perturbation theory calculation with degenerate seaquarks by Becirevic, Prelovsek and Zupan, which we generalize to the staggered(and non-degenerate) case. As a by-product, we obtain the continuum partiallyquenched results with non-degenerate sea quarks. We analyze the effects ofnon-leading chiral terms, and find a relation among the coefficients governingthe analytic valence mass dependence at this order. Our results are useful inanalyzing lattice computations of form factors $B\to\pi$ and $D\to K$ when thelight quarks are simulated with the staggered action.
label: human

text: We investigate heavy-light semileptonic decays in the framework of staggered chiral perturbation theory (SχPT), focusing on the impact of lattice discretization effects on form factors relevant for precision determinations of CKM matrix elements. Starting from a heavy-meson chiral Lagrangian augmented with staggered light quarks, we derive the chiral and continuum extrapolation formulae for the relevant heavy-to-light transition matrix elements at next-to-leading order. Taste-breaking effects are incorporated systematically, and their contributions to the chiral logarithms and analytic terms in the semileptonic form factors are explicitly identified. We present results for generic heavy-light decays, with particular attention to processes such as \(B \to \pi \ell \nu\) and \(D \to K \ell \nu\), which are central to current and future lattice QCD studies. Our analysis clarifies how staggered taste splittings modify the momentum and light-quark mass dependence of the form factors, and we provide parameterizations suitable for fitting lattice data. We also discuss the matching of the SχPT expressions to continuum chiral perturbation theory and identify the low-energy constants that control the discretization corrections.
label: llm

text: Spectral variability is the main tool for constraining emission models of BL  Lac objects. By means of systematic observations of the BL Lac prototype PKS2155-304 in the infrared-optical band, we explore variability on the scales ofmonths, days and hours. We made our observations with the robotic 60 cmtelescope REM located at La Silla, Chile. VRIJHK filters were used. PKS2155-304 was observed from May to December 2005. The wavelength intervalexplored, the total number of photometric points and the short integration timerender our photometry substantially superior to previous ones for this source.On the basis of the intensity and colour we distinguish three different statesof the source, each of duration of months, which include all those described inthe literature. In particular, we report the highest state ever detected in theH band. The source varied by a factor of 4 in this band, much more than in theV band (a factor ~2). The source softened with increasing intensity, contraryto the general pattern observed in the UV-X-ray bands. On five nights ofNovember we had nearly continuous monitoring for 2-3 hours. A variabilityepisode with a time scale of ~24 h is well documented, a much more rapid flarewith t=1-2 h, is also apparent, but is supported by relatively few points.
label: human

text: We present near-infrared and optical multiband observations of the BL Lac object PKS 2155-304 obtained with the Rapid Eye Mount (REM) telescope during an intensive monitoring campaign in 2005. The source was observed quasi-simultaneously in the VRIJHK bands over several months, providing one of the most densely sampled datasets of its low-energy emission in this period. Our primary goals were to characterize the variability amplitude and timescales in the near-IR/optical regime, to search for correlated behavior between bands, and to constrain the spectral energy distribution (SED) of the synchrotron component. The REM data reveal significant variability in all bands, with typical flux changes of tens of percent on timescales of days and more modest variations on intra-night timescales. We detect a clear trend of increasing variability amplitude toward shorter wavelengths, consistent with expectations for synchrotron-dominated emission from a relativistic jet. Cross-correlation analysis indicates that the variations in the near-IR and optical bands are highly correlated, with no measurable time lag within our temporal resolution. The broad-band near-IR/optical SED is well described by a single power law, whose spectral index exhibits modest but systematic changes correlated with the source flux level.
label: llm

text: In this manuscript we investigate the capabilities of the Discrete DipoleApproximation (DDA) to simulate scattering from particles that are much largerthan the wavelength of the incident light, and describe an optimized publiclyavailable DDA computer program that processes the large number of dipolesrequired for such simulations. Numerical simulations of light scattering byspheres with size parameters x up to 160 and 40 for refractive index m=1.05 and2 respectively are presented and compared with exact results of the Mie theory.Errors of both integral and angle-resolved scattering quantities generallyincrease with m and show no systematic dependence on x. Computational timesincrease steeply with both x and m, reaching values of more than 2 weeks on acluster of 64 processors. The main distinctive feature of the computer programis the ability to parallelize a single DDA simulation over a cluster ofcomputers, which allows it to simulate light scattering by very largeparticles, like the ones that are considered in this manuscript. Currentlimitations and possible ways for improvement are discussed.
label: human

text: The discrete dipole approximation (DDA) is extended and systematically analyzed for simulating light scattering by particles whose characteristic dimensions greatly exceed the incident wavelength. We investigate numerical stability, convergence behavior, and accuracy of DDA solutions for large size parameters, emphasizing the roles of dipole spacing, lattice geometry, and iterative solver performance. Benchmark comparisons with Mie theory for spheres and with finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) simulations for nonspherical particles demonstrate that, under appropriate discretization and preconditioning, DDA can yield quantitatively reliable results even for size parameters exceeding several tens. These findings delineate practical guidelines and computational constraints for applying DDA to large-particle scattering problems in atmospheric optics, astrophysics, and nanophotonics.
label: llm

text: We report on FUSE spectra of three U Gem-type, long period, dwarf novae, UUAql, BV Cen and CH UMa taken during their quiescence intervals. We discuss theline identifications in their spectra and attempt to characterize the source(s)of their FUV flux distribution. Archival IUE spectrum of CH UMa and BV Cen inquiescence were identified as having a matching flux level with the FUSEspectra and these were combined with each FUSE spectrum to broaden thewavelength coverage and further constrain model fits. Multi-component syntheticspectral fits from our model grids, consisting of single temperature whitedwarfs, two-temperature white dwarfs, accretion disks and white dwarfs plusaccretion disks, were applied to the FUSE spectra alone and to the combinedFUSE + IUE spectra. We present the results of our model analyses and theirimplications.
label: human

text: We present Far Ultraviolet Spectroscopic Explorer (FUSE) observations of the dwarf novae UU Aql, BV Cen, and CH UMa in quiescence, obtained to investigate the properties of their accreting white dwarfs and residual disk emission. The far-ultraviolet spectra in the 905–1187 Å range are analyzed using synthetic white dwarf atmosphere models and accretion disk models to constrain effective temperatures, surface gravities, and accretion rates. For all three systems, we find that the quiescent far-ultraviolet flux is dominated by a hot white dwarf photosphere with temperatures in the range of approximately 25,000–40,000 K, with only modest contributions from a cool, optically thin disk or boundary layer. We discuss the implications of these temperatures for compressional heating and long-term accretion histories, comparing our results with other well-studied dwarf novae in similar orbital period regimes.
label: llm

text: We present wide-field BVI photometry for about 11,500 stars in thelow-metallicity cluster NGC 5466. We have detected the red giant branch bumpfor the first time, although it is at least 0.2 mag fainter than expectedrelative to the turnoff. The number of red giants (relative to main sequenceturnoff stars) is in excellent agreement with stellar models from theYonsei-Yale and Teramo groups, and slightly high compared to Victoria-Reginamodels. This adds to evidence that an abnormally large ratio of red giant tomain-sequence stars is not correlated with cluster metallicity. We discusstheoretical predictions from different research groups and find that theinclusion or exclusion of helium diffusion and strong limit Coulombinteractions may be partly responsible.  We also examine indicators of dynamical history: the mass function exponentand the blue straggler frequency. NGC 5466 has a very shallow mass function,consistent with large mass loss and recently-discovered tidal tails. The bluestraggler sample is significantly more centrally concentrated than the HB orRGB stars. We see no evidence of an upturn in the blue straggler frequency atlarge distances from the center. Dynamical friction timescales indicate thatthe stragglers should be more concentrated if the cluster's present densitystructure has existed for most of its history. NGC 5466 also has an unusuallylow central density compared to clusters of similar luminosity. In spite ofthis, the specific frequency of blue stragglers that puts it right on thefrequency -- cluster M_V relation observed for other clusters.
label: human

text: We present a comprehensive CCD photometric study of the low-metallicity globular cluster NGC 5466, with particular emphasis on its red giant and blue straggler populations. Deep V and I images were obtained with a wide-field imager, yielding precise photometry for several thousand stars over a region extending beyond the cluster’s half-light radius. The resulting color–magnitude diagram (CMD) reaches well below the main-sequence turnoff and clearly delineates the red giant branch (RGB), horizontal branch, and blue straggler star (BSS) sequences. By fitting theoretical isochrones to the observed CMD, we derive an age of approximately 12–13 Gyr and confirm a low metallicity of [Fe/H] ≈ −2.0 for NGC 5466. The RGB luminosity function displays a well-defined bump whose location is consistent with the cluster’s metallicity and with standard stellar evolution models. We find no compelling evidence for an unusually enhanced mass-loss rate along the RGB, based on the morphology of the horizontal branch and the distribution of evolved stars. A catalog of blue straggler candidates is constructed using both photometric selection in the CMD and spatial information to minimize field contamination. The BSS population is moderately centrally concentrated relative to the subgiant and main-sequence stars, but shows a shallower radial profile than that observed in more dynamically evolved clusters. This suggests that NGC 5466 is in an intermediate stage of dynamical evolution, where mass segregation is present but not yet extreme. The luminosity distribution of the BSS indicates a mixture of relatively bright and faint objects.
label: llm

text: We point out some pitfalls related to the concept of an oracle property asused in Fan and Li (2001, 2002, 2004) which are reminiscent of the well-knownpitfalls related to Hodges' estimator. The oracle property is often aconsequence of sparsity of an estimator. We show that any estimator satisfyinga sparsity property has maximal risk that converges to the supremum of the lossfunction; in particular, the maximal risk diverges to infinity whenever theloss function is unbounded. For ease of presentation the result is set in theframework of a linear regression model, but generalizes far beyond thatsetting. In a Monte Carlo study we also assess the extent of the problem infinite samples for the smoothly clipped absolute deviation (SCAD) estimatorintroduced in Fan and Li (2001). We find that this estimator can perform ratherpoorly in finite samples and that its worst-case performance relative tomaximum likelihood deteriorates with increasing sample size when the estimatoris tuned to sparsity.
label: human

text: Sparse estimators, which set a subset of estimated parameters identically to zero with probability approaching one, have gained prominence in high-dimensional statistics due to their interpretability and computational advantages. We show that a broad class of such estimators can be constructed to possess the so-called oracle property, whereby they asymptotically identify the true model and estimate the nonzero parameters as efficiently as if the true model were known in advance. However, we demonstrate that this oracle behavior is analogous to the classical Hodges’ estimator phenomenon, in which striking asymptotic optimality coexists with poor and unstable finite-sample performance. In particular, we establish that estimators satisfying the oracle property can exhibit severe non-uniformity in their distributions, large finite-sample risks, and pronounced sensitivity to small perturbations of the data-generating process. These findings call into question the practical relevance of the oracle property as a benchmark for estimator performance and model selection.
label: llm

text: We provide a model for how Kennicutt-Schmidt (KS) laws, which describe thecorrelation between star formation rate and gas surface or volume density,depend on the molecular line chosen to trace the gas. We show that, for linesthat can be excited at low temperatures, the KS law depends on how the linecritical density compares to the median density in a galaxy's star-formingmolecular clouds. High critical density lines trace regions with similarphysical properties across galaxy types, and this produces a linear correlationbetween line luminosity and star formation rate. Low critical density linesprobe regions whose properties vary across galaxies, leading to a starformation rate that varies superlinearly with line luminosity. We show that asimple model in which molecular clouds are treated as isothermal and homogenouscan quantitatively reproduce the observed correlations between galacticluminosities in far infrared and in the CO(1->0) and HCN(1->0) lines, andnaturally explains why these correlations have different slopes. We predictthat IR-line luminosity correlations should change slope for galaxies in whichthe median density is close to the line critical density. This prediction maybe tested by observations of lines such as HCO^+(1->0) with intermediatecritical densities, or by HCN(1->0) observations of intensely star-forming highredshift galaxies with very high densities. Recent observations by Gao et al.hint at just such a change in slope. We argue that deviations from linearity inthe HCN(1->0)-IR correlation at high luminosity are consistent with theassumption of a constant star formation efficiency.
label: human

text: The Kennicutt–Schmidt (KS) laws relate gas content to star formation, but the impact of different molecular gas tracers on their form and universality remains uncertain. In this work, we investigate how commonly used tracers of molecular gas, including CO rotational transitions and high-density tracers such as HCN and HCO⁺, influence the inferred KS relations on sub-kiloparsec and global scales. We compile a heterogeneous sample of nearby star-forming galaxies and starbursts with matched multiwavelength data to derive surface densities of star formation and molecular gas.
