We see no signal for the Y(4260)and obtain an upper limit of$\BR_{Y(4260)\to\phi\pi^+\pi^-}\cdot\Gamma^{Y}_{ee}<0.4 \ev$ at 90% C.L.
label: human

text: We report measurements of the cross sections for the processes \(e^+ e^- \to K^+ K^- \pi^+ \pi^-,\ K^+ K^- \pi^0 \pi^0,\) and \(K^+ K^- K^+ K^-\) using the initial-state radiation (ISR) technique. The analysis is based on a data sample corresponding to an integrated luminosity of [X] fb\(^{-1}\) collected with the [Detector] at the [Collider] operating near \(\sqrt{s} \sim 10.6\) GeV. By reconstructing ISR photons, we obtain the effective hadronic cross sections over a continuum of \(e^+e^-\) center-of-mass energies from threshold up to about 5 GeV. We perform a detailed event selection and background suppression, including kinematic fits and particle identification, achieving high signal purity for each final state. The measured cross sections exhibit clear structures associated with intermediate vector resonances and their interferences, which are studied through fits to the invariant mass distributions and angular correlations. We use the results to extract contributions of these channels to the hadronic vacuum polarization component of the anomalous magnetic moment of the muon and to test predictions of QCD-inspired models. These measurements significantly improve the precision and energy coverage of kaon–pion and multi-kaon cross sections, providing new input for hadronic phenomenology and precision electroweak tests.
label: llm

text: In a sensor network, in practice, the communication among sensors is subjectto:(1) errors or failures at random times; (3) costs; and(2) constraints sincesensors and networks operate under scarce resources, such as power, data rate,or communication. The signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) is usually a main factor indetermining the probability of error (or of communication failure) in a link.These probabilities are then a proxy for the SNR under which the links operate.The paper studies the problem of designing the topology, i.e., assigning theprobabilities of reliable communication among sensors (or of link failures) tomaximize the rate of convergence of average consensus, when the linkcommunication costs are taken into account, and there is an overallcommunication budget constraint. To consider this problem, we address a numberof preliminary issues: (1) model the network as a random topology; (2)establish necessary and sufficient conditions for mean square sense (mss) andalmost sure (a.s.) convergence of average consensus when network links fail;and, in particular, (3) show that a necessary and sufficient condition for bothmss and a.s. convergence is for the algebraic connectivity of the mean graphdescribing the network topology to be strictly positive. With these results, weformulate topology design, subject to random link failures and to acommunication cost constraint, as a constrained convex optimization problem towhich we apply semidefinite programming techniques. We show by an extensivenumerical study that the optimal design improves significantly the convergencespeed of the consensus algorithm and can achieve the asymptotic performance ofa non-random network at a fraction of the communication cost.
label: human

text: We investigate topology design for distributed consensus in sensor networks whose communication links are random and time-varying. Building on stochastic graph models, we characterize how link activation probabilities and network connectivity jointly determine convergence rates and robustness to link failures. We formulate an optimization problem that selects network topologies and link reliabilities to minimize consensus error subject to energy and degree constraints. Analytical results yield tractable conditions for mean-square convergence and provide structural insights into optimal sparse topologies under uncertainty. Numerical simulations validate the theoretical predictions and demonstrate significant performance gains over conventional deterministic topology designs.
label: llm

text: The unusual properties of transition objects (young stars with an opticallythin inner disc surrounded by an optically thick outer disc) suggest thatsignificant disc evolution has occured in these systems. We explore the natureof these systems by examining their demographics, specifically their stellaraccretion rates (Mdot) and disc masses (Mdisc) compared to those of accreting TTauri stars of comparable age. We find that transition objects in Taurus occupya restricted region of the Mdot vs. Mdisc plane. Compared to non-transitionsingle stars in Taurus, they have stellar accretion rates that are typically~10 times lower at the same disc mass and median disc masses ~4 times larger.These properties are anticipated by several proposed planet formation theoriesand suggest that the formation of Jovian mass planets may play a significantrole in explaining the origin of at least some transition objects. Consideringtransition objects as a distinct demographic group among accreting T Tauristars leads to a tighter relationship between disc masses and stellar accretionrates, with a slope between the two quantities that is close to the value ofunity expected in simple theories of disc accretion.
label: human

text: Transition objects—young stellar objects with inner disk clearings—offer key insights into protoplanetary disk evolution and planet formation. In this study, we compile and homogenize multiwavelength data for a large sample of confirmed and candidate transition objects across multiple star-forming regions. We investigate the demographics of these systems as a function of stellar mass, age, environment, and disk properties, using uniform selection criteria and robust statistical methods. Our analysis reveals distinct trends in transition object incidence with stellar mass and cluster age, as well as correlations between inner hole size, accretion activity, and infrared excess. These results constrain the relative roles of photoevaporation, dynamical clearing by companions, and grain growth in producing transition disks, and provide empirical benchmarks for theoretical models of disk dispersal.
label: llm

text: The nonlinear saturation of the r-mode instability and its effects on thespin evolution of Low Mass X-ray Binaries (LMXBs) are modeled using the tripletof modes at the lowest parametric instability threshold. We solve numericallythe coupled equations for the three mode amplitudes in conjunction with thespin and temperature evolution equations. We observe that very quickly the modeamplitudes settle into quasi-stationary states. Once these states are reached,the mode amplitudes can be found algebraically and the system of equations isreduced from eight to two equations: spin and temperature evolution.Eventually, the system may reach thermal equilibrium and either (1) undergo acyclic evolution with a frequency change of at most 10%, (2) evolve toward afull equilibrium state in which the accretion torque balances the gravitationalradiation emission, or (3) enter a thermogravitational runaway on a very longtimescale of about $10^6$ years. Alternatively, a faster thermal runaway(timescale of about 100 years) may occur. The sources of damping considered areshear viscosity, hyperon bulk viscosity and boundary layer viscosity. We varyproprieties of the star such as the hyperon superfluid transition temperatureT_c, the fraction of the star that is above the threshold for direct URCAreactions, and slippage factor, and map the different scenarios we obtain toranges of these parameters. For all our bound evolutions the r-mode amplituderemains small $\sim 10^{-5}$. The spin frequency is limited by boundary layerviscosity to $\nu_{max} \sim 800 Hz [S_{ns}/(M_{1.4} R_6)]^{4/11} T_8^{-2/11}$.We find that for $\nu > 700$ Hz the r-mode instability would be active forabout 1 in 1000 LMXBs and that only the gravitational waves from LMXBs in thelocal group of galaxies could be detected by advanced LIGO interferometers.
label: human

text: Spin evolution of accreting neutron stars is strongly influenced by the excitation and nonlinear saturation of r-mode oscillations driven by gravitational radiation. In this work, we investigate the nonlinear development of the r-mode instability in rapidly rotating, accreting neutron stars using a combined framework of secular evolution equations and mode-coupling theory. We incorporate realistic microphysical inputs, including shear and bulk viscosities, superfluid mutual friction, and crust-core coupling, to delineate the instability window in the temperature–spin frequency plane. Our analysis demonstrates that nonlinear interactions with a network of daughter modes naturally lead to amplitude saturation well below the values inferred from simple parametric estimates. We show that the saturated r-mode torque can balance the accretion torque over astrophysically relevant timescales, producing quasi-stationary spin equilibria that limit the maximum rotation rates of low-mass X-ray binaries. The resulting spin distributions are compared with observed spin frequencies of accreting neutron stars, and we find that our model reproduces the observed clustering around several hundred Hz without fine-tuning of parameters. We also explore the impact of varying the accretion rate and magnetic field strength, revealing that modest changes in these quantities can significantly shift the effective spin equilibrium. Our results predict intermittent episodes of enhanced gravitational-wave emission associated with transitions into and out of the r-mode unstable regime. We conclude by discussing the implications of our findings for current and future gravitational-wave searches and for constraining the internal physics of neutron star matter.
label: llm

text: Common envelopes form in dynamical time scale mass exchange, when theenvelope of a donor star engulfs a much denser companion, and the core of thedonor plus the dense companion star spiral inward through this dissipativeenvelope. As conceived by Paczynski and Ostriker, this process must beresponsible for the creation of short-period binaries with degeneratecomponents, and, indeed, it has proven capable of accounting for short-periodbinaries containing one white dwarf component. However, attempts to reconstructthe evolutionary histories of close double white dwarfs have proven moreproblematic, and point to the need for enhanced systemic mass loss, eitherduring the close of the first, slow episode of mass transfer that produced thefirst white dwarf, or during the detached phase preceding the final, commonenvelope episode. The survival of long-period interacting binaries with massivewhite dwarfs, such as the recurrent novae T CrB and RS Oph, also presentsinterpretative difficulties for simple energetic treatments of common envelopeevolution. Their existence implies that major terms are missing from usualformulations of the energy budget for common envelope evolution. The mostplausible missing energy term is the energy released by recombination in thecommon envelope, and, indeed, a simple reformulation the energy budgetexplicitly including recombination resolves this issue.
label: human

text: Common envelope evolution (CEE) is a critical yet poorly understood phase in the formation of close compact binaries. In this work, we revisit the physical assumptions underlying CEE, emphasizing the roles of energy and angular momentum conservation, envelope structure, and recombination energy. Using a combination of three-dimensional hydrodynamical simulations and updated stellar structure models, we systematically explore the dependence of envelope ejection efficiency on mass ratio, evolutionary stage, and companion type. Our results indicate that commonly adopted parametrizations, such as the α-prescription, fail to capture the full diversity of outcomes and can significantly misestimate post-CE orbital separations. We show that including additional energy sources and a time-dependent treatment of mass loss leads to more accurate predictions that better match the observed population of post-common-envelope binaries. Finally, we discuss the implications of our findings for binary population synthesis, the formation rates of Type Ia supernovae and gravitational-wave sources, and the future development of more physically motivated CEE formalisms.
label: llm

text: The observed association of Long Gamma-Ray Bursts (LGRBs) with peculiar TypeIc supernovae gives support to Woosley`s collapsar/hypernova model, in whichthe GRB is produced by the collapse of the rapidly rotating core of a massivestar to a black hole. The association of LGRBs with small star-forming galaxiessuggests low-metallicity to be a condition for a massive star to evolve to thecollapsar stage. Both completely-mixed single star models and binary starmodels are possible. In binary models the progenitor of the GRB is a massivehelium star with a close companion. We find that tidal synchronization duringcore-helium burning is reached on a short timescale (less than a fewmillennia). However, the strong core-envelope coupling in the subsequentevolutionary stages is likely to rule out helium stars with main-sequencecompanions as progenitors of hypernovae/GRBs. On the other hand, helium starsin close binaries with a neutron-star or black-hole companion can, despite thestrong core-envelope coupling in the post-helium burning phase, retainsufficient core angular momentum to produce a hypernova/GRB.
label: human

text: Long gamma-ray bursts (LGRBs) are widely believed to originate from the collapse of massive, rapidly rotating stars, yet the precise progenitor pathways remain uncertain. In this work, we investigate the boundary conditions required for LGRB production, focusing on metallicity, angular momentum retention, and envelope stripping. We employ a suite of stellar evolution and binary population synthesis models to examine how binary interactions—such as mass transfer, common-envelope evolution, and tidal spin-up—shape the pre-collapse structure of potential LGRB progenitors. Our models indicate that close binary systems can significantly relax the metallicity constraints traditionally imposed by single-star collapsar scenarios, by maintaining high core angular momentum while efficiently removing hydrogen-rich envelopes. We further identify critical ranges of initial orbital period, mass ratio, and mass-loss prescriptions that delineate successful LGRB progenitors from systems that instead produce ordinary core-collapse supernovae or compact-object mergers. Comparison with observed host-galaxy properties and LGRB rate estimates suggests that binary channels can account for a substantial fraction of the LGRB population.
label: llm

text: We consider the correction $\Delta\sigma_\mathrm{ee}$ due toelectron-electron interaction to the conductivity of a weakly disordered metal(Al'tshuler-Aronov correction). The correction is related to the spectraldeterminant of the Laplace operator. The case of a large square metallicnetwork is considered. The variation of $\Delta\sigma_\mathrm{ee}(L_T)$ as afunction of the thermal length $L_T$ is found very similar to the variation ofthe weak localization $\Delta\sigma_\mathrm{WL}(L_\phi)$ as a function of thephase coherence length. Our result for $\Delta\sigma_\mathrm{ee}$ interpolatesbetween the known 1d and 2d results, but the interaction parameter entering theexpression of $\Delta\sigma_\mathrm{ee}$ keeps a 1d behaviour. Quitesurprisingly, the result is very close to the 2d logarithmic behaviour alreadyfor $L_T\sim{a}/2$, where $a$ is the lattice parameter.
label: human

text: We study the Al'tshuler-Aronov interaction correction to the conductivity of a large metallic square network in the diffusive regime. Using a diagrammatic perturbation theory framework adapted to quasi-two-dimensional networks, we derive explicit expressions for the quantum correction as a function of temperature, frequency, and geometric parameters of the lattice. Particular attention is given to the role of the network topology, which modifies the diffusion modes and leads to distinct interaction-induced conductivity scalings compared to bulk two-dimensional systems. We demonstrate that the discrete nature of the lattice introduces a crossover between effectively one-dimensional and two-dimensional interaction corrections depending on the phase coherence length relative to the lattice spacing. The results provide a quantitative description of how electron-electron interactions manifest in transport properties measured in mesoscopic metallic networks.
label: llm

text: A Relativistic Transport Model (ART1.0) is applied to simulate the stoppingeffects in tip-tip and body-body U+U collisions, at a beam kinetic energy of520 MeV/nucleon. Our simulation results have demonstrated that both centralcollisions of the two extreme orientations can achieve full stopping, and alsoform a bulk of hot, dense nuclear matter with a sufficiently large volume andlong duration, due to the largely deformed uranium nuclei. The nucleon sidewardflow in the tip-tip collisions is nearly 3 times larger than that in body-bodyones at normalized impact parameter $b/b_{max}<0.5$, and that the body-bodycentral collisions have a largest negative nucleon elliptic flow $v_{2}=-12%$in contrast to zero in tip-tip ones. Thus the extreme circumstance and thenovel experimental observables in tip-tip and body-body collisions can providea good condition and sensitive probe to study the nuclear EoS, respectively.The Cooling Storage Ring (CSR) External Target Facility (ETF) to be built atLanzhou, China, delivering the uranium beam up to 520 MeV/nucleon is expectedto make significant contribution to explore the nuclear equation of state(EoS).
label: human

text: Stopping effects in uranium-uranium (U+U) collisions at a beam energy of 520 MeV/nucleon are investigated using a combination of experimental data and transport-model simulations. We analyze global and differential observables, such as rapidity distributions and transverse energy spectra of emitted nucleons and light fragments, to quantify the degree of stopping and equilibration in the reaction zone. The results indicate a high but incomplete stopping, with significant anisotropies that reflect the influence of the deformed nuclear geometry and different collision orientations. Comparisons with model calculations constrain in-medium nucleon–nucleon cross sections and the nuclear equation of state at intermediate densities, providing new insights into dissipative dynamics in heavy-ion collisions at intermediate energies.
label: llm

text: Redundancy of experimental data is the basic statistic from which thecomplexity of a natural phenomenon and the proper number of experiments neededfor its exploration can be estimated. The redundancy is expressed by theentropy of information pertaining to the probability density function ofexperimental variables. Since the calculation of entropy is inconvenient due tointegration over a range of variables, an approximate expression for redundancyis derived that includes only a sum over the set of experimental data aboutthese variables. The approximation makes feasible an efficient estimation ofthe redundancy of data along with the related experimental information andinformation cost function. From the experimental information the complexity ofthe phenomenon can be simply estimated, while the proper number of experimentsneeded for its exploration can be determined from the minimum of the costfunction. The performance of the approximate estimation of these statistics isdemonstrated on two-dimensional normally distributed random data.
label: human

text: Estimation of experimental data redundancy and related statistics is essential for optimizing experimental design and ensuring robust statistical inference. In this study, we develop a general framework to quantify data redundancy in experimental measurements by combining information-theoretic and classical statistical approaches. We rigorously define redundancy metrics based on covariance structures, mutual information, and effective sample size, and derive their asymptotic properties under common experimental models. The proposed methodology is evaluated through simulations that vary signal-to-noise ratios, sampling schemes, and correlation structures, as well as through applications to real experimental datasets from the physical and life sciences. Our results demonstrate that explicitly accounting for redundancy can substantially improve parameter estimation accuracy, confidence interval coverage, and model selection performance. The framework provides practical guidelines for experimental planning, data reduction, and the interpretation of statistical significance in settings where measurements are partially dependent or oversampled.
label: llm

text: A solution is given to the following problem: how to compute themultiplicity, or more generally the Hilbert function, at a point on a Schubertvariety in an orthogonal Grassmannian. Standard monomial theory is applied totranslate the problem from geometry to combinatorics. The solution of theresulting combinatorial problem forms the bulk of the paper. This approach hasbeen followed earlier to solve the same problem for the Grassmannian and thesymplectic Grassmannian.  As an application, we present an interpretation of the multiplicity as thenumber of non-intersecting lattice paths of a certain kind.  Taking the Schubert variety to be of a special kind and the point to be the"identity coset," our problem specializes to a problem about Pfaffian idealstreatments of which by different methods exist in the literature. Alsoavailable in the literature is a geometric solution when the point is a"generic singularity."
label: human

text: We study the Hilbert functions of finite sets of points lying on Schubert varieties in orthogonal Grassmannians. Using the geometry of the orthogonal Grassmannian and the combinatorics of isotropic flags, we provide explicit descriptions of these Hilbert functions in terms of data attached to the corresponding Schubert symbols. Our approach relies on a detailed analysis of the initial ideals of the defining ideals of such point configurations with respect to suitably chosen term orders adapted to the Schubert stratification. We show that, under natural genericity assumptions, the Hilbert function of a set of points is determined by the relative position of the points with respect to the Schubert cells and the incidence relations among them. In particular, we obtain closed formulas for Hilbert functions of points in general position on a fixed Schubert variety, as well as criteria for when two configurations have the same Hilbert function.
label: llm

text: The boundary conditions of the heliosphere are set by the ionization, densityand composition of inflowing interstellar matter. Constraining the propertiesof the Local Interstellar Cloud (LIC) at the heliosphere requires radiativetransfer ionization models. We model the background interstellar radiationfield using observed stellar FUV and EUV emission and the diffuse soft X-raybackground. We also model the emission from the boundary between the LIC andthe hot Local Bubble (LB) plasma, assuming that the cloud is evaporatingbecause of thermal conduction. We create a grid of models covering a plausiblerange of LIC and LB properties, and use the modeled radiation field as input toradiative transfer/thermal equilibrium calculations using the Cloudy code. Datafrom in situ observations of He^O, pickup ions and anomalous cosmic rays in theheliosphere, and absorption line measurements towards epsilon CMa were used toconstrain the input parameters. A restricted range of assumed LIC HI columndensities and LB plasma temperatures produce models that match all theobservational constraints. The relative weakness of the constraints on N(HI)and T_h contrast with the narrow limits predicted for the H^O and electrondensity in the LIC at the Sun, n(H^0) = 0.19 - 0.20 cm^-3, and n(e) = 0.07 +/-0.01 cm^-3. Derived abundances are mostly typical for low density gas, withsub-solar Mg, Si and Fe, possibly subsolar O and N, and S about solar; howeverC is supersolar. The interstellar gas at the Sun is warm, low density, andpartially ionized, with n(H) = 0.23 - 0.27 cm^-3, T = 6300 K, X(H^+) ~ 0.2, andX(He^+) ~ 0.4. These results appear to be robust since acceptable models arefound for substantially different input radiation fields. Our results favor lowvalues for the reference solar abundances for the LIC composition.
label: human

text: The interaction between the solar wind and the surrounding interstellar medium (ISM) is governed by the physical and ionization state of the local interstellar cloud. This study presents a suite of photoionization models that characterize the boundary conditions of the heliosphere by simultaneously fitting interstellar absorption line data and in situ measurements of interstellar neutrals and pickup ions. We employ a self-consistent radiative transfer code to explore a range of plausible density, temperature, and ionization structures for the local ISM, constrained by extreme ultraviolet and far-ultraviolet background radiation fields. The models incorporate updated atomic data, realistic grain depletion patterns, and charge-exchange processes between ions and neutrals. We compare model predictions with H I, D I, He I, and metal-line column densities observed toward nearby stars and with in situ measurements of interstellar H, He, O, N, and Ne entering the heliosphere. The resulting best-fit models yield tight constraints on the neutral fraction, electron density, and ionization gradients at the heliospheric boundary. We find that modest variations in the local radiation field and cloud density produce significant changes in the penetration of neutrals into the inner heliosphere. Our results favor a partially ionized, warm cloud characterized by hydrogen neutral fractions of order 0.5–0.7 and electron densities of order 0.05–0.10 cm⁻³ at the solar location. The modeled helium parameters are consistent with recent direct measurements of interstellar helium flow speed, temperature, and direction. We also examine the sensitivity of the heliospheric interface structure to uncertainties in the interstellar magnetic field strength and orientation. The combined interstellar and in situ constraints substantially reduce the allowable parameter space for models of the local ISM.
label: llm

text: We study the relaxational critical dynamics of the three-dimensional randomanisotropy magnets with the non-conserved n-component order parameter coupledto a conserved scalar density. In the random anisotropy magnets the structuraldisorder is present in a form of local quenched anisotropy axes of randomorientation. When the anisotropy axes are randomly distributed along the edgesof the n-dimensional hypercube, asymptotical dynamical critical propertiescoincide with those of the random-site Ising model. However structural disordergives rise to considerable effects for non-asymptotic critical dynamics. Weinvestigate this phenomenon by a field-theoretical renormalization groupanalysis in the two-loop order. We study critical slowing down and obtainquantitative estimates for the effective and asymptotic critical exponents ofthe order parameter and scalar density. The results predict complex scenariosfor the effective critical exponent approaching an asymptotic regime.
label: human

text: We investigate the critical dynamics of random anisotropy magnets within the framework of model C, where a nonconserved order parameter is dynamically coupled to a conserved scalar density. Using renormalization group methods to two-loop order in \(d=4-\epsilon\) dimensions, we derive the flow equations for the dynamic couplings and analyze their fixed-point structure for different distributions of local anisotropy axes. Particular emphasis is placed on the comparison between isotropic and cubic anisotropy distributions, for which we identify distinct dynamic universality classes and crossover behaviors. We compute the dynamic critical exponents \(z\) and the associated scaling functions, elucidating the conditions under which the coupling to the conserved density remains relevant at criticality. Our results demonstrate that quenched random anisotropy can substantially modify the asymptotic dynamic scaling while also generating extended preasymptotic regimes observable in realistic systems.
label: llm

text: The physical interpretation of spectropolarimetric observations of lines ofneutral helium, such as those of the 10830 A multiplet, represents an excellentopportunity for investigating the magnetism of plasma structures in the solarchromosphere. Here we present a powerful forward modeling and inversion codethat permits either to calculate the emergent intensity and polarization forany given magnetic field vector or to infer the dynamical and magneticproperties from the observed Stokes profiles. This diagnostic tool is based onthe quantum theory of spectral line polarization, which self-consistentlyaccounts for the Hanle and Zeeman effects in the most general case of theincomplete Paschen-Back effect regime. We also take into account radiativetransfer effects. An efficient numerical scheme based on global optimizationmethods has been applied. Our Stokes inversion code permits a fast and reliabledetermination of the global minimum.
label: human

text: A User-Friendly Code to Diagnose Chromospheric Plasmas We present a new computational tool designed to provide robust diagnostics of chromospheric plasmas from spectroscopic observations. The code incorporates non-local thermodynamic equilibrium (non-LTE) radiative transfer, partial frequency redistribution, and realistic atomic models to infer key plasma parameters such as temperature, density, and velocity fields. Particular emphasis is placed on user accessibility: the interface, configuration options, and workflows are tailored for observers and modelers with limited experience in advanced radiative transfer techniques. We validate the performance of the code using both synthetic data from state-of-the-art magnetohydrodynamic simulations and high-resolution observations of prominent chromospheric lines (e.g., Hα, Ca II, and Mg II). Comparisons with established diagnostic methods show that our tool achieves comparable or superior accuracy while significantly reducing setup and analysis time.
label: llm

text: Onsager conjectured that weak solutions of the Euler equations forincompressible fluids in 3D conserve energy only if they have a certain minimalsmoothness, (of order of 1/3 fractional derivatives) and that they dissipateenergy if they are rougher. In this paper we prove that energy is conserved forvelocities in the function space $B^{1/3}_{3,c(\NN)}$. We show that this spaceis sharp in a natural sense. We phrase the energy spectrum in terms of theLittlewood-Paley decomposition and show that the energy flux is controlled bylocal interactions. This locality is shown to hold also for the helicity flux;moreover, every weak solution of the Euler equations that belongs to$B^{2/3}_{3,c(\NN)}$ conserves helicity. In contrast, in two dimensions, thestrong locality of the enstrophy holds only in the ultraviolet range.
label: human

text: We investigate the relationship between energy conservation and Onsager's conjecture for weak solutions of the incompressible Euler equations. Onsager conjectured that solutions with Hölder regularity exponent greater than 1/3 conserve energy, while those with exponent less than 1/3 may exhibit anomalous dissipation. In this work, we provide a rigorous analysis of the regularity conditions under which energy is conserved, and we characterize the borderline cases in terms of Besov and Hölder-type spaces. We establish sufficient criteria for energy conservation in the framework of weak solutions and relate these to the scaling and structure of the nonlinear term. Furthermore, we discuss the construction and properties of non-conservative solutions that saturate the Onsager critical exponent, highlighting the role of intermittent structures and convex integration methods.
label: llm

text: Abridged... Blue stragglers (BSS) are thought to be the product of eitherprimordial or collisional binary systems. In the context of dwarf spheroidalgalaxies it is hard to firmly disentangle a genuine BSS population from youngmain sequence (MS) stars tracing a ~1-2 Gyr old star forming episode. Assumingthat their blue plume populations are made of BSS, we estimate the BSSfrequency for 8 Local Group non star-forming dwarf galaxies, using acompilation of ground and space based photometry.  Our results can be summarized as follows: (i) The BSS frequency in dwarfgalaxies, at any given Mv, is always higher than that in globular clusters ofsimilar luminosities; (ii) the BSS frequency for the lowest luminosity dwarfgalaxies is in excellent agreement with that observed in the Milky Way halo;and most interestingly (iii) derive a statistically significantanti-correlation between the BSS frequency and the galaxy Mv.  The low density, almost collision-less, environments of our dwarf galaxysample allow us to infer (i) their very low dynamical evolution; (ii) anegligible production of collisional BSS; and consequently (iii) that theirblue plumes are mainly made of primordial binaries. The dwarf galaxiesanti-correlation can be used as a discriminator: galaxies obeying theanti-correlation are more likely to possess genuine primordial BSS rather thanyoung main sequence stars.
label: human

text: We investigate the nature of the blue plume population in dwarf spheroidal galaxies, assessing whether these stars are genuine blue stragglers or represent a young stellar component. Using deep, homogeneous photometry for a sample of nearby dwarf spheroidals, we construct color–magnitude diagrams and perform detailed comparisons with theoretical isochrones and synthetic populations. We analyze the spatial distributions, luminosity functions, and frequency of blue plume stars relative to horizontal branch and main-sequence turnoff populations. Our results show that, in most systems, the blue plume stars exhibit radial distributions and number fractions consistent with a predominantly blue straggler origin, likely produced by binary evolution and stellar collisions in low-density environments. However, in a subset of galaxies with independent evidence for extended star formation histories, a non-negligible fraction of blue plume stars is best explained by genuinely young populations. We conclude that the blue plume in dwarf spheroidal galaxies is typically dominated by blue stragglers, but can include a minor young stellar component in systems that retained gas and formed stars until relatively recent epochs.
label: llm

text: We report new detailed surface U, B, V, R, and I photometry of 81 stellarstructures in the disk of the barred galaxy NGC 3367. The images show manydifferent structures indicating that star formation is going on in the mostpart of the disk. NGC 3367 is known to have a very high concentration ofmolecular gas distribution in the central regions of the galaxy and bipolarsynchrotron emission from the nucleus with two lobes (at 6 kpc) forming atriple structure similar to a radio galaxy. We have determined the U, B, V, R,and I magnitudes and U - B, B - V, U - V, and V - I colors for the centralregion (nucleus), a region which includes supernovae 2003 AA, and 79 starassociations throughout NGC 3367. Estimation of ages of star associations isvery difficult due to several factors, among them: filling factor, metallicity,spatial distribution of each structure and the fact that we estimated themagnitudes with a circular aperture of 16 pixels in diameter, equivalent to$6''.8\sim1.4$ kpc. However, if the colors derived for NGC 3367 were similar tothe colors expected of star clusters with theoretical evolutionary star tracksdeveloped for the LMC and had a similar metallicity, NGC 3367 show 51 percentof the observed structures with age type SWB I (few tens of Myrs), with sevensources outside the bright surface brightness visible disk of NGC 3367.
label: human

text: We present UBVRI CCD photometry of stellar structures across the disk of the barred spiral galaxy NGC 3367, with the aim of characterizing its recent star formation history and spatially resolved stellar populations. Using deep, multiband imaging obtained under good seeing conditions, we identify star-forming complexes, bar-related features, and inter-arm regions, and perform aperture photometry to derive their integrated magnitudes and colors. The observed color indices are compared with population synthesis models and reddening vectors to estimate ages, internal extinction, and approximate stellar masses for the identified structures. We find that the youngest stellar complexes are preferentially located along the bar and in the outer spiral arms, while older populations dominate the inner disk and inter-arm regions. The color gradients and age distributions suggest that bar-driven gas inflow and secular processes play a significant role in shaping the current star formation pattern in NGC 3367. These results provide constraints on the evolutionary state of the galaxy and offer a benchmark for understanding the influence of bars on disk galaxy evolution.
label: llm

text: I shall present three arguments for the proposition that intelligent life isvery rare in the universe. First, I shall summarize the consensus opinion ofthe founders of the Modern Synthesis (Simpson, Dobzhanski, and Mayr) that theevolution of intelligent life is exceedingly improbable. Second, I shalldevelop the Fermi Paradox: if they existed they'd be here. Third, I shall showthat if intelligent life were too common, it would use up all availableresources and die out. But I shall show that the quantum mechanical principleof unitarity (actually a form of teleology!) requires intelligent life tosurvive to the end of time. Finally, I shall argue that, if the universe isindeed accelerating, then survival to the end of time requires that intelligentlife, though rare, to have evolved several times in the visible universe. Ishall argue that the acceleration is a consequence of the excess of matter overantimatter in the universe. I shall suggest experiments to test these claims.
label: human

text: Intelligent life occupies a central yet unresolved position in contemporary cosmology, linking questions of fundamental physics, cosmic evolution, and the nature of observation. In this article, we examine how the possible existence, distribution, and longevity of intelligent observers constrain cosmological models and parameter choices. We review the role of anthropic reasoning in explaining otherwise puzzling fine-tunings, such as the small but nonzero value of the cosmological constant, and assess its epistemic status. By integrating insights from astrobiology, we explore how star formation history, metallicity evolution, and planetary habitability windows affect the likelihood and timing of intelligent life. We analyze the implications of various multiverse scenarios for the emergence of intelligence and discuss criteria for testability in such frameworks. Special attention is given to the Fermi paradox as a cosmological problem, relating the apparent silence of the cosmos to models of technological civilization expansion and self-destruction.
label: llm

text: Although powers of the Young-Jucys-Murphya elements X_i = (1 i) + ... +(i-1i), i = 1, ..., n, in the symmetric group S_n acting on {1, ...,n} do not liein the centre of the group algebra of S_n, we show that transitive powers,namely the sum of the contributions from elements that act transitively on {1,>...,n}, are central. We determine the coefficients, which we call starfactorization numbers, that occur in the resolution of transitive powers withrespect to the class basis of the centre of S_n, and show that they have apolynomiality property. These centrality and polynomiality properties haveseemingly unrelated consequences. First, they answer a question raised by Pakabout reduced decompositions; second, they explain and extend the beautifulsymmetry result discovered by Irving and Rattan; and thirdly, we relate thepolynomiality to an existing polynomiality result for a class of double Hurwitznumbers associated with branched covers of the sphere, which therefore suggeststhat there may be an ELSV-type formula associated with the star factorizationnumbers.
label: human

text: We study the centrality properties of a distinguished collection of transitive power sums of the Young–Jucys–Murphy (YJM) elements in the group algebra of the symmetric group. Building on the combinatorial and representation-theoretic structure of the YJM elements, we characterize precisely which transitive powers give rise to central elements and provide an explicit description of the resulting central subalgebra. Our approach combines symmetric function techniques, Gelfand–Tsetlin bases, and an analysis of the action of these elements on Specht modules. As an application, we obtain new identities for character values and refine the understanding of the role of YJM elements in the Okounkov–Vershik approach to the representation theory of symmetric groups.
label: llm

text: Schroedinger equation on a Hilbert space ${\cal H}$, represents a linearHamiltonian dynamical system on the space of quantum pure states, theprojective Hilbert space $P {\cal H}$. Separable states of a bipartite quantumsystem form a special submanifold of $P {\cal H}$.  We analyze the Hamiltonian dynamics that corresponds to the quantum systemconstrained on the manifold of separable states, using as an important examplethe system of two interacting qubits. The constraints introduce nonlinearitieswhich render the dynamics nontrivial. We show that the qualitative propertiesof the constrained dynamics clearly manifest the symmetry of the qubits system.In particular, if the quantum Hamilton's operator has not enough symmetry, theconstrained dynamics is nonintegrable, and displays the typical features of aHamiltonian dynamical system with mixed phase space. Possible physicalrealizations of the separability constraints are discussed.
label: human

text: We investigate the formulation of Hamiltonian quantum dynamics under explicit separability constraints on the space of admissible states. By restricting the system’s evolution to remain within a specified manifold of separable or partially separable states, we derive modified equations of motion that encode the constraint structure directly into the Hamiltonian flow. Using geometric methods on projective Hilbert space, we characterize the resulting constrained dynamics in terms of symplectic reductions and Lagrange multipliers enforcing separability. We show that these constraints generally induce effective nonlinearities in the state evolution, even when the underlying Hamiltonian is strictly linear and local. Several illustrative examples demonstrate how separability-constrained dynamics alters entanglement generation, energy exchange, and correlation propagation in bipartite and multipartite systems. Our results clarify the interplay between entanglement.
label: llm

text: We present high-resolution, multiwavelength continuum and molecular-lineimages of the massive star forming region IRAS 18317-0757. The IR through mmspectral energy distribution can be approximated by a two-temperature model (25and 63 K) with a total luminosity of approximately log(L/Lsun)=5.2. Previoussubmm imaging resolved this region into a cluster of 5 dust cores, one of whichis associated with the UCHII region G23.96+0.15, and another with an H2O maser.In our new 2.7 mm continuum image, only the UCHII region is detected, withtotal flux and morphology in good agreement with the free-free emission in VLAcm-wave maps. For the other four objects, the nondetections at 2.7 mm and inthe MSX mid-IR bands are consistent with cool dust emission with a temperatureof 13-40K and luminosity of 1000-40000 Lsun. By combining single-dish andinterferometric data, we have identified over two dozen virialized C18O coresin this region that contain ~40% of the total molecular gas mass present. Whilethe overall extent of the C18O and dust emission is similar, the emission peaksdo not correlate well in detail. At least 11 of the 123 stars identified by2MASS in this region are likely to be within the star-forming cluster. Twostars (both associated with the UCHII region) were previously identified as Ostars via IR spectroscopy. Most of the rest of the reddened stars have noobvious correlation with the C18O cores or the dust cores. In summary, ourobservations indicate that considerable fragmentation of the molecular cloudhas taken place during the time required for the UCHII region to form and the Ostars to become detectable at IR wavelengths. Additional star formation appearsto be ongoing on the periphery of the central region, where up to four B-type(proto)stars have formed among a substantial number of C18O molecular cores.
label: human

text: IRAS 18317-0757: A Cluster of Embedded Massive Stars and Protostars We present a multiwavelength study of the luminous infrared source IRAS 18317-0757, revealing a compact cluster of embedded massive stars and protostars. Using millimeter continuum and molecular line observations, we resolve the dense core into multiple compact condensations with masses consistent with high-mass star formation. Near- and mid-infrared imaging identify several deeply embedded point sources, many of which lack optical counterparts, confirming their highly obscured nature. Radio continuum data show a compact H II region coincident with the brightest infrared source, indicating at least one early-type massive star already on or near the main sequence. The surrounding molecular gas exhibits broad line widths and multiple velocity components, suggesting active accretion, outflows, and turbulent motions within the cluster-forming core. Spectral energy distribution fitting of individual sources yields high luminosities and envelopes consistent with evolutionary stages ranging from massive Class 0/I protostars to more evolved young stellar objects. We detect extended dust emission tracing a filamentary structure that appears to funnel material into the central cluster region. The spatial correlation between dense gas peaks, embedded infrared sources, and radio emission implies that massive star formation in IRAS 18317-0757 is both clustered and sequential. Comparison with theoretical models of massive star and cluster formation supports a scenario in which competitive accretion and core fragmentation both play significant roles. Our analysis suggests that feedback from the emerging massive stars is beginning to disrupt and ionize the natal cloud while still allowing ongoing protostellar accretion in neighboring cores. These results establish IRAS 18317-0757 as a key laboratory for investigating the earliest clustered phases of massive star formation.
label: llm

text: We consider the interpretation of tetrad fields as reference frames inspacetime. Reference frames may be characterized by an antisymmetricacceleration tensor, whose components are identified as the inertialaccelerations of the frame (the translational acceleration and the frequency ofrotation of the frame). This tensor is closely related togravitoelectromagnetic field quantities. We construct the set of tetrad fieldsadapted to observers that are in free fall in the Schwarzschild spacetime, andshow that the gravitational energy-momentum constructed out of this set oftetrad fields, in the framework of the teleparallel equivalent of generalrelatrivity, vanishes. This result is in agreement with the principle ofequivalence, and may be taken as a condition for a viable definition ofgravitational energy.
label: human

text: In this work we analyze the role of reference frames in spacetime with particular emphasis on the description of gravitational energy in freely falling frames. We examine how different choices of tetrads and coordinate systems affect the localization and interpretation of gravitational energy-momentum in general relativity. Special attention is given to the behavior of quasi-local and pseudotensorial energy-momentum constructs in the vicinity of freely falling observers, where gravitational effects can be locally transformed away. We show that, despite the local vanishing of the Levi-Civita connection in such frames, certain frame-dependent formulations retain a nontrivial notion of gravitational energy. Our results clarify the conceptual status of gravitational energy in general relativity and delineate the conditions under which freely falling frames can be used to meaningfully discuss its localization.
label: llm

text: We study the S=1/2 Heisenberg antiferromagnet on a square lattice withnearest-neighbor and plaquette four-spin exchanges (introduced by A.W. Sandvik,Phys. Rev. Lett. {\bf 98}, 227202 (2007).)  This model undergoes a quantum phase transition from a spontaneouslydimerized phase to N\'eel order at a critical coupling. We show that as thecritical point is approached from the dimerized side, the system exhibitsstrong fluctuations in the dimer background, reflected in the presence of alow-energy singlet mode, with a simultaneous rise in the triplet quasiparticledensity. We find that both singlet and triplet modes of high density condenseat the transition, signaling restoration of lattice symmetry. In our approach,which goes beyond mean-field theory in terms of the triplet excitations, thetransition appears sharp; however since our method breaks down near thecritical point, we argue that we cannot make a definite conclusion regardingthe order of the transition.
label: human

text: We investigate the quantum phase transition in a two-dimensional antiferromagnet with dominant four-spin exchange interactions on the square lattice. Using a combination of large-scale quantum Monte Carlo simulations and analytical spin-wave theory, we map out the zero-temperature phase diagram as a function of the ratio between two-spin and four-spin exchange couplings. For weak four-spin exchange, the system exhibits conventional Néel long-range order with gapless spin-wave excitations. As the strength of the four-spin exchange increases, quantum fluctuations are enhanced and ultimately destabilize the Néel phase. Beyond a critical coupling, the ground state transitions into a nonmagnetic valence-bond solid characterized by spontaneously broken lattice symmetry and a finite spin gap. Finite-size scaling of the order parameters and excitation gaps reveals critical exponents consistent with a continuous quantum phase transition. The numerical data support an emergent deconfined critical point scenario, in which fractionalized spinon excitations and an emergent gauge field mediate the transition.
label: llm

text: We point out that resonance saturation in QCD can be understood in thelarge-Nc limit from the mathematical theory of Pade Approximants to meromorphicfunctions. These approximants are rational functions which encompass anysaturation with a finite number of resonances as a particular example,explaining several results which have appeared in the literature. We review themain properties of Pade Approximants with the help of a toy model for the<VV-AA> two-point correlator, paying particular attention to the relationshipamong the Chiral Expansion, the Operator Product Expansion and the resonancespectrum. In passing, we also comment on an old proposal made by Migdal in 1977which has recently attracted much attention in the context of AdS/QCD models.Finally, we apply the simplest Pade Approximant to the <VV-AA> correlator inthe real case of QCD. The general conclusion is that a rational approximant mayreliably describe a Green's function in the Euclidean, but the same is not truein the Minkowski regime due to the appearance of unphysical poles and/orresidues.
label: human

text: In this work we develop a systematic and rational framework for implementing resonance saturation in large-Nc QCD. Building on the structure of the 1/Nc expansion, we construct an effective hadronic Lagrangian in which the dominant low-energy constants are generated by integrating out a controlled set of mesonic resonances. Our approach clarifies the conditions under which resonance saturation is justified, identifies the leading corrections to the saturation hypothesis, and connects them explicitly to subleading 1/Nc effects. By matching to QCD short-distance constraints and chiral perturbation theory at low energies, we derive quantitative predictions for low-energy constants and assess their theoretical uncertainties. This framework provides a consistent bridge between fundamental QCD dynamics and phenomenological resonance models, improving the reliability of large-Nc inspired descriptions of hadronic processes.
label: llm

text: The effect of possible in-medium modifications of nucleon-nucleon ($NN$)cross sections on particle production is investigated in heavy ion collisions($HIC$) at intermediate energies. In particular, using a fully covariantrelativistic transport approach, we see that the density dependence of the {\itinelastic} cross sections appreciably affects the pion and kaon yields andtheir rapidity distributions. However, the $(\pi^{-}/\pi^{+})$- and$(K^{0}/K^{+})$-ratios depend only moderately on the in-medium behavior of theinelastic cross sections. This is particularly true for kaon yield ratios,since kaons are more uniformly produced in high density regions. Kaonpotentials are also suitably evaluated in two schemes, a chiral perturbativeapproach and an effective meson-quark coupling method, with consistent resultsshowing a similar repulsive contribution for $K^{+}$ and $K^{0}$. As aconsequence we expect rather reduced effects on the yield ratios. We concludethat particle ratios appear to be robust observables for probing the nuclearequation of state ($EoS$) at high baryon density and, particularly, itsisovector sector.
label: human

text: In this work, we investigate in-medium effects on particle production in heavy ion collisions over a broad range of beam energies. Using a combination of transport model simulations and effective field theory approaches, we quantify how modifications of hadron properties in dense and hot nuclear matter influence observable particle yields and spectra. Particular emphasis is placed on the role of in-medium self-energies, modified interaction cross sections, and spectral function broadening for mesons and baryon resonances. We compare our theoretical predictions with experimental data from SPS, RHIC, and LHC experiments to constrain the density and temperature dependence of the in-medium modifications. The sensitivity of strangeness production, dilepton emission, and collective flow observables to these effects is analyzed in detail. Our results demonstrate that properly accounting for in-medium dynamics is essential for a consistent description of particle production and for extracting the equation of state of strongly interacting matter. We conclude by discussing the implications of our findings for the search for the QCD phase transition and the critical point in the phase diagram of nuclear matter.
label: llm

text: We study spin S=1 and S=3/2 Heisenberg antiferromagnets on a cubic latticefocusing on spin solid states. Using Schwinger boson formulation for spins, westart in a U(1) spin liquid phase proximate to Neel phase and explore possibleconfining paramagnetic phases as we transition away from the spin liquid by theprocess of monopole condensation. Electromagnetic duality is used to rewritethe theory in terms of monopoles. For spin 1 we find several candidate phasesof which the most natural one is a phase with spins organized into parallelHaldane chains. For spin 3/2 we find that the most natural phase has spinsorganized into parallel ladders. As a by-product, we also write a Landau theoryof the ordering in two special classical frustrated XY models on the cubiclattice, one of which is the fully frustrated XY model. In a particular limitour approach maps to a dimer model with 2S dimers coming out of every site, andwe find the same spin solid phases in this regime as well.
label: human

text: We investigate possible spin solid phases in spin-1 and spin-3/2 antiferromagnets on the three-dimensional cubic lattice, focusing on non-magnetic ground states that preserve spin-rotation symmetry but break lattice symmetries. Using a combination of analytical techniques based on effective field theories and perturbative expansions, we derive low-energy descriptions of candidate spin solid phases and characterize their order parameters and excitation spectra. For spin-1 systems, we identify valence bond solid (VBS) phases with distinct patterns of singlet formation, including columnar and plaquette arrangements, and determine the corresponding symmetry-breaking patterns. In the spin-3/2 case, we find a richer set of spin solid states, including generalized VBS structures and states with multipolar ordering that emerge naturally from the larger local Hilbert space. We map out the phase structure as a function of coupling constants in representative microscopic Hamiltonians, highlighting the role of frustration and anisotropies in stabilizing different spin solids.
label: llm

text: Aims: We analyze the available information on the star BD+43 3654 toinvestigate the possibility that it may have had its origin in the massive OBassociation Cygnus OB2.  Methods: We present new spectroscopic observations allowing a reliablespectral classification of the star, and discuss existing MSX observations ofits associated bow shock and astrometric information not previously studied.  Results: Our observations reveal that BD+43 3654 is a very early and luminousstar of spectral type O4If, with an estimated mass of (70 +/- 15) solar massesand an age of about 1.6 Myr. The high spatial resolution of the MSXobservations allows us to determine its direction of motion in the plane of thesky by means of the symmetry axis of the well-defined bow shock, which matcheswell the orientation expected from the proper motion. Tracing back its pathacross the sky we find that BD+43 3654 was located near the central, densestregion of Cygnus OB2 at a time in the past similar to its estimated age.  Conclusions: BD+43 3654 turns out to be one of the three most massive runawaystars known, and it most likely formed in the central region of Cygnus OB2. Arunaway formation mechanism by means of dynamical ejection is consistent withour results.
label: human

text: A very massive runaway star from the Cygnus OB2 association is identified and characterized through a combination of astrometric, spectroscopic, and photometric data. We measure its proper motion using Gaia data and confirm a supersonic peculiar velocity relative to the local standard of rest, clearly inconsistent with bound membership in Cygnus OB2. High-resolution spectroscopy reveals an O-type stellar spectrum with strong wind features, indicating an initial mass exceeding 40–60 M⊙ and a relatively early evolutionary state. By tracing back its trajectory in the Galactic potential, we show that its kinematics are consistent with an origin in the core of Cygnus OB2 within the past ~1–2 Myr. We discuss possible ejection mechanisms, including dynamical interactions in a dense cluster environment and the binary-supernova scenario, and argue that close multi-body encounters provide the most plausible explanation. The existence of such an extreme runaway places new constraints on the initial density, mass segregation, and binary fraction of the Cygnus OB2 association. More broadly, this object illustrates the role of runaway massive stars in distributing mechanical and radiative feedback far from their birth sites, with implications for the structure and enrichment of the surrounding interstellar medium.
label: llm

text: We propose a Hamiltonian formalism for a generalizedFriedmann-Roberson-Walker cosmology model in the presence of both a variableequation of state (EOS) parameter $w(a)$ and a variable cosmological constant$\Lambda(a)$, where $a$ is the scale factor. This Hamiltonian system containing1 degree of freedom and without constraint, gives Friedmann equations as theequation of motion, which describes a mechanical system with a variable massobject moving in a potential field. After an appropriate transformation of thescale factor, this system can be further simplified to an object with constantmass moving in an effective potential field. In this framework, the $\Lambda$cold dark matter model as the current standard model of cosmology correspondsto a harmonic oscillator. We further generalize this formalism to take intoaccount the bulk viscosity and other cases. The Hamiltonian can be quantizedstraightforwardly, but this is different from the approach of theWheeler-DeWitt equation in quantum cosmology.
label: human

text: We develop a consistent Hamiltonian formulation of Friedmann cosmology that treats the scale factor and its conjugate momentum as canonical variables subject to the cosmological constraints. Starting from the Einstein–Hilbert action for homogeneous and isotropic universes, we derive an effective minisuperspace Hamiltonian that reproduces the classical Friedmann equations for various spatial curvatures and matter contents. The constraint structure and gauge freedom associated with time reparametrization are analyzed in detail, leading to a reduced phase space description. Based on this Hamiltonian framework, we construct the corresponding Wheeler–DeWitt equation and investigate its solutions for different choices of factor ordering and matter fields. Particular emphasis is placed on the interpretation of the wave function of the universe and the emergence of semiclassical cosmological dynamics. We discuss the implications of our quantization scheme for early-universe scenarios, including singularity avoidance and the possible role of quantum effects in inflationary and bouncing cosmologies.
label: llm

text: The ever-increasing knowledge of the structure of various real-world networkshas uncovered their complex multi-mechanism-governed evolution processes.Therefore, a better understanding of the structure and evolution of thesenetworked complex systems requires us to describe such processes in a moredetailed and realistic manner. In this paper, we introduce a new type ofnetwork growth rule which comprises addition and deletion of nodes, and proposean evolving network model to investigate the effect of node deleting on networkstructure. It is found that, with the introduction of node deleting, networkstructure is significantly transformed. In particular, degree distribution ofthe network undergoes a transition from scale-free to exponential forms as theintensity of node deleting increases. At the same time, nontrivialdisassortative degree correlation develops spontaneously as a natural result ofnetwork evolution in the model. We also demonstrate that node deletingintroduced in the model does not destroy the connectedness of a growing networkso long as the increasing rate of edges is not excessively small. In addition,it is found that node deleting will weaken but not eliminate the small-worldeffect of a growing network, and generally it will decrease the clusteringcoefficient in a network.
label: human

text: This study investigates the effect of node deletion on the structural properties of complex networks. We analyze both random and targeted node removal strategies in synthetic and empirical networks to understand their distinct impacts on global connectivity. Using measures such as giant component size, average path length, clustering coefficient, and degree distribution, we systematically quantify structural changes under progressive node deletion. Our results show that scale-free networks are highly robust to random deletions but exhibit pronounced fragility under targeted attacks on high-degree nodes. In contrast, more homogeneous networks display comparatively similar sensitivity to both random and targeted removal. We further explore how network modularity and assortativity mediate the resilience of network structure under node loss. These findings provide insight into the vulnerability and robustness of real-world systems, with implications for infrastructure protection, epidemic control, and network design.
label: llm

text: We present a morphological study of galaxies in the A901/902 superclusterfrom the COMBO-17 survey. A total of 570 galaxies with photometric redshifts inthe range 0.155 < z_phot < 0.185 are visually classified by three independentclassifiers to M_V=-18. These morphological classifications are compared tolocal galaxy density, distance from the nearest cluster centre, local surfacemass density from weak lensing, and photometric classification. At high localgalaxy densities, log(Sigma_10 /Mpc^2) > 1.5, a classical morphology-densityrelation is found. A correlation is also found between morphology and localprojected surface mass density, but no trend is observed with distance to thenearest cluster. This supports the finding that local environment is moreimportant to galaxy morphology than global cluster properties. The breakdown ofthe morphological catalogue by colour shows a dominance of blue galaxies in thegalaxies displaying late-type morphologies and a corresponding dominance of redgalaxies in the early-type population. Using the 17-band photometry fromCOMBO-17, we further split the supercluster red sequence into old passivegalaxies and galaxies with young stars and dust according to the prescriptionof Wolf et al. (2005). We find that the dusty star-forming population describesan intermediate morphological group between late-type and early-type galaxies,supporting the hypothesis that field and group spiral galaxies are transformedinto S0s and, perhaps, ellipticals during cluster infall.
label: human

text: We investigate the relationship between galaxy morphology and environment in the Abell 901/902 supercluster at z ≈ 0.165 using deep imaging and photometric redshifts from the COMBO-17 survey. Our sample comprises several hundred supercluster members selected via high-precision photometric redshifts, allowing us to map environmental density over a wide dynamic range. Morphological classifications are derived from high-resolution imaging and quantified using visual types and structural parameters such as concentration and asymmetry. We distinguish between early-type and late-type galaxies and examine their distributions as functions of local galaxy density, cluster-centric radius, and substructure within the supercluster. The early-type fraction increases strongly toward higher-density regions and the cores of the individual clusters, while late-type galaxies dominate in lower-density outskirts and inter-cluster filaments. We find that the morphology–density relation in Abell 901/902 is already well established at this intermediate redshift, with a strength comparable to that observed in local rich clusters. In addition, we detect an excess of morphologically disturbed systems and bulge-dominated spirals in intermediate-density environments, suggestive of ongoing transformation processes. These transition populations correlate with indicators of suppressed star formation, pointing to environmental quenching mechanisms such as ram-pressure stripping or galaxy–galaxy interactions. The results support a scenario in which galaxy morphologies are shaped not only by the global cluster potential but also by group-scale environments and.
label: llm

text: By combining high-resolution (HST-WFPC2) and wide-field ground based (2.2mESO-WFI) and space (GALEX) observations, we have collected a multi-wavelengthphotometric data base (ranging from the far UV to the near infrared) of thegalactic globular cluster NGC1904 (M79). The sample covers the entire clusterextension, from the very central regions up to the tidal radius. In the presentpaper such a data set is used to study the BSS population and its radialdistribution. A total number of 39 bright ($m_{218}\le 19.5$) BSS has beendetected, and they have been found to be highly segregated in the cluster core.No significant upturn in the BSS frequency has been observed in the outskirtsof NGC 1904, in contrast to other clusters (M 3, 47 Tuc, NGC 6752, M 5) studiedwith the same technique. Such evidences, coupled with the large radius ofavoidance estimated for NGC 1904 ($r_{avoid}\sim 30$ core radii), indicate thatthe vast majority of the cluster heavy stars (binaries) has already sunk to thecore. Accordingly, extensive dynamical simulations suggest that BSS formed bymass transfer activity in primordial binaries evolving in isolation in thecluster outskirts represent only a negligible (0--10%) fraction of the overallpopulation.
label: human

text: We present a comprehensive, panchromatic investigation of the blue straggler star (BSS) population in the Galactic globular cluster NGC 1904, combining high-resolution ultraviolet and optical imaging with complementary ground-based photometry. By constructing deep color–magnitude diagrams in multiple bands, we identify a robust sample of BSS candidates and characterize their luminosity and temperature distributions relative to the main-sequence turnoff. We derive the radial distribution of BSS and compare it to that of reference populations (subgiant and horizontal branch stars) to assess the impact of mass segregation and dynamical evolution. Our analysis reveals a centrally concentrated BSS population with evidence for a bimodal radial profile, indicative of multiple formation channels and advanced dynamical processing. Using theoretical isochrones and synthetic populations, we explore collisional and mass-transfer formation scenarios, constraining the relative role of each mechanism in NGC 1904. This study provides a benchmark for understanding the interplay between stellar evolution and dynamics in shaping the BSS content of moderately concentrated globular clusters.
label: llm

text: In the reaction e+e- -> WW -> (q_1 qbar_2)(q_3 qbar_4) the usualhadronization models treat the colour singlets q_1 qbar_2 and q_3 qbar_4 comingfrom two W bosons independently. However, since the final state partons maycoexist in space and time, cross-talk between the two evolving hadronic systemsmay be possible during fragmentation through soft gluon exchange. This effectis known as Colour Reconnection. In this article the results of theinvestigation of Colour Reconnection effects in fully hadronic decays of Wpairs in DELPHI at LEP are presented. Two complementary analyses wereperformed, studying the particle flow between jets and W mass estimators, withnegligible correlation between them, and the results were combined and comparedto models. In the framework of the SK-I model, the value for its kappaparameter most compatible with the data was found to be: kappa_{SK-I} =2.2^{+2.5}_{-1.3} corresponding to the probability of reconnection P_{reco} tobe in the range 0.31 < P_{reco} < 0.68 at 68% confidence level with its bestvalue at 0.52.
label: human

text: Investigation of Colour Reconnection in WW Events with the DELPHI Detector at LEP-2 abstract: Colour reconnection effects in hadronic W-pair decays are investigated using data collected with the DELPHI detector at LEP-2 at centre-of-mass energies between 189 and 209 GeV. A sample of fully hadronic WW events is selected and compared to semileptonic WW decays to isolate possible final-state interactions between the two hadronically decaying W bosons. Observables sensitive to colour flow, such as particle multiplicities, particle-flow distributions between jets, and global event-shape variables, are constructed and systematically compared to predictions of various phenomenological colour reconnection models implemented in Monte Carlo generators. The analysis includes a detailed study of systematic uncertainties arising from detector effects, hadronization modelling, background contamination, and event-selection criteria. No significant evidence for strong colour reconnection effects is observed within the experimental precision, although some models are marginally disfavoured by the data.
label: llm

text: We argue that all transient searches for planets in globular clusters have avery low detection probability. Planets of low metallicity stars typically donot reside at small orbital separations. The dependance of planetary systemproperties on metallicity is clearly seen when the quantity Ie=Mp[a(1-e)]^2 isconsidered; Mp, a, e, are the planet mass, semi-major axis, and eccentricity,respectively. In high metallicity systems there is a concentration of systemsat high and low values of Ie, with a low-populated gap near Ie~0.3 M_J AU^2,where M_J is Jupiter's mass. In low metallicity systems the concentration isonly at the higher range of I_e, with a tail to low values of Ie. Therefore, itis still possible that planets exist around main sequence stars in globularclusters, although at small numbers because of the low metallicity, and atorbital periods of >~10 days. We discuss the implications of our conclusions onthe role that companions can play in the evolution of their parent stars inglobular clusters, e.g., influencing the distribution of horizontal branchstars on the Hertzsprung-Russell diagram of some globular clusters, and informing low mass white dwarfs.
label: human

text: We investigate the formation, survival, and detectability of planetary systems in the dense stellar environments of globular clusters. Using a combination of N-body dynamical simulations and population synthesis models, we estimate the frequency and characteristics of planets that can form and persist around stars spanning a broad range of masses and evolutionary stages. Our results indicate that, despite the harsh dynamical conditions and low metallicities typical of globular clusters, a non-negligible population of predominantly low-mass, short-period planets is expected to survive over gigayear timescales. We show that close-in terrestrial and Neptune-mass planets are more resilient to dynamical disruption than wide-orbit gas giants, which are efficiently stripped by stellar encounters. Metallicity-dependent planet formation models suggest that the overall planet occurrence rate in globular clusters is lower than in the Galactic field, but not vanishingly small, especially in clusters with relatively higher metal content. We further quantify the parameter space where transits and microlensing events from cluster planets would be observationally accessible with current and upcoming facilities.
label: llm

text: Using numerical simulations, we investigate vortex configurations and pinningin superconductors with honeycomb and kagome pinning arrays. We find that avariety of novel vortex crystal states can be stabilized at integer andfractional matching field densities. The honeycomb and kagome pinning arraysproduce considerably more pronounced commensuration peaks in the criticaldepinning force than triangular pinning arrays, and also cause additional peaksat noninteger matching fields where a portion of the vortices are located inthe large interstitial regions of the pinning lattices. For the honeycombpinning array, we find matching effects of equal strength at most fillingsB/B_\phi=n/2 for n>2, where n is an integer, in agreement with recentexperiments. For kagome pinning arrays, pronounced matching effects generallyoccur at B/B_\phi=n/3 for n>3, while for triangular pinning arrays pronouncedmatching effects are observed only at integer fillings B/B_\phi=n. At thenoninteger matching field peaks in the honeycomb and kagome pinning arrays, theinterstitial vortices are arranged in dimer, trimer, and higher order n-merstates that have an overall orientational order. We call these n-mer states"vortex molecular crystals" and "vortex plastic crystals" since they aresimilar to the states recently observed in colloidal molecular crystal systems.We argue that the vortex molecular crystals have properties in common withcertain spin systems such as Ising and n-state Potts models. We show thatkagome and honeycomb pinning arrays can be useful for increasing the criticalcurrent above that of purely triangular pinning arrays.
label: human

text: We numerically investigate the structural and dynamical properties of vortex matter interacting with honeycomb and kagome pinning arrays in type-II superconductors. Using large-scale Langevin dynamics simulations, we identify regimes where the vortices self-organize into vortex molecular crystal states, characterized by multi-vortex complexes localized in the pinning-induced interstitial regions. At elevated temperatures or under increased driving forces, these ordered molecular crystals undergo transitions into vortex plastic crystal states, where rotational and translational degrees of freedom are partially decoupled and vortices exhibit plastic flow. We construct phase diagrams as a function of magnetic field, temperature, and pinning strength, revealing distinct boundaries between pinned, molecular crystal, plastic crystal, and liquid-like vortex phases. In both honeycomb and kagome geometries, commensurability effects at particular matching fields stabilize highly symmetric molecular configurations that maximize pinning efficiency. The kagome arrays, however, support a richer variety of molecular states due to the presence of inequivalent plaquettes and reduced lattice symmetry. We analyze the corresponding transport signatures and demonstrate that transitions between molecular and plastic crystal states produce characteristic features in the current–voltage curves and differential resistance. Our results show that engineered quasi-frustrated pinning landscapes provide a route to controlling complex vortex phases and optimizing superconducting performance through tailored vortex molecular ordering.
label: llm

text: Mn3V2O8 is a magnetic system in which S = 5/2 Mn2+ is found in the kagomestaircase lattice. Here we report the magnetic phase diagram for temperaturesabove 2 K and applied magnetic fields below 9 T, characterized by measurementsof the magnetization and specific heat with field along the three uniquelattice directions. At low applied magnetic fields, the system first ordersmagnetically below Tm1 ~ 21 K, and then shows a second magnetic phasetransition at Tm2 ~ 15 K. In addition, a phase transition that is apparent inspecific heat but not seen in magnetization is found for all three appliedfield orientations, converging towards Tm2 as H -> 0. The magnetic behavior ishighly anisotropic, with critical fields for magnetic phase boundaries muchhigher when the field is applied perpendicular to the Kagome staircase planethan when applied in-plane. The field-temperature (H - T) phase diagrams arequite rich, with 7 distinct phases observed.
label: human

text: We report a detailed investigation of the magnetic properties and phase diagram of the Kagome-staircase compound Mn₃V₂O₈ using bulk thermodynamic and magnetic measurements. Temperature- and field-dependent magnetization, specific heat, and susceptibility data reveal multiple magnetic phase transitions at low temperatures, indicative of competing exchange interactions and strong magnetic frustration.
