Furthermore, the leading mechanisms of theobserved charge order are quantified via our first-principles derivation of thelow-energy effective Hamiltonian
label: human

text: Charge ordering in half-doped manganites remains a subject of significant interest due to its complex interplay between electronic, lattice, and spin degrees of freedom. In this study, we investigate the nature of charge disproportionation in these materials, revealing that the charge difference between nominal Mn3+ and Mn4+ sites is substantially weaker than traditionally assumed. Utilizing a combination of advanced spectroscopic techniques and theoretical modeling, we identify the leading mechanisms driving charge ordering beyond simple ionic pictures. Our results indicate that electron-lattice coupling and orbital ordering contribute critically to stabilizing the charge-ordered state, rather than purely electrostatic interactions. Furthermore, the role of collective electronic correlations and subtle structural distortions are shown to be essential in understanding the observed weak charge disproportionation. These findings challenge conventional charge ordering paradigms and underscore the need for refined models incorporating multiscale interactions. Ultimately, this work provides a more nuanced understanding of the charge ordering phenomena in manganites, with implications for their electronic and magnetic properties.
label: llm

text: There exist methods for determining effective conservative interactions incoarse grained particle based mesoscopic simulations. The resulting models canbe used to capture thermal equilibrium behavior, but in the model system westudy do not correctly represent transport properties. In this article wesuggest the use of force covariance to determine the full functional form ofdissipative and stochastic interactions. We show that a combination of theradial distribution function and a force covariance function can be used todetermine all interactions in dissipative particle dynamics. Furthermore we usethe method to test if the effective interactions in dissipative particledynamics (DPD) can be adjusted to produce a force covariance consistent with aprojection of a microscopic Lennard-Jones simulation. The results indicate thatthe DPD ansatz may not be consistent with the underlying microscopic dynamics.We discuss how this result relates to theoretical studies reported in theliterature.
label: human

text: This study presents a novel approach for deriving effective stochastic interactions in dissipative particle dynamics (DPD) through the analysis of force covariance. By examining the statistical properties of fluctuating forces between particles, we establish a direct link between microscopic force correlations and macroscopic stochastic terms in the DPD framework. The method enables the extraction of consistent noise amplitudes and dissipative coefficients, ensuring thermodynamic consistency and improved physical accuracy. Applying this technique to model systems demonstrates enhanced agreement with underlying molecular dynamics simulations, capturing essential hydrodynamic and thermal fluctuations. The approach offers a systematic pathway to parameterize DPD interactions based on detailed force statistics, reducing reliance on heuristic tuning. Overall, this work contributes to the rigorous foundation of stochastic mesoscale modeling and facilitates more predictive simulations of complex fluids.
label: llm

text: The configurations of single and double bonds in polycyclic hydrocarbons areabstracted as Kekul\'e states of graphs. Sending a so-called soliton over anopen channel between ports (external nodes) of the graph changes the Kekul\'estate and therewith the set of open channels in the graph. This switchingbehaviour is proposed as a basis for molecular computation. The proposal ishighly speculative but may have tremendous impact.  Kekul\'e states with the same boundary behaviour (port assignment) can beregarded as equivalent. This gives rise to the abstraction of Kekul\'e cells.The basic theory of Kekul\'e states and Kekul\'e cells is developed here, up tothe classification of Kekul\'e cells with $\leq 4$ ports. To put the theory incontext, we generalize Kekul\'e states to semi-Kekul\'e states, which form thesolutions of a linear system of equations over the field of the bits 0 and 1.We briefly study so-called omniconjugated graphs, in which every portassignment of the right signature has a Kekul\'e state. Omniconjugated graphsmay be useful as connectors between computational elements. We finallyinvestigate some examples with potentially useful switching behaviour.
label: human

text: Molecular computation represents a promising paradigm for information processing at the nanoscale, where chemical structures can encode and manipulate data through their inherent physical properties. This paper introduces the concept of Kekulé cells, a novel framework for molecular computation based on the alternating bond structures found in conjugated organic molecules. We demonstrate that benzenoid hydrocarbons exhibiting Kekulé resonance can function as bistable computational units, with distinct electronic configurations serving as binary states. The switching between resonance structures can be controlled through external stimuli such as pH changes, redox reactions, or photonic excitation, enabling programmable logic operations. We present a theoretical model for cascading Kekulé cells into molecular circuits capable of performing Boolean operations and basic arithmetic functions. Experimental validation using polyacene derivatives shows successful implementation of AND, OR, and NOT gates with switching times on the order of picoseconds. Our simulations indicate that Kekulé cell networks could achieve computational densities exceeding 10^15 gates per cubic centimeter, orders of magnitude beyond current semiconductor technology.
label: llm

text: We report the discovery of a new white dwarf/M dwarf binary, HS1857+5144,identified in the Hamburg Quasar Survey (HQS). Time-resolved opticalspectroscopy and photometry were carried out to determine the properties ofthis new cataclysmic variable progenitor pre-CV). The light curves ofHS1857+5144 display a sinusoidal variation with a period of Porb=383.52 min andpeak-to-peak amplitudes of 0.7 mag and 1.1 mag in the B-band and R-band,respectively. The large amplitude of the brightness variation results from areflection effect on the heated inner hemisphere of the companion star,suggesting a very high temperature of the white dwarf. Our radial velocitystudy confirms the photometric period as the orbital period of the system. Amodel atmosphere fit to the spectrum of the white dwarf obtained at minimumlight provides limits to its mass and temperature of Mwd=~0.6-1.0 Msun andTwd=~70000-100000 K, respectively. The detection of HeII 4686 absorptionclassifies the primary star of HS1857+5144 as a DAO white dwarf. Combining theresults from our spectroscopy and photometry, we estimate the mass of thecompanion star and the binary inclination to be Msec=~0.15-0.30 Msun andi=~45-55 deg, respectively. We classify HS1857+5144 as one of the youngestpre-CV known to date. The cooling age of the white dwarf suggests that thepresent system has just emerged from a common envelope phase ~10^5 yr ago.HS1857+5144 will start mass transfer within or below the 2-3h period gap.
label: human

text: HS1857+5144 is identified as a hot and young pre-cataclysmic variable (pre-CV) system exhibiting distinctive properties that provide valuable insights into binary star evolution. Spectroscopic and photometric observations reveal that the system consists of a hot white dwarf primary and a low-mass companion star close to filling its Roche lobe. The temperature of the white dwarf is notably high, indicative of a recent common-envelope phase and ongoing thermal relaxation. Light curve analysis shows variability consistent with ellipsoidal modulation and possible irradiation effects on the secondary star’s atmosphere. Radial velocity measurements enable the determination of the binary orbital period, which is found to be unusually short for pre-CVs, suggesting an early stage in orbital shrinkage. The system’s parameters imply rapid evolutionary timescales before it transitions into a classical cataclysmic variable. Comparisons with theoretical models highlight the importance of HS1857+5144 for testing predictions of angular momentum loss mechanisms and mass transfer initiation. Its youth and temperature provide a rare observational window into the post-common-envelope phase prior to stable mass accretion. This study enhances understanding of the physical processes governing the early evolution of close white dwarf binaries. HS1857+5144 thus serves as a critical benchmark for constraining pre-cataclysmic variable population synthesis and evolutionary tracks.
label: llm

text: We continue our study of chaotic mixing and transport of passive particles ina simple model of a meandering jet flow [Prants, et al, Chaos {\bf 16}, 033117(2006)]. In the present paper we study and explain phenomenologically aconnection between dynamical, topological, and statistical properties ofchaotic mixing and transport in the model flow in terms of dynamical traps,singular zones in the phase space where particles may spend arbitrary long butfinite time [Zaslavsky, Phys. D {\bf 168--169}, 292 (2002)]. The transport ofpassive particles is described in terms of lengths and durations of zonalflights which are events between two successive changes of sign of zonalvelocity. Some peculiarities of the respective probability density functionsfor short flights are proven to be caused by the so-called rotational-islandstraps connected with the boundaries of resonant islands (including those of thevortex cores) filled with the particles moving in the same frame. Whereas, thestatistics of long flights can be explained by the influence of the so-calledballistic-islands traps filled with the particles moving from a frame to frame.
label: human

text: We investigate the transport properties of passive tracers in a kinematic model of a meandering jet flow, which serves as an idealized representation of oceanic currents such as the Gulf Stream. The flow field consists of a steady background jet perturbed by a traveling wave, creating a time-periodic velocity field that exhibits complex Lagrangian dynamics. Through numerical simulations and theoretical analysis, we identify the formation of dynamical traps—coherent structures that temporarily confine fluid parcels and significantly delay cross-jet transport. We demonstrate that these traps arise from the interplay between the mean flow and the meandering perturbation, and their boundaries correspond to invariant manifolds of hyperbolic trajectories in the flow. The transition to chaotic advection occurs when particle trajectories become sensitive to initial conditions, leading to enhanced mixing and the breakdown of transport barriers. Our results reveal that the efficiency of cross-jet exchange depends critically on the meander amplitude and frequency, with implications for understanding pollutant dispersion and biological connectivity in oceanic jet systems.
label: llm

text: Cooperative diversity systems are wireless communication systems designed toexploit cooperation among users to mitigate the effects of multipath fading. Infairly general conditions, it has been shown that these systems can achieve thediversity order of an equivalent MISO channel and, if the node geometrypermits, virtually the same outage probability can be achieved as that of theequivalent MISO channel for a wide range of applicable SNR. However, much ofthe prior analysis has been performed under the assumption of perfect timingand frequency offset synchronization. In this paper, we derive the estimationbounds and associated maximum likelihood estimators for frequency offsetestimation in a cooperative communication system. We show the benefit ofadaptively tuning the frequency of the relay node in order to reduce estimationerror at the destination. We also derive an efficient estimation algorithm,based on the correlation sequence of the data, which has mean squared errorclose to the Cramer-Rao Bound.
label: human

text: This paper investigates fundamental limits and algorithmic solutions for frequency synchronization in collaborative communication systems. We derive theoretical bounds that characterize the performance of frequency offset estimation under various signal and noise conditions. Building on these bounds, we propose novel synchronization algorithms that leverage cooperation among network nodes to enhance estimation accuracy and reduce computational complexity. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed methods achieve near-optimal performance in diverse scenarios, outperforming conventional single-node synchronization techniques. We also analyze the trade-offs between synchronization accuracy, communication overhead, and algorithm robustness. The findings provide valuable insights and practical guidelines for the design of frequency synchronization protocols in next-generation collaborative wireless networks.
label: llm

text: The coupling of the manganite stripe phase to the lattice and to strain hasbeen investigated via transmission electron microscopy studies ofpolycrystalline and thin film manganites. In polycrystalline \PCMOfiftwo alockin to $q/a^*=0.5$ in a sample with $x>0.5$ has been observed for the firsttime. Such a lockin has been predicted as a key part of the Landau CDW theoryof the stripe phase. Thus it is possible to constrain the size of theelectron-phonon coupling in the CDW Landau theory to between 0.04% and 0.05% ofthe electron-electron coupling term. In the thin film samples, films of thesame thickness grown on two different substrates exhibited differentwavevectors. The different strains present in the films on the two substratescan be related to the wavevector observed via Landau theory. It is demonstratedthat the the elastic term which favours an incommensurate modulation has asimilar size to the coupling between the strain and the wavevector, meaningthat the coupling of strain to the superlattice is unexpectedly strong.
label: human

text: This study investigates the interplay between electron-phonon interactions and strain effects in manganite materials. Using a combination of spectroscopic measurements and theoretical modeling, we demonstrate that the electron-phonon coupling in these compounds is significantly weaker than previously assumed. Contrary to conventional expectations, the electronic transport properties appear to be minimally influenced by lattice vibrations. Instead, we find a pronounced coupling between the electronic states and mechanical strain, which strongly affects the manganites' structural and magnetic phases. Our results suggest that strain engineering can be an effective route to modulate the electronic and magnetic behavior in these materials. These findings challenge the dominant role traditionally attributed to electron-phonon interactions in manganites and open new pathways for device applications exploiting strain effects. Overall, this work provides fresh insight into the fundamental mechanisms governing the complex physics of manganites.
label: llm

text: In an earlier paper, the effect of the nearby known supernova remnants (SNRs)on the local cosmic-rays (CRs) was studied, considering different possibleforms of the particle injection time. The present work is a continuation of theprevious work, but assumes a more realistic model of CR propagation in theGalaxy. The previous work assumed an unbounded three-dimensional diffusionregion, whereas the present one considers a flat cylindrical disc bounded inboth the radial and vertical directions. The study has found that the effect ofthe vertical halo boundary $H$ on the local SNR contribution to the observed CRanisotropy is negligible as long as $H\gtrsim 2kpc$. Considering the values ofthe halo height $H\gtrsim 2kpc$ obtained by different authors, the present worksuggests that the study of the effect of local sources on the CR anisotropy canbe carried out without having much information on $H$ and hence, using the muchsimpler three-dimentional unbounded solution. Finally, the present workdiscusses about the possibility of explaining the observed anisotropy below theknee by a single dominant source with properly chosen source parameters, andclaims that the source may be an \textit{undetected} old SNR with acharacteristic age of $\sim 1.5\times 10^5 yr$ located at a distance of $\sim0.57 kpc$ from the Sun.
label: human

text: This study reexamines the influence of nearby supernova remnants (SNRs) on the flux and composition of local cosmic rays detected near Earth. Utilizing updated astrophysical data and refined propagation models, we analyze the contributions of several well-known SNRs within a few hundred parsecs. Our results indicate that the energy spectra and anisotropies observed in cosmic ray measurements are consistent with a significant input from these local remnants. We also explore the temporal evolution of cosmic ray injection from SNRs and its impact on spectral features at different energies. The findings suggest that nearby SNRs play a crucial role in shaping the local cosmic ray environment, with implications for interpreting observational data from space- and ground-based detectors. This work underscores the importance of incorporating detailed source history and spatial distribution in cosmic ray transport models to better understand their origin and propagation.
label: llm

text: In this paper we analyse the effect produced by the temperature in the vacuumpolarization associated with charged massless scalar field in the presence ofmagnetic flux tube in the cosmic string spacetime. Three differentconfigurations of magnetic fields are taken into account: $(i)$ a homogeneousfield inside the tube, $(ii)$ a field proportional to $1/r$ and $(iii)$ acylindrical shell with $\delta$-function. In these three cases, the axis of theinfinitely long tube of radius $R$ coincides with the cosmic string. Becausethe complexity of this analysis in the region inside the tube, we consider thethermal effect in the region outside. In order to develop this analysis, weconstruct the thermal Green function associated with this system for the threeabove mentioned situations considering points in the region outside the tube.We explicitly calculate in the high-temperature limit, the thermal average ofthe field square and the energy-momentum tensor.
label: human

text: This paper investigates the vacuum polarization effects induced by a magnetic flux tube in the background of a cosmic string spacetime at finite temperature. Using quantum field theoretical methods in curved spacetime, we analyze how the presence of both the cosmic string’s conical geometry and the magnetic flux influence the vacuum expectation values of physical observables. The study employs the finite-temperature field theory formalism to derive thermal corrections to the vacuum polarization tensor, highlighting modifications in the vacuum structure due to temperature variations. Our results reveal significant alterations in the vacuum polarization profiles near the magnetic flux tube, which depend sensitively on the temperature and the geometric parameters of the cosmic string. These findings contribute to a deeper understanding of quantum effects in topologically nontrivial backgrounds with thermal environments, relevant for early universe cosmology and condensed matter analogs.
label: llm

text: Motivation: Profile hidden Markov Models (pHMMs) are a popular and veryuseful tool in the detection of the remote homologue protein families.Unfortunately, their performance is not always satisfactory when proteins arein the 'twilight zone'. We present HMMER-STRUCT, a model construction algorithmand tool that tries to improve pHMM performance by using structural informationwhile training pHMMs. As a first step, HMMER-STRUCT constructs a set of pHMMs.Each pHMM is constructed by weighting each residue in an aligned proteinaccording to a specific structural property of the residue. Properties usedwere primary, secondary and tertiary structures, accessibility and packing.HMMER-STRUCT then prioritizes the results by voting. Results: We used the SCOPdatabase to perform our experiments. Throughout, we apply leave-one-family-outcross-validation over protein superfamilies. First, we used the MAMMOTH-multstructural aligner to align the training set proteins. Then, we performed twosets of experiments. In a first experiment, we compared structure weightedmodels against standard pHMMs and against each other. In a second experiment,we compared the voting model against individual pHMMs. We compare methodperformance through ROC curves and through Precision/Recall curves, and assesssignificance through the paired two tailed t-test. Our results show significantperformance improvements of all structurally weighted models over defaultHMMER, and a significant improvement in sensitivity of the combined models overboth the original model and the structurally weighted models.
label: human

text: This study investigates the structural properties of profile Hidden Markov Models (HMMs) with the aim of enhancing their understanding and application in sequence analysis. Profile HMMs are widely used in bioinformatics for modeling sequence families and detecting homologous sequences. Despite their extensive use, the intricate structural characteristics governing their performance have not been thoroughly analyzed in existing literature. Here, we present a comprehensive examination of profile HMM architectures and the impact of different structural components on model accuracy and robustness. We analyze the effects of varying state configurations, emission probabilities, and transition dynamics within profile HMMs. Our methodology involves both theoretical analysis and empirical evaluation using benchmark biological sequence datasets. Results demonstrate that certain structural patterns significantly improve the discrimination capability of profile HMMs. Additionally, we identify critical dependencies between model complexity and generalization to unseen sequences. This work also explores optimization strategies that balance model expressiveness and computational efficiency. The findings offer valuable insights for designing profile HMMs tailored to specific sequence analysis tasks. Furthermore, we discuss implications for future development of profile-based probabilistic models in computational biology. Overall, this study contributes to a deeper mechanistic understanding and practical enhancement of profile HMMs as powerful tools in biological sequence analysis.

text: The scaling behaviors of graphene nanoribbon (GNR) Schottky barrierfield-effect transistors (SBFETs) are studied by solving the non-equilibriumGreen's function (NEGF) transport equation in an atomistic basis setself-consistently with a three-dimensional Poisson equation. The armchair edgeGNR channel shares similarities with a zigzag CNT, but it has a differentgeometry and quantum confinement boundary condition in the transversedirection. The results indicate that the I-V characteristics are ambipolar andstrongly depend on the GNR width because the bandgap of the GNR isapproximately inversely proportional to its width, which agrees with recentexperiments. A multiple gate geometry improves immunity to short channeleffects, but it offers smaller improvement than it does for Si MOSFETs in termsof the on-current and transconductance. Reducing the oxide thickness is moreuseful for improving transistor performance than using a high-k gate insulator.Significant increase of the minimal leakage current is observed when thechannel length is scaled below 10nm because the small effective massfacilitates strong source-drain tunneling. The GNRFET, therefore, does notpromise extending the ultimate scaling limit of Si MOSFETs. The intrinsicswitching speed of a GNR SBFET, however, is several times faster than that ofSi MOSFETs, which could lead to promising high speed electronics applications,where the large leakage of GNR SBFETs is of less concern.

text: This study presents a comprehensive investigation into the scaling behaviors of graphene nanoribbon field-effect transistors (GNR FETs) using three-dimensional quantum simulations. By employing an atomistic modeling approach, the electronic transport properties of GNR FETs are analyzed under varying channel lengths and widths, revealing critical insights into device performance limits at the nanoscale. The simulations incorporate full quantum mechanical effects, including tunneling and carrier confinement, to accurately capture the influence of dimensional scaling. Results indicate that gate control and short-channel effects are strongly dependent on the nanoribbon width, highlighting the trade-off between device miniaturization and electrostatic integrity. Furthermore, the study identifies scaling constraints imposed by edge roughness and quantum capacitance, which significantly affect the subthreshold slope and ON/OFF current ratio. These findings provide a deeper understanding of the fundamental mechanisms governing GNR FET operation and offer valuable guidelines for optimizing device design. Ultimately, this work advances the prospects of graphene-based nanoelectronics by elucidating the challenges and opportunities presented by aggressive scaling in three-dimensional device architectures.

text: The nonadiabatic Heisenberg model (NHM) proposed as an extension of theHeisenberg model makes a contribution to the eigenstate problem ofsuperconductivity. The Hamiltonian H^n derived within this group-theoreticalmodel has superconducting eigenstates if and only if the considered materialpossesses a narrow, roughly half-filled "superconducting" energy band ofspecial symmetry in its band structure. This paper shows that thehigh-temperature superconductor YBa_2Cu_3O_7 possesses such a superconductingband. This new result together with previous observations about othersuperconductors and non-superconductors corroborates the theoretical evidencewithin the NHM that stable superconducting states are connected withsuperconducting bands. It is proposed that the type of superconductivity, i.e.,whether the material is a conventional low-T_c or a high-T_c superconductor, isdetermined by the energetically lowest boson excitations that carry the crystalspin 1*hbar and are sufficiently stable to transport this crystal spin-angularmomentum through the crystal. This mechanism provides the electron-phononmechanism that enters the BCS theory in conventional superconductors.

text: This study investigates the stability of the superconducting state in the high-temperature superconductor YBa₂Cu₃O₇ (YBCO) through a combination of experimental measurements and theoretical analysis. We examine the effects of temperature variation, external magnetic fields, and structural defects on the superconducting phase to understand the robustness of Cooper pair formation under different perturbations. Magnetization and resistivity measurements reveal critical thresholds beyond which the superconducting state degrades, highlighting the role of vortex dynamics and flux pinning. Additionally, we analyze the influence of oxygen stoichiometry on the superconducting transition temperature and its impact on stability. Our results demonstrate that optimal oxygen content and defect engineering significantly enhance the resilience of the superconducting state against external disturbances. These findings provide insight into improving the practical performance of YBCO-based superconducting materials in technological applications.
label: llm

text: We discuss the emission of gravitational radiation produced in encounters ofdark matter galactic halos. To this aim we perform a number of numericalsimulations of typical galaxy mergers, computing the associated gravitationalradiation waveforms as well as the energy released in the processes. Oursimulations yield dimensionless gravitational wave amplitudes of the order of$10^{-13}$ and gravitational wave frequencies of the order of $10^{-16}$ Hz,when the galaxies are located at a distance of 10 Mpc. These values are of thesame order as those arising in the gravitational radiation originated by strongvariations of the gravitational field in the early Universe, and therefore,such gravitational waves cannot be directly observed by ground-based detectors.We discuss the feasibility of an indirect detection by means of the B-modepolarization of the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) induced by such waves.Our results show that the gravitational waves from encounters of dark mattergalactic halos leave much too small an imprint on the CMB polarization to beactually observed with ongoing and future missions.

text: This study explores the generation and characteristics of gravitational waves produced during galaxy encounters, focusing on their detectability and astrophysical implications. By modeling the dynamics of interacting galaxies, we analyze the gravitational wave signals emitted as a result of their complex mass distributions and relative motions. Our results suggest that although these waves are weaker than those from compact binaries, they provide valuable insights into large-scale structure formation and galaxy evolution. These findings open new avenues for future gravitational wave observations to complement electromagnetic studies of galaxy interactions.
label: llm

text: In this paper we consider stationary force-free magnetosphere of an alignedrotator when plasma in the open field line region rotates differentially due topresence of a zone with the accelerating electric field in the polar cap ofpulsar. We study the impact of differential rotation on the current densitydistribution in the magnetosphere. Using split-monopole approximation we obtainanalytical expressions for physical parameters of differentially rotatingmagnetosphere. We find the range of admitted current density distributionsunder the requirement that the potential drop in the polar cap is less than thevacuum potential drop. We show that the current density distribution coulddeviate significantly from the ``classical'' Michel distribution and could bemade almost constant over the polar cap even when the potential drop in theaccelerating zone is of the order of 10 per cents of the vacuum potential drop.We argue that differential rotation of the open magnetic field lines could playan important role in adjusting between the magnetosphere and the polar capcascade zone and could affect the value of pulsar breaking index.

text: This study presents analytical solutions for the force-free magnetosphere of an aligned rotator under the assumption of differential rotation within the split-monopole approximation. By extending classical models of pulsar magnetospheres, we incorporate spatially varying angular velocity profiles to capture more realistic magnetospheric dynamics. The derived solutions reveal how differential rotation influences the structure of magnetic field lines and the distribution of currents in the magnetosphere. Our results highlight key differences from rigidly rotating cases, including modifications to the electromagnetic energy outflow and field topology. These findings provide a deeper theoretical framework for interpreting observational phenomena related to pulsar wind acceleration and magnetospheric emission.

text: Author offers and researches a new, cheap method for the extraction offreshwater from the Earth atmosphere. text: The extraction of freshwater and energy from the atmosphere presents a promising interdisciplinary approach to addressing global water scarcity and energy challenges. Atmospheric water vapor represents a vast, renewable source of freshwater that remains largely untapped. Recent advances in materials science and atmospheric engineering have enabled the development of novel technologies for efficient water harvesting directly from air. These techniques often integrate with renewable energy systems, creating synergistic cycles for simultaneous energy generation and freshwater production. One prominent method involves the use of hygroscopic materials that capture moisture at ambient temperatures, minimizing energy consumption. Additionally, solar-driven atmospheric water generators harness sunlight to facilitate phase changes, reducing reliance on external power sources. Beyond water collection, the atmosphere also offers opportunities for clean energy extraction through wind and solar radiation. Integrating atmospheric water extraction with energy harvesting can improve overall system sustainability and economic viability. Comparative analyses demonstrate that atmospheric extraction methods can complement traditional water and energy infrastructure, particularly in arid and off-grid regions. Key challenges remain in scaling these technologies, optimizing material efficiency, and reducing operational costs. Life cycle assessments indicate potential environmental benefits by lowering dependency on fossil fuels and groundwater depletion. Future research should prioritize hybrid systems that couple atmospheric water extraction with localized renewable energy sources. Policy frameworks and investment strategies will be critical for translating laboratory successes into widespread application.

text: We study 7 Gamma Ray Bursts (GRBs), detected both by the BATSE instrument,on-board the Compton Gamma Ray Observatory, and by the Wide Field Camera (WFC),on-board BeppoSAX. These bursts have measured spectroscopic redshifts and are asizeable fraction of the bursts defining the correlation between the peakenergy E_peak (i.e. the peak of the vFv spectrum) and the total promptisotropic energy E_iso (the so called "Amati" relation). Recent theoreticalinterpretations of this correlation assume that black-body emission dominatesthe time resolved spectra of GRBs, even if, in the time integrated spectrum,its presence may be hidden by the change of its temperature and by the dilutionof a possible non-thermal power law component. We perform a time resolvedspectral analysis, and show that the sum of a power-law and a black-body givesacceptable fits to the time dependent spectra within the BATSE energy range,but overpredicts the flux in the WFC X-ray range. Moreover, a fit with a cutoffpower-law plus a black-body is consistent with the WFC data, but the black-bodycomponent contributes a negligible fraction of the total flux. On the contrary,we find that fitting the spectra with a Band model or a simple cutoff power-lawmodel yields an X-ray flux and spectral slope which well matches the WFCspectra.

text: Gamma-Ray Bursts (GRBs) represent some of the most energetic phenomena in the universe, yet their prompt emission mechanisms remain a topic of active investigation. Recent observations have suggested the possible presence of thermal, black-body-like components in the spectra of certain GRBs, challenging purely non-thermal emission models. In this study, we analyze a comprehensive sample of GRB prompt emission spectra collected by multiple space-based observatories to identify and characterize potential black-body features. Utilizing advanced spectral fitting techniques, we test models combining non-thermal synchrotron emission with thermal black-body components. Our results indicate that a subset of GRBs exhibits statistically significant black-body signatures, typically manifesting as a distinct, narrow peak superimposed on a broader non-thermal spectrum. These findings imply the existence of a photospheric emission region contributing to the observed radiation, offering insights into the jet composition and dynamics. We discuss the implications of thermal components for GRB emission theories and highlight future observational strategies to further clarify their role.

text: We have analyzed the HI aperture synthesis image of the Large MagellanicCloud (LMC), using an objective and quantitative measure of topology tounderstand the HI distribution hosting a number of holes and clumps of varioussizes in the medium. The HI distribution shows different topology at fourdifferent chosen scales. At the smallest scales explored (19-29 pc), the HImass is distributed in such a way that numerous clumps are embedded on top of alow density background. At the larger scales from 73 to 194 pc, it shows ageneric hole topology. These holes might have been formed mainly by stellarwinds from hot stars. At the scales from 240 to 340 pc, slightly above the diskscale-height of the gaseous disk, major clumps in the HI map change thedistribution to have a slight clump topology. These clumps include the giantcloud associations in the spiral arms and the thick filaments surroundingsuperholes. At the largest scales studied (390-485 pc), the hole topology ispresent again. Responsible to the hole topology at this scale are a fewsuperholes which seem mainly associated with supernova explosions in the outerdisk. The gaps between the bar and spiral arms have a minor effect on thetopology at this scale.

text: We present a comprehensive topological analysis of neutral hydrogen (HI) distributions in the Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC) using high-resolution 21-cm line observations. Our study employs persistent homology and Betti number calculations to characterize the multiscale structural features of the HI gas across column densities ranging from 10^19 to 10^22 cm^-2. We identify three distinct topological regimes corresponding to diffuse gas, filamentary structures, and dense cloud complexes, each exhibiting unique topological signatures. The filamentary network shows a characteristic length scale of approximately 100-200 pc, consistent with turbulent driving mechanisms in the interstellar medium. We find that regions of active star formation correlate strongly with topological transitions where the Euler characteristic changes sign, suggesting that topology plays a crucial role in identifying sites of gravitational collapse. Our genus statistics reveal that the HI distribution is predominantly sponge-like at intermediate column densities, transitioning to a more meatball-like topology at higher densities. Comparison with hydrodynamic simulations indicates that the observed topological features are consistent with supersonic turbulence driven by stellar feedback and galactic shear.

text: GRB 060614 is a remarkable GRB observed by Swift with puzzling properties,which challenge current progenitor models. The lack of any bright SN down tovery strict limits and the vanishing spectral lags are typical of short GRBs,strikingly at odds with the long (102s) duration of this event. Here we presentspectral and temporal analysis of the Swift observations. We show that theburst presents standard optical, UV and X-ray afterglows. An achromatic breakis observed simultaneously in optical and X-rays, at a time consistent with thebreak in the R-band light curve measured by the VLT. The achromatic behaviourand the consistent post-break decay slopes make GRB 060614 one of the bestexamples of a jet break for a Swift burst. The optical, UV and X-rays afterglowlight curves have also an earlier break at ~30 ks. In the optical, there isstrong spectral evolution around this break, suggesting the passage of a breakfrequency through the optical/UV band. The very blue spectrum at early timesand the trend in the light curves (rising at low frequencies, and decaying athigher energies) suggest this may be the injection frequency. The early X-raylight curve is well interpreted as the X-ray counterpart of the burst extendedemission. Spectral analysis of BAT/XRT data in the 80s overlap time show thatthe Ep of the burst has decreased to as low as 8keV at the beginning of the XRTobservation. The Ep continues to decrease through the XRT energy band and exitsit at about 500s after the trigger. The average Ep of the burst is likely < 24keV but larger than 8 keV. The initial peak observed by BAT is howeverdistinctly harder than the rest with Ep ~300 keV as measured by Konus Wind.Considering the time-averaged spectral properties, GRB 060614 is consistentwith the Eiso-Ep_rest, Egamma-Ep_rest, and Liso-Ep correlations.
label: human

text: We present detailed observations of GRB 060614 obtained with the Swift satellite, highlighting its unique properties that distinguish it from typical gamma-ray bursts (GRBs). The prompt emission exhibited a long duration but lacked an associated supernova, challenging the conventional classification of GRBs into long and short categories. Our analysis reveals the burst’s temporal and spectral characteristics during the prompt phase that resemble those of long-duration GRBs. However, the absence of a bright supernova signature suggests a different progenitor or emission mechanism at play. The X-ray afterglow of GRB 060614 was monitored extensively and displayed a smooth, well-behaved decay consistent with standard afterglow models. We detect no significant flares or unusual variability in the afterglow emission, supporting a stable external shock scenario. Multi-wavelength observations across optical and X-ray bands further reinforce the typical nature of the afterglow despite the prompt phase anomaly. Spectral energy distribution fitting indicates that the afterglow is dominated by synchrotron emission from electrons accelerated in an external forward shock. We discuss potential progenitor scenarios, including a compact object merger with extended emission or a failed supernova. The lack of a supernova detection down to deep limits disfavors a conventional massive star collapse origin. GRB 060614 thus challenges the neat division between long and short GRBs, suggesting a more complex classification scheme. Our findings contribute to the growing evidence that the GRB population is more heterogeneous than previously thought. This study highlights the importance of rapid follow-up observations to uncover the diverse nature of GRBs. We conclude that GRB 060614 represents a new class of bursts that bridge the gap between traditional long and short GRBs, with implications for progenitor models and the physics of relativistic jets.
label: llm

text: Many features of dimensional reduction schemes are determined by the breakingof higher dimensional general covariance associated with the selection of aparticular subset of coordinates. By investigating residual covariance weintroduce lower dimensional tensors --generalizing to one side Kaluza-Kleingauge fields and to the other side extrinsic curvature and torsion of embeddedspaces-- fully characterizing the geometry of dimensional reduction. We obtaingeneral formulas for the reduction of the main tensors and operators ofRiemannian geometry. In particular, we provide what is probably the maximalpossible generalization of Gauss, Codazzi and Ricci equations and various otherstandard formulas in Kaluza-Klein and embedded spacetimes theories. Aftergeneral covariance breaking, part of the residual covariance is perceived byeffective lower dimensional observers as an infinite dimensional gauge group.This reduces to finite dimensions in Kaluza-Klein and other few remarkablebackgrounds, all characterized by the vanishing of appropriate lowerdimensional tensors.

text: This article investigates the universal characteristics arising in dimensional reduction schemes that result from the explicit breaking of general covariance in higher-dimensional theories. By systematically analyzing various reduction approaches, we identify common structural features that persist regardless of the specific compactification or truncation method employed. Through this lens, we elucidate how the breakdown of full diffeomorphism invariance constrains effective lower-dimensional dynamics and influences the emergence of residual gauge symmetries. Our findings offer a unified framework that generalizes and connects several known dimensional reduction mechanisms, providing deeper insight into their geometric and physical underpinnings. These results have potential implications for the consistent formulation of effective field theories derived from higher-dimensional gravitational models.
label: llm

text: Recent studies of the near-infrared (NIR) properties of dwarf irregulargalaxies (dIs) and blue compact dwarfs (BCDs) have provided improved estimatesfor the NIR luminosity of old stellar populations in these galaxies. These canbe used to derive gas fractions, and thereby to evaluate how BCDs have evolvedwith respect to dIs. Oxygen abundances have been derived for four BCDs in theVirgo Cluster from a run at Gemini-North in 2003. Combining these newabundances with published values, we study the correlations among themetallicity, Ks luminosity, gas mass, baryonic mass, and gas fraction. Withinerrors, the two types of dwarfs appear to share a common relation between theoxygen abundance and the luminosity in Ks. The correlation between metallicityand the gas fraction is the same for BCDs as for dIs, indicating that BCDevolution has been similar to dIs. Since dIs appear to have evolved as isolatedsystems, the BCD bursts are unlikely to be a consequence of gas infall ormerging.

text: Star forming dwarf galaxies offer a unique laboratory for studying chemical evolution in low-mass cosmic environments. This article presents a comprehensive analysis of the chemical properties observed in a representative sample of these galaxies. Using spectroscopic data from ground- and space-based telescopes, we measure elemental abundances including oxygen, nitrogen, and iron. Our findings reveal that star forming dwarfs exhibit significantly lower metallicities compared to larger galaxies, consistent with their reduced star formation histories and gas inflow/outflow processes. We also examine the correlation between chemical enrichment and galactic parameters such as stellar mass and star formation rate. The results support theoretical models where episodic star formation and feedback regulate the chemical evolution in these small systems. Finally, implications for understanding galaxy formation and the role of dwarf galaxies in cosmic metal enrichment are discussed.
label: llm

text: We explore the main physical processes which potentially affect thetopological signal in the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) for a range oftoroidal universes. We consider specifically reionisation, the integratedSachs-Wolfe (ISW) effect, the size of the causal horizon, topological defectsand primordial gravitational waves. We use three estimators: the informationcontent, the S/N statistic and the Bayesian evidence. While reionisation hasnearly no effect on the estimators, we show that taking into account the ISWstrongly decreases our ability to detect the topological signal. We also studythe impact of varying the relevant cosmological parameters within the 2 sigmaranges allowed by present data. We find that only Omega_Lambda, whichinfluences both ISW and the size of the causal horizon, significantly altersthe detection for all three estimators considered here.

text: This article investigates the observational signatures and theoretical frameworks associated with detecting non-trivial topologies in cosmological models. We analyze how distinct topological features of the universe, beyond simple connectedness, could imprint measurable patterns on cosmic microwave background radiation and large-scale structure surveys. By employing both analytic methods and numerical simulations, we assess the sensitivity of current and future observational techniques to detect these subtle signals. Our results suggest that certain compact topologies produce identifiable correlations, though their detectability strongly depends on the scale and geometry of the universe. We also discuss the implications of our findings for cosmological parameter estimation and the constraints they impose on viable topological models. Ultimately, this work contributes to a deeper understanding of how global spatial properties might be inferred from local observational data.
label: llm

text: We report on a spectroscopic determination of the atmospheric parameters andchemical abundance of the parent star of the recently discovered transitingplanet {TrES-2}. A detailed LTE analysis of a set of \ion{Fe}{1} and\ion{Fe}{2} lines from our Keck spectra yields $T_\mathrm{eff} = 5850\pm 50$ K,$\log g = 4.4\pm 0.1$, and [Fe/H] $= -0.15\pm 0.10$. Several independent checks(e.g., additional spectroscopy, line-depth ratios) confirm the reliability ofour spectroscopic $T_\mathrm{eff}$ estimate. The mass and radius of the star,needed to determine the properties of the planet, are traditionally inferred bycomparison with stellar evolution models using $T_\mathrm{eff}$ and somemeasure of the stellar luminosity, such as the spectroscopic surface gravity(when a trigonometric parallax is unavailable, as in this case). We apply herea new method in which we use instead of $\log g$ the normalized separation$a/R_\star$ (related to the stellar density), which can be determined directlyfrom the light curves of transiting planets with much greater precision. Withthe $a/R_\star$ value from the light curve analysis of Holman et al.\citeyearpar{holman07b} and our $T_\mathrm{eff}$ estimate we obtain $M_\star =0.980\pm0.062 M_\odot$ and $R_\star = 1.000_{-0.033}^{+0.036} R_\odot$, and anevolutionary age of $5.1^{+2.7}_{-2.3}$ Gyr, in good agreement with otherconstraints based on the strength of the emission in the \ion{Ca}{2} H & K linecores, the Lithium abundance, and rotation. The new stellar parameters yieldimproved values for the planetary mass and radius of $M_p = 1.198 \pm 0.053M_\mathrm{Jup}$ and $R_p = 1.220^{+0.045}_{-0.042} R_\mathrm{Jup}$, confirmingthat {TrES-2} is the most massive among the currently known nearby ($d\lesssim300$ pc) transiting hot Jupiters. text: This study presents refined determinations of the stellar and planetary parameters for the transiting exoplanet system TrES-2, aiming to improve the precision and accuracy of its fundamental characteristics. We combined high-quality photometric transit data with updated stellar atmospheric models and spectroscopic measurements to achieve a comprehensive analysis. By employing state-of-the-art modeling techniques, including improved limb-darkening coefficients and rigorous error estimation, we obtained tighter constraints on the host star’s radius, mass, and effective temperature. These enhancements directly translated into more precise measurements of the radius, mass, and density of TrES-2b, a hot Jupiter known for its unusually dark atmosphere. Our results indicate a slight revision in planetary radius and density compared to previous studies, with implications for the planet’s internal structure and atmospheric composition. We also discuss the impact of stellar parameter uncertainties on the derived planetary characteristics and emphasize the importance of multi-disciplinary approaches to characterizing exoplanet systems. Finally, this work underscores how improved stellar characterizations can reduce systematic errors and biases in exoplanet research, which is critical for interpreting population-level trends. The methods and findings presented here provide a valuable framework for future investigations of transiting exoplanets around Sun-like stars.
label: llm

text: We give an operator theoretic approach to the constructions ofmultiresolutions as they are used in a number of basis constructions withwavelets, and in Hilbert spaces on fractals. Our approach starts with thefollowing version of the classical Baumslag-Solitar relations $u t = t^2 u$where $t$ is a unitary operator in a Hilbert space $\mathcal H$ and $u$ is anisometry in $\mathcal H$. There are isometric dilations of this system into abigger Hilbert space, relevant for wavelets. For a variety of carefullyselected dilations, the ``bigger'' Hilbert space may be $L^2(\br)$, and thedilated operators may be the unitary operators which define a dyadic waveletmultiresolutions of $L^2(\br)$ with the subspace $\mathcal H$ serving as thecorresponding resolution subspace. That is, the initialized resolution which isgenerated by the wavelet scaling function(s). In the dilated Hilbert space, theBaumslag-Solitar relations then take the more familiar form $u t u^{-1} = t^2$.  We offer an operator theoretic framework including the standard construction;and we show how the representations of certain discrete semidirect groupproducts serve to classify the possibilities. For this we analyze and compareseveral types of unitary representations of these semidirect products: theinduced representations in Mackey's theory, the wavelet representations on$L^2(\br)$, the irreducible representation on the dual, the finite dimensionalrepresentations, and the the regular representation.
label: human

text: This article investigates the representation theory of Baumslag-Solitar groups through the lens of duality principles. By developing a novel duality framework, we elucidate the interplay between these groups and their associated operator algebras. The approach leverages categorical dualities to construct and classify unitary representations, providing a deeper understanding of their structure. We apply this dual perspective to both discrete and continuous representation spaces, revealing new connections with harmonic analysis and geometric group theory. Key results include explicit characterizations of irreducible representations and insights into their decomposition behavior. Furthermore, the duality approach facilitates the analysis of induced representations and the exploration of rigidity phenomena within Baumslag-Solitar groups. Our findings contribute to the broader field by offering a unified approach to representations that extends beyond classical methods. This work opens avenues for further research into dualities in non-abelian and solvable group representations.
label: llm

text: The "power of choice" has been shown to radically alter the behavior of anumber of randomized algorithms. Here we explore the effects of choice onmodels of tree and network growth. In our models each new node has k randomlychosen contacts, where k > 1 is a constant. It then attaches to whichever oneof these contacts is most desirable in some sense, such as its distance fromthe root or its degree. Even when the new node has just two choices, i.e., whenk=2, the resulting network can be very different from a random graph or tree.For instance, if the new node attaches to the contact which is closest to theroot of the tree, the distribution of depths changes from Poisson to atraveling wave solution. If the new node attaches to the contact with thesmallest degree, the degree distribution is closer to uniform than in a randomgraph, so that with high probability there are no nodes in the network withdegree greater than O(log log N). Finally, if the new node attaches to thecontact with the largest degree, we find that the degree distribution is apower law with exponent -1 up to degrees roughly equal to k, with anexponential cutoff beyond that; thus, in this case, we need k >> 1 to see apower law over a wide range of degrees.
label: human

text: The dynamics of network growth are profoundly influenced by the mechanisms through which nodes establish connections. This study explores the role of choice in shaping network structures, emphasizing how selective attachment impacts the emergence of hubs and the overall topology. By introducing choice-based models, we demonstrate that agents exercising limited options can significantly alter the degree distribution compared to purely random or preferential attachment processes. Our analysis reveals that the power of choice enhances the likelihood of forming highly connected nodes, thereby accelerating the development of scale-free characteristics. We also investigate the implications of choice on network resilience and information diffusion, highlighting its potential to both reinforce and diversify connectivity patterns. Through a combination of theoretical modeling and numerical simulations, this work provides new insights into the fundamental principles governing complex networks. These findings underscore the importance of individual decision-making in the evolution of real-world networks across social, technological, and biological domains.
label: llm

text: In this paper we study random induced subgraphs of the binary $n$-cube,$Q_2^n$. This random graph is obtained by selecting each $Q_2^n$-vertex withindependent probability $\lambda_n$. Using a novel construction ofsubcomponents we study the largest component for$\lambda_n=\frac{1+\chi_n}{n}$, where $\epsilon\ge \chi_n\ge n^{-{1/3}+\delta}$, $\delta>0$. We prove that there exists a.s. a unique largestcomponent $C_n^{(1)}$. We furthermore show that $\chi_n=\epsilon$, $|C_n^{(1)}|\sim \alpha(\epsilon) \frac{1+\chi_n}{n} 2^n$ and for $o(1)=\chi_n\gen^{-{1/3}+\delta}$, $| C_n^{(1)}| \sim 2 \chi_n \frac{1+\chi_n}{n} 2^n$ holds.This improves the result of \cite{Bollobas:91} where constant $\chi_n=\chi$ isconsidered. In particular, in case of $\lambda_n=\frac{1+\epsilon} {n}$, ouranalysis implies that a.s. a unique giant component exists.
label: human

text: This paper investigates the emergence and size of large connected components within random induced subgraphs of the n-dimensional hypercube. By selecting vertices independently with a fixed probability, we analyze the phase transition behavior that governs the formation of giant components. Our results characterize threshold functions for the appearance of large components and provide asymptotic estimates for their expected size. We employ probabilistic combinatorial techniques and spectral methods to establish sharp bounds on the connectivity properties of these random subgraphs. Additionally, the work explores implications for theoretical computer science and network reliability models that are naturally represented by n-cubes. The findings deepen the understanding of structural properties inherent in high-dimensional discrete geometries under random vertex sampling.
label: llm

text: Aims. We probe the effect of turbulent diffusion on the chemistry at theinterface between a cold neutral medium (CNM) cloudlet and the warm neutralmedium (WNM). Methods. We perform moving grid, multifluid, 1D, hydrodynamicalsimulations with chemistry including thermal and chemical diffusion. Thediffusion coefficients are enhanced to account for turbulent diffusion. Wepost-process the steady-states of our simulations with a crude model ofradiative transfer to compute line profiles. Results. Turbulent diffusionspreads out the transition region between the CNM and the WNM. We find that theCNM slightly expands and heats up: its CH and H$_2$ content decreases due tothe lower density. It also brings H$_2$ into contactwith the warm gas with enhanced production of CH$^+$, H$_3^+$, OH and H$_2$O atthe interface. text: The chemistry of diffuse interstellar clouds is influenced by a complex interplay of physical processes, among which turbulent diffusion plays a critical role. In particular, the formation rates of molecules like CO are significantly modified in the presence of efficient turbulent diffusion. The interplay between diffusion and photodissociation processes also emerges as an important factor controlling molecular abundances. Regions with moderate turbulence show an optimized balance that promotes molecular complexity while preventing excessive dissociation. We find that the chemical timescales in diffuse clouds are shortened by turbulent transport, leading to non-equilibrium chemistry that differs markedly from static models.
