text: [ABRIDGED] We recently presented evidence of a connection between thebrightness profiles of nearby early-type galaxies and the properties of the AGNthey host. The radio loudness of the AGN appears to be univocally related tothe host's brightness profile: radio-loud nuclei are only hosted by ``core''galaxies while radio-quiet AGN are only found in ``power-law'' galaxies. Weextend our analysis here to a sample of 42 nearby (V < 7000 km/s) Seyfertgalaxies hosted by early-type galaxies. We used the available HST images tostudy their brightness profiles. Having excluded complex and highly nucleatedgalaxies, in the remaining 16 objects the brightness profiles can besuccessfully modeled with a Nuker law with a steep nuclear cusp characteristicof ``power-law'' galaxies (with logarithmic slope 0.51 - 1.07). This result iswhat is expected for these radio-quiet AGN based on our previous findings, thusextending the validity of the connection between brightness profile and radioloudness to AGN of a far higher luminosity. We explored the robustness of thisresult against a different choice of the analytic form for the brightnessprofiles, using a Sersic law. In no object could we find evidence of a centrallight deficit with respect to a pure Sersic model, the defining feature of``core'' galaxies in this modeling framework. We conclude that, regardless ofthe modeling strategy, the dichotomy of AGN radio loudness can be univocallyrelated to the host's brightness profile. Our general results can be re-phrasedas ``radio-loud nuclei are hosted by core galaxies, while radio-quiet AGN arefound in non-core galaxies''.
label: human

text: This study investigates the structural properties of early-type galaxies that host Seyfert nuclei, focusing on their brightness profiles to explore the relationship between the host galaxy and its active galactic nucleus (AGN). We analyze high-resolution imaging data to characterize the central luminosity distribution and identify distinct photometric components. Our sample comprises a well-defined set of early-type galaxies with confirmed Seyfert activity, allowing for a systematic comparison with inactive counterparts. We find that the inner brightness profiles frequently deviate from pure de Vaucouleurs profiles, displaying central light excesses interpreted as nuclear cusps or disks. These features suggest that the presence of an AGN is linked to specific central structural components within the host galaxy. Further, we investigate correlations between brightness profile parameters and AGN properties such as luminosity and type. Our results indicate that galaxies hosting Seyfert nuclei tend to have steeper central brightness gradients compared to inactive galaxies, implying a connection between the central stellar density and nuclear activity. This supports scenarios where central gas inflows and star formation contribute to both the buildup of central components and AGN fueling. We discuss the implications of these findings for models of galaxy evolution and AGN feedback mechanisms in early-type systems. Ultimately, this work highlights the importance of detailed photometric profiling to unravel the co-evolution of galaxies and their active nuclei.
label: llm

text: Let $(\cX, \rho)$ be a discrete metric space. We suppose that the group$\sZ^n$ acts freely on $X$ and that the number of orbits of $X$ with respect tothis action is finite. Then we call $X$ a $\sZ^n$-periodic discrete metricspace. We examine the Fredholm property and essential spectra of band-dominatedoperators on $l^p(X)$ where $X$ is a $\sZ^n$-periodic discrete metric space.Our approach is based on the theory of band-dominated operators on $\sZ^n$ andtheir limit operators.  In case $X$ is the set of vertices of a combinatorial graph, the graphstructure defines a Schr\"{o}dinger operator on $l^p(X)$ in a natural way. Weillustrate our approach by determining the essential spectra of Schr\"{o}dingeroperators with slowly oscillating potential both on zig-zag and on hexagonalgraphs, the latter being related to nano-structures.
label: human

text: This article investigates the essential spectra of difference operators defined on \(\mathbb{Z}^n\)-periodic graphs, extending classical spectral theory to a broad combinatorial and geometric setting. We develop a framework to characterize the essential spectrum by leveraging the periodicity and exploiting the underlying graph structure, which generalizes results known for periodic operators on lattices and manifolds. Using Floquet–Bloch decomposition techniques adapted to discrete graphs, we derive conditions under which the essential spectrum can be explicitly identified as the union of spectra of fiber operators. Our approach connects the spectral properties of the difference operators to the geometry and combinatorics of the periodic graph, providing insight into spectral gaps and band structure phenomena. Several examples illustrate how the theoretical results apply to well-known graph models and demonstrate the influence of graph topology on spectral.
label: llm

text: We consider the nonminimally coupled lambda phi^4 scalar field theory in deSitter space and construct the renormalization group improved renormalizedeffective theory at the one-loop level. Based on the corresponding quantumFriedmann equation and the scalar field equation of motion, we calculate thequantum radiative corrections to the scalar spectral index n_s, gravitationalwave spectral index n_g and the ratio r of tensor to scalar perturbations. Whencompared with the standard (tree-level) values, we find that the quantumcontributions are suppressed by lambda N^2 where N denotes the number ofe-foldings. Hence there is an N^2 enhancement with respect to the naiveexpectation, which is due to the infrared enhancement of scalar vacuumfluctuations characterising de Sitter space. Since observations constrainlambda to be very small lambda ~ 10^(-12) and N ~ 50-60, the quantumcorrections in this inflationary model are unobservably small.
label: human

text: This article investigates the impact of quantum radiative corrections on slow-roll inflationary models within the framework of effective field theory. By computing one-loop corrections to the inflaton potential, we analyze how quantum effects modify the dynamics of the slow-roll parameters, potentially leading to observable deviations in the inflationary power spectrum. Our results show that radiative corrections can introduce subtle but significant shifts in the inflationary trajectory, affecting predictions of scalar spectral indices and tensor-to-scalar ratios. We also discuss the renormalization group flow of the inflaton self-couplings and its implications for the stability and consistency of the inflationary scenario. This study provides a comprehensive quantitative assessment of quantum corrections, highlighting their importance in refining theoretical predictions for upcoming cosmological observations.
label: llm

text: Following the early Swift X-ray observations of the latest outburst of therecurrent nova RS Ophiuchi in February 2006 (Paper I), we present new 1Dhydrodynamical models of the system which take into account all three phases ofthe remnant evolution. The models suggest a novel way of modelling the systemby treating the outburst as a sudden increase then decrease in wind mass-lossrate and velocity. The differences between this wind model and previousPrimakoff-type simulations are described. A more complex structure, even in 1D,is revealed through the presence of both forward and reverse shocks, with aseparating contact discontinuity. The effects of radiative cooling areinvestigated and key outburst parameters such as mass-loss rate, ejectavelocity and mass are varied. The shock velocities as a function of time arecompared to the ones derived in Paper I. We show how the manner in which thematter is ejected controls the evolution of the shock and that for awell-cooled remnant, the shock deceleration rate depends on the amount ofenergy that is radiated away.
label: human

text: We present one-dimensional hydrodynamical simulations aimed at modeling the wind-driven shocks observed during the 2006 outburst of the recurrent nova RS Ophiuchi. Using parameters derived from Swift X-ray observations, we reproduce the temporal evolution of the shock velocity and temperature profiles in the nova ejecta interacting with the red giant wind. Our models explore a range of mass loss rates and wind velocities to constrain the physical conditions driving the observed emission. The simulations successfully capture the development of forward and reverse shocks, as well as the cooling processes shaping the X-ray light curve. We find that the shock dynamics are sensitive to the density structure of the ambient medium, supporting a scenario of a dense circumstellar environment shaped by the red giant companion. Comparison with observational data suggests that energy injection from the nova wind occurs over an extended period, which influences the shock strength and emission characteristics. These results provide a coherent framework for interpreting the complex shock interactions in RS Ophiuchi and offer insights applicable to other recurrent nova systems.
label: llm

text: Given a field $F$, an \'etale extension $L/F$ and an Azumaya algebra $A/L$,one knows that there are extensions $E/F$ such that $A \otimes_F E$ is a splitalgebra over $L \otimes_F E$. In this paper we bound the degree of a minimalsplitting field of this type from above and show that our bound is sharp incertain situations, even in the case where $L/F$ is a split extension. Thisgives in particular a number of generalizations of the classical fact that whenthe tensor product of two quaternion algebras is not a division algebra, thetwo quaternion algebras must share a common quadratic splitting field.  In another direction, our constructions combined with results of Karpenkoalso show that for any odd prime number $p$, the generic algebra of index$p^n$, and exponent $p$ cannot be expressed nontrivially as the corestrictionof an algebra over any extension field if $n < p^2$.
label: human

text: This article investigates the construction and properties of corestriction (or transfer) functors applied to central simple algebras over field extensions. We develop a detailed analysis of how corestrictions interact with splitting fields and provide criteria under which splitting behavior is preserved or reflected. Our results elucidate the relationship between the splitting fields of an algebra and those of its corestriction, offering new insights into the structure of division algebras via field arithmetic. These findings contribute to a deeper understanding of the interplay between algebraic operations and field extensions in the theory of central simple algebras.
label: llm

text: In the conventional formulation of N=1 supersymmetry, a vector multiplet issupposed to be in the adjoint representation of a given gauge group. We presenta new formulation with a vector multiplet in the non-adjoint representation ofSO(N) gauge group. Our basic algebra is [ T^I, T^J ] = f^{I J K} T^K, [ T^I,U^i ] = - (T^I)^{i j} U^j, [ U^i, U^j ] = - (T^I)^{i j} T^I, where T^I are thegenerators of SO(N), while U^i are the new 'generators' in certain non-adjointreal representation R of SO(N). We use here the word `generator' in the broadersense of the word. Such a representation can be any real representation ofSO(N) with the positive definite metric, satisfying (T^I)^{i j} = - (T^I)^{j i}and (T^I)^{[ i j |} (T^I)^{| k ] l} \equiv 0. The first non-trivial examplesare the spinorial 8_S and conjugate spinorial 8_C representations of SO(8)consistent with supersymmetry. We further couple the system to chiralmultiplets, and show that a Higgs mechanism can give positive definite (mass)^2to the new gauge fields for U^i. We show an analogous system working with N=1supersymmetry in 10D, and thereby N=4 system in 4D interacting with extramultiplets in the representation R. We also perform superspace reformulation asan independent confirmation.
label: human

text: In this paper, we investigate the construction of supersymmetric vector multiplets that transform in non-adjoint representations of the orthogonal group SO(N). Unlike conventional formulations where vector multiplets reside in the adjoint representation, our approach extends the framework to accommodate alternative representation spaces. We develop a consistent set of transformation rules and gauge-covariant derivatives compatible with supersymmetry, ensuring closure of the supersymmetry algebra off-shell. The resulting models exhibit novel features, including modified gauge interactions and new auxiliary fields necessary for off-shell closure. We perform an explicit construction for selected non-adjoint representations and analyze the implications for supersymmetric gauge theories. Our results highlight potential applications in model building beyond conventional gauge theories, possibly impacting string-inspired or higher-dimensional scenarios. Furthermore, we discuss the constraints and conditions under which these multiplets can be embedded into larger supersymmetric frameworks. This work opens avenues for exploring richer representation structures within supersymmetric field theories and their phenomenological consequences.
label: llm

text: ASTROD is a relativity mission concept encompassing multi-purposes. One ofits main purposes is to detect gravitational waves sensitive to low-frequencyband similar to LISA, but shifted to lower frequencies. In this aspect, ASTRODwould complement LISA in probing the Universe and study strong-field black holephysics. Since ASTROD will be after LISA, in the Cosmic Vision time-frame2015-2025, a ten-fold improvement over LISA accelerometer noise goal would bepossible, allowing us to test relativistic gravity to 1 ppb and improve thegravitational-wave sensitivity. In this paper, we address to this possibleimprovement, especially in the frequency range below 0.1 mHz. We look intopossible thermal noise improvement, magnetic noise improvement, spuriousdischarging noise improvement and local gravitational noise improvement. Wediscuss various possibilities of lower-frequency gravitational-wave responsesand their significance to potential astrophysical sources.
label: human

text: The Astrodynamical Space Test of Relativity using Optical Devices (ASTROD) mission concept aims to detect low-frequency gravitational waves with unprecedented sensitivity. This study presents a detailed analysis of the ASTROD instrument’s sensitivity in the frequency range below 0.1 Hz, where terrestrial detectors face significant limitations due to seismic and environmental noise. We model the key noise sources affecting the measurement, including laser frequency noise, acceleration noise, and shot noise, and incorporate them into a comprehensive sensitivity curve. The simulation results demonstrate that ASTROD can achieve strain sensitivities several orders of magnitude better than existing space-based detectors in the millihertz to sub-millihertz band. Such sensitivity enhancements open new opportunities for observing gravitational waves from massive black hole binaries, galactic binaries, and stochastic backgrounds. We also discuss the mission design considerations that enable this low-frequency performance, including spacecraft configuration and orbit selection.
label: llm

text: Massive merging black holes will be the primary sources of powerfulgravitational waves at low frequency, and will permit to test generalrelativity with candidate galaxies close to a binary black hole merger. In thispaper we identify the typical mass ratio of the two black holes but then showthat the distance when gravitational radiation becomes the dominant dissipativeeffect (over dynamical friction) does not depend on the mass ratio. However thedynamical evolution in the gravitational wave emission regime does. For thetypical range of mass ratios the final stage of the merger is preceded by arapid precession and a subsequent spin-flip of the main black hole. Thisalready occurs in the inspiral phase, therefore can be described analyticallyby post-Newtonian techniques. We then identify the radio galaxies with asuper-disk as those in which the rapidly precessing jet produces effectively apowerful wind, entraining the environmental gas to produce the appearance of athick disk. These specific galaxies are thus candidates for a merger of twoblack holes to happen in the astronomically near future.
label: human

text: The spin-flip phenomenon in supermassive black hole binary mergers represents a critical process in understanding the evolution of black hole spin orientations during galaxy coalescence. In this study, we analyze the mechanisms driving the abrupt reorientation of spin axes as two supermassive black holes approach final coalescence. Utilizing a combination of numerical relativity simulations and semi-analytical modeling, we explore how gravitational wave emission and orbital angular momentum interplay influence spin dynamics. Our results indicate that spin flips occur predominantly during the late inspiral and merger phases, with the magnitude of the reorientation dependent on the initial spin magnitudes and orbital configurations. We also investigate the astrophysical consequences of spin flips, particularly their impact on jet directions and gravitational recoil velocities. These findings illuminate the complex interplay between binary black hole dynamics and their observable signatures in active galactic nuclei. This work provides new insights into the final spin states of merged supermassive black holes, with implications for galaxy evolution and gravitational wave astrophysics.
label: llm

text: Recent three-dimensional radiative hydrodynamics simulations ofprotoplanetary disks report disparate disk behaviors, and these differencesinvolve the importance of convection to disk cooling, the dependence of diskcooling on metallicity, and the stability of disks against fragmentation andclump formation. To guarantee trustworthy results, a radiative physicsalgorithm must demonstrate the capability to handle both the high and lowoptical depth regimes. We develop a test suite that can be used to demonstratean algorithm's ability to relax to known analytic flux and temperaturedistributions, to follow a contracting slab, and to inhibit or permitconvection appropriately. We then show that the radiative algorithm employed byMeji\'a (2004) and Boley et al. (2006) and the algorithm employed by Cai et al.(2006) and Cai et al. (2007, in prep.) pass these tests with reasonableaccuracy. In addition, we discuss a new algorithm that couples flux-limiteddiffusion with vertical rays, we apply the test suite, and we discuss theresults of evolving the Boley et al. (2006) disk with this new routine.Although the outcome is significantly different in detail with the newalgorithm, we obtain the same qualitative answers. Our disk does not cool fastdue to convection, and it is stable to fragmentation. We find an effective$\alpha\approx 10^{-2}$. In addition, transport is dominated by low-ordermodes.
label: human

text: This study introduces a comprehensive framework for evaluating disk stability simulations through three-dimensional radiative hydrodynamics modeling. We propose a standardized testing protocol designed to benchmark numerical methods and physical assumptions applied in disk evolution studies. The emphasis is placed on capturing coupled radiation transport and hydrodynamic instabilities within protoplanetary and accretion disks. By incorporating an advanced treatment of radiation feedback, our approach aims to improve the fidelity of disk temperature and density profiles over time. The methodology employs high-resolution simulations that resolve critical scale heights and cooling timescales, enabling a robust analysis of fragmentation criteria. We validate our testing standard using a series of controlled numerical experiments comparing different radiative transfer approximations and hydrodynamic solvers. New results demonstrate that neglecting multidimensional radiative effects can lead to significant inaccuracies in predicted disk stability thresholds. Our findings reveal a strong dependence of fragmentation onset on opacity and irradiation parameters, highlighting the importance of radiative feedback in disk evolution. Furthermore, we identify key numerical challenges and suggest best practices for mitigating artifacts such as artificial fragmentation. The proposed standard provides a reproducible baseline to facilitate more consistent comparisons across different simulation platforms.
label: llm

text: In this paper, the study of the gravitational collapse of cylindricallydistributed two perfect fluid system has been carried out. It is assumed thatthe collapsing speeds of the two fluids are very large. We explore thiscondition by using the high-speed approximation scheme. There arise two cases,i.e., bounded and vanishing of the ratios of the pressures with densities oftwo fluids given by $c_s, d_s$. It is shown that the high-speed approximationscheme breaks down by non-zero pressures $p_1, p_2$ when $c_s, d_s$ are boundedbelow by some positive constants. The failure of the high-speed approximationscheme at some particular time of the gravitational collapse suggests theuncertainity on the evolution at and after this time. In the bounded case, thenaked singularity formation seems to be impossible for the cylindrical twoperfect fluids. For the vanishing case, if a linear equation of state is used,the high-speed collapse does not break down by the effects of the pressures andconsequently a naked singularity forms. This work provides the generalisationof the results already given by Nakao and Morisawa [1] for the perfect fluid.
label: human

text: This study investigates the dynamical behavior of the high-speed cylindrical collapse involving two interacting perfect fluids. We formulate the governing equations within the framework of general relativity, assuming cylindrical symmetry and ideal fluid conditions for both components. The analysis focuses on the nonlinear evolution of the collapse under initial configurations characterized by distinct fluid properties. Numerical simulations are employed to explore scenarios where the collapse velocity approaches relativistic speeds, highlighting key aspects of the coupled fluid dynamics. Our results reveal the emergence of complex shock structures and energy exchange mechanisms between the two fluids during the implosion. The interplay between fluid equations of state significantly influences the collapse outcomes, including singularity formation and matter distribution. We further discuss the conditions under which the collapse leads to horizon formation and potential gravitational wave emission. This work contributes to a deeper understanding of multi-fluid gravitational collapse phenomena in astrophysical and cosmological contexts.
label: llm

text: Based on the fact that for an isotropic material model the elastic predictorand the projected stress tensors have the same eigenvectors, it is shown thatthe scalar damage can be obtained directly from the projection algorithm. Thiseliminates the difficulty of a proper definition of equivalent strain whichserves as a driving force for evolution of damage in concrete. Moreover, ifeigenvectors are known it is not more nec-essary to use invariants of thestress tensor for the formulation of loading surface. In the present model theloading surface is represented in the polynomial form. This has two advantages:(i) it automatically fulfils C1 continuity and (ii) plane stress formulation isachieved by simply setting the third stress to zero. The perform-ance of themodel is illustrated on example of a mixed-mode fracture of concrete. It isshown that for the pre-sent example the model prediction strongly depends onthe choice of the stress degradation law.
label: human

text: This article presents a novel scalar damage model for concrete that eliminates the need for an explicit damage evolution law. The proposed approach introduces a damage variable implicitly linked to the material’s stress-strain response, simplifying the constitutive description while capturing key nonlinear behaviors. By integrating inherent material degradation mechanisms within the scalar damage formulation, the model offers enhanced robustness and computational efficiency. Validation against experimental data demonstrates its capability to accurately predict the onset and progression of damage under various loading conditions. Comparative analysis with traditional damage models highlights improved numerical stability and reduced calibration complexity. The model’s adaptability makes it suitable for simulating concrete behavior in structural analysis and design applications. Overall, this work contributes a practical and reliable tool for damage assessment in concrete materials without relying on explicitly defined damage evolution laws.
label: llm

text: We study a lattice realization of a Luttinger liquid interacting with a bathof quantum spins in terms of an antiferromagnetic S=1/2 Heisenberg chain, whereeach spin is also coupled to a \sigma=1/2 Kondo spin degree of freedom. Thismodel describes the low-energy spin dynamics in quasi one dimensionalmaterials, where the electronic spins of the magnetic ions interact with thoseof impurities, nuclei and possibly other spin species present in theirenvironment. For large ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic Kondo interaction J'there are two phases corresponding to an effective spin-1 Heisenberg chain anda dimerised spin-1/2 ladder, respectively. For weak Kondo interaction weestablish that the Kondo interaction drives the system to a strong couplingregime. This suggests that J'=0 is the only critical point in the system.
label: human

text: This work investigates the interplay between a one-dimensional Luttinger liquid and a quantum spin bath within the framework of the Kondo necklace model. By employing the flow equation method, we derive a set of renormalization group equations that capture the coupling dynamics and emergent correlations in the system. Our analysis reveals how the Kondo interaction induces non-trivial renormalization of the Luttinger parameters, leading to distinct phases characterized by spin entanglement and charge transport properties. We identify critical regimes where the quantum spin bath strongly influences the low-energy behavior, resulting in crossover phenomena between Luttinger liquid and Kondo screened phases. These findings offer new insights into correlated electron systems and present a versatile approach for studying similar quantum impurity problems.
label: llm

text: We present the projected velocity dispersion profile for the remote(d=233kpc) Galactic dwarf spheroidal (dSph) galaxy Leo II, based on 171discrete stellar radial velocities that were obtained from medium-resolutionspectroscopy using the FLAMES/GIRAFFE spectrograph at the European SouthernObservatory, Chile. The dispersion profile of those stars with good membershipprobabilities is essentially flat with an amplitude of 6.6+-0.7 km/s over thefull radial extent of our data, which probe to the stellar boundary of thisgalaxy. We find no evidence of any significant apparent rotation or velocityasymmetry which suggests that tidal effects cannot be invoked to explain LeoII's properties. From basic mass modeling, employing Jeans' equation, we derivea mass out to the limiting radius of (2.7+-0.5) 10^7 Msun and a global mass tolight ratio of 27-45 in solar units, depending on the adopted total luminosity.A cored halo profile and a mild amount of tangential velocity anisotropy isfound to account well for Leo II's observed kinematics, although we cannotexclude the possibility of a cusped halo with radially varying velocityanisotropy. All in all, this galaxy exhibits dark matter properties whichappear to be concordant with the other dSph satellites of the Milky Way, namelya halo mass profile which is consistent with a central core and a total masswhich is similar to the common mass scale seen in other dSphs.
label: human

text: We present a detailed analysis of the stellar kinematics of the Leo II dwarf spheroidal galaxy, one of the most remote satellites of the Milky Way. Using new spectroscopic data from large-aperture telescopes, we measure line-of-sight velocities for a sample of member stars to probe the galaxy’s internal dynamics. Our results reveal a velocity dispersion profile consistent with a dark matter dominated system, supporting the presence of an extended dark matter halo. We discuss the implications of these findings for models of dwarf galaxy formation and the role of environmental effects in shaping their evolution. This study adds a crucial data point to the growing body of evidence for the complex interplay between baryons and dark matter in low-mass galaxies.
label: llm

text: We discuss the impact of charged massive particle big bangnucleosynthesis(CBBN) to explore the nature of the reheating of the Universe inthe case that a new extremely long-lived charged massive particle(CHAMP)exists. If the mass of the CHAMP is within collider reach and it's lifetime islonger than $10^4$sec, the comparison between the CBBN prediction and observed$^6$Li abundances may indicate nonstandard reheating in the early Universewithout relying on details of the decay properties. Even if the CHAMP mass isoutside the reach of colliders, the cosmological considerations may provide anontrivial hint for the existence of such very heavy long-lived CHAMPs from thelate Universe if the daughter particles are the dominant component of thepresent dark matter. We consider a low reheating temperature model as anexample of the nonstandard reheating scenarios.
label: human

text: We investigate the role of extremely long-lived charged massive particles (CHAMPs) as a novel probe for the reheating phase following cosmic inflation. By analyzing the abundance and decay characteristics of CHAMPs, we establish constraints on the reheating temperature and its associated energy scale. Our results demonstrate that the presence of such particles can leave distinctive imprints on primordial matter distributions and cosmic microwave background observables. This approach offers a complementary pathway to traditional methods, enhancing our understanding of the universe’s thermal history during its earliest moments.
label: llm

text: A finite group $G$ is of central type (in the non-classical sense) if itadmits a non-degenerate cohomology class $[c]\in H^2(G,\C^*)$ ($G$ actstrivially on $\C^*$). Groups of central type play a fundamental role in theclassification of semisimple triangular complex Hopf algebras and can bedetermined by their representation theoretical properties.  Suppose that a finite group $Q$ acts on an abelian group $A$ so that thereexists a bijective 1-cocycle $\pi\in Z^1(Q,\ach)$, where$\ach=\rm{Hom}(A,\C^*)$ is endowed with the diagonal $Q$-action. Under thisassumption, Etingof and Gelaki gave an explicit formula for a non-degenerate2-cocycle in $Z^2(G,\C^*)$, where $G:=A\rtimes Q$. Hence, the semidirectproduct $G$ is of central type.  In this paper we present a more general correspondence between bijective andnon-degenerate cohomology classes. In particular, given a bijective class$[\pi]\in H^1(Q,\ach)$ as above, we construct non-degenerate classes$[c_{\pi}]\in H^2(G,\C^*)$ for certain extensions $1\to A\to G\to Q\to 1$ whichare not necessarily split. We thus strictly extend the above family of centraltype groups.
label: human

text: This article investigates the structural properties of groups of central type by examining the interplay between their cohomology classes and group extensions. We focus particularly on the characterization of non-degenerate 2-cocycles and their role in defining bijective cohomology classes that give rise to specific group algebra decompositions. Utilizing techniques from homological algebra and group theory, we establish criteria under which a cohomology class can be identified as both non-degenerate and bijective, thereby contributing to the understanding of projective representations of finite groups. The study further explores the connection between these cohomology classes and the classification of central type groups, highlighting new examples and counterexamples that challenge existing classifications. Our results demonstrate that the existence of a bijective, non-degenerate class significantly influences the structure and representation theory of the underlying group. We also discuss the implications of these findings for the construction of Hopf algebras and related algebraic structures. The methods developed herein provide a framework for future investigations into the cohomological aspects of group extensions and their applications in.
label: llm

text: We provide a grid of PHOENIX spectra of red giant and supergiant stars, thatextend through optical and near-IR wavelengths. For the first time, models arealso provided with modified surface abundances of C, N and O, as a step towardsaccounting for the changes known to occur due to convective dredge-up (and tobe enhanced in the case of rotation). The aims are (i) to assess how wellcurrent models reproduce observed spectra, (ii) to quantify the effects of theabundance changes on the spectra, and (iii) to determine how these changesaffect estimates of fundamental stellar parameters.  Observed giant star spectra can be fitted very well at solar metallicity downto about 3400K. Modified surface abundances are preferred in only a minority ofcases for luminosity class II, possibly indicating mixing in excess of standardfirst dredge-up.  Supergiant stars show a larger variety of near-IR spectra, and good fits arecurrently obtained for about one third of the observations only. Modifiedsurface abundances help reproducing strong CN bands, but do not suffice toresolve all the difficulties. The effect of the abundance changes on theestimated Teff depends on the wavelength range of observation and can amountseveral 100K. Reasons for the remaining discrepancies are discussed.
label: human

text: This study presents a comprehensive analysis of near-infrared (near-IR) spectral features of red supergiant and giant stars, focusing on models that incorporate both solar and mixing-induced surface abundance ratios. We employ detailed atmospheric models to simulate the spectral output in the near-IR region, aiming to improve our understanding of the physical and chemical properties influencing these evolved stars. Our models account for variations in surface abundances caused by internal mixing processes, which are known to modify the observed spectra compared to models assuming solar abundance patterns. By comparing synthetic spectra with observed near-IR data, we identify key diagnostic lines sensitive to changes in elemental abundances, such as those of carbon, nitrogen, and oxygen. The results highlight the significant impact of mixing-induced abundance alterations on spectral morphology, particularly affecting molecular band strengths and atomic line profiles. We discuss the implications of these findings for stellar evolution theories, especially concerning the late stages of massive star lifecycles. Additionally, our study provides refined spectral templates that can aid in the classification and analysis of red supergiants and giants in various stellar populations.
label: llm

text: We consider that the pre-inflation era is radiation-dominated, transitingsmoothly to the inflationary era. We work out in detail the dynamics ofinflaton fluctuations across the phase transition and the proper choices ofinitial vacuum states. It is found that this phase transition can suppresslong-wavelength quantum fluctuations of inflaton. This may attribute to thelarge-scale CMB anisotropy a lower power than predicted in the standard$\Lambda$CDM model. In constraining this transitional effect by WMAP anisotropydata, we use the WMAP best-fit scale-invariant $\Lambda$CDM model with thedensity power spectrum replaced by the one found in this work. We find that thetransition occurs at least about 10 e-folds before the comoving scalescomparable to our present horizon size cross the Hubble radius duringinflation.
label: human

text: This study investigates the influence of a pre-inflation radiation-dominated epoch on the anisotropy patterns observed in the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB). By incorporating a radiation-dominated phase prior to the onset of inflation, we analyze modifications to the primordial power spectrum and their subsequent impact on CMB temperature fluctuations. Using a combination of analytical approximations and numerical simulations, we compute the changes in the angular power spectrum, focusing on large-scale multipole moments. Our results indicate that the presence of a pre-inflation radiation era can introduce distinctive signatures, such as suppressed power at the lowest multipoles, potentially addressing certain anomalies observed in current CMB data. We discuss the implications of these findings for inflationary model building and propose observational tests that could distinguish between scenarios with and without this early radiation phase.
label: llm

text: P2P IPTV applications arise on the Internet and will be massively used in thefuture. It is expected that P2P IPTV will contribute to increase the overallInternet traffic. In this context, it is important to measure the impact of P2PIPTV on the networks and to characterize this traffic. Dur- ing the 2006 FIFAWorld Cup, we performed an extensive measurement campaign. We measured networktraffic generated by broadcasting soc- cer games by the most popular P2P IPTVapplications, namely PPLive, PPStream, SOPCast and TVAnts. From the collecteddata, we charac- terized the P2P IPTV traffic structure at different timescales by using wavelet based transform method. To the best of our knowledge,this is the first work, which presents a complete multiscale analysis of theP2P IPTV traffic. Our results show that the scaling properties of the TCPtraffic present periodic behavior whereas the UDP traffic is stationary andlead to long- range depedency characteristics. For all the applications, thedownload traffic has different characteristics than the upload traffic. Thesignaling traffic has a significant impact on the download traffic but it hasnegligible impact on the upload. Both sides of the traffic and its granularityhas to be taken into account to design accurate P2P IPTV traffic models.
label: human

text: This study presents a comprehensive characterization of peer-to-peer (P2P) IPTV traffic, focusing on its scaling properties and temporal behavior. P2P IPTV has become a prominent approach for live video streaming, leveraging distributed resources to alleviate server bottlenecks. Understanding the traffic dynamics is essential for network management and performance optimization. We collected extensive traffic traces from multiple P2P IPTV applications under real-world conditions. Our analysis applies scaling techniques including multifractal and long-range dependence assessments to capture traffic variability over multiple time scales. Results reveal significant burstiness and self-similarity in traffic patterns, which traditional Poisson-based models fail to capture accurately. The presence of heavy-tailed distributions indicates that traffic exhibits long memory effects, influencing buffer management and congestion control strategies. Furthermore, we identify distinct phases in stream delivery corresponding to user behavior and network conditions. These findings provide valuable insights for designing scalable and robust P2P IPTV systems. We discuss implications for traffic engineering, such as adaptive resource allocation policies that consider scaling characteristics. Finally, this work lays a foundation for future research on modeling and simulation of P2P IPTV traffic under diverse deployment scenarios.
label: llm

text: We analyse and compare the complexity of several algorithms for computingmodular polynomials. We show that an algorithm relying on floating pointevaluation of modular functions and on interpolation, which has received littleattention in the literature, has a complexity that is essentially (up tologarithmic factors) linear in the size of the computed polynomials. Inparticular, it obtains the classical modular polynomials $\Phi_\ell$ of primelevel $\ell$ in time O (\ell^3 \log^4 \ell \log \log \ell). Besides treatingmodular polynomials for $\Gamma^0 (\ell)$, which are an important ingredient inmany algorithms dealing with isogenies of elliptic curves, the algorithm iseasily adapted to more general situations. Composite levels are handled just aseasily as prime levels, as well as polynomials between a modular function andits transform of prime level, such as the Schl\"afli polynomials and theirgeneralisations. Our distributed implementation of the algorithm confirms thetheoretical analysis by computing modular equations of record level around10000 in less than two weeks on ten processors.
label: human

text: Modular polynomials play a central role in computational number theory and cryptography, particularly in algorithms related to elliptic curves and class field theory. Efficient computation of these polynomials is essential due to their large size and complexity. In this paper, we present new algorithms that compute modular polynomials in quasi-linear time with respect to their output size. Our approach leverages fast multiplication techniques and novel interpolation methods to significantly reduce the computational overhead compared to classical approaches. We provide rigorous complexity analyses demonstrating the improved asymptotic behavior of our algorithms. Extensive experiments confirm that our methods outperform existing implementations, opening new avenues for practical applications that rely on modular polynomials.
label: llm

text: How do blogs cite and influence each other? How do such links evolve? Doesthe popularity of old blog posts drop exponentially with time? These are someof the questions that we address in this work. Our goal is to build a modelthat generates realistic cascades, so that it can help us with link predictionand outlier detection.  Blogs (weblogs) have become an important medium of information because oftheir timely publication, ease of use, and wide availability. In fact, theyoften make headlines, by discussing and discovering evidence about politicalevents and facts. Often blogs link to one another, creating a publiclyavailable record of how information and influence spreads through an underlyingsocial network. Aggregating links from several blog posts creates a directedgraph which we analyze to discover the patterns of information propagation inblogspace, and thereby understand the underlying social network. Not only areblogs interesting on their own merit, but our analysis also sheds light on howrumors, viruses, and ideas propagate over social and computer networks.  Here we report some surprising findings of the blog linking and informationpropagation structure, after we analyzed one of the largest available datasets,with 45,000 blogs and ~ 2.2 million blog-postings. Our analysis also shedslight on how rumors, viruses, and ideas propagate over social and computernetworks. We also present a simple model that mimics the spread of informationon the blogosphere, and produces information cascades very similar to thosefound in real life.
label: human

text: The study of information diffusion through online social networks has become increasingly significant in understanding collective behavior. This paper investigates cascading behavior within large-scale blog graphs, focusing on how ideas and content propagate across interconnected blogging communities. We construct an extensive blog network dataset, capturing hyperlinks and temporal posting information to model the dynamics of information flow. Our methodology employs graph-theoretic measures combined with cascade detection algorithms to identify and characterize patterns of content propagation. Results indicate that cascades exhibit heavy-tailed size distributions, suggesting that while most cascades remain small, a few achieve widespread reach. We observe that structural properties of the underlying blog graph, such as node centrality and clustering coefficients, heavily influence cascade formation and growth. Additionally, temporal analysis reveals that cascades often follow bursty activity patterns, influenced by both endogenous and exogenous factors. Comparative evaluation against random and null models confirms the significance of network topology in facilitating cascades. The findings highlight the role of influential blogs as super-spreaders, accelerating diffusion across modular communities. We discuss the implications of cascading behavior for viral marketing, opinion dynamics, and misinformation spread in digital media. Our work contributes to a deeper understanding of collective online behavior by linking structural and temporal dimensions of cascades.
label: llm

text: Recently, Berry phase in the semiclassical dynamical of Bloch electrons hasbeen found to make a correction to the phase-space density of states and ageneral multi-band formula for finite-temperature orbital magnetization hasbeen given [Phys. Rev. Lett. \textbf{97}, 026603 (2006)], where the orbitalmagnetization $\mathcal{M}$ consists of two parts, i.e., the conventional part$M_{c}$ and the Berry-phase correction part $M_{\Omega}$. Using this generalformula, we theoretically investigate the orbital magnetization and its effectson thermoelectric transport and magnetic susceptibility properties of thetwo-dimensional \textit{kagom\'{e}} lattice with spin anisotropies included.The study in this paper is highly interesting by the occurrence of nonzeroChern number in the lattice. The spin chirality parameter $\phi$ (see text)results in profound effects on the orbital magnetization properties. It isfound that the two parts in orbital magnetization opposite each other. Inparticular, we show that $M_{c}$ and $M_{\Omega}$ yield the paramagnetic anddiamagnetic responses, respectively. It is further shown that the orbitalmagnetization displays fully different behavior in the metallic and insulatingregions, which is due to the different roles $M_{c}$ and $M_{\Omega}$ play inthese two regions. The anomalous Nernst conductivity is also calculated, whichdisplays a peak-valley structure as a function of the electron Fermi energy.
label: human

text: This study investigates the orbital magnetization and its consequential effects within a spin-chiral ferromagnetic Kagome lattice. By employing a combination of theoretical modeling and numerical simulations, we analyze the interplay between spin chirality and electronic band topology that gives rise to orbital magnetization in this geometrically frustrated system. The Kagome lattice, known for its characteristic flat bands and Dirac points, provides a unique platform to explore unconventional magnetic phenomena. We demonstrate that the noncoplanar spin configurations induce finite Berry curvature, which significantly contributes to the orbital magnetization. Our results reveal that the orbital magnetization exhibits nontrivial dependence on both the strength of the spin chirality and the electron filling factor. Additionally, the study highlights the role of spin-orbit coupling as a key factor that enhances the orbital magnetic response. We also discuss the implications of orbital magnetization on anomalous Hall conductivity, establishing a direct link between topological features and measurable macroscopic properties. These findings deepen the understanding of how geometric frustration and spin textures influence orbital degrees of freedom in magnetic materials. The results offer potential pathways for designing spintronic devices leveraging orbital magnetism in Kagome-based compounds. Overall, this work provides a comprehensive framework for exploring emergent magnetic effects in complex lattice geometries driven by spin chirality.
label: llm

text: The process of annealing of a CdTe:Cl ingot during its cooling after growthwas studied. The annealing was performed in two stages: a high-temperaturestage, with an approximate equality of chlorine and cadmium vacancyconcentrations established at the thermodynamic equilibrium between the crystaland vapors of volatile components, and a low-temperature stage, with chargeddefects interacting to form neutral associations. The chlorine concentrationsnecessary to obtain semi-insulating crystals were determined for various ingotcooling rates in the high temperature stage. The dependence of the chlorineconcentration [Cl+Te] in the ingot on the temperature of annealing in thehigh-temperature stage was found. The carrier lifetimes and drift mobilitieswere obtained in relation to the temperature and cadmium vapor pressure in thepostgrowth annealing of the ingot.
label: human

text: This study investigates the fundamental principles governing postgrowth annealing processes of CdTe:Cl ingots aimed at producing semi-insulating crystals with optimized electrical properties. By systematically analyzing the effects of annealing temperature, duration, and ambient conditions, we demonstrate how defect passivation and dopant activation can be controlled to enhance resistivity. The results highlight the interplay between chlorine-related defect complexes and native point defects, which critically influence the semi-insulating behavior. Advanced characterization techniques corroborate the correlation between annealing parameters and the resulting crystal quality, including carrier lifetimes and uniformity. These findings provide essential guidelines for tailoring annealing protocols to achieve high-performance CdTe:Cl semi-insulating substrates for radiation detector and optoelectronic applications.
label: llm

text: In the paper the role of conservation laws in evolutionary processes, whichproceed in material systems (in material media) and lead to generation ofphysical fields, is shown using skew-symmetric differential forms.  In present paper the skew-symmetric differential forms on deforming(nondifferentiable) manifolds were used in addition to exterior forms, whichhave differentiable manifolds as a basis. Such skew-symmetric forms (which werenamed evolutionary ones since they possess evolutionary properties), as well asthe closed exterior forms, describe the conservation laws. But in contrast toexterior forms, which describe conservation laws for physical fields, theevolutionary forms correspond to conservation laws for material systems.  The evolutionary forms possess an unique peculiarity, namely, the closedexterior forms are obtained from these forms. It is just this that enables oneto describe the process of generation of physical fields, to discloseconnection between physical fields and material systems and to resolve manyproblems of existing field theories.
label: human

text: This article explores the foundational role of conservation laws in the generation and behavior of physical fields within the framework of modern field theories. We examine how symmetries underlying conservation principles, such as energy, momentum, and charge, lead to the emergence and dynamics of fundamental fields. The study synthesizes key theoretical formulations, highlighting the interplay between conserved quantities and field equations. By analyzing examples across classical and quantum field theories, we demonstrate the unifying principles that govern diverse physical phenomena. Additionally, the article discusses the implications of these principles for developing consistent and predictive field models. Our findings reinforce the central importance of conservation laws as guiding principles in understanding and constructing physical field theories.
label: llm

text: Surface based geometries of microfabricated wires or patterned magnetic filmscan be used to magnetically trap and manipulate ultracold neutral atoms orBose-Einstein condensates. We investigate the magnetic properties of such atomchips using a scanning magnetoresistive (MR) microscope with high spatialresolution and high field sensitivity. We show that MR sensors are ideallysuited to observe small variations of the magnetic field caused byimperfections in the wires or magnetic materials which ultimately lead tofragmentation of ultracold atom clouds. Measurements are also provided for themagnetic field produced by a thin current-carrying wire with small geometricmodulations along the edge. Comparisons of our measurements with a full numericcalculation of the current flow in the wire and the subsequent magnetic fieldshow excellent agreement. Our results highlight the use of scanning MRmicroscopy as a convenient and powerful technique for precisely characterizingthe magnetic fields produced near the surface of atom chips.
label: human

text: This study presents the development and application of scanning magnetoresistance microscopy as a powerful technique for characterizing magnetic fields near atom chips. Atom chips are integral to precisely manipulating cold atoms through microscale magnetic potentials, and detailed field mapping is essential for optimizing their performance. Our approach employs magnetoresistive sensors scanned in close proximity to the chip surface, providing high spatial resolution and sensitivity to magnetic field variations. We demonstrate the capability of this method to detect subtle magnetic field inhomogeneities and imperfections that impact atom trapping and coherence. Quantitative analysis of field distributions obtained through scanning magnetoresistance microscopy offers insights into fabrication-induced defects and allows for improved chip design. The results highlight the potential of this imaging technique as a diagnostic tool for advancing quantum technologies based on atom chips.
label: llm

text: The IEEE 802.11e standard revises the Medium Access Control (MAC) layer ofthe former IEEE 802.11 standard for Quality-of-Service (QoS) provision in theWireless Local Area Networks (WLANs). The Enhanced Distributed Channel Access(EDCA) function of 802.11e defines multiple Access Categories (AC) withAC-specific Contention Window (CW) sizes, Arbitration Interframe Space (AIFS)values, and Transmit Opportunity (TXOP) limits to support MAC-level QoS andprioritization. We propose an analytical model for the EDCA function whichincorporates an accurate CW, AIFS, and TXOP differentiation at any trafficload. The proposed model is also shown to capture the effect of MAC layerbuffer size on the performance. Analytical and simulation results are comparedto demonstrate the accuracy of the proposed approach for varying traffic loads,EDCA parameters, and MAC layer buffer space.
label: human

text: This article presents a comprehensive analysis of the 802.11e Enhanced Distributed Channel Access (EDCA) function, a key mechanism designed to provide quality of service (QoS) in wireless local area networks. We systematically evaluate the performance of EDCA in terms of throughput, delay, and fairness across different traffic categories under varying network conditions. Our study employs both analytical modeling and extensive simulations to capture the behavior of EDCA queues and priority differentiation. The results reveal insights into parameter settings that optimize QoS for multimedia applications while maintaining overall network efficiency. Finally, we discuss the practical implications of our findings for the design and deployment of future WLAN systems supporting diverse service requirements.
label: llm

text: Let $(\clb,\lambda_t,\psi)$ be a $C^*$-dynamical system where $(\lambda_t: t\in \IT_+)$ be a semigroup of injective endomorphism and $\psi$ be an$(\lambda_t)$ invariant state on the $C^*$ subalgebra $\clb$ and $\IT_+$ iseither non-negative integers or real numbers. The central aim of thisexposition is to find a useful criteria for the inductive limit state $\clb\raro^{\lambda_t} \clb$ canonically associated with $\psi$ to be pure. Weachieve this by exploring the minimal weak forward and backward Markovprocesses associated with the Markov semigroup on the corner von-Neumannalgebra of the support projection of the state $\psi$ to prove thatKolmogorov's property [Mo2] of the Markov semigroup is a sufficient conditionfor the inductive state to be pure. As an application of this criteria we finda sufficient condition for a translation invariant factor state on a onedimensional quantum spin chain to be pure. This criteria in a sense complementscriteria obtained in [BJKW,Mo2] as we could go beyond lattice symmetric states.
label: human

text: This article investigates the structural properties of pure inductive limit states within the framework of operator algebras and their connection to Kolmogorov's property. We establish criteria under which a pure inductive limit state exhibits Kolmogorov-type mixing behavior, thus extending classical notions of dynamical randomness to a non-commutative setting. Our analysis leverages advanced techniques in C*-algebra theory, measure-theoretic dynamics, and ergodic theory to characterize the purity and asymptotic independence properties of these states. Applications of our results illuminate the interplay between algebraic invariants and probabilistic independence in infinite quantum systems. The findings contribute to a deeper understanding of the ergodic hierarchy in operator algebras and open avenues for further exploration of quantum dynamical systems exhibiting Kolmogorov’s property.
label: llm

text: The frequency distribution of DNA bases A, C, G, T exhibit fractalfluctuations ubiquitous to dynamical systems in nature. The power spectra offractal fluctuations exhibit inverse power law form signifying long-rangecorrelations between local (small-scale) and global (large-scale)perturbations. The author has developed a general systems theory based onclassical statistical physics for fractal fluctuations which predicts that theprobability distribution of eddy amplitudes and the variance (square of eddyamplitude)spectrum of fractal fluctuations follow the universal Boltzmanninverse power law expressed as a function of the golden mean. The modelpredicted distribution is very close to statistical normal distribution forfluctuations within two standard deviations from the mean and exhibits a fatlong tail. In this paper it is shown that DNA base CG frequency distribution inTakifugu rubripes (Puffer fish) Genome Release 4 exhibit universal inversepower law form consistent with model prediction. The observed long-rangecorrelations in the DNA bases implies that the non-coding 'junk' or 'selfish'DNA which appear to be redundant, may also contribute to the efficientfunctioning of the protein coding DNA, a result supported by recent studies.
label: human

text: This study investigates the frequency distribution of the cytosine-guanine (CG) base pairs in the genome of Takifugu rubripes, commonly known as the puffer fish. By analyzing the genomic sequences, we identify a universal spectrum that characterizes CG content variation across different regions of the genome. Our findings reveal that the CG frequency distribution follows a distinct pattern consistent with underlying genomic structure and evolutionary constraints. Statistical modeling and comparative analysis demonstrate that this spectrum is conserved and provides insight into genome organization and methylation patterns. Additionally, the results contribute to a broader understanding of nucleotide distribution in vertebrate genomes and its implications for gene regulation. This work establishes a foundational framework for exploring CG distribution dynamics in other species and their evolutionary significance.
label: llm

text: Admitting the validity of Lorentz transformations for the space as timecoordinates of the same event we derive their differential form in order tounderline the correct prerequisites for the application of time and lengthcontraction or dilation effects. Furthermore we quantify the simultaneity erroroccurring in the relativity theory. Having done this, we analyse the root causeof these effects and identify it with a finite phase velocity associated withthe moving frame. We define this phase velocity by analogy to the de Brogliewave associated with a moving particle. Based on this construct we demonstratethat the phase of the de Broglie waves further extended for stationaryparticles is a relativistic invariant being the same for all correspondingobservers. Also the phase of the electromagnetic waves transporting energy atlight speed is a relativistic invariant. Therefore the universe and its matter/ energy may be seen as a superposition of waves propagating such that theirphase is the same for all corresponding observers. The wave phase may replacethe time as an invariant and universal reference.
label: human

text: The Lorentz transformations are fundamental to our understanding of special relativity, providing the mathematical framework for describing how space and time coordinates change between inertial reference frames moving at constant velocities relative to each other. This article revisits the derivation and interpretation of the Lorentz transformations, aiming to deepen the conceptual insights beyond standard textbook presentations. We explore alternative approaches to deriving these transformations, highlighting the underlying physical principles such as the invariance of the speed of light and the relativity of simultaneity. By examining the geometric structure of spacetime, we connect the Lorentz transformations to hyperbolic rotations, offering a more intuitive visualization of their effects. Additionally, we investigate how Lorentz transformations impact the formulation of fundamental physical laws, emphasizing their role in unifying electricity and magnetism. The pedagogical implications of these deeper perspectives are discussed, providing educators with tools to better communicate complex relativistic ideas to students.
label: llm

text: We present a novel comprehensive first-principles theoretical study of theelectronic properties and relative stabilities of edge-oxidized zigzag graphenenanoribbons. The oxidation schemes considered include hydroxyl, carboxyl,ether, and ketone groups. Using screened exchange density functional theory, weshow that these oxidized ribbons are more stable than hydrogen-terminatednanoribbons except for the case of the etheric groups. The stable oxidizedconfigurations maintain a spin-polarized ground state with antiferromagneticordering localized at the edges, similar to the fully hydrogenatedcounterparts. More important, edge oxidation is found to lower the onsetelectric field required to induce half-metallic behavior and extend the overallfield range at which the systems remain half-metallic. Once the half-metallicstate is reached, further increase of the external electric field intensityproduces a rapid decrease in the spin magnetization up to a point where themagnetization is quenched completely. Finally, we find that oxygen containingedge groups have a minor effect on the energy difference between theantiferromagnetic ground state and the above-lying ferromagnetic state.
label: human

text: This study investigates the electronic and magnetic properties of zigzag graphene nanoribbons (ZGNRs) with edge oxidation, focusing on the enhancement of half-metallicity. Using first-principles density functional theory calculations, we demonstrate that the introduction of oxygen functional groups at the ribbon edges significantly modifies the electronic band structure. The edge-oxidized ZGNRs exhibit a robust half-metallic behavior, characterized by a spin-polarized current confined to one spin channel, which is tunable via external electric fields. Our results reveal that oxygen atoms induce localized states that strengthen spin polarization and stabilize the half-metallic phase against structural perturbations. Additionally, we analyze the effect of varying oxidation degrees on the half-metallic gap, establishing a correlation between functionalization patterns and spin-dependent electronic properties. These findings suggest that edge oxidation is an effective chemical strategy to engineer spintronic materials based on graphene nanoribbons. The enhanced half-metallicity in edge-oxidized ZGNRs opens new avenues for the design of nanoscale devices with controllable spin transport characteristics.
label: llm

text: The chemical composition of Earth's atmosphere has undergone substantialevolution over the course of its history. It is possible, even likely, thatterrestrial planets in other planetary systems have undergone similar changes;consequently, the age distribution of nearby stars is an importantconsideration in designing surveys for Earth-analogues. Valenti & Fischer(2005) provide age and metallicity estimates for 1039 FGK dwarfs in the SolarNeighbourhood. Using the Hipparcos catalogue as a reference to calibratepotential biases, we have extracted volume-limited samples of nearby stars fromthe Valenti-Fischer dataset. Unlike other recent investigations, our analysisshows clear evidence for an age-metallicity relation in the local disk, albeitwith substantial dispersion at any epoch. The mean metallicity increases from-0.3 dex at a lookback time of ~10 Gyrs to +0.15 dex at the present day.Supplementing the Valenti-Fischer measurements with literature data to give acomplete volume-limited sample, the age distribution of nearby FGK dwarfs isbroadly consistent with a uniform star-formation rate over the history of theGalactic disk. In striking contrast, most stars known to have planetarycompanions are younger than 5 Gyrs; however, stars with planetary companionswithin 0.4 AU have a significantly flatter age distribution, indicating thatthose systems are stable on timescales of many Gyrs. Several of the older,lower metallicity host stars have enhanced [alpha/Fe] ratios, implyingmembership of the thick disk. If the frequency of terrestrial planets is alsocorrelated with stellar metallicity, then the median age of such planetarysystem is likely to be ~3 Gyrs. We discuss the implications of this hypothesisin designing searches for Earth analogues among the nearby stars.
label: human

text: The search for Earth analogues around the nearest stars is a fundamental objective in contemporary exoplanetary science and astrobiology. This study investigates the relationship between stellar age and metallicity within the Solar Neighbourhood to better understand the potential habitability and formation conditions of terrestrial planets. Using a sample of nearby stars with well-determined ages and metallicities, we analyze the age-metallicity relation (AMR) to identify trends that may influence planet formation processes. Our results indicate a complex, non-linear AMR, where metallicity shows significant scatter at all stellar ages, challenging simplistic models of chemical enrichment. Additionally, the age distribution of stars in the vicinity of the Sun reveals a preference for relatively young to intermediate-age populations, suggesting a dynamically evolving local Galactic environment. These findings have important implications for the likelihood of finding Earth-like planets, as metallicity is a critical factor in planetary core formation and disk chemistry. The interplay between stellar age, metallicity, and the local star formation history helps refine target selection criteria for future exoplanet surveys focused on Earth analogues. Moreover, by incorporating the local age distribution, we can better constrain the temporal evolution of habitable zone conditions. This work contributes to a more nuanced understanding of how stellar properties influence planet formation and the prospects for life-bearing environments nearby. Ultimately, these insights aid in optimizing observational strategies for detecting true Earth counterparts around our nearest stellar neighbors.
label: llm

text:
We performed interferometric observations of a high-mass protostellarcandidate IRAS 18566+0408 in the 
h3 (J,K)=(1,1), (2,2) and (3,3) inversiontransitions, the SiO J=2-1 and HCN J=1-0 lines, and the 43 and 87 GHz continuumemission using the VLA and OVRO. The 87 GHz continuum emission reveals twocontinuum peaks MM-1 and MM-2 along a molecular ridge. The dominant peak MM-1coincides with a compact emission feature at 43 GHz, and arises mostly from thedust emission. For dust emissivity index $ eta$ of 1.3, the masses in the dustpeaks amount to 70 \msun for MM-1, and 27 \msun for MM-2. Assuming internalheating, the central luminosities of MM-1 and MM-2 are $6 	imes 10^4$ and $8	imes 10^3$ \lsun, respectively.  The SiO emission reveals a well collimated outflow emanating from MM-1. Thejet-like outflow is also detected in 
h3 at velocities similar to the SiOemission. The outflow, with a mass of 27 \msun, causes significant heating inthe gas to temperatures of 70 K, much higher than the temperature of $\lsim 15$K in the extended core. Compact ($< 3''$) and narrow line ($<1.5$ \kms-1) 
h3(3,3) emission features are found associated with the outflow. They likelyarise from weak population inversion in 
h3 similar to the maser emission.  Toward MM-1, there is a compact 
h3 structure with a linewidth thatincreases from 5.5 \kms-1 FHWM measured at 3$''$ resolution to 8.7 \kms-1\measured at 1$''$ resolution. This linewidth is much larger than the FWHM of$<$ 2 \kms-1 in the entire core, and does not appear to originate from theoutflow. This large linewidth may arise from rotation/infall, or relativemotions of unresolved protostellar cores.
label: human

text: This study presents observations of a jet-like outflow associated with the high-mass (proto)stellar object IRAS 18566+0408. Using high-resolution molecular line data, we investigate the morphology and kinematics of the outflow to better understand massive star formation processes. Our analysis reveals a well-collimated bipolar outflow structure extending over several arcseconds from the central protostar. The outflow axis aligns closely with indicators of the protostellar disk orientation, suggesting a direct link between accretion and ejection mechanisms. Velocity gradients observed in CO and SiO emission lines provide strong evidence for high-velocity jet components embedded within the molecular outflow. The derived outflow mass and momentum rates are consistent with those expected from massive protostellar objects at an early evolutionary stage. Furthermore, the data indicate episodic ejections, possibly related to accretion bursts, which contribute to intermittent jet activity. This jet-like outflow likely plays a crucial role in regulating angular momentum and clearing surrounding material. Comparison with theoretical models supports magneto-centrifugal launching as the driving mechanism of the jet. Our findings offer important constraints on the feedback effects of outflows in massive star formation environments. The detailed characterization of IRAS 18566+0408 enhances our understanding of how high-mass stars accumulate mass while simultaneously driving energetic outflows. Future observations at higher resolution and different wavelengths will be essential to probing the innermost jet launching regions. This work contributes to the growing body of evidence that jet-like outflows are integral to the formation of massive (proto)stars.
label: llm

text: We show that in any model of non-eternal inflation satisfying the null energycondition, the area of the de Sitter horizon increases by at least one Planckunit in each inflationary e-folding. This observation gives an operationalmeaning to the finiteness of the entropy S_dS of an inflationary de Sitterspace eventually exiting into an asymptotically flat region: the asymptoticobserver is never able to measure more than e^(S_dS) independent inflationarymodes. This suggests a limitation on the amount of de Sitter space outside thehorizon that can be consistently described at the semiclassical level, fittingwell with other examples of the breakdown of locality in quantum gravity, suchas in black hole evaporation. The bound does not hold in models of inflationthat violate the null energy condition, such as ghost inflation. Thisstrengthens the case for the thermodynamical interpretation of the bound asconventional black hole thermodynamics also fails in these models, stronglysuggesting that these theories are incompatible with basic gravitationalprinciples.
label: human

text: This article explores a novel quantitative approach to de Sitter entropy within the context of cosmological models exhibiting eternal inflation. By formulating a precise measure, we aim to clarify the thermodynamic properties associated with de Sitter horizons and their implications for the multiverse framework. Our analysis addresses how fluctuations during inflation influence the entropy landscape and the conditions under which eternal inflation persists. We also discuss the relationship between horizon entropy and information loss, providing insights into the fundamental nature of spacetime in an accelerating universe. Ultimately, this work contributes to a deeper understanding of entropy as a central concept linking quantum gravity, cosmology, and inflationary theory.
label: llm

text: We present the optical identification and spectroscopy of the host galaxy ofGRB 050826 at a redshift z = 0.296 +/- 0.001. Image subtraction amongobservations obtained on three consecutive nights, reveals a fading object 5hours after the burst, confirming its identification as the optical afterglowof this event. Deep imaging shows that the optical afterglow is offset by 0.4arcseconds (~1.76 kpc) from the center of its irregular host galaxy, which istypical for long-duration gamma-ray bursts. Combining these results with X-raymeasurements acquired by the Swift XRT instrument, we find that GRB 050826falls entirely within the subluminous, subenergetic group of long gamma-raybursts at low redshift (z < 0.3). The results are discussed in the context ofmodels that possibly account for this trend, including the nature of thecentral engine, the evolution of progenitor properties as a function ofredshift, and incompleteness in current gamma-ray burst samples.
label: human

text: Gamma-ray burst GRB 050826 presents an intriguing case as a subluminous event located at a relatively low redshift of z = 0.296. In this study, we analyze multiwavelength afterglow observations to characterize its luminosity and temporal properties in comparison to the broader population of gamma-ray bursts (GRBs). Our results place GRB 050826 distinctly within the lower luminosity tail of the GRB afterglow distribution, suggesting a continuum rather than a dichotomy between classical bright and faint bursts. We discuss the implications of this finding for progenitor models and jet energetics, highlighting how subluminous GRBs can provide critical insights into the diversity of explosion mechanisms. This work contributes to a more nuanced understanding of GRB afterglow luminosity functions and their astrophysical significance.
label: llm

text: We first reported evidence for differential rotation of Kappa1 Ceti in PaperI. In this paper we demonstrate that the differential rotation pattern closelymatches that for the Sun. This result is based on additional MOST(Microvariability & Oscillations of STars) observations in 2004 and 2005, tocomplement the 2003 observations discussed in Paper I. Using StarSpotz, aprogram developed specifically to analyze MOST photometry, we have solved fork, the differential rotation coefficient, and P_{EQ}, the equatorial rotationperiod using the light curves from all three years. The spots range in latitudefrom 10 to 75 degrees and k = 0.090^{+0.006}_{-0.005} -- less than the solarvalue but consistent with the younger age of the star. k is also wellconstrained by the independent spectroscopic estimate of vsini. We demonstrateindependently that the pattern of differential rotation with latitude in factconforms to solar.  Details are given of the parallel tempering formalism used in finding themost robust solution which gives P_{EQ} = 8.77^{+0.03}_{-0.04} days -- smallerthan that usually adopted, implying an age < 750 My. Our values of P_{EQ} and kcan explain the range of rotation periods determined by others by spots oractivity at a variety of latitudes. Historically, Ca II activity seems to occurconsistently between latitudes 50 and 60 degrees which might indicate apermanent magnetic feature. Knowledge of k and P_{EQ} are key to understandingthe dynamo mechanism and rotation structure in the convective zone as wellassessing age for solar-type stars. We recently published values of k andP_{EQ} for epsilon Eri based on MOST photometry and expect to analyze MOSTlight curves for several more spotted, solar-type stars.
label: human

text: The young solar-type star Kappa1 Ceti provides a valuable analogue for understanding stellar magnetic activity and rotational evolution. Using photometric data obtained from the Microvariability and Oscillations of STars (MOST) satellite, we conducted a detailed analysis of the star’s surface differential rotation. High-precision time series photometry spanning multiple rotational cycles allowed us to track the modulation of starspot signatures. We applied spot modeling techniques to measure latitude-dependent rotation rates, revealing a significant differential rotation pattern. Our results indicate that the equatorial regions rotate faster than higher latitudes, consistent with theoretical predictions for solar-type stars. The measured differential rotation shear for Kappa1 Ceti is approximately 0.07 rad/day, which is larger than that observed on the Sun, suggesting a correlation with the star’s younger age and faster rotation. We discuss the implications of these findings for dynamo processes operating in young, active stars. The observed rotational shear influences the magnetic field generation and surface magnetic topology. Comparison with other solar analogs highlights trends relating differential rotation amplitude to stellar age and mass. The results contribute to refining models of angular momentum evolution in pre-main sequence and early main sequence stars. We also explore how differential rotation impacts the observed photometric variability and magnetic activity cycles. This study demonstrates the effectiveness of space-based photometry in probing stellar rotation and magnetic phenomena with unprecedented precision.
label: llm

text: We consider wetting of a one-dimensional random walk on a half-line $x\ge 0$in a short-ranged potential located at the origin $x=0$. We demonstrateexplicitly how the presence of a quenched chemical disorder affects thepinning-depinning transition point. For small disorders we develop aperturbative technique which enables us to compute explicitly the averagedtemperature (energy) of the pinning transition. For strong disorder we computethe transition point both numerically and using the renormalization groupapproach. Our consideration is based on the following idea: the randompotential can be viewed as a periodic potential with the period $n$ in thelimit $n\to\infty$.
