label: llm

text: In the present paper we present results of calculations obtained with the useof the theoretical method described in our preceding paper [1] and performdetail analysis of alpha helix-random coil transition in alanine polypeptidesof different length. We have calculated the potential energy surfaces ofpolypeptides with respect to their twisting degrees of freedom and construct aparameter-free partition function of the polypeptide using the suggested method[1]. From the build up partition function we derive various thermodynamicalcharacteristics for alanine polypeptides of different length as a function oftemperature. Thus, we analyze the temperature dependence of the heat capacity,latent heat and helicity for alanine polypeptides consisting of 21, 30, 40, 50and 100 amino acids. Alternatively, we have obtained same thermodynamicalcharacteristics from the use of molecular dynamics simulations and comparedthem with the results of the new statistical mechanics approach. The comparisonproves the validity of the statistical mechanic approach and establishes itsaccuracy.
label: human

text: This study presents a comprehensive analysis of ab initio theoretical predictions regarding the alpha helix-coil phase transition in polypeptides. Utilizing advanced quantum mechanical methods, we investigate the thermodynamic parameters governing the stability and conformational changes of alpha helices. Our results highlight the critical role of intramolecular hydrogen bonding and entropic contributions in driving the phase transition. Comparative evaluation with experimental data demonstrates the accuracy and limitations of current ab initio models in capturing the cooperative nature of helix formation and unfolding. Furthermore, the influence of solvent effects and amino acid sequence variability on the transition dynamics is examined. This work provides valuable insights into the microscopic mechanisms underlying protein secondary structure stability and offers guidance for refining theoretical approaches in protein folding studies.
label: llm

text: The intrinsic distribution of spectral indices in GeV energies ofgamma-ray--loud blazars is a critical input in determining the spectral shapeof the unresolved blazar contribution to the diffuse extragalactic gamma-raybackground, as well as an important test of blazar emission theories. Wepresent a maximum-likelihood method of determining the intrinsic spectral indexdistribution (ISID) of a population of gamma-ray emitters which accounts forerror in measurement of individual spectral indices, and we apply it to EGRETblazars. We find that the most likely Gaussian ISID for EGRET blazars has amean of 2.27 and a standard deviation of 0.20. We additionally find someindication that FSRQs and BL Lacs may have different ISIDs (with BL Lacs beingharder). We also test for spectral index hardening associated with blazarvariability for which we find no evidence. Finally, we produce simulated GLASTspectral index datasets and perform the same analyses. With improved statisticsdue to the much larger number of resolvable blazars, GLAST data will help usdetermine the ISIDs with much improved accuracy. Should any difference existbetween the ISIDs of BL Lacs and FSRQs or between the ISIDs of blazars in thequiescent and flaring states, GLAST data will be adequate to separate theseISIDs at a significance better than 3 sigma.
label: human

text: The Energetic Gamma-Ray Experiment Telescope (EGRET) has significantly advanced our understanding of blazar emission by cataloging their gamma-ray spectral properties. In this study, we systematically analyze the spectral index distribution of EGRET-detected blazars to characterize their gamma-ray emission behavior. Our results reveal a broad range of spectral indices, indicating diverse particle acceleration and radiation mechanisms within these active galactic nuclei. We explore correlations between spectral indices and blazar subclasses, including flat-spectrum radio quasars and BL Lac objects, to refine theoretical emission models. The analysis further highlights potential selection biases inherent in EGRET data due to sensitivity limitations. Looking forward, we assess how the upcoming Gamma-ray Large Area Space Telescope (GLAST) will enhance spectral resolution and source detection capabilities. The improved sensitivity and energy coverage of GLAST are expected to provide a more comprehensive and unbiased census of blazar spectral properties. This will enable more precise constraints on their emission models, contributing to a deeper understanding of the physical processes powering gamma-ray blazars.
label: llm

text: In wireless ad hoc networks, distributed nodes can collaboratively form anantenna array for long-distance communications to achieve high energyefficiency. In recent work, Ochiai, et al., have shown that such collaborativebeamforming can achieve a statistically nice beampattern with a narrow mainlobe and low sidelobes. However, the process of collaboration introducessignificant delay, since all collaborating nodes need access to the sameinformation. In this paper, a technique that significantly reduces thecollaboration overhead is proposed. It consists of two phases. In the firstphase, nodes transmit locally in a random access fashion. Collisions, when theyoccur, are viewed as linear mixtures of the collided packets. In the secondphase, a set of cooperating nodes acts as a distributed antenna system andbeamform the received analog waveform to one or more faraway destinations. Thisstep requires multiplication of the received analog waveform by a complexnumber, which is independently computed by each cooperating node, and whichenables separation of the collided packets based on their final destination.The scheme requires that each node has global knowledge of the networkcoordinates. The proposed scheme can achieve high throughput, which in certaincases exceeds one.
label: human

text: This paper presents a novel high-throughput cross-layer scheme designed specifically for distributed wireless ad hoc networks. By integrating routing, medium access control, and physical layer functionalities, the proposed approach optimizes network performance in terms of throughput and latency. The scheme leverages adaptive resource allocation and cooperative communication techniques to effectively manage interference and improve link reliability. A decentralized algorithm enables each node to make local decisions based on real-time network conditions, facilitating scalable and robust operation without centralized control. Extensive simulations demonstrate significant throughput gains compared to conventional layered protocols under various network densities and mobility scenarios. Moreover, the proposed scheme exhibits enhanced fairness and energy efficiency, balancing load distribution across the network. Analytical modeling further validates the empirical results and provides insights into the impact of key system parameters. The cross-layer design framework contributes to overcoming the challenges posed by dynamic topology and unpredictable wireless channels inherent to ad hoc environments. This research offers practical guidelines for implementing high-performance protocols in next-generation decentralized wireless networks.
label: llm

text: We study the effect of physical aging on the mechanical properties of a modelpolymer glass using molecular dynamics simulations. The creep compliance isdetermined simultaneously with the structural relaxation under a constantuniaxial load below yield at constant temperature. The model successfullycaptures universal features found experimentally in polymer glasses, includingsignatures of mechanical rejuvenation. We analyze microscopic relaxationtimescales and show that they exhibit the same aging characteristics as themacroscopic creep compliance. In addition, our model indicates that the entiredistribution of relaxation times scales identically with age. Despite largechanges in mobility, we observe comparatively little structural change exceptfor a weak logarithmic increase in the degree of short-range order that may becorrelated to an observed decrease in aging with increasing load.
label: human

text: This study presents a comprehensive investigation into the aging and plastic deformation behaviors of polymer glasses through advanced computer simulations. We employ molecular dynamics techniques to model the structural evolution and mechanical response of polymer glasses subjected to varying thermal and mechanical histories. Our results reveal significant changes in the glass transition dynamics and relaxation processes associated with physical aging. The simulations detail how plastic deformation mechanisms, such as shear band formation and localized yielding, are influenced by the aging state of the material. Quantitative analyses demonstrate the interplay between microscopic molecular rearrangements and macroscopic mechanical properties, offering insights into the time-dependent mechanical stability of polymer glasses. These findings contribute to a deeper understanding of polymer glass behavior, with implications for designing materials with improved durability and performance.
label: llm

text: We investigate the behaviour of an original traffic model. The modelconsiders a single multi-lane street, populated by autonomous vehicles directedfrom either end to the other. Lanes have no intrinsic directionality, and thevehicles are inserted at random at either end and any lane. Collision avoidanceis fully automatic and, to enhance the transport capacity of the street,vehicles form_trains_ in which they may travel at high speed quite close to thevehicle in front.  We report on the transit times for vehicles under a wide variety ofconditions: vehicle insertion probability & imbalance and their maximum speeddistribution. We also outline an interesting feature of the model, that thecomplex interactions of many vehicles are considerably more powerful than asimple "keep left" directive which each vehicle should obey.
label: human

text: This study investigates the dynamic behavior of autonomous vehicles navigating a single multi-lane urban street to understand traffic flow characteristics under fully automated conditions. Using agent-based simulations, we model interactions among self-driving cars with varying speeds and lane-changing strategies to analyze emergent traffic patterns and identify conditions that optimize throughput. Our results reveal that coordinated lane usage and adaptive speed control significantly reduce congestion and improve average travel times compared to traditional human-driven traffic models. Additionally, the simulations highlight the impact of vehicle density and lane number on traffic stability and the formation of stop-and-go waves. The findings provide insights into the design of autonomous traffic management systems aimed at maximizing efficiency and safety on urban roadways.
label: llm

text: It is widely believed that the perovskite Sr$_2$RuO$_4$ is an unconventionalsuperconductor with broken time reversal symmetry. It has been predicted thatsuperconductors with broken time reversal symmetry should have spontaneouslygenerated supercurrents at edges and domain walls. We have done careful imagingof the magnetic fields above Sr$_2$RuO$_4$ single crystals using scanning Hallbar and SQUID microscopies, and see no evidence for such spontaneouslygenerated supercurrents. We use the results from our magnetic imaging to placeupper limits on the spontaneously generated supercurrents at edges and domainwalls as a function of domain size. For a single domain, this upper limit isbelow the predicted signal by two orders of magnitude. We speculate on thecauses and implications of the lack of large spontaneous supercurrents in thisvery interesting superconducting system.
label: human

text: We report a comprehensive investigation into the upper limit of spontaneous supercurrents in the unconventional superconductor Sr$_2$RuO$_4$. Using a combination of sensitive magnetometry and nanoscale scanning probe techniques, we have sought direct evidence of spontaneous edge currents predicted by chiral p-wave pairing theories. Our measurements establish an upper bound on the magnitude of any such supercurrents that is significantly lower than many theoretical predictions. These findings challenge prevailing models of time-reversal symmetry breaking in Sr$_2$RuO$_4$ and suggest that if spontaneous supercurrents exist, they must be weaker or more spatially confined than previously thought. We discuss possible implications for the order parameter symmetry and the nature of the superconducting phase in this material. Our results provide critical constraints that will guide future theoretical and experimental efforts to resolve the pairing mechanism in Sr$_2$RuO$_4$.
label: llm

text: A new framework for asset price dynamics is introduced in which the conceptof noisy information about future cash flows is used to derive the priceprocesses. In this framework an asset is defined by its cash-flow structure.Each cash flow is modelled by a random variable that can be expressed as afunction of a collection of independent random variables called market factors.With each such "X-factor" we associate a market information process, the valuesof which are accessible to market agents. Each information process is a sum oftwo terms; one contains true information about the value of the market factor;the other represents "noise". The noise term is modelled by an independentBrownian bridge. The market filtration is assumed to be that generated by theaggregate of the independent information processes. The price of an asset isgiven by the expectation of the discounted cash flows in the risk-neutralmeasure, conditional on the information provided by the market filtration. Whenthe cash flows are the dividend payments associated with equities, an explicitmodel is obtained for the share-price, and the prices of options ondividend-paying assets are derived. Remarkably, the resulting formula for theprice of a European call option is of the Black-Scholes-Merton type. Theinformation-based framework also generates a natural explanation for the originof stochastic volatility.
label: human

text: Information-Based Asset Pricing explores the role of information flow in determining asset prices within financial markets. This paper develops a framework in which asset prices dynamically incorporate heterogeneous information as it becomes available to market participants. We model information arrival using stochastic processes that capture both public and private signals, reflecting realistic market conditions. The impact of asymmetric information on price formation and market efficiency is examined, highlighting conditions under which prices reveal underlying fundamentals. Using both theoretical analysis and empirical data, the model demonstrates how information asymmetry can lead to price volatility and deviations from fundamental values. We further investigate how risk preferences shape agents’ reactions to information, influencing equilibrium price dynamics. The framework provides insights into phenomena such as price momentum, volatility clustering, and informational cascades. Our results contribute to a deeper understanding of how information is processed and incorporated into prices in continuous-time settings. This work has implications for portfolio management, market regulation, and the design of information dissemination mechanisms.
label: llm

text: Disclinations, first observed in mesomorphic phases, are relevant to a numberof ill-ordered condensed matter media, with continuous symmetries or frustratedorder. They also appear in polycrystals at the edges of grain boundaries. Theyare of limited interest in solid single crystals, where, owing to their largeelastic stresses, they mostly appear in close pairs of opposite signs. Therelaxation mechanisms associated with a disclination in its creation, motion,change of shape, involve an interplay with continuous or quantized dislocationsand/or continuous disclinations. These are attached to the disclinations or areakin to Nye's dislocation densities, well suited here. The notion of 'extendedVolterra process' takes these relaxation processes into account and coversdifferent situations where this interplay takes place. These concepts areillustrated by applications in amorphous solids, mesomorphic phases andfrustrated media in their curved habit space. The powerful topological theoryof line defects only considers defects stable against relaxation processescompatible with the structure considered. It can be seen as a simplified caseof the approach considered here, well suited for media of high plasticityor/and complex structures. Topological stability cannot guarantee energeticstability and sometimes cannot distinguish finer details of structure ofdefects.
label: human

text: This article presents a comprehensive reappraisal of the concepts of disclinations, dislocations, and continuous defects within the framework of materials science and solid mechanics. We revisit classical theories that describe these topological defects, highlighting their fundamental roles in determining the mechanical and physical properties of crystalline and non-crystalline materials. The study systematically contrasts the geometric and energetic characteristics of disclinations and dislocations, clarifying their distinct yet interconnected nature. By integrating recent advances in differential geometry and continuum mechanics, we propose an extended theoretical model that unifies the treatment of discrete and continuous defect fields. This approach allows for a more nuanced understanding of defect interactions and their influence on material behavior at multiple length scales. Additionally, the implications of continuous defect distributions for plastic deformation and microstructural evolution are examined. We also discuss the experimental challenges in identifying and distinguishing these defects, emphasizing the need for advanced characterization techniques. Our findings suggest that revisiting the foundational definitions and classifications of defects can lead to improved predictive models for material performance. The article concludes by outlining potential pathways for future research, particularly in the context of complex engineered materials and metamaterials.
label: llm

text: We report new magnetic field measurements for 14 classical T Tauri stars(CTTSs). We combine these data with one previous field determination in orderto compare our observed field strengths with the field strengths predicted bymagnetospheric accretion models. We use literature data on the stellar mass,radius, rotation period, and disk accretion rate to predict the field strengththat should be present on each of our stars according to these magnetosphericaccretion models. We show that our measured field values do not correlate withthe field strengths predicted by simple magnetospheric accretion theory. Wealso use our field strength measurements and literature X-ray luminosity datato test a recent relationship expressing X-ray luminosity as a function ofsurface magnetic flux derived from various solar feature and main sequence starmeasurements. We find that the T Tauri stars we have observed have weaker thanexpected X-ray emission by over an order of magnitude on average using thisrelationship. We suggest the cause for this is actually a result of the verystrong fields on these stars which decreases the efficiency with which gasmotions in the photosphere can tangle magnetic flux tubes in the corona.
label: human

text: Classical T Tauri stars (CTTS) represent a critical phase in the early evolution of low-mass stars, characterized by active accretion and strong magnetic activity. Understanding their magnetic fields is essential to elucidate the mechanisms governing star-disk interaction and angular momentum regulation. This study synthesizes recent observational and theoretical advancements in measuring and modeling magnetic field geometries and strengths in CTTS. High-resolution spectropolarimetric data reveal complex, often multipolar field topologies that influence accretion funnel flows and surface spot distributions. The interplay between stellar magnetospheres and circumstellar disks is shown to have profound implications for disk truncation radii and accretion variability. Furthermore, magnetic field evolution during the pre-main-sequence phase is examined in the context of stellar rotation and internal structural changes. These insights contribute to a more comprehensive framework for star formation and early stellar magnetic phenomena.
label: llm

text: We propose a new mechanism to produce ultracold polar molecules withmicrowave fields. The proposed mechanism converts trapped ultracold atoms ofdifferent species into vibrationally excited molecules by a single microwavetransition and entirely depends on the existence of a permanent dipole momentin the molecules. As opposed to production of molecules by photoassociation ormagnetic-field Feshbach resonances our method does not rely on the structureand lifetime of excited states or existence of Feshbach resonances. Inaddition, we determine conditions for optimal creation of polar molecules invibrationally excited states of the ground-state potential by changingfrequency and intensity of the microwave field. We also explore the possibilityto produce vibrationally cold molecules by combining the microwave field withan optical Raman transition or by applying a microwave field to Feshbachmolecules. The production mechanism is illustrated for two polar molecules: KRband RbCs.
label: human

text: The manipulation of polar molecules using electromagnetic fields has opened new avenues in quantum control and precision measurement. This article explores the theoretical and experimental prospects for producing and controlling polar molecules through the application of microwave fields. We analyze how microwave radiation can induce transitions between rotational states, facilitating the formation of ultracold polar molecules with tailored properties. Key challenges, such as mitigating loss mechanisms and achieving high phase-space densities, are addressed within current technological constraints. The potential applications of these microwave-induced molecular assemblies in quantum simulation, quantum computation, and ultracold chemistry are discussed. Our findings highlight the promising role of microwave fields as versatile tools in the advancement of polar molecule research.
label: llm

text: We present multi-wavelength optical and infrared photometry of 170 previouslyknown low mass stars and brown dwarfs of the 5 Myr Collinder 69 cluster (LambdaOrionis). The new photometry supports cluster membership for most of them, withless than 15% of the previous candidates identified as probable non-members.The near infrared photometry allows us to identify stars with IR excesses, andwe find that the Class II population is very large, around 25% for stars (inthe spectral range M0 - M6.5) and 40% for brown dwarfs, down to 0.04 Msun,despite the fact that the H(alpha) equivalent width is low for a significantfraction of them. In addition, there are a number of substellar objects,classified as Class III, that have optically thin disks. The Class II membersare distributed in an inhomogeneous way, lying preferentially in a filamentrunning toward the south-east. The IR excesses for the Collinder 69 membersrange from pure Class II (flat or nearly flat spectra longward of 1 micron), totransition disks with no near-IR excess but excesses beginning within the IRACwavelength range, to two stars with excess only detected at 24 micron.Collinder 69 thus appears to be at an age where it provides a naturallaboratory for the study of primordial disks and their dissipation.
label: human

text: We present a comprehensive study of accretion processes in low-mass stars and brown dwarfs within the Lambda Orionis cluster, utilizing data obtained from the Spitzer Space Telescope. By analyzing infrared excesses and emission line diagnostics, we identify accretion signatures across a range of substellar and stellar masses. Our findings reveal that accretion rates decrease with decreasing object mass, highlighting distinct disk evolution pathways in brown dwarfs compared to low-mass stars. Additionally, we discuss the implications for disk lifetimes and planet formation potential in this young cluster environment. These results contribute valuable insights into the early stages of stellar and substellar evolution in star-forming regions.
label: llm

text: The stability of two-dimensional (2D) layers and membranes is subject of along standing theoretical debate. According to the so called Mermin-Wagnertheorem, long wavelength fluctuations destroy the long-range order for 2Dcrystals. Similarly, 2D membranes embedded in a 3D space have a tendency to becrumpled. These dangerous fluctuations can, however, be suppressed byanharmonic coupling between bending and stretching modes making that atwo-dimensional membrane can exist but should present strong heightfluctuations. The discovery of graphene, the first truly 2D crystal and therecent experimental observation of ripples in freely hanging graphene makesthese issues especially important. Beside the academic interest, understandingthe mechanisms of stability of graphene is crucial for understanding electronictransport in this material that is attracting so much interest for its unusualDirac spectrum and electronic properties. Here we address the nature of theseheight fluctuations by means of straightforward atomistic Monte Carlosimulations based on a very accurate many-body interatomic potential forcarbon. We find that ripples spontaneously appear due to thermal fluctuationswith a size distribution peaked around 70 \AA which is compatible withexperimental findings (50-100 \AA) but not with the current understanding ofstability of flexible membranes. This unexpected result seems to be due to themultiplicity of chemical bonding in carbon.
label: human

text: Intrinsic ripples in graphene represent a fundamental aspect of its two-dimensional structure, influencing both its mechanical and electronic properties. These ripples arise spontaneously due to thermal fluctuations and the interplay of lattice vibrations, leading to a non-flat morphology even in suspended graphene sheets. Understanding the origin and characteristics of such intrinsic corrugations is critical for the advancement of graphene-based nanoelectronic devices and flexible materials. In this study, we employ a combination of atomic-scale simulations and theoretical modeling to investigate the formation mechanisms and statistical properties of intrinsic ripples. Our results demonstrate that the amplitude and wavelength of these ripples depend sensitively on temperature, sample size, and substrate interactions. We also find that ripple formation stabilizes graphene against out-of-plane distortions, thereby preserving its structural integrity. Moreover, the presence of ripples modulates local electronic band structure, inducing variations in charge carrier mobility and electron scattering rates. The insights gained from this work contribute to a deeper understanding of two-dimensional crystal stability and open pathways for engineering graphene’s properties through controlled ripple formation. These findings have significant implications for the design of next-generation graphene-based electronic and mechanical systems.
label: llm

text: We present imaging data and photometry for the COSMOS survey in 15photometric bands between 0.3um and 2.4um. These include data taken on theSubaru 8.3m telescope, the KPNO and CTIO 4m telescopes, and the CFHT 3.6mtelescope. Special techniques are used to ensure that the relative photometriccalibration is better than 1% across the field of view. The absolutephotometric accuracy from standard star measurements is found to be 6%. Theabsolute calibration is corrected using galaxy spectra, providing colorsaccurate to 2% or better. Stellar and galaxy colors and counts agree well withthe expected values. Finally, as the first step in the scientific analysis ofthese data we construct panchromatic number counts which confirm that both thegeometry of the universe and the galaxy population are evolving.
label: human

text: The first data release of the COSMOS optical and near-infrared (near-IR) survey presents a comprehensive multiwavelength dataset covering a 2 square degree equatorial field. This release includes calibrated images and photometric catalogs obtained from observations conducted using multiple ground-based telescopes equipped with wide-field cameras. The dataset spans broad-band filters ranging from the ultraviolet to the near-IR, enabling detailed studies of galaxy populations across a wide range of redshifts. Careful data reduction and photometric calibration techniques were employed to ensure uniformity and accuracy, facilitating robust measurements of galaxy properties such as photometric redshifts, stellar masses, and star formation rates. We also provide extensive quality assessments and comparisons with previous surveys to demonstrate the reliability and depth of the data.
label: llm

text: Cornell University, the California Institute for Technology, and the JetPropulsion Laboratory are jointly studying the construction of a 25 m diametertelescope for submillimeter astronomy on a high mountain in northern Chile.This Cornell Caltech Atacama Telescope (CCAT) will combine high sensitivity, awide field of view, and a broad wavelength range to provide an unprecedentedcapability for deep, large area, multi-color submillimeter surveys tocomplement narrow field, high resolution studies with ALMA. CCAT observationswill address fundamental themes in contemporary astronomy, notably theformation and evolution of galaxies, the nature of the dark matter and darkenergy that comprise most of the content of the universe, the formation ofstars and planets, the conditions in circumstellar disks, and the conditionsduring the early history of the Solar system. The candidate CCAT site, at 5600m in northern Chile, enjoys superb observing conditions. To accommodate largeformat bolometer cameras, CCAT is designed with a 20 arcmin field of view. CCATwill incorporate closed loop active control of its segmented primary mirror tomaintain a half wavefront error of 10 mum rms or less. Instrumentation underconsideration includes both short (650 mum-200 mum) and long (2 mm-750 mum)wavelength bolometer cameras, direct detection spectrometers, and heterodynereceiver arrays. The University of Colorado, a Canadian university consortium,and the UK Astronomy Technology Centre on behalf of the UK community arepursuing participation in the CCAT consortium. When complete early in the nextdecade, CCAT will be the largest and most sensitive facility of its class aswell as the highest altitude astronomical facility on Earth.

text: The Cornell Caltech Atacama Telescope (CCAT) is a next-generation submillimeter observatory designed to advance our understanding of the cold universe. Located at a high-altitude site in the Atacama Desert of northern Chile, CCAT benefits from exceptionally dry and stable atmospheric conditions optimal for submillimeter and millimeter wavelength observations. This telescope features a large primary mirror aperture of 6 meters, enabling high angular resolution and sensitivity to faint cosmic signals. The scientific goals of CCAT include probing the formation and evolution of galaxies, investigating star and planet formation processes, and studying the cosmic microwave background with unprecedented detail. CCAT’s innovative instrumentation suite incorporates advanced bolometer arrays and heterodyne receivers to provide broad wavelength coverage and high spectral resolution. The project emphasizes synergy with other major facilities such as ALMA and the James Webb Space Telescope, aiming to create a comprehensive multiwavelength picture of astrophysical phenomena. Technical challenges in mirror surface accuracy, site infrastructure, and data processing have been addressed through collaborative engineering efforts. Overall, CCAT represents a powerful tool poised to make transformative contributions to submillimeter astronomy and cosmology in the coming decades.
label: llm

text: We introduce and study the notion of a dual Feynman transform of a modularoperad. This generalizes and gives a conceptual explanation of Kontsevich'sdual construction producing graph cohomology classes from a contractibledifferential graded Frobenius algebra. The dual Feynman transform of a modularoperad is indeed linear dual to the Feynman transform introduced by Getzler andKapranov when evaluated on vacuum graphs. In marked contrast to the Feynmantransform, the dual notion admits an extremely simple presentation viagenerators and relations; this leads to an explicit and easy description of itsalgebras. We discuss a further generalization of the dual Feynman transformwhose algebras are not necessarily contractible. This naturally gives rise to atwo-colored graph complex analogous to the Boardman-Vogt topological treecomplex.

text: This paper introduces the concept of the dual Feynman transform within the framework of modular operads, extending classical operadic constructions to a broader, more flexible setting. We develop a rigorous algebraic formalism that captures the interplay between modular operads and their associated graph complexes, emphasizing the role of duality in this context. Our approach elucidates the structural properties of modular operads, providing new insights into their homotopy-theoretic and combinatorial aspects. We demonstrate how the dual Feynman transform facilitates computations of modular graph homology and connects with known invariants arising in topological field theories. Several illustrative examples are presented to highlight the applicability of the theory to concrete problems in algebraic topology and mathematical physics.
label: llm

text: The description of the statistical properties of dust emission givesimportant constraints on the physics of the interstellar medium but it is alsoa useful way to estimate the contamination of diffuse interstellar emission inthe cases where it is considered a nuisance. The main goals of this analysis ofthe power spectrum and non-Gaussian properties of 100 micron dust emission are1) to estimate the power spectrum of interstellar matter density in threedimensions, 2) to review and extend previous estimates of the cirrus noise dueto dust emission and 3) to produce simulated dust emission maps that reproducethe observed statistical properties. The main results are the following. 1) Thecirrus noise level as a function of brightness has been previouslyoverestimated. It is found to be proportional to <I> instead of <I>^1.5, where<I> is the local average brightness at 100 micron. This scaling is inaccordance with the fact that the brightness fluctuation level observed at agiven angular scale on the sky is the sum of fluctuations of increasingamplitude with distance on the line of sight. 2) The spectral index of dustemission at scales between 5 arcmin and 12.5 degrees is <gamma>=-2.9 on averagebut shows significant variations over the sky. Bright regions havesystematically steeper power spectra than diffuse regions. 3) The skewness andkurtosis of brightness fluctuations is high, indicative of strongnon-Gaussianity. 4) Based on our characterization of the 100 micron powerspectrum we provide a prescription of the cirrus confusion noise as a functionof wavelength and scale. 5) Finally we present a method based on a modificationof Gaussian random fields to produce simulations of dust maps which reproducethe power spectrum and non-Gaussian properties of interstellar dust emission.

text: This study investigates the statistical properties of dust emission in the far-infrared (FIR) regime, focusing on its spatial and spectral characteristics across various interstellar environments. Utilizing data from high-resolution FIR surveys, we analyze the intensity fluctuations and their distributions to characterize the underlying physical processes governing dust emission. The power spectrum analysis reveals scale-dependent variations consistent with turbulent structures influencing dust grain alignment and temperature distributions. We further examine the correlation between FIR emission and gas tracers to understand dust-gas coupling and energy exchange mechanisms. Statistical metrics such as skewness and kurtosis are employed to quantify non-Gaussian features that arise from density inhomogeneities and radiative transfer effects. Our results demonstrate a clear dependence of emission statistics on environmental factors like radiation field intensity, metallicity, and dust composition. We also explore how these statistical properties vary with wavelength, providing insights into the size distribution and emissivity of dust grains. Comparisons with theoretical dust emission models underline the importance of incorporating multi-scale turbulence and complex grain physics. The findings have implications for interpreting FIR observations in both the Milky Way and external galaxies, particularly in the context of star formation studies. This work contributes to improving dust emission templates used in cosmic microwave background foreground subtraction. Ultimately, our analysis enhances the understanding of dust infrared emission as a tracer of the interstellar medium’s physical state.
label: llm

text: We have used Suprime-Cam on the Subaru Telescope to conduct a V- and I-bandimaging survey of fields sampling the spheroid of the Andromeda galaxy alongits south-east minor axis. Our photometric data are deep enough to resolvestars down to the red clump. Based on a large and reliable sample of red giantstars available from this deep wide-field imager, we have derived metallicitydistributions vs. radius and a surface brightness profile over projecteddistances of R=23-66 kpc from the galaxy's center. The metallicitydistributions across this region shows a clear high mean metallicity and abroad distribution ([Fe/H] ~ -0.6 +/- 0.5), and indicates no metallicitygradient within our observed range. The surface brightness profile at R>40 kpcis found to be flatter than previously thought. It is conceivable that thispart of the halo samples as yet unidentified, metal-rich substructure.

text: We present a deep imaging survey of the spheroidal component of the Andromeda Galaxy (M31) along its South-East minor axis using the Subaru Telescope's Suprime-Cam wide-field imager. Our observations cover a contiguous area that extends from the inner halo out to approximately 100 kpc, providing critical insights into the spatial distribution and stellar populations of M31’s extended spheroid. By analyzing resolved star counts, we investigate the structural properties and metallicity gradients, revealing a complex, multi-component halo that includes both smooth and substructured elements. The data indicate a gradual decline in metallicity with increasing galactocentric distance, consistent with hierarchical assembly scenarios and the accretion of smaller satellite galaxies. We also identify several previously unreported stellar overdensities, which may represent remnants of disrupted dwarf galaxies or streams.
label: llm

text: This comment critically examines the statistical methods employed in the study titled "A new experimental limit for the stability of the electron" by Klapdor-Kleingrothaus, Krivosheina, and Titkova. We highlight potential shortcomings in the data analysis approach, including the treatment of background signals and uncertainty estimation. Alternative statistical techniques are suggested that may provide more robust and reliable bounds on electron stability. Our assessment aims to clarify the conclusions drawn and to contribute to improved standards in experimental particle physics research.

text: The random initialization of weights of a multilayer perceptron makes itpossible to model its training process as a Las Vegas algorithm, i.e. arandomized algorithm which stops when some required training error is obtained,and whose execution time is a random variable. This modeling is used to performa case study on a well-known pattern recognition benchmark: the UCI ThyroidDisease Database. Empirical evidence is presented of the training timeprobability distribution exhibiting a heavy tail behavior, meaning a bigprobability mass of long executions. This fact is exploited to reduce thetraining time cost by applying two simple restart strategies. The first assumesfull knowledge of the distribution yielding a 40% cut down in expected timewith respect to the training without restarts. The second, assumes nullknowledge, yielding a reduction ranging from 9% to 23%.

text: Training multilayer perceptrons (MLPs) for classification tasks often exhibits significant variability in convergence time, which can be characterized by heavy-tailed distributions. This study investigates the presence and implications of heavy-tailed training time behavior in MLPs applied to the UCI Thyroid Disease database. By analyzing extensive training runs, we demonstrate that a small subset of training attempts requires disproportionately longer epochs to converge, indicating heavy tail phenomena. Leveraging this insight, we propose exploiting heavy-tailed distributions to optimize training strategies, such as early stopping and adaptive restart mechanisms. Empirical results show that these techniques reduce average training time while maintaining or improving classification accuracy. Furthermore, our findings suggest that acknowledging heavy tails can enhance resource allocation and improve robustness in neural network training.
label: llm

text: We study both analytically and numerically the gravitational fields of starsin f(R) gravity theories. We derive the generalized Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkovequations for these theories and show that in metric f(R) models theParameterized Post-Newtonian parameter $\gamma_{\rm PPN} = 1/2$ is a robustoutcome for a large class of boundary conditions set at the center of the star.This result is also unchanged by introduction of dark matter in the SolarSystem. We find also a class of solutions with $\gamma_{\rm PPN} \approx 1$ inthe metric $f(R)=R-\mu^4/R$ model, but these solutions turn out to be unstableand decay in time. On the other hand, the Palatini version of the theory isfound to satisfy the Solar System constraints. We also consider compact starsin the Palatini formalism, and show that these models are not inconsistent withpolytropic equations of state. Finally, we comment on the equivalence betweenf(R) gravity and scalar-tensor theories and show that many interesting Palatinif(R) gravity models can not be understood as a limiting case of aJordan-Brans-Dicke theory with $\omega \to -3/2$.
label: human

text: This paper investigates spherically symmetric spacetimes within the framework of f(R) gravity theories, which generalize Einstein’s General Relativity by allowing the gravitational Lagrangian to be an arbitrary function of the Ricci scalar R. We derive the field equations for static and dynamic spherically symmetric metrics and analyze their properties under various functional forms of f(R). Particular emphasis is placed on identifying exact solutions and characterizing the conditions under which these solutions reduce to those of General Relativity. The stability and physical viability of the obtained spacetimes are studied through energy conditions and perturbative methods. Applications to astrophysical objects such as black holes and compact stars are discussed, highlighting deviations from classical predictions. Our results contribute to a deeper understanding of how modified gravity theories influence the structure and evolution of spherically symmetric gravitational systems.
label: llm

text: Link homotopy has been an active area of research for knot theorists sinceits introduction by Milnor in the 1950s. We introduce a new equivalencerelation on spatial graphs called component homotopy, which reduces to linkhomotopy in the classical case. Unlike previous attempts at generalizing linkhomotopy to spatial graphs, our new relation allows analogues of some standardlink homotopy results and invariants.  In particular we can define a type of Milnor group for a spatial graph undercomponent homotopy, and this group determines whether or not the spatial graphis splittable. More surprisingly, we will also show that whether the spatialgraph is splittable up to component homotopy depends only on the link homotopyclass of the links contained within it. Numerical invariants of the relationwill also be produced.
label: human

text: This article explores the extension of Milnor invariants, originally defined for classical links, to the setting of spatial graphs embedded in three-dimensional space. We develop a framework to define and compute Milnor-type invariants that capture the higher-order linking information inherent in spatial graphs beyond traditional knot and link theory. Our approach generalizes the classical invariants by incorporating the combinatorial and topological complexity of graph embeddings, including vertices and multiple edges. We establish foundational properties of these invariants, proving their invariance under ambient isotopy and their behavior under graph operations such as edge contraction and subdivision. Applications of the extended Milnor invariants are demonstrated through explicit computations for several families of spatial graphs, revealing new insights into their topological classification.
label: llm

text: It has been shown based on radio variability arguments that some BALQSOs(broad absorption line quasars) are viewed along the polar axis (orthogonal toaccretion disk) in the recent article of Zhou et al. These arguments are basedon the brightness temperature, $T_{b}$ exceeding $10^{12} ^{\circ}$ K whichleads to the well-known inverse Compton catastrophe unless the radio jet isrelativistic and is viewed along its axis. In this letter, we expand the Zhouet al sample of polar BALQSOs to the entire SDSS DR5. In the process, weclarify a mistake in their calculation of brightness temperature. The expandedsample of high $T_{b}$ BALQSOS, has an inordinately large fraction of LoBALQSOs(low ionization BALQSOs). We consider this an important clue to understandingthe nature of the polar BALQSOs. This is expected in the polar BALQSOanalytical/numerical models of Punsly in which LoBALQSOs occur when the line ofsight is very close to the polar axis, where the outflow density is thehighest.
label: human

text: Polar Broad Absorption Line (BAL) quasars represent a distinctive subclass of quasars characterized by high-velocity outflows observed along the polar axis. This study investigates the physical properties and underlying mechanisms responsible for their broad absorption features by combining observational data with theoretical modeling. We analyze multi-wavelength spectroscopic and polarimetric observations to constrain the geometry, kinematics, and ionization state of the absorbing material. Our findings suggest that the polar BAL outflows originate from regions close to the central engine and exhibit a highly collimated structure consistent with radiatively driven wind models. The results also indicate a significant difference in the orientation and physical conditions of polar BAL quasars compared to their equatorial counterparts. We discuss the implications of these differences for quasar unification schemes and the role of BAL winds in feedback processes affecting host galaxy evolution.
label: llm

text: Extending network lifetime of battery-operated devices is a key design issuethat allows uninterrupted information exchange among distributive nodes inwireless sensor networks. Collaborative beamforming (CB) and cooperativetransmission (CT) have recently emerged as new communication techniques thatenable and leverage effective resource sharing among collaborative/cooperativenodes. In this paper, we seek to maximize the lifetime of sensor networks byusing the new idea that closely located nodes can use CB/CT to reduce the loador even avoid packet forwarding requests to nodes that have critical batterylife. First, we study the effectiveness of CB/CT to improve the signal strengthat a faraway destination using energy in nearby nodes. Then, a 2D disk case isanalyzed to assess the resulting performance improvement. For general networks,if information-generation rates are fixed, the new routing problem isformulated as a linear programming problem; otherwise, the cost for routing isdynamically adjusted according to the amount of energy remaining and theeffectiveness of CB/CT. From the analysis and simulation results, it is seenthat the proposed schemes can improve the lifetime by about 90% in the 2D disknetwork and by about 10% in the general networks, compared to existing schemes.
label: human

text: This paper investigates strategies to enhance the operational lifetime of wireless sensor networks (WSNs) through the integration of collaborative beamforming and cooperative transmission techniques. By leveraging spatial diversity and cooperative signal processing, sensor nodes can transmit data more efficiently, thereby reducing individual energy consumption. The proposed framework enables multiple nodes to coherently combine their signals, effectively increasing transmission range and reliability without additional power expenditure. Analytical models are developed to quantify the energy savings and lifetime extension achievable under varying network topologies and channel conditions. Simulation results demonstrate significant improvements in network longevity compared to conventional single-node transmission schemes. Furthermore, the study explores practical considerations such as synchronization challenges and protocol overheads inherent in collaborative approaches. The findings highlight the potential of combining beamforming and cooperative transmission as a promising solution for sustainable, energy-efficient wireless sensor network design.
label: llm

text: We consider the Kalman - Yakubovich - Popov (KYP) inequality \[\begin{pmatrix} X-A^* XA-C^*C & -A^*X B- C^*D\cr -B^*X A-D^* C & I- B^*X B-D^*D\end{pmatrix} \ge 0 \] for contractive operator matrices $ \begin{pmatrix}A&B\cr C &D \end{pmatrix}:\begin{pmatrix}\mathfrak{H}\cr\mathfrak{M}\end{pmatrix}\to\begin{pmatrix}\mathfrak{H}\cr\mathfrak{N} \end{pmatrix}, $where $\mathfrak{H},$ $\mathfrak{M}$, and $\mathfrak{N}$ are separable Hilbertspaces. We restrict ourselves to the solutions $X$ from the operator interval$[0, I_\mathfrak{H}]$. Several equivalent forms of KYP are obtained. Using theparametrization of the blocks of contractive operator matrices, the Kre\u{\i}nshorted operator, and the M\"obius representation of the Schur classoperator-valued function we find several equivalent forms of the KYPinequality. Properties of solutions are established and it is proved that theminimal solution of the KYP inequality satisfies the corresponding algebraicRiccati equation and can be obtained by the iterative procedure with thespecial choice of the initial point. In terms of the Kre\u{\i}n shortedoperators a necessary condition and some sufficient conditions for uniquenessof the solution are established.
label: human

text: The Kalman–Yakubovich–Popov (KYP) lemma serves as a fundamental bridge between frequency-domain properties and state-space representations in control theory. This paper investigates the discrete-time version of the KYP inequality specifically for passive, linear time-invariant systems. We establish necessary and sufficient conditions for a system to be passive by relating its transfer function's positive realness to a specific linear matrix inequality. The analysis demonstrates that such passivity is equivalent to the existence of a positive semi-definite solution to the discrete KYP inequality. Furthermore, we explore the implications of this result for the internal stability and dissipativity of the underlying state-space model. These findings provide a robust framework for designing and analyzing discrete-time filters and controllers that must adhere to strict energy constraints.
label: llm

text: ``Top--down'' models explain the observation of ultra high energy cosmic rays(UHECR; $E \gsim 5 \cdot 10^{19}$ eV) through the decay of very massive,long--lived ``$X$ particles''. If superparticles with masses near a TeV exist,$X$ decays also lead to a significant flux of very energetic neutralinos,assumed to be the (stable or long--lived) lightest superparticles. There is arange of energies where neutrinos get absorbed in the Earth, but neutralinoscan still traverse it. These neutralinos could in principle be detected. Wecalculate the detection rate in planned experiments such as OWL and EUSO. Forbino--like neutralinos, which have been considered previously, we finddetection rates below 1 event per Teraton of target and year in all cases;often the rates are much smaller. In contrast, if the neutralino ishiggsino--like, more than ten events per year per Teraton might be observed, ifthe mass of the $X$ particle is near its lower bound of $\sim 10^{12}$ GeV.
label: human

text: Neutralinos remain among the most compelling candidates for cold dark matter within the framework of supersymmetric extensions to the Standard Model. While direct detection experiments have placed stringent limits on low-mass regions, the search for very high energy (VHE) neutralinos offers a unique window into the multi-TeV mass scale. This paper evaluates the potential for observing characteristic signals from the annihilation or decay of VHE neutralinos in upcoming cosmic ray observatories. We calculate the predicted fluxes of gamma rays, neutrinos, and antimatter particles produced through secondary cascades in various high-density astrophysical environments. Particular attention is given to the sensitivity and resolution of future instruments such as the Cherenkov Telescope Array and next-generation neutrino telescopes. Our findings suggest that these detectors will significantly enhance the reach into the heavy neutralino parameter space, potentially uncovering signatures that are currently inaccessible to current technology.
label: llm

text: In the context of Free Probability Theory, we study two differentconstructions that provide new examples of factors of type ${\rm II_1}$ withprescribed fundamental group. First we investigate state-preserving groupactions on the almost periodic free Araki-Woods factors satisfying both acondition of mixing and a condition of free malleability in the sense of Popa.Typical examples are given by the free Bogoliubov shifts. Take an ICC $w$-rigidgroup $G$ such that $\mathcal{F}(L(G)) = \{1\}$ (e.g. $G = \Z^2 \rtimes \SL(2,\Z)$). For any countable subgroup $S \subset \R^*_+$, we show that there existsan action of $G$ on $L(\F_\infty)$ such that $L(\F_\infty) \rtimes G$ is a type${\rm II_1}$ factor and its fundamental group is $S$. The second constructionis based on a free product. Take $(B(H), \psi)$ any factor of type ${\rm I}$endowed with a faithful normal state and denote by $\Gamma \subset \R^*_+$ thesubgroup generated by the point spectrum of $\psi$. We show that thecentralizer $(L(G) \ast B(H))^{\tau \ast \psi}$ is a type ${\rm II_1}$ factorand its fundamental group is $\Gamma$. Our proofs rely on Popa'sdeformation/rigidity strategy using his intertwining-by-bimodules technique.
label: human

text: This paper investigates the range of the fundamental group for type ${\rm II_1}$ factors, a central problem in the theory of von Neumann algebras since their inception by Murray and von Neumann. The fundamental group $\mathcal{F}(M)$ of a factor $M$ is defined as the set of positive scalars $t$ such that the amplification $M_t$ is isomorphic to $M$. While it was long conjectured that $\mathcal{F}(M)$ could be any subgroup of the positive real line, providing explicit constructions for arbitrary countable groups remained a significant challenge for decades. Utilizing Sorin Popa’s deformation/rigidity theory, we provide a general construction of type ${\rm II_1}$ factors whose fundamental groups are exactly prescribed countable subgroups of $\mathbb{R}_+^*$. The construction employs a group measure space approach, focusing on crossed products arising from actions of groups that satisfy specific rigidity or property (T) conditions. By carefully engineering the actions of these groups on probability spaces, we ensure that the symmetries of the resulting von Neumann algebra are strictly controlled. Specifically, we demonstrate that for any given countable subgroup $S \subset \mathbb{R}_+^*$, there exists a separable type ${\rm II_1}$ factor $M$ such that $\mathcal{F}(M) = S$.
label: llm

text: We examine Gaussian-basis Monte Carlo method (GBMC) introduced by Corney andDrummond. This method is based on an expansion of the density-matrix operatorrho by means of the coherent Gaussian-type operator basis Lambda and does notsuffer from the minus sign problem. The original method, however, often failsin reproducing the true ground state and causes systematic errors of calculatedphysical quantities because the samples are often trapped in some metastable orsymmetry broken states. To overcome this difficulty, we combine thequantum-number projection scheme proposed by Assaad, Werner, Corboz, Gull andTroyer in conjunction with the importance sampling of the original GBMC method.This improvement allows us to carry out the importance sampling in thequantum-number-projected phase-space. Some comparisons with the previousquantum-number projection scheme indicate that, in our method, the convergencewith the ground state is accelerated, which makes it possible to extend theapplicability and widen the range of tractable parameters in the GBMC method.The present scheme offers an efficient practical way of computation forstrongly correlated electron systems beyond the range of system sizes,interaction strengths and lattice structures tractable by other computationalmethods such as the quantum Monte Carlo method.
label: human

text: Understanding the ground-state properties of itinerant and strongly correlated electron systems remains a central challenge in condensed matter physics due to the breakdown of conventional one-electron approximations. In this paper, we introduce a Gaussian-basis Monte Carlo (GBMC) method designed to numerically investigate the many-body wavefunctions of these complex electronic systems. The approach utilizes a set of non-orthogonal Gaussian functions to represent the electronic states, enabling an efficient stochastic sampling of the Hamiltonian in a flexible and computationally manageable basis. We apply this method to several benchmark lattice models, demonstrating its capacity to accurately capture the subtle interplay between kinetic energy and strong electron-electron interactions. Our findings suggest that the GBMC method provides a robust and versatile framework for exploring quantum phase transitions and the emergence of collective electronic phenomena in strongly correlated regimes.
label: llm

text: The angular distribution of the emitted electrons, following the two-photonionization of the hydrogen-like ions, is studied within the framework of secondorder perturbation theory and the Dirac equation. Using a density matrixapproach, we have investigated the effects which arise from the polarization ofthe incoming light as well as from the higher multipoles in the expansion ofthe electron--photon interaction. For medium- and high-Z ions, in particular,the non-dipole contributions give rise to a significant change in the angulardistribution of the emitted electrons, if compared with the electric-dipoleapproximation. This includes a strong forward emission while, in dipoleapproxmation, the electron emission always occurs symmetric with respect to theplane which is perpendicular to the photon beam. Detailed computations for thedependence of the photoelectron angular distributions on the polarization ofthe incident light are carried out for the ionization of H, Xe$^{53+}$, andU$^{91+}$ (hydrogen-like) ions.
label: human

text: This study investigates the angular distribution of photoelectrons emitted during the two-photon ionization of hydrogen-like ions. A rigorous relativistic framework based on the Dirac equation is employed to describe the interaction between the bound electron and the external electromagnetic field. We calculate the differential cross-sections across a wide range of nuclear charges and photon energies, explicitly accounting for higher-order multipole effects. The results demonstrate that relativistic corrections significantly alter the symmetry and peak positions of the angular distribution, particularly for high-$Z$ ions where non-relativistic approximations fail. These findings provide critical insights into the dynamics of nonlinear light-matter interactions and emphasize the necessity of a relativistic treatment in high-energy atomic processes.
label: llm

text: In this paper we present the guidelines for an extrasolar planet taxonomy.The discovery of an increasing number of extrasolar planets showing a vastvariety of planetary parameters, like Keplerian orbital elements andenvironmental parameters, like stellar masses, spectral types, metallicityetc., prompts the development of a planetary taxonomy. In this work viaprincipal component analysis followed by hierarchical clustering analysis, wereport the definition of five robust groups of planets. We also discuss thephysical relevance of such analysis, which may provide a valid basis fordisentangling the role of the several physical parameters involved in theprocesses of planet formation and subsequent evolution. For instance, we wereable to divide the hot Jupiters into two main groups on the basis of theirstellar masses and metallicities. Moreover, for some groups, we find strongcorrelations between metallicity, semi-major axis and eccentricity. Theimplications of these findings are discussed.
label: human

text: The rapid discovery of thousands of exoplanets has created a critical need for a more robust classification framework that extends beyond traditional mass-period diagrams. This paper introduces a novel statistical approach to exoplanet taxonomy that utilizes unsupervised machine learning algorithms to identify latent structures within multi-dimensional parameter spaces. We apply this methodology to a comprehensive dataset of confirmed exoplanets, incorporating physical properties such as radius, mass, equilibrium temperature, and stellar host characteristics. Our analysis reveals several distinct clusters that challenge existing categorical boundaries, highlighting previously unrecognized subgroups among super-Earths and sub-Neptunes. Unlike conventional manual grouping, this data-driven technique objectively quantifies the probabilistic boundaries between planetary types while accounting for inherent observational biases. These findings provide a more nuanced understanding of planetary formation pathways and offer a scalable framework for classifying future discoveries from next-generation sky surveys.
label: llm

text: We have carried out neutron powder-diffraction measurements on zincparatacamite Zn$_x$Cu$_{4-x}$(OH)$_6$Cl$_2$ with $x=1$, and studied the heatcapacity in fields of up to 9 T for $0.5 \leq x \leq 1$. The $x=1$ phase hasrecently been shown to be an outstanding realisation of the $S=1/2$ kagom\'{e}antiferromagnet. A weak mixing of Cu$^{2+}$/Zn$^{2+}$ between the Cu and the Znsites, corresponding to $\sim 9$% of all Cu$^{2+}$ for $x=1$, is observed usingneutron diffraction. This ``antisite disorder'' provides a consistentexplanation of the field dependence of the heat capacity for $0.8 \leq x \leq1$. From comparison of the derived Cu$^{2+}$ occupancy of the Zn sites for $x =0.8... 1$ with the magnetic susceptibility, we argue that for $x = 0.8... 1$zinc paratacamite is a spin liquid without a spin gap. The presence of unpairedbut nevertheless strongly interacting spins gives rise to a macroscopicallydegenerate ground state manifold, with increasingly glassy dynamics as $x$ islowered.
label: human

text: The $S=1/2$ kagome antiferromagnet represents one of the most prominent models for exploring the effects of extreme geometric frustration in quantum systems. Identifying a physical material that faithfully realizes this model has long been a central goal, as it is predicted to host an elusive quantum spin liquid ground state. In this study, we characterize the magnetic behavior of a new experimental realization of the $S=1/2$ kagome lattice through high-resolution spectroscopy and bulk thermodynamic measurements. Our investigations focus on the low-temperature regime to determine whether the system undergoes a magnetic phase transition or remains disordered due to quantum fluctuations. The experimental data show no signs of long-range magnetic ordering down to temperatures significantly lower than the exchange coupling constant, suggesting a highly entangled and disordered ground state. Ultimately, these observations establish this compound as a premier candidate for studying the physics of frustrated magnets and the emergence of non-trivial topological order.
label: llm

text: The main result of this article is the fact that the currents defined byLevin give a description of the polylogarithm of an abelian scheme at thetopological level. This result was a conjecture of Levin. This provides amethod to explicit the Eisenstein classes of an abelian scheme at thetopological level. These classes are of special interest since they have amotivic origin by a theorem of Kings. In a forthcoming article, we use the mainresult of this paper to prove that the Eisenstein classes of the universalabelian scheme over an Hilbert-Blumenthal variety degenerate at the boundary ofthe Baily-Borel compactification of the base in a special value of an$L$-function associated to the underlying totally real number field. As acorollary, we get a non vanishing result for some of these Eisenstein classesin this geometric situation.
label: human

text: Cet article est consacré à la construction et à l’étude de la réalisation de Hodge du polylogarithme associé à un schéma abélien sur une base lisse. Nous définissons cet objet comme une variation de structures de Hodge mixtes sur le complémentaire de la section nulle, en suivant l’approche formelle développée initialement pour le cas multiplicatif. La construction s'appuie sur l’analyse de l’extension universelle du schéma abélien et sur les propriétés de dégénérescence des structures de Hodge associées. Nous démontrons que la classe du polylogarithme ainsi obtenue est caractérisée de manière unique par sa restriction le long des sections de torsion et par son comportement résiduel. Un aspect central de ce travail consiste à relier explicitement cette réalisation aux classes d’Eisenstein-Hodge, généralisant ainsi les résultats classiques connus pour les courbes elliptiques.
label: llm

text: Context. Gas within a galaxy is forced to establish pressure balance againstgravitational forces. The shape of an unperturbed gaseous disk can be used toconstrain dark matter models. Aims. We derive the 3-D HI volume densitydistribution for the Milky Way out to a galactocentric radius of 40 kpc and aheight of 20 kpc to constrain the Galactic mass distribution. Methods. We usedthe Leiden/Argentine/Bonn all sky 21-cm line survey. The transformation frombrightness temperatures to densities depends on the rotation curve. We exploredseveral models, reflecting different dark matter distributions. Each of thesemodels was set up to solve the combined Poisson-Boltzmann equation in aself-consistent way and optimized to reproduce the observed flaring. Results.Besides a massive extended halo of M ~ 1.8 10^{12} Msun, we find aself-gravitating dark matter disk with M=2 to 3 10^{11} Msun, including a darkmatter ring at 13 < R < 18.5 kpc with M = 2.2 to 2.8 10^{10} Msun. Theexistence of the ring was previously postulated from EGRET data and coincideswith a giant stellar structure that surrounds the Galaxy. The resulting MilkyWay rotation curve is flat up to R~27 kpc and slowly decreases outwards. The\hi gas layer is strongly flaring. The HWHM scale height is 60 pc at R = 4 kpcand increases to ~2700$ pc at R=40 kpc. Spiral arms cause a noticeable imprinton the gravitational field, at least out to R = 30 kpc. Conclusions. Our massmodel supports previous proposals that the giant stellar ring structure is dueto a merging dwarf galaxy. The fact that the majority of the dark matter in theMilky Way for $R \la 40$ kpc can be successfully modeled by a self-gravitatingisothermal disk raises the question of whether this massive disk may have beencaused by similar merger events in the past.
label: human

text: The determination of the dark matter distribution within the Milky Way remains a fundamental challenge in modern galactic dynamics. This second paper in our series focuses on utilizing the neutral hydrogen (HI) gas distribution as a direct tracer of the Galactic gravitational potential. Neutral hydrogen is particularly well-suited for this purpose due to its presence across the entire Galactic disk and its sensitive response to the vertical force field. We model the HI distribution by assuming a state of hydrostatic equilibrium between the gas pressure and the total gravitational attraction of the Galaxy. Our approach incorporates a multi-component mass model that includes the stellar bulge, the stellar disk, and a massive dark matter halo. We utilize high-resolution 21-cm line emission data to accurately measure the vertical thickness and the radial surface density of the HI layer. The flaring of the gas disk—the increase in its vertical scale height with galactocentric radius—serves as the primary indicator of the total matter density. By analyzing the gas kinematics, we are able to disentangle the gravitational influence of baryonic matter from that of the dark matter component. Our results suggest that the dark matter halo must possess a slightly flattened oblate geometry to match the observed gas scale heights. We calculate the local dark matter density to be approximately 0.013 solar masses per cubic parsec, aligning with recent astrometric measurements. The radial density profile of the dark matter is found to follow a Navarro-Frenk-White distribution with a high degree of precision. We also investigate the role of non-thermal pressure sources, including magnetic fields and cosmic ray pressure, in maintaining the gas equilibrium. Neglecting these non-thermal components would result in an artificial overestimation of the dark matter density in the outer Galactic regions.
label: llm

text: Effective Field Theory(EFT) is, the unique, model independent and systematiclow-energy version of QCD for processes involving momenta below the pion mass.A low-energy photo-nuclear observable in three-body systems, photonpolarization parameter at thermal neutron energies is calculated by usingpionless EFT up to next-to-next to leading order(N$^2$LO). In order to make acomparative study of this model, we compared our results for photonpolarization parameter with the realistic Argonne $v_{18}$ two-nucleon andUrbana IX or Tucson-Melbourne three-nucleon interactions. Three-body currentsgive small but significant contributions to some of the observables in theneutron-deuteron radiative capture cross section at thermal neutron energies.In this formalism the three-nucleon forces are needed up to N$^2$LO for cut-offindependent results. Our result converges order by order in low energyexpansion and also cut-off independent at this order.
label: human

text: This paper investigates the radiative capture process $n + d \to \text{}^3\text{H} + \gamma$ at thermal neutron energies to examine the electromagnetic properties of the three-nucleon system. Using a rigorous few-body framework, we calculate the transition matrix elements by employing realistic nuclear potentials and considering the contributions of meson exchange currents. The analysis focuses specifically on the photon polarization parameter, which characterizes the orientation of the emitted radiation following the capture of polarized neutrons. Our results demonstrate that this parameter is a sensitive probe of the underlying nuclear dynamics and provides essential theoretical benchmarks for future low-energy experimental measurements.
label: llm

text: We report quantitative relations between corruption level and economicfactors, such as country wealth and foreign investment per capita, which arecharacterized by a power law spanning multiple scales of wealth and investmentsper capita. These relations hold for diverse countries, and also remain stableover different time periods. We also observe a negative correlation betweenlevel of corruption and long-term economic growth. We find similar results fortwo independent indices of corruption, suggesting that the relation betweencorruption and wealth does not depend on the specific measure of corruption.The functional relations we report have implications when assessing therelative level of corruption for two countries with comparable wealth, and forquantifying the impact of corruption on economic growth and foreigninvestments.
label: human

text: This study investigates the complex interplay between systemic corruption and key macroeconomic indicators to establish clear quantitative relationships across diverse national contexts. Employing multivariate regression analysis on a global dataset, we examine how the Corruption Perceptions Index correlates with GDP per capita, foreign direct investment, and income inequality. The findings reveal a robust negative correlation, demonstrating that higher levels of corruption significantly impede economic growth and distort market efficiencies. These results underscore the critical importance of institutional transparency and governance reform as essential drivers for long-term economic stability and development.
label: llm

text: In the present paper we consider countable state $p$-adic Potts model on theCayley tree. A construction of $p$-adic Gibbs measures which depends on weights$\l$ is given, and an investigation of such measures is reduced to examinationof an infinite-dimensional recursion equation. Studying of the derived equationunder some condition on weights, we prove absence of the phase transition. Notethat the condition does not depend on values of the prime $p$, and an analoguesfact is not true when the number of spins is finite. For homogeneous model itis shown that the recursive equation has only one solution under that conditionon weights. This means that there is only one $p$-adic Gibbs measure $\m_\l$.The boundedness of the measure is also established. Moreover, continuousdependence the measure $\m_\l$ on $\l$ is proved. At the end we formulate onelimit theorem for $\m_\l$.
label: human

text: This paper investigates the construction and properties of $p$-adic Gibbs measures for the Potts model with a countable set of states on a Cayley tree of order $k$. We generalize the traditional finite-state $p$-adic Potts model by considering an infinite state space within the framework of non-Archimedean analysis. The model is characterized through a system of $p$-adic functional equations that represent the consistency conditions for the measures on the tree structure. By analyzing these equations, we establish the existence of translation-invariant $p$-adic Gibbs measures under specific constraints on the model's coupling constants. Our study reveals that the behavior of these measures is significantly influenced by the $p$-adic valuation of the parameters and the topological structure of the tree. We provide sufficient conditions for the uniqueness of the $p$-adic Gibbs measure, as well as scenarios where multiple measures may emerge, indicating a phase transition.
label: llm

text: We derive constraints that must be satisfied by the sources of ~10^{15} to~10^{18} eV cosmic rays, under the assumption that the sources are Galactic. Weshow that while these constraints are not satisfied by ordinary supernovae(SNe), which are believed to be the sources of <10^{15} eV cosmic rays, theymay be satisfied by the recently discovered class of trans-relativisticsupernovae (TRSNe), which were observed in association with gamma-ray bursts.We define TRSNe as SNe that deposit a large fraction, f_R>10^{-2}, of theirkinetic energy in mildly relativistic, \gamma\beta>1, ejecta. The high velocityejecta enable particle acceleration to ~10^{18} eV, and the large value of f_R(compared to f_R~10^{-7} for ordinary SNe) ensures that if TRSNe produce theobserved ~10^{18} eV cosmic ray flux, they do not overproduce the flux at lowerenergies. This, combined with the estimated rate and energy production ofTRSNe, imply that Galactic TRSNe may be the sources of cosmic rays withenergies up to ~10^{18}eV .
label: human

text: Trans-relativistic supernovae (TRSNe) occupy a critical energetic regime between standard supernovae and highly relativistic gamma-ray bursts, characterized by shock velocities that approach the speed of light. We investigate the efficiency of diffusive shock acceleration in these events and calculate the resulting energy spectra for both protons and heavier nuclei. Our analysis demonstrates that the high energy density and shock velocities of TRSNe allow for the acceleration of particles to energies far exceeding the "knee" of the cosmic ray spectrum, potentially reaching the ultra-high-energy regime. Consequently, these results suggest that TRSNe are primary candidates for the origin of extragalactic cosmic rays and provide a theoretical framework for interpreting future multi-messenger observations.
label: llm

text: We give two classes of spherically symmetric exact solutions of the couplegravitational and electromagnetic fields with charged source in the tetradtheory of gravitation. The first solution depends on an arbitrary function$H({R},t)$. The second solution depends on a constant parameter $\eta$. Thesesolutions reproduce the same metric, i.e., the Reissner--Nordstr$\ddot{o}$mmetric. If the arbitrary function which characterizes the first solution andthe arbitrary constant of the second solution are set to be zero, then the twoexact solutions will coincide with each other. We then calculate the energycontent associated with these analytic solutions using the superpotentialmethod. In particular, we examine whether these solutions meet the conditionwhich M{\o}ller required for a consistent energy-momentum complex: Namely, wecheck whether the total four-momentum of an isolated system behaves as afour-vector under Lorentz transformations. It is then found that the arbitraryfunction should decrease faster than $1/\sqrt{R}$ for $R\to \infty$. It is alsoshown that the second exact solution meets the M{\o}ller's condition.
label: human

text: This paper investigates the representation of the Reissner-Nordström spacetime within the framework of the tetrad theory of gravitation, also known as teleparallel gravity. Unlike standard General Relativity which relies on the metric tensor, this theory utilizes a tetrad field as the fundamental dynamical variable to describe the gravitational field.
