To incorporate the effects of a charged source, we couple the gravitational field equations with the energy-momentum tensor of a static, spherically symmetric electromagnetic field. We employ a specific set of field equations derived from a Lagrangian density that is constructed from the torsion tensor and its invariants. A specific diagonal tetrad is proposed and analyzed to determine its suitability in satisfying the resulting electro-vacuum field equations. It is demonstrated that the derived solution successfully recovers the metric components associated with the classical Reissner-Nordström black hole under the appropriate coordinate transformations. Furthermore, we calculate the non-vanishing components of the torsion tensor and the corresponding energy distribution for this specific geometric configuration.
label: llm

text: We theoretically demonstrate the formation of multiple bi-stability regionsin the temperature pattern on the interface between a cuprous oxide quantumwell and DCM2:CA:PS organic compound. The Frenkel molecular exciton of the DCM2is brought into resonance with the $1S$ quadrupole Wannier-Mott exciton in thecuprous oxide by "solvatochromism" with CA. The resulting hybrid is thermalizedwith surrounding helium bath. This leads to strongly non-linear temperaturedependence of the laser field detuning from the quadrupole exciton energy bandwhich is associated with the temperature induced red shift of the Wannierexciton energy. Numerical up and down-scan for the detuning revealshysteresis-like temperature distribution. The obtained \emph{multiple}bi-stability regions are at least three orders of magnitude bigger ($meV$) thanthe experimentally observed bi-stability in bulk cuprous oxide ($\mu eV$). Theeffective absorption curve exhibits highly asymmetrical behavior for theFrenkel-like (above the $1S$ energy) and Wannier-like (below the $1S$ energy)branches of the hybrid.
label: human

text: This paper investigates the nonlinear optical properties of hybrid heterostructures composed of cuprous oxide ($Cu_2O$) and organic semiconductors. While traditional photo-thermal effects are well-documented, achieving robust and tunable bi-stability remains a significant challenge for the development of next-generation photonic switching devices. We develop a comprehensive theoretical framework to analyze the coupled interaction between incident radiation and the thermal-electronic dynamics at the $Cu_2O$/organic interface. The results demonstrate that the synergy between the high thermal sensitivity of $Cu_2O$ and the large thermo-optic coefficients of the organic layer significantly lowers the power threshold required for bi-stable switching. Compared to monolithic inorganic configurations, the hybrid heterostructure architecture exhibits a pronounced enhancement in the hysteresis width of the optical transmission spectrum. Time-resolved simulations further reveal that the dynamical response and stability of the system are critically governed by interfacial thermal resistance and carrier relaxation rates.
label: llm

text: The science of complex networks is a new interdisciplinary branch of sciencewhich has arisen recently on the interface of physics, biology, social andcomputer sciences, and others. Its main goal is to discover general lawsgoverning the creation and growth as well as processes taking place onnetworks, like e.g. the Internet, transportation or neural networks. It turnedout that most real-world networks cannot be simply reduced to a compound ofsome individual components. Fortunately, the statistical mechanics, being oneof pillars of modern physics, provides us with a very powerful set of tools andmethods for describing and understanding these systems. In this thesis, wewould like to present a consistent approach to complex networks based onstatistical mechanics, with the central role played by the concept ofstatistical ensemble of networks. We show how to construct such a theory andpresent some practical problems where it can be applied. Among them, we payattention to the problem of finite-size corrections and the dynamics of asimple model of mass transport on networks.
label: human

text: Recent years have witnessed a paradigm shift in the study of complex systems, driven by the realization that the underlying architecture of many real-world networks is neither purely regular nor completely random. This article provides a comprehensive overview of the statistical mechanics framework applied to the topology and evolution of complex networks. We explore how the principles of equilibrium and non-equilibrium statistical physics can be utilized to characterize the macroscopic properties of large-scale graphs. Central to this approach is the analysis of degree distributions, clustering coefficients, and the emergence of scale-free architectures through mechanisms such as preferential attachment. Furthermore, we examine the critical phenomena associated with these structures, including phase transitions in network connectivity and the robustness of systems against random failures. The intersection of network topology and dynamical processes, such as spreading phenomena and synchronization, is also discussed in the context of statistical ensembles. By treating nodes and edges as interacting components of a thermodynamic system.
label: llm

text: X-ray transients appeared in optically non-active galactic nuclei have beenobserved in recent years. The most popular model explaining this kind ofphenomena is the conventional tidal disruption model. In this model, when astar moves within the tidal radius of a black hole, part of the star materialswill fall into the black hole through an accretion disk, which gives rise tothe luminous flare. We propose that the X-ray emission may not necessarily comefrom radiation of the accretion disk alone. Instead, it may be related to ajet. As the jet travels in the interstellar medium, a shock is produced andsynchrotron radiation is expected. We compared the model light curve and thesynchrotron radiation spectrum with the observed data, and find that our modelexplains the observed light curve and late-time spectrum well. Our modelpredicts that these transient active galactic nuclei could be sources of thefuture gamma-ray satellites, e.g. GLAST and the emission region will beexpanding with time.
label: human

text: Most galaxies in the local universe harbor supermassive black holes (SMBHs) that exist in a primarily quiescent state, lacking the persistent accretion disks characteristic of active galactic nuclei. However, high-energy surveys have increasingly identified rare, dramatic X-ray outbursts originating from these otherwise dormant galactic centers. These transient phenomena are widely interpreted as tidal disruption events (TDEs), occurring when a star passes within the Roche radius of the central SMBH and is subsequently shredded by tidal forces. The resulting accretion of stellar debris produces a luminous flare that typically peaks in the soft X-ray or extreme ultraviolet bands. Observational data indicate that these flares can increase a galaxy's X-ray luminosity by several orders of magnitude before undergoing a characteristic power-law decay over months or years. By modeling the light curves and spectral evolution of these events, researchers can derive critical parameters such as the mass and spin of the underlying black hole.
label: llm

text: In this paper we derive new expected scaling relations for clusters withgiant radio halos in the framework of the re-acceleration scenario in asimplified, but physically motivated, form, namely: radio power (P_R) vs sizeof the radio emitting region (R_H), and P_R vs total cluster mass (M_H)contained in the emitting region and cluster velocity dispersion (sigma_H) inthis region.  We search for these correlations by analyzing the most recent radio and X-raydata available in the literature for a well known sample of clusters with giantradio halos. In particular we find a good correlation between P_R and R_H and avery tight ``geometrical'' scaling between M_H and R_H. From these correlationsP_R is also expected to scale with M_H and sigma_H and this is confirmed by ouranalysis. We show that all the observed trends can be well reconciled withexpectations in the case of a slight variation of the mean magnetic fieldstrength in the radio halo volume with M_H. A byproduct correlation between R_Hand sigma_H is also found, and can be further tested by optical studies. Inaddition, we find that observationally R_H scales non-linearly with the virialradius of the host cluster, and this immediately means that the fraction of thecluster volume which is radio emitting increases with cluster mass and thusthat the non-thermal component in clusters is not self-similar.
label: human

text: Radio halos represent large-scale synchrotron emission found in the central regions of merging galaxy clusters, providing crucial information about magnetic fields and relativistic particles. Despite significant progress, the precise physical mechanisms responsible for the energization of these electrons remain a subject of active research. In this study, we present a comprehensive analysis of new scaling relations between radio luminosity and various thermal properties of the hosting clusters. By utilizing an expanded sample of clusters, we demonstrate a strong correlation between radio power at 1.4 GHz and the total gravitational mass derived from recent X-ray and Sunyaev-Zel'dovich observations. Notably, our findings reveal a previously unobserved steepening in the scaling relations for clusters with lower masses and lower temperatures. These empirical results are found to be highly consistent with the theoretical predictions of the turbulent re-acceleration model, where cluster mergers supply the necessary energy to the particles. Overall, this work reinforces the scenario that radio halos are transient features linked to the dynamical evolution of the intra-cluster medium.
label: llm

text: Qualitatively new aspects of the (linear and non-linear) stability of shearedrelativistic (slab) jets are analyzed. The linear problem has been solved for awide range of jet models well inside the ultrarelativistic domain (flow Lorentzfactors up to 20; specific internal energies $\approx 60c^2$). As a distinctfeature of our work, we have combined the analytical linear approach withhigh-resolution relativistic hydrodynamical simulations, which has allowed usi) to identify, in the linear regime, resonant modes specific to therelativistic shear layer ii) to confirm the result of the linear analysis withnumerical simulations and, iii) more interestingly, to follow the instabilitydevelopment through the non-linear regime. We find that very high-orderreflection modes with dominant growth rates can modify the global, long-termstability of the relativistic flow. We discuss the dependence of these resonantmodes on the jet flow Lorentz factor and specific internal energy, and on theshear layer thickness. The results could have potential applications in thefield of extragalactic relativistic jets.
label: human

text: The Kelvin-Helmholtz instability plays a critical role in the stability and evolution of relativistic astrophysical jets. While traditional models often assume a sharp velocity discontinuity, realistic flows are characterized by finite shear layers that fundamentally alter the instability's behavior. In this study, we perform a comprehensive linear stability analysis of transverse perturbations in sheared relativistic flows using a combination of numerical and analytical techniques. Our results identify the emergence of resonant modes that occur when the perturbation phase velocity coincides with the local flow speed within the shear profile. We find that these resonant modes significantly enhance growth rates across a wide range of Mach numbers and Lorentz factors compared to standard Kelvin-Helmholtz modes. These findings offer a new framework for understanding the structural evolution and energy dissipation processes occurring at the boundaries of high-energy cosmic outflows.
label: llm

text: We discuss in this article a property of action of groups by isometriescalled "well displacing". An action is said to be well displacing, if thedisplacement function is equivalent to the the displacement function for theaction on the Cayley graph. We relate this property with the fact that orbitmaps are quasi-isometric embeddings. We first describe countrexamples thatshows this two notions are unrelated in general. On the other hand we explainthat for a certain class of groups -- in particular hyperbolic groups -- thesetwo properties are equivalent. In the course of our discussion, we introduce anintrinsic property of the group -- that we called the U-property -- which saysquantitatively how the norm an element is controlled by the translation lengthof finitely many related conjugacy classes. This property play a central rolein our discussion.
label: human

text: This paper investigates the quantitative geometric properties of well displacing representations for discrete groups acting on metric spaces. We define a representation as well displacing if the translation length of group elements is bounded below by a linear function of their word length. The primary objective is to characterize the interplay between these displacement properties and the coarse geometry of the resulting orbit maps. Utilizing techniques from geometric group theory, we establish that well displacing representations are closely linked to the existence of quasi-isometric orbit embeddings. We prove that for certain classes of hyperbolic groups, any representation satisfying a stable displacement condition must induce a Morse orbit map. Additionally, the study explores how these representations behave under small perturbations within the character variety of the group.
label: llm

text: We have employed a 3-d energy-conserving radiation MHD code to simulate thevertical structure and thermodynamics of a shearing box whose parameters werechosen so that the radiation and gas pressures would be comparable. The upperlayers of this disk segment are magnetically-dominated, creating conditionsappropriate for both photon bubble and Parker instabilities. We find littleevidence for photon bubbles, even though the simulation has enough spatialresolution to see them and their predicted growth rates are high. On the otherhand, there is strong evidence for Parker instabilities, and they appear todominate the evolution of the magnetically supported surface layers. The diskphotosphere is complex, with large density inhomogeneities at both thescattering and effective (thermalization) photospheres of the evolvinghorizontally-averaged structure. Both the dominant magnetic support and theinhomogeneities are likely to have strong effects on the spectrum andpolarization of thermal photons emerging from the disk atmosphere. Theinhomogeneities are also large enough to affect models of reflection spectrafrom the atmospheres of accretion disks.
label: human

text: We investigate the vertical surface structure of an accretion disk annulus within the transition regime where radiation and gas pressures are of comparable magnitude. Utilizing three-dimensional radiation magnetohydrodynamic simulations in a local shearing box, we examine the interplay between turbulent transport and radiative diffusion. Our analysis reveals that this intermediate pressure state leads to a distinct density stratification that differs from both radiation-dominated and gas-dominated extremes. We find that the disk photosphere is notably extended due to the significant contribution of radiation pressure to hydrostatic equilibrium in the upper layers. Furthermore, the simulations demonstrate that magnetic buoyancy effectively transports energy to the surface, resulting in a temperature profile that remains relatively flat across a wide range of optical depths. These structural features suggest that standard thin-disk models may oversimplify the boundary conditions necessary for accurate spectral modeling. Ultimately, these results provide critical insights into the stability and observational signatures of accretion disks in systems such as luminous X-ray binaries and active galactic nuclei.
label: llm

text: High-energy gamma-rays propagating in the intergalactic medium can interactwith background infrared photons to produce e+e- pairs, resulting in theabsorption of the intrinsic gamma-ray spectrum. TeV observations of the distantblazar 1ES 1101-232 were thus recently used to put an upper limit on theinfrared extragalactic background light density. The created pairs canupscatter background photons to high energies, which in turn may pair produce,thereby initiating a cascade. The pairs diffuse on the extragalactic magneticfield (EMF) and cascade emission has been suggested as a means for measuringits intensity. Limits on the IR background and EMF are reconsidered taking intoaccount cascade emissions. The cascade equations are solved numerically.Assuming a power-law intrinsic spectrum, the observed 100 MeV - 100 TeVspectrum is found as a function of the intrinsic spectral index and theintensity of the EMF. Cascades emit mainly at or below 100 GeV. The observedTeV spectrum appears softer than for pure absorption when cascade emission istaken into account. The upper limit on the IR photon background is found to berobust. Inversely, the intrinsic spectra needed to fit the TeV data areuncomfortably hard when cascade emission makes a significant contribution tothe observed spectrum. An EMF intensity around 1e-8 nG leads to acharacteristic spectral hump in the GLAST band. Higher EMF intensities divertthe pairs away from the line-of-sight and the cascade contribution to thespectrum becomes negligible.
label: human

text: The propagation of high-energy gamma rays through the intergalactic medium is significantly influenced by their interaction with the extragalactic background light (EBL). As these energetic photons travel from distant cosmic sources such as blazars, they undergo electron-positron pair production upon colliding with EBL photons. This interaction results in a significant attenuation of the primary high-energy gamma-ray flux above specific energy thresholds. The resulting ultra-relativistic electrons and positrons subsequently undergo inverse Compton scattering with the cosmic microwave background. This secondary interaction initiates an electromagnetic cascade that redistributes the energy from the primary photons into a lower-energy spectral component. Analyzing these cascades provides a crucial tool for probing the intensity and spectral shape of the EBL across different cosmological epochs. Furthermore, the spatial and temporal characteristics of the secondary gamma-ray emission are highly sensitive to the properties of the intergalactic magnetic field (IGMF). Small-scale magnetic field fluctuations can deflect the charged particles within the cascade, thereby broadening the angular distribution of the observed radiation. Recent observational data from imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescopes and space-based detectors offer new constraints on these cascading processes. Current theoretical models must account for both the evolving density of the EBL and the potential impact of plasma instabilities on the energy loss of pairs.
label: llm

text: To enlighten the nature of the order-disorder and order-order transitions inblock copolymer melts confined in narrow capillaries we analyze peculiaritiesof the conventional Landau weak crystallization theory of systems confined tocylindrical geometry. This phenomenological approach provides a quantitativeclassification of the cylindrical ordered morphologies by expansion of theorder parameter spatial distribution into the eigenfunctions of the Laplaceoperator. The symmetry of the resulting ordered morphologies is shown tostrongly depend both on the boundary conditions (wall preference) and the ratioof the cylinder radius and the wave length of the critical order parameterfluctuations, which determine the bulk ordering of the system underconsideration. In particular, occurrence of the helical morphologies is arather general consequence of the imposed cylindrical symmetry for narrowenough capillaries. We discuss also the ODT and OOT involving some othersimplest morphologies. The presented results are relevant also to otherordering systems as charge-density waves appearing under addition of an ionicsolute to a solvent in its critical region, weakly charged polyelectrolytesolutions in poor solvent, microemulsions etc.
label: human

text: The structural organization of particles confined within narrow geometries exhibits complex symmetries that differ significantly from bulk phases. This paper examines the emergence of radial, angular, and helical ordering in systems constrained by cylindrical capillary walls. Through high-resolution simulations, we observe that particles spontaneously arrange into discrete concentric shells to minimize local free energy. Within these layers, the competition between geometric frustration and packing density generates intricate angular correlations and long-range helical motifs. We quantify how the structural transition between different helical states depends critically on the dimensionless ratio of the particle diameter to the capillary radius. These results enhance our understanding of phase behavior in extreme confinement and have practical implications for the development of advanced nanofluidic devices.
label: llm

text: This thesis consists of two parts which share only a slight overlap.  The first part is concerned with the study of ideals in the ring$C^\infty(M,R)$ of smooth functions on a compact smooth manifold M or moregenerally submodules of a finitely generated $C^\infty(M,R)$-module V. Wedefine a topology on the space of all submodules of V of a fixed finitecodimension d. Its main property is that it is compact Hausdorff and, in thecase of ideals in the ring itself, it contains as a subspace the configurationspace of d distinct unordered points in M and therefore gives a"compactification" of this configuration space. We present a concretedescription of this space for low codimensions.  The main focus is then put on the second part which is concerned with ageneralization of Vassiliev's h-principle. This principle in its simplest formasserts that the jet prolongation map $j^r:C^\infty(M,E)\to\Gamma(J^r(M,E))$,defined on the space of smooth maps from a compact manifold M to a Euclideanspace E and with target the space of smooth sections of the jet bundle$J^r(M,E)$, is a cohomology isomorphism when restricted to certain"nonsingular" subsets (these are defined in terms of a certain subset$R\subseteq J^r(M,E)$). Our generalization then puts this theorem in a moregeneral setting of topological $C^\infty(M,R)$-modules. As a reward we get astrengthening of this result asserting that all the homotopy fibres have zerohomology.
label: human

text: Vassiliev's h-principle provides a powerful framework for studying the topology of spaces of smooth maps that avoid specified discriminant sets. While traditionally applied to spaces of embeddings and non-singular maps, the scope of this principle has remained constrained by the specific geometry of the avoided strata. In this paper, we propose a comprehensive generalization of Vassiliev’s result that encompasses a wider variety of multi-singularity constraints and target manifolds. By employing a localized scanning argument combined with a refined spectral sequence analysis, we demonstrate that the approximation holds for mapping spaces under milder regularity conditions. We establish that the natural inclusion of the space of maps avoiding high-codimension singularities into the space of formal sections is a weak homotopy equivalence. This extension is further illustrated through the computation of the cohomology of spaces of maps with bounded multiplicity, which recovers and extends several classical results in singularity theory. Ultimately, this generalized h-principle offers a unified perspective on the relationship between local differential constraints and the global topology of functional spaces.
label: llm

text: We explore the phase structure of two-color and two-flavor QCD in the spaceof the quark chemical potential \mu_q and the isospin chemical potential \mu_I.Using a mean-field model we calculate the chiral and diquark condensates,\sigma and \Delta, self-consistently. In weak coupling and in the chiral limit,we confirm the interval of the isospin chemical potential,0.71\Delta_0<\mu_I<0.75\Delta_0, in which a single plane-waveLarkin-Ovchinnikov-Fulde-Ferrell (LOFF) phase is favored over isotropicsuperfluidity and normal quark matter. The LOFF window becomes slightly widerat high density. For stronger coupling with nonzero quark mass, which isrelevant to currently available numerical simulations in lattice two-color QCD,the single plane-wave LOFF phase appears only at sufficiently high density. Theprediction obtained for the LOFF region could be tested with lattice since wecan prove that the present system is free from the fermion sign problem. Wedraw the energy landscape on which local minima corresponding to the isotropicsuperfluid phase and the LOFF phase and a local maximum corresponding to thegapless phase are manifest. Our results clearly illustrate the path from thethe unstable gapless phase down to the LOFF phase.
label: human

text: This study investigates the emergence and stability of the Larkin-Ovchinnikov-Fulde-Ferrell (LOFF) state within the framework of two-color quark matter. Unlike standard three-color QCD, two-color QCD offers a unique environment for exploring dense matter physics because it is free from the numerical sign problem. We consider the effects of a chemical potential mismatch between different quark flavors, which naturally leads to the formation of non-zero momentum Cooper pairs. Utilizing an effective Nambu-Jona-Lasinio model, we derive the Ginzburg-Landau expansion for the free energy to characterize the inhomogeneous superconducting phase. Our analysis explores how the spatial modulation of the diquark condensate varies across a wide range of temperatures and densities. The results indicate that the LOFF state remains energetically favorable over the homogeneous phase in specific regions of the phase diagram where asymmetry is high. These conclusions contribute to a deeper understanding of color superconductivity and may have significant implications for the internal structure of dense astrophysical objects.
label: llm

text: We present the SFI++ dataset, a homogeneously derived catalog of photometricand rotational properties and the Tully-Fisher distances and peculiarvelocities derived from them. We make use of digital optical images, opticallong-slit spectra, and global HI line profiles to extract parameters ofrelevance to disk scaling relations, incorporating several previously publisheddatasets as well as a new photometric sample of some 2000 objects. According tothe completeness of available redshift samples over the sky area, we exploitboth a modified percolation algorithm and the Voronoi-Delaunay method to assignindividual galaxies to groups as well as clusters, thereby reducing scatterintroduced by local orbital motions. We also provide corrections to thepeculiar velocities for both homogeneous and inhomogeneous Malmquist bias,making use of the 2MASS Redshift Survey density field to approximate largescale structure. We summarize the sample selection criteria, corrections madeto raw observational parameters, the grouping techniques, and our procedure forderiving peculiar velocities. The final SFI++ peculiar velocity catalog of 4861field and cluster galaxies is large enough to permit the study not just of theglobal statistics of large scale flows but also of the {\it details} of thelocal velocity field.
label: human

text: This paper presents the second installment of the SFI++ project, providing a comprehensive I-band Tully-Fisher (TF) catalog designed for the study of cosmic flows in the local universe. We detail the derivation of galaxy distances and peculiar velocities for a large sample of spiral galaxies using high-quality photometric and spectroscopic data. The TF relation is calibrated with careful consideration of observational errors and internal extinction to ensure high precision in distance estimates. We implement rigorous corrections for Malmquist bias and other selection effects, which are essential for an unbiased interpretation of the peculiar velocity field. The resulting dataset features enhanced sky coverage and sampling density compared to previous iterations, offering a detailed map of the local velocity distribution. This catalog serves as a fundamental tool for analyzing the large-scale structure of the universe and testing cosmological models against observed matter distributions.
label: llm

text: At the quantization of fields, due to the non-linear character of the timereversal, the creation-annihilation operators for the negative frequency modesshould be replaced to the operators of antiparticles not directly in the fieldoperators, but in the operator products. For the standard minimal Lagrangians(asymmetrical under the complex conjugated fields) it is shown that the chargeconjugation (C-) symmetry conditions for the Hamiltonian and the chargeoperator lead to the identities for the operator products allowing one toreplace the negative frequency operator products to the positive frequencyones. At the same time the operators in observables become normal ordered andthe zero-point energy does not appear. Only the symmetrized under the fieldoperators Lagrangians lead to the zero-point energy. The confrontation by theexperiments of the such C-symmetric quantization of fields and the solutionsome of the vacuum energy problems are discussed.
label: human

text: Traditional methods of field quantization frequently result in divergent vacuum energy densities, necessitating the manual application of normal ordering to obtain finite physical results. This paper introduces a novel quantization scheme based on $C$-symmetry, where charge conjugation is treated as a fundamental requirement for the construction of the operator algebra. Within this framework, we analyze the structural properties of field operators and show that a symmetric treatment of particles and antiparticles dictates a specific, unambiguous operator arrangement. We demonstrate that this $C$-symmetric approach naturally yields a vanishing vacuum expectation value for the Hamiltonian, effectively recovering the standard effects of normal ordering through intrinsic symmetry properties rather than *ad hoc* prescriptions. These results suggest that $C$-symmetry provides a more consistent theoretical foundation for field quantization, potentially simplifying the conceptual landscape of renormalization in quantum field theory.
label: llm

text: The field of extrasolar planets has rapidly expanded to include the detectionof planets with masses smaller than that of Uranus. Many of these are expectedto have little or no hydrogen and helium gas and we might find Earth analogsamong them. In this paper we describe our detailed interior models for a richvariety of such massive terrestrial and ocean planets in the 1-to-10 earth-massrange (super-Earths). The grid presented here allows the characterization ofthe bulk composition of super-Earths detected in transit and with a measuredmass. We show that, on average, planet radius measurements to better than 5%,combined with mass measurements to better than 10% would permit us todistinguish between an icy or rocky composition. This is due to the fact thatthere is a maximum radius a rocky terrestrial planet may achieve for a givenmass. Any value of the radius above this maximum terrestrial radius impliesthat the planet contains a large (> 10%) amount of water (ocean planet).
label: human

text: The discovery of thousands of exoplanets has revealed a significant population of super-Earths, yet their internal compositions remain largely speculative. This study develops detailed interior models to investigate the precision with which we can infer the bulk properties of these planets from observed masses and radii. We employ a multi-layered modeling framework incorporating iron cores, silicate mantles, and volatile layers under various thermodynamic conditions. Our analysis highlights the profound impact of compositional degeneracies, where significantly different internal structures result in nearly identical observable parameters. We further examine how uncertainties in the equations of state and mineralogical assumptions propagate into large uncertainties regarding the core mass fraction and water content. By incorporating stellar abundance data as a proxy for planetary composition, we demonstrate a potential reduction in these degeneracies, though significant ambiguity remains.
label: llm

text: We have explored the magnetic flux evolution and temperature variation in acoronal-hole region, using Big Bear Solar Observatory (BBSO) deep magnetogramsand {\it SOHO}/EIT images observed from 2005 October 10 to 14. For comparison,we also investigated a neighboring quiet region of the Sun. The coronal holeevolved from its mature stage to its disappearance during the observing period.We have obtained the following results: (1) When the coronal hole was welldeveloped on October 10, about 60 % of the magnetic flux was positive. The EUVbrightness was 420 counts pixel$^{-1}$, and the coronal temperature, estimatedfrom the line ratio of the EIT 195 {\AA} and 171 {\AA} images, was 1.07 MK. (2)On October 14, when the coronal hole had almost disappeared, 51 % of themagnetic flux was positive, the EUV radiance was 530 counts pixel$^{-1}$, andthe temperature was 1.10 MK. (3) In the neighboring quiet region, the fractionof positive flux varied between 0.49 and 0.47. The EUV brightness displayed anirregular variation, with a mean value of 870 counts pixel$^{-1}$. Thetemperature was almost constant at 1.11 MK during the five-day observation. Ourresults demonstrate that in a coronal hole less imbalance of the magnetic fluxin opposite polarities leads to stronger EUV brightness and higher coronaltemperatures.
label: human

text: Coronal holes are key regions of the solar atmosphere characterized by open magnetic field lines and the source of high-speed solar wind streams. However, the complex interplay between the evolution of small-scale magnetic structures and the local thermal properties within these regions is still under active investigation. This paper presents a detailed analysis of the magnetic field evolution and the associated temperature variations within an equatorial coronal hole. We utilized magnetograms from the Helioseismic and Magnetic Imager and multi-wavelength observations from the Atmospheric Imaging Assembly on board the Solar Dynamics Observatory. By applying Differential Emission Measure techniques, we derived the temporal changes in the plasma temperature and emission measure across the region of interest. Our analysis reveals that magnetic flux emergence and cancellation events are frequently associated with localized heating and temperature spikes. We further observed that the average temperature of the coronal hole fluctuates in response to the large-scale reorganization of the underlying magnetic network. These findings suggest that magnetic reconnection at the footpoints of open field lines plays a critical role in maintaining the thermal structure of the corona. This study provides new insights into the magnetic drivers of coronal heating and helps clarify the physical processes occurring at the base of the solar wind.
label: llm

text: Magnetic activity in the photosphere and chromosphere of the M dwarf EY Drais studied and possible correlations between the two are investigated usingphotometric observations in the V and R bands and optical and near infraredspectroscopy. The longitudinal spot configuration in the photosphere isobtained from the V band photometry, and the chromospheric structures areinvestigated using variations in the H alpha line profile and observations ofthe Paschen beta line. The shape of the V band light-curve indicates two activeregions on the stellar surface, about 0.4 in phase apart. The spectroscopicobservations show enhanced H alpha emission observed close to the phases of thephotometrically detected starspots. This could indicate chromospheric plagesassociated with the photospheric starspots. Some indications of prominencestructures are also seen. The chromospheric pressure is limited to logTR < -4based on the non-detection of emission in the Paschen beta wavelength region.
label: human

text: EY Dra is a highly active, rapidly rotating M-type dwarf known for its prominent magnetic activity and frequent flaring. This study presents a comprehensive multi-wavelength analysis of its photospheric and chromospheric behavior using both high-cadence photometry and medium-resolution spectroscopy. Photometric light curves reveal significant rotational modulation, which we model to characterize the spatial distribution and evolution of large-scale starspots on the stellar surface. Simultaneously, spectroscopic data show persistent and intense emission in the H$\alpha$ and Ca II H&K lines, signaling a robustly heated chromosphere. We determine a precise rotation period and identify several high-energy flare events that contribute significantly to the star's overall energy budget. Analysis of the Balmer decrement suggests that the chromospheric plasma resides in high-pressure environments typical of young, magnetically active stars. These findings reinforce EY Dra’s status as a key laboratory for studying the coupling between interior dynamos and atmospheric activity in low-mass stars.
label: llm

text: Pulse shape discrimination (PSD) is one of the most distinctive features ofliquid scintillators. Since the introduction of the scintillation techniques inthe field of particle detection, many studies have been carried out tocharacterize intrinsic properties of the most common liquid scintillatormixtures in this respect. Several application methods and algorithms able toachieve optimum discrimination performances have been developed. However, thevast majority of these studies have been performed on samples of smalldimensions. The Counting Test Facility, prototype of the solar neutrinoexperiment Borexino, as a 4 ton spherical scintillation detector immersed in1000 tons of shielding water, represents a unique opportunity to extend thesmall-sample PSD studies to a large-volume setup. Specifically, in this work weconsider two different liquid scintillation mixtures employed in CTF,illustrating for both the PSD characterization results obtained either with theprocessing of the scintillation waveform through the optimum Gatti's method, orvia a more conventional approach based on the charge content of thescintillation tail. The outcomes of this study, while interesting per se, arealso of paramount importance in view of the expected Borexino detectorperformances, where PSD will be an essential tool in the framework of thebackground rejection strategy needed to achieve the required sensitivity to thesolar neutrino signals.
label: human

text: This paper investigates the effectiveness of pulse-shape discrimination (PSD) techniques within the Counting Test Facility (CTF), the prototype for the Borexino solar neutrino experiment. The primary objective is to distinguish between alpha particles and beta-gamma events to significantly reduce internal radioactive backgrounds that mimic neutrino signals. Data were collected using a liquid scintillator composed of pseudocumene and PPO, monitored by a high-resolution array of photomultiplier tubes. We applied various statistical methods, including the optimum Gatti filter and the tail-to-total charge ratio, to analyze the scintillation decay time profiles of different particle species. Our results demonstrate a high degree of separation between particle types, achieving alpha rejection efficiencies exceeding 95% while maintaining minimal beta sacrifice. This level of discrimination is crucial for identifying radon-progeny contamination and other intrinsic backgrounds that interfere with the observation of the low-energy solar neutrino spectrum. Ultimately, these findings validate the PSD capabilities of the CTF and establish essential parameters for the successful background rejection strategies in large-scale liquid scintillator detectors.
label: llm

text: The expansion of ionization fronts in uniform and spherically symmetricpower-law density distributions is a well-studied topic. However, in manysituations, such as a star formed at the edge of a molecular cloud core, anoffset power-law density distribution would be more appropriate. In this papera few of the main issues of the formation and expansion of HII regions in suchmedia are outlined and results are presented for the particular cases where theunderlying power laws are 1/r^2 and 1/r^3. A simple criterion is developed fordetermining whether the initial photoionized region will be unbounded, whichdepends on the power-law exponent and the ratio of the equivalent Stroemgrenradius produced by the star in a uniform medium to the stellar offset distance.In the expansion stage, the ionized volumes will eventually become unboundedunless pressure balance with the external medium is reached before theionization front velocity becomes supersonic with respect to the ionized gas.
label: human

text: While traditional models often assume ionizing stars are centrally located within molecular clouds, many HII regions evolve around sources significantly displaced from the local density peak. This study investigates the dynamical expansion of an HII region within a power-law density distribution where the ionizing star is positioned at an arbitrary offset from the center. Our results demonstrate that this off-center positioning leads to highly asymmetric ionization fronts, characterized by accelerated growth toward lower-density regions and the early onset of "champagne flow" morphologies. These findings provide a critical theoretical framework for interpreting the non-spherical shapes and complex kinematic signatures frequently observed in ultra-compact and blister-type HII regions.
label: llm

text: The semiring-based constraint satisfaction problems (semiring CSPs), proposedby Bistarelli, Montanari and Rossi \cite{BMR97}, is a very general framework ofsoft constraints. In this paper we propose an abstraction scheme for softconstraints that uses semiring homomorphism. To find optimal solutions of theconcrete problem, the idea is, first working in the abstract problem andfinding its optimal solutions, then using them to solve the concrete problem.  In particular, we show that a mapping preserves optimal solutions if and onlyif it is an order-reflecting semiring homomorphism. Moreover, for a semiringhomomorphism $\alpha$ and a problem $P$ over $S$, if $t$ is optimal in$\alpha(P)$, then there is an optimal solution $\bar{t}$ of $P$ such that$\bar{t}$ has the same value as $t$ in $\alpha(P)$.
label: human

text: This paper addresses the computational complexity of soft constraint satisfaction problems by proposing a formal abstraction framework. The core of the methodology relies on semiring homomorphisms to map original problem values into a simplified abstract domain. This transformation preserves the algebraic structure of the constraints, allowing for the derivation of approximate solutions with significantly reduced search effort. We establish key theoretical properties, proving that the proposed abstraction ensures the soundness of the resulting optimal preference levels. Finally, our evaluation demonstrates that this semiring-based approach effectively balances the trade-off between computational efficiency and solution accuracy across various optimization scenarios.
label: llm

text: We study the IR-through-UV interstellar extinction curves towards 328Galactic B and late-O stars. We use a new technique which employs stellaratmosphere models in lieu of unreddened "standard" stars. This technique iscapable of virtually eliminating spectral mismatch errors in the curves. Italso allows a quantitative assessment of the errors and enables a rigoroustesting of the significance of relationships between various curve parameters,regardless of whether their uncertainties are correlated. Analysis of thecurves gives the following results: (1) In accord with our previous findings,the central position of the 2175 A extinction bump is mildly variable, itswidth is highly variable, and the two variations are unrelated. (2) Strongcorrelations are found among some extinction properties within the UV region,and within the IR region. (3) With the exception of a few curves with extreme(i.e., large) values of R(V), the UV and IR portions of Galactic extinctioncurves are not correlated with each other. (4) The large sightline-to-sightlinevariation seen in our sample implies that any average Galactic extinction curvewill always reflect the biases of its parent sample. (5) The use of an averagecurve to deredden a spectral energy distribution (SED) will result insignificant errors, and a realistic error budget for the dereddened SED mustinclude the observed variance of Galactic curves. While the observed largesightline-to-sightline variations, and the lack of correlation among thevarious features of the curves, make it difficult to meaningfully characterizeaverage extinction properties, they demonstrate that extinction curves respondsensitively to local conditions. Thus, each curve contains potentially uniqueinformation about the grains along its sightline.
label: human

text: Interstellar extinction curves serve as a primary diagnostic tool for investigating the physical and chemical properties of cosmic dust. In this fifth installment of our series, we provide a detailed examination of the extinction morphology spanning from the infrared (IR) to the far-ultraviolet (UV) wavelengths. The study utilizes a vast dataset of stellar sightlines to derive a self-consistent set of extinction parameters across diverse galactic environments. We find that the general shape of these curves is largely dictated by the ratio of total-to-selective extinction, $R_V$, but significant regional anomalies persist. Our analysis highlights the morphological diversity of the 2175 Å extinction bump, demonstrating that its position and width vary independently of other curve features. In the ultraviolet, the curvature of the far-UV rise is shown to be more variable than predicted by traditional one-parameter models. Conversely, the infrared portion of the spectrum displays a remarkable degree of uniformity across different interstellar environments. We quantify the correlations between these different spectral regions to identify underlying physical processes such as grain coagulation and shattering. The data suggest that variations in the UV slope are primarily driven by the relative abundance of small carbonaceous grains. Our findings challenge existing assumptions regarding the universality of the extinction law in high-redshift environments. This comprehensive analysis establishes a new benchmark for calibrating the effects of dust on astronomical observations across the electromagnetic spectrum.
label: llm

text: Random walks on expander graphs were thoroughly studied, with the importantmotivation that, under some natural conditions, these walks mix quickly andprovide an efficient method of sampling the vertices of a graph. Alon,Benjamini, Lubetzky and Sodin studied non-backtracking random walks on regulargraphs, and showed that their mixing rate may be up to twice as fast as that ofthe simple random walk. As an application, they showed that the maximal numberof visits to a vertex, made by a non-backtracking random walk of length $n$ ona high-girth $n$-vertex regular expander, is typically $(1+o(1))\frac{\logn}{\log\log n}$, as in the case of the balls and bins experiment. They furtherasked whether one can establish the precise distribution of the visits such awalk makes.  In this work, we answer the above question by combining a generalized form ofBrun's sieve with some extensions of the ideas in Alon et al. Let $N_t$ denotethe number of vertices visited precisely $t$ times by a non-backtracking randomwalk of length $n$ on a regular $n$-vertex expander of fixed degree and girth$g$. We prove that if $g=\omega(1)$, then for any fixed $t$, $N_t/n$ istypically $\frac{1}{\mathrm{e}t!}+o(1)$. Furthermore, if $g=\Omega(\log\logn)$, then $N_t/n$ is typically $\frac{1+o(1)}{\mathrm{e}t!}$ uniformly on all$t \leq (1-o(1))\frac{\log n}{\log\log n}$ and 0 for all $t \geq(1+o(1))\frac{\log n}{\log\log n}$. In particular, we obtain the above resulton the typical maximal number of visits to a single vertex, with an improvedthreshold window. The essence of the proof lies in showing that variablescounting the number of visits to a set of sufficiently distant vertices areasymptotically independent Poisson variables.
label: human

text: Non-backtracking random walks have gained significant attention due to their applications in network analysis and spectral graph theory. This paper investigates the distribution of visits to a small target set of vertices by a non-backtracking random walk on a large, locally tree-like graph. We specifically focus on the regime where the target set is rare enough that the expected number of visits remains constant as the graph size grows. Our primary goal is to establish conditions under which the number of visits to this set can be accurately modeled by a Poisson distribution. We prove that for a sequence of $d$-regular graphs with high girth, the total number of hits converges in total variation distance to a Poisson law. The results highlight the fundamental differences between standard random walks and non-backtracking variants, particularly regarding the correlation of successive steps. To achieve this, we employ the Chen-Stein method, adapted to account for the local constraints inherent in non-backtracking transitions. We provide explicit error bounds that depend on the expansion properties of the underlying graph and the size of the target set. Furthermore, we extend our analysis to include excursions and return times, demonstrating that the inter-arrival times between visits are approximately exponential. These findings offer a robust framework for understanding hitting time distributions in sparse networks where backtracking is prohibited. Ultimately, our work provides theoretical justification for using Poisson limits in the study of search processes and community detection algorithms.
label: llm

text: Typical astronomical spectrographs have a resolution ranging between a fewhundred to 200.000. Deconvolution and correlation techniques are being employedwith a significance down to 1/1000 th of a pixel. HeAr and ThAr lamps areusually used for calibration in low and high resolution spectroscopy,respectively. Unfortunately, the emitted lines typically cover only a smallfraction of the spectrometer's spectral range. Furthermore, their exactposition depends strongly on environmental conditions. A problem is the strongintensity variation between different (intensity ratios {>300). In addition,the brightness of the lamps is insufficient to illuminate a spectrograph via anintegrating sphere, which in turn is important to calibrate a long-slitspectrograph, as this is the only way to assure a uniform illumination of thespectrograph pupil.  Laboratory precision laser spectroscopy has experienced a major advance withthe development of optical frequency combs generated by pulsed femto-secondlasers. These lasers emit a broad spectrum (several hundred nanometers in thevisible and near infra-red) of equally-spaced "comb" lines with almost uniformintensity (intensity ratios typically <10). Self-referencing of the laserestablishes a precise ruler in frequency space that can be stabilized to the10e-18 uncertainty level, reaching absolute frequency inaccuracies at the10e-12 level per day when using the Global Positioning System's (GPS) timesignal as the reference. The exploration of the merits of this new technologyholds the promise for broad-band, highly accurate and reproducible calibrationrequired for reliable operation of current and next generation astronomicspectrometers.
label: human

text: High-precision spectroscopy remains a cornerstone of modern physics, chemistry, and observational astronomy. Traditional wavelength calibration sources, such as thorium-argon lamps and gas absorption cells, are increasingly limited by their inherent spectral instability and non-uniform line distribution. This paper reviews the emergence of optical frequency combs (OFCs) as the next generation of calibration standards, offering unprecedented accuracy and long-term stability. By providing a vast array of phase-locked, equidistant spectral lines, OFCs act as a "frequency ruler" that is directly traceable to the SI second via atomic clocks. We explore the technical architectures required to adapt these combs for diverse spectroscopic needs, including the necessary use of Fabry-Pérot cavities for mode-filtering. In the field of astronomy, these specialized "astro-combs" enable the detection of Earth-like exoplanets by achieving sub-meter-per-second precision in radial velocity measurements. Beyond astrophysics, OFC-based calibration is revolutionizing laboratory-based molecular spectroscopy by facilitating broad-bandwidth measurements with extremely high resolution. The transition from bulky mode-locked lasers to chip-scale micro-combs represents a significant leap toward portable and robust calibration systems for field deployment. This shift addresses the historical challenges of line-spacing mismatch and system complexity that previously hindered widespread industrial adoption. Experimental results demonstrate that these new techniques can improve instrumental precision by several orders of magnitude compared to legacy methods. Ultimately, the integration of optical frequency combs into spectrometer design marks a transformative era for metrology and high-resolution spectral analysis.
label: llm

text: Mixed action lattice calculations allow for an additive lattice spacingdependent mass renormalization of mesons composed of one sea and one valencequark, regardless of the type of fermion discretization methods used in thevalence and sea sectors. The value of the mass renormalization depends upon thelattice actions used. This mixed meson mass shift is an important latticeartifact to determine for mixed action calculations; because it modifies thepion mass, it plays a central role in the low energy dynamics of all hadroniccorrelation functions. We determine the leading order, $\mathcal{O}(a^2)$, andnext to leading order, $\mathcal{O}(a^2 m_\pi^2)$, additive mass shift of\textit{valence-sea} mesons for a mixed lattice action with domain-wall valencefermions and rooted staggered sea fermions, relevant to the majority of currentlarge scale mixed action lattice efforts. We find that on the asqtad improvedcoarse MILC lattices, this additive mass shift is well parameterized in latticeunits by $\Delta(am)^2 = 0.034(2) -0.06(2) (a m_\pi)^2$, which in physicalunits, using $a=0.125$ fm, corresponds to $\Delta(m)^2 = (291\pm 8\textrm{MeV})^2 -0.06(2) m_\pi^2$. In terms of the mixed action effective fieldtheory parameters, the corresponding mass shift is given by $a^2\Delta_\mathrm{Mix} = (316 \pm 4 \textrm{MeV})^2$ at leading order plusnext-to-leading order corrections including the necessary chiral logarithms forthis mixed action calculation, determined in this work. Within the precision ofour calculation, one can not distinguish between the full next-to-leading ordereffective field theory analysis of this additive mixed meson mass shift and theparameterization given above.
label: human

text: We present a systematic study of meson masses using a mixed-action lattice quantum chromodynamics (QCD) framework. This approach employs chiral domain-wall valence quarks calculated on top of ensembles of asqtad-improved staggered sea fermion configurations. The numerical simulations are performed across multiple lattice spacings and sea quark masses to rigorously explore the scaling behavior of the theory. We specifically calculate the masses of pseudoscalar mesons consisting of various combinations of light and strange valence quarks. The resulting spectrum is analyzed within the framework of mixed-action chiral perturbation theory to account for discretization effects and unitarization violations inherent in the mixed-action setup. Our results demonstrate that the domain-wall valence action effectively preserves chiral symmetry properties even at finite lattice spacing. These findings provide a crucial benchmark for future high-precision calculations of hadronic matrix elements and decay constants in the transition to the physical point.
label: llm

text: We study semiparametric efficiency bounds and efficient estimation ofparameters defined through general moment restrictions with missing data.Identification relies on auxiliary data containing information about thedistribution of the missing variables conditional on proxy variables that areobserved in both the primary and the auxiliary database, when such distributionis common to the two data sets. The auxiliary sample can be independent of theprimary sample, or can be a subset of it. For both cases, we derive bounds whenthe probability of missing data given the proxy variables is unknown, or known,or belongs to a correctly specified parametric family. We find that theconditional probability is not ancillary when the two samples are independent.For all cases, we discuss efficient semiparametric estimators. An estimatorbased on a conditional expectation projection is shown to require milderregularity conditions than one based on inverse probability weighting.
label: human

text: This paper investigates the problem of achieving semiparametric efficiency in Generalized Method of Moments (GMM) frameworks when primary datasets are supplemented with auxiliary information. We develop a unified estimation framework that incorporates auxiliary moments or summary statistics to improve the precision of structural parameter estimates. By deriving the semiparametric efficiency bound for this setting, we characterize the optimal way to combine heterogeneous data sources without imposing restrictive distributional assumptions. Our proposed estimator is shown to be asymptotically efficient and remains robust even when the auxiliary data comes from a population with slightly different characteristics. Numerical simulations and empirical results demonstrate that integrating auxiliary data leads to substantial efficiency gains over standard GMM estimators that rely solely on primary data.
label: llm

text: The new scheme of stochastic quantization is proposed. This quantizationprocedure is equivalent to the deformation of an algebra of observables in themanner of deformation quantization with an imaginary deformation parameter (thePlanck constant). We apply this method to the models of nonrelativistic andrelativistic particles interacting with an electromagnetic field. In the firstcase we establish the equivalence of such a quantization to the Fokker-Planckequation with a special force. The application of the proposed quantizationprocedure to the model of a relativistic particle results in a relativisticgeneralization of the Fokker-Planck equation in the coordinate space, which inthe absence of the electromagnetic field reduces to the relativistic diffusion(heat) equation. The stationary probability distribution functions for astochastically quantized particle diffusing under a barrier and a particle inthe potential of a harmonic oscillator are derived.
label: human

text: The generalization of the diffusion equation to the relativistic regime remains a central challenge in both statistical mechanics and quantum field theory. This study presents a formal derivation of the relativistic diffusion equation through the framework of stochastic quantization. By introducing a fictitious stochastic time, we define a Langevin equation that governs the evolution of a scalar field within a four-dimensional Lorentzian manifold. We demonstrate that the associated Fokker-Planck equation leads directly to a covariant diffusion operator that maintains formal consistency with the principles of special relativity. The derived equation successfully avoids the causality issues inherent in earlier phenomenological models while recovering the standard heat equation in the non-relativistic limit. These results provide a rigorous mathematical foundation for modeling dissipative processes in high-energy physics and relativistic fluid dynamics.
label: llm

text: The recent PRB, henceforth referred as Ref.[1], experimentally resolves theintrinsic shape of the c-axis current-voltage characteristics (IVC) of HTSC anddemonstrates that at sufficiently high heat loads the heating-induced IVCnonlinearities exceed the intrinsic ones so radically that the latter might besafely ignored.  The author of the comment fails to take account of the experimental findingsby Ref.[1] and seeks to cast doubt on all its conclusions through reference toa brush-like IVC, which is claimed to be free of heating. I will show that thisclaim lacks substantiation; indeed it can be stated with certainty that the IVCis not free from heating. I will further show that the data selected for thiscomment make it possible to explore for the first time the effect oftemperature on a range of loads where the genuine response is not hidden byheating and to demonstrate for the first time that $R(T)$ of the same sample isresponsible for a rich variety of IVC behaviours taken above and below $T_c$ atbath temperatures spanned over 180K. Thus these data in fact provide strongnovel evidence in favour of the major conclusions by Ref.[1], in particular theextrinsic cause of the key findings by intrinsic tunnelling spectroscopy.
label: human

text: This reply addresses the specific concerns raised regarding our previous investigation into the fundamental characteristics of intrinsic tunnelling in layered materials. We provide a point-by-point clarification to demonstrate that the phenomena originally reported are indeed intrinsic to the material's electronic structure rather than measurement artefacts. The critique primarily suggests that certain spectral features could arise from extrinsic heating or contact non-uniformities. However, a rigorous analysis of our current-voltage characteristics across varying temperatures reveals a consistency that is incompatible with the suggested artefact models. We further introduce supplementary data showing that the observed quasiparticle peaks maintain their integrity even under high-bias conditions that would typically destabilize superficial layers. This evidence reinforces the distinction between universal intrinsic properties and the localized, sample-dependent irregularities highlighted in the comment. By clarifying the experimental boundary conditions, we show that our original interpretations provide the most coherent explanation for the collective data set. Ultimately, the validity of our original findings is upheld, and the essence of intrinsic tunnelling remains clearly distinguishable from the proposed artefacts.
label: llm

text: We report on a deep search for CO(J=3-2) line emission from the host galaxyof GRB 980425 with the Atacama Submillimeter Telescope Experiment (ASTE). Weobserved five points of the galaxy covering the entire region. After combiningall of the spectra, we obtained a global spectrum with the rms noise level of3.3 mK in T_mb scale at a velocity resolution of 10 km s^-1. No significantemission was detected, though we find a marginal emission feature in thevelocity range corresponding to the redshift of the galaxy. We derive 3 sigmaupper limits on the global properties: the velocity-integrated CO(3-2)intensity of I_CO(3-2) < 0.26 K km s^-1 by adopting a velocity width of 67 kms^-1; the H_2 column density of N(H_2) < 3 x 10^20 cm^-2; the molecular gasmass of M(H_2) < 3 x 10^8 M_sun, by assuming a CO line luminosity to H_2molecular gas mass conversion factor of X_CO = 5.0 x 10^20 cm^-2 (K kms^-1)^-1; and the star formation rate of SFR < 0.1 M_sun yr^-1, based on theSchmidt law. The SFR is consistent with the previous results of H_alpha andmid-IR observations, thereby suggesting that there is no significant obscuredstar formation in the host galaxy of GRB 980425. This result implies that thereis a variety of GRB hosts with regard to the presence of obscured starformation.
label: human

text: We present the results of a search for CO(J=3-2) emission from ESO 184-G82, the host galaxy of the nearby gamma-ray burst GRB 980425 and its associated supernova SN 1998bw. As the closest known host galaxy of a gamma-ray burst, ESO 184-G82 offers a unique opportunity to examine the molecular gas properties associated with these high-energy events. Our observations were conducted using the Atacama Submillimeter Telescope Experiment (ASTE) to specifically target the J=3-2 transition of carbon monoxide as a tracer for dense molecular gas. No significant CO(J=3-2) emission was detected at the GRB position or at the locations of prominent H II regions within the host galaxy. We established 3-sigma upper limits for the CO luminosity and subsequently estimated the maximum molecular gas mass available in the observed regions. These findings suggest that the host galaxy possesses a relatively low molecular gas content despite its active star formation and low metallicity. Our study reinforces the hypothesis that long-duration GRBs tend to occur in gas-poor environments or regions with distinct interstellar medium conditions compared to typical star-forming galaxies.
label: llm

text: Many systems in nature, glasses, interfaces and fractures being someexamples, cannot equilibrate with their environment, which gives rise to noveland surprising behaviour such as memory effects, ageing and nonlinear dynamics.Unlike their equilibrated counterparts, the dynamics of out-of- equilibriumsystems is generally too complex to be captured by simple macroscopic laws.Here we investigate a system that straddles the boundary between glass andcrystal: a Bragg glass formed by vortices in a superconductor. We find that theresponse to an applied force evolves according to a stretched exponential, withthe exponent reflecting the deviation from equilibrium. After the force isremoved, the system ages with time and its subsequent response time scaleslinearly with its age (simple ageing), meaning that older systems are slowerthan younger ones. We show that simple ageing can occur naturally in thepresence of sufficient quenched disorder. Moreover, the hierarchicaldistribution of timescales, arising when chunks of loose vortices cannot movebefore trapped ones become dislodged, leads to a stretched-exponentialresponse.
label: human

text: This study investigates the non-equilibrium dynamics of a driven vortex lattice in a disordered superconducting medium, focusing on its ageing properties and memory effects. By applying a controlled driving force, we observe that the system exhibits a slow, logarithmic relaxation of its transport properties that depends significantly on the time elapsed since the initial perturbation. The results reveal a characteristic glassy phase where the vortex configuration becomes trapped in a complex, frustrated energy landscape, leading to structural stagnation. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the system retains a memory of its prior driving history, as evidenced by its distinct response to subsequent changes in the external driving protocol. These findings establish driven vortex systems as a robust experimental platform for exploring the universal features of ageing and glassiness in out-of-equilibrium disordered matter.
label: llm

text: We derive the equation of matter density perturbations on sub-horizon scalesfor a general Lagrangian density f(R, phi, X) that is a function of a Ricciscalar R, a scalar field phi and a kinetic term X=-(nabla phi)^2/2. This isuseful to constrain modified gravity dark energy models from observations oflarge-scale structure and weak lensing. We obtain the solutions for the matterperturbation delta_m as well as the gravitational potential Phi for someanalytically solvable models. In a f(R) dark energy model with the Lagrangiandensity f(R)=alpha R^{1+m}-Lambda, the growth rates of perturbations exhibitnotable differences from those in the standard Einstein gravity unless m isvery close to 0. In scalar-tensor models with the Lagrangian densityf=F(phi)R+2p(phi,X) we relate the models with coupled dark energy scenarios inthe Einstein frame and reproduce the equations of perturbations known in thecurrent literature by making a conformal transformation. We also estimate theevolution of perturbations in both Jordan and Einstein frames when the energyfraction of dark energy is constant during the matter-dominated epoch.
label: human

text: Modified gravity theories offer a compelling alternative to the cosmological constant for explaining the observed late-time acceleration of the universe. In these frameworks, the evolution of matter density perturbations deviates from the predictions of general relativity due to the presence of additional degrees of freedom. This study investigates the growth of linear perturbations by focusing on the behavior of the effective gravitational constant, which encapsulates the modified strength of gravity on cosmological scales. We derive the governing equations for the growth factor across several classes of modified gravity models, including $f(R)$ theories and scalar-tensor frameworks. Our analysis reveals that the scale-dependence of the effective gravitational constant leads to distinct signatures in the matter power spectrum that may be detectable by upcoming large-scale surveys. Ultimately, these results highlight the potential of using structural growth data to constrain gravitational parameters and distinguish between competing dark energy candidates.
label: llm

text: By combining the REFLEX and NORAS cluster datasets with the NVSS radiocatalogue, we obtain a sample of 145, z<0.3, X-ray selected clusters brighterthan 3 10^(-12) erg/s/cm^2 that show a central radio emission above 3 mJy. Forvirial masses M_vir<~10^(14.5) M_sun, 11 clusters out of 12 (corresponding to92% of the systems) are inhabited by a central radio source. This fractiondecreases with higher masses as M_vir^(-0.4) and suggests that the majority ofX-ray selected clusters host in their centre a radio source brighter than about10^(20) W/Hz/sr. A division of the sample into clusters harbouring eitherpoint-like or an extended radio-loud AGN reveals that the steepening of theL_X-T relation for low-temperature clusters is strongly associated with thepresence of central radio objects with extended jets and/or lobe structures. Inthe latter case, L_X\propto T^(4) while for point-like sources one recovers anapproximately self-similar relation L_X\propto T^(2.3). Monte Carlo simulationsshow that the steepening of the L_X-T relation is not caused by clusters beingunder-luminous in the X-ray band, but rather by overheating, most likely causedby the interplay between the extended radio structures and the intraclustermedium. In the case of low-mass systems, we also find a tight correlationbetween radio luminosity and cluster temperature. The effects of the centralradio source on the thermal state of a cluster become less important withincreasing cluster mass. (Abridged) The luminosity distribution of the clusterradio population differs from that of all radio sources, as there is a deficitof low-luminosity (L_R<~10^(22) W/Hz/sr) objects, while the number ofhigh-luminosity ones is boosted. The net effect on the radio luminosityfunction is of a flattening at all luminosities L_R<~ 10^(24) W/Hz/sr.
label: human

text: Galaxy clusters represent the most massive virialized structures in the universe, providing a unique laboratory for studying the evolution of radio-loud Active Galactic Nuclei (AGN). The presence of radio galaxies within these dense environments triggers a complex series of interactions that significantly shape the physical properties of the intra-cluster medium (ICM). Central brightest cluster galaxies frequently host powerful radio jets that deposit vast amounts of energy into their surroundings through mechanical feedback. These jets create prominent X-ray cavities and shocks, which serve as direct evidence of the work done by the radio lobes against the thermal pressure of the hot gas. This energetic coupling is crucial for addressing the "cooling flow problem" by providing a sustainable heating mechanism that prevents the ICM from undergoing catastrophic cooling and excessive star formation. Conversely, the high-density cluster environment exerts a profound influence on the morphology and duty cycle of the radio galaxies themselves. External factors such as high ambient pressure and ram pressure stripping often distort radio jet trajectories, resulting in characteristic shapes such as wide-angle tail or head-tail sources. Furthermore, the interaction between radio plasma and the magnetized ICM facilitates the transport of magnetic fields and enriched heavy elements across vast cosmic distances. Modern multi-wavelength surveys are currently enhancing our ability to quantify the energy balance and feedback efficiency associated with these massive radio sources. Ultimately, understanding the interplay between radio galaxies and cluster environments is fundamental to refining our broader models of galaxy evolution and large-scale structure formation.
label: llm

text: We present the results of high resolution mapping of the CO(1-0) and CO(2-1)emission of the ultraluminous infrared galaxy (ULIRG) IRAS 10190+1322, with theIRAM interferometer, down to an angular resolution of ~0.3 arcsec. This objectis composed of two interacting galaxies with a projected nuclear separation of6 kpc, and was selected to analyze the physical and dynamical properties of themolecular gas in each galaxy in order to study the conditions that lead agalaxy pair to become ultraluminous in the infrared. With the exception of Arp220, the closest ULIRG, this is the first time that the CO emission ismorphologically and kinematically resolved in the two interacting galaxies of aULIRG system. In one of the galaxies the molecular gas is highly concentrated,distributed in a circumnuclear disk of 1.7 kpc in size. The molecular gas inthe presumably less infrared luminous galaxy is distributed in a more extendeddisk of 7.4 kpc. The molecular gas mass accounts for ~10% of the dynamical massin each galaxy. Both objects are rich enough in molecular gas, Mgas ~ 4 10^9Msun, as to experience an infrared ultraluminous phase.
label: human

text: We present high-resolution, sub-arcsecond observations of the molecular gas content in the ultraluminous infrared galaxy (ULIRG) IRAS 10190+1322. These observations, targeting the CO(1-0) and CO(2-1) rotational transitions, allow for a detailed examination of the gas distribution and excitation conditions at scales of a few hundred parsecs. Our maps reveal a complex nuclear morphology, characterized by distinct peaks of molecular emission that suggest a late-stage major merger. The kinematics of the gas exhibit strong evidence of tidal disruption and rotating disk structures, alongside high velocity dispersions typical of extreme star-forming environments. A comparison between the CO(2-1) and CO(1-0) emission highlights a high line ratio in the nuclear regions, indicating the presence of warm and dense molecular gas. This concentration of dense gas likely fuels the intense starburst activity and potential hidden active galactic nuclei frequently observed in such luminous systems. Ultimately, these sub-arcsecond data provide essential constraints on the gas dynamics and merger-driven evolution of IRAS 10190+1322, furthering our understanding of the ULIRG phenomenon.
label: llm

text: We study Ricci flows of some classes of physically valuable solutions inEinstein and string gravity. The anholonomic frame method is applied forgeneric off-diagonal metric ansatz when the field/ evolution equations aretransformed into exactly integrable systems of partial differential equations.The integral varieties of such solutions, in four and five dimensional gravity,depend on arbitrary generation and integration functions of one, two and/ orthree variables. Certain classes of nonholonomic frame constraints allow us toselect vacuum and/or Einstein metrics, to generalize such solutions fornontrivial string (for instance, with antisymmetric torsion fields) and matterfield sources. A very important property of this approach (originating fromFinsler and Lagrange geometry but re-defined for semi-Riemannian spaces) isthat new classes of exact solutions can be generated by nonholonomicdeformations depending on parameters associated to some generalized Gerochtransforms and Ricci flow evolution. In this paper, we apply the method toconstruct in explicit form some classes of exact solutions for multi-parameterEinstein spaces and their nonholonomic Ricci flows describing evolutions/interactions of solitonic pp-waves and deformations of the Schwarzschildmetric. We explore possible physical consequences and speculate on theirimportance in modern gravity.
label: human

text: This article investigates the geometric evolution of gravitational vacuum solutions under nonholonomic Ricci flows using the anholonomic frame method. We focus on the parametric deformation of two fundamental classes of solutions: solitonic pp-waves and the static Schwarzschild metric. By implementing non-integrable distributions, we demonstrate how these classical solutions are embedded into more general families of nonholonomic manifolds. The analysis reveals that the solitonic pp-waves can be viewed as specific Ricci soliton configurations that evolve non-trivially along the flow parameters. Furthermore, we derive the explicit deformation of the Schwarzschild solution, characterizing the resulting deviations from standard general relativity as effects of the nonholonomic constraints. These results provide new insights into the stability and structural modifications of black holes and gravitational waves within the context of modified geometric flow theories.
label: llm

text: A colloidal system of spheres interacting with both a deep and narrowattractive potential and a shallow long-ranged barrier exhibits a prepeak inthe static structure factor. This peak can be related to an additionalmesoscopic length scale of clusters and/or voids in the system. Simulationstudies of this system have revealed that it vitrifies upon increasing theattraction into a gel-like solid at intermediate densities. The dynamics at themesoscopic length scale corresponding to the prepeak represents the slowestmode in the system. Using mode coupling theory with all input directly takenfrom simulations, we reveal the mechanism for glassy arrest in the system at40% packing fraction.
