By comparing the MLCS2k2 fits used in that studyto the results from other light-curve fitters applied to the same data, wedemonstrate that this is related to the interpretation of SN color excesses(after correction for a light-curve shape-color relation) and the presence of acolor gradient across the local sample. If the slope of the linear relation($\beta$) between SN color excess and luminosity is fit empirically, then thebubble disappears. If, on the other hand, the color excess arises purely fromMilky Way-like dust, then SN data clearly favors a Hubble bubble. Wedemonstrate that SN data give $\beta \simeq 2$, instead of the $\beta \simeq 4$one would expect from purely Milky-Way-like dust. This suggests that either SNintrinsic colors are more complicated than can be described with a singlelight-curve shape parameter, or that dust around SN is unusual. Disentanglingthese possibilities is both a challenge and an opportunity for large-survey SNIa cosmology.
label: human

text: The possible existence of a local "Hubble bubble" has significant implications for our understanding of the cosmic expansion rate and large-scale density fluctuations. This study investigates whether the apparent variation in the local Hubble constant is a physical phenomenon or an artifact of systematic errors in Type Ia supernova (SN Ia) distance measurements. We specifically analyze the treatment of SN Ia colors and the impact of interstellar dust extinction within external galaxies on the derived cosmological distances. By utilizing a comprehensive sample of SNe Ia, we compare different reddening laws and color-correction models to assess their influence on the measured local expansion rate. Our results indicate that the perceived Hubble bubble signature is highly sensitive to the specific assumptions made regarding the intrinsic color-luminosity relationship of SNe Ia. We find that once a more robust treatment of dust extinction and intrinsic color variation is applied, the statistical evidence for a significant local expansion anomaly diminishes considerably. Consequently, we conclude that the "Hubble bubble" likely reflects a systematic bias in supernova calibrations rather than a genuine large-scale feature of the local universe.
label: llm

text: An easy-to-implement form of the Metropolis Algorithm is described which,unlike most standard techniques, is well suited to sampling from multi-modaldistributions on spaces with moderate numbers of dimensions (order ten) inenvironments typical of investigations into current constraints onBeyond-the-Standard-Model physics. The sampling technique makes use ofpre-existing information (which can safely be of low or uncertain quality)relating to the distribution from which it is desired to sample. Thisinformation should come in the form of a ``bank'' or ``cache'' of space pointsof which at least some may be expected to be near regions of interest in thedesired distribution. In practical circumstances such ``banks of clues'' areeasy to assemble from earlier work, aborted runs, discarded burn-in samplesfrom failed sampling attempts, or from prior scouting investigations. Thetechnique equilibrates between disconnected parts of the distribution withoutuser input. The algorithm is not lead astray by ``bad'' clues, but there is nofree lunch: performance gains will only be seen where clues are helpful.
label: human

text: Efficient sampling from high-dimensional or complex probability distributions remains a significant computational challenge in statistical inference and machine learning. Traditional methods, such as standard Markov Chain Monte Carlo, often struggle with slow convergence rates and entrapment in local optima when the target landscape is poorly understood. This paper introduces a novel sampling framework that utilizes a pre-constructed 'bank' of clues to intelligently guide the proposal distribution toward regions of interest. These clues, derived from initial exploratory runs or domain-specific heuristics, act as navigational markers that prioritize the exploration of high-probability mass areas. Experimental results across several benchmark datasets demonstrate that this approach significantly reduces autocorrelation and accelerates convergence compared to conventional sampling algorithms. Ultimately, the proposed technique provides a scalable and robust solution for complex Bayesian modeling where traditional strategies often prove insufficient.
label: llm

text: Hayashi and Carthew (Nature 431 [2004], 647) have shown that the packing ofcone cells in the Drosophila retina resembles soap bubble packing, and thatchanging E- and N-cadherin expression can change this packing, as well as cellshape.  The analogy with bubbles suggests that cell packing is driven by surfaceminimization. We find that this assumption is insufficient to model theexperimentally observed shapes and packing of the cells based on their cadherinexpression. We then consider a model in which adhesion leads to a surfaceincrease, balanced by cell cortex contraction. Using the experimentallyobserved distributions of E- and N-cadherin, we simulate the packing and cellshapes in the wildtype eye. Furthermore, by changing only the correspondingparameters, this model can describe the mutants with different numbers ofcells, or changes in cadherin expression.
label: human

text: The *Drosophila* retina serves as a highly organized model system for investigating the biophysical principles that govern precise tissue patterning and morphogenesis. During pupal development, the retinal epithelium undergoes a series of stereotypical cell rearrangements to form a crystalline hexagonal lattice of ommatidia. In this study, we demonstrate that the spatial distribution of interommatidial cells is primarily driven by the interplay between differential cell adhesion and actomyosin-mediated cortex contractility. We show that E-cadherin and N-cadherin facilitate specific cell-sorting behaviors, while contractile forces at the cell junctions work to minimize surface area and refine boundary lengths. By integrating quantitative live-imaging with computational vertex modeling, we establish that the final equilibrium geometry of the retina is determined by the balance of these opposing mechanical forces.
label: llm

text: A Higgs boson produced in association with one or more bottom quarks is ofgreat theoretical and experimental interest to the high-energy community. Aprecise prediction of its total and differential cross-section can have a greatimpact on the discovery of a Higgs boson with large bottom-quark Yukawacoupling, like the scalar (h^0 and H^0) and pseudoscalar (A^0) Higgs bosons ofthe Minimal Supersymmetric Standard Model (MSSM) in the region of large\tan\beta. In this paper we apply the threshold resummation formalism todetermine both differential and total cross-sections for b g \to b\Phi (where\Phi = h^0, H^0), including up to next-to-next-to-next-to-leading order (NNNLO)soft plus virtual QCD corrections at next-to-leading logarithmic (NLL)accuracy. We present results for both the Fermilab Tevatron and the CERN LargeHadron Collider (LHC).
label: human

text: This study investigates the production of a Higgs boson associated with a single bottom quark, a process that provides critical insights into the bottom-quark Yukawa coupling. We present refined theoretical predictions by incorporating higher-order soft-gluon corrections to the cross-section at the Large Hadron Collider. Our calculations demonstrate that these corrections significantly increase the predicted production rates and lead to a substantial reduction in scale uncertainties. These results offer more precise benchmarks for experimental searches and contribute to the ongoing effort to characterize rare Higgs boson production channels.
label: llm

text: Regularity and topology conditions are imposed on the exact Type IIBsolutions on $AdS_4 \times S^2 \times S^2 \times \Sigma $ with 16supersymmetries, which were derived in a companion paper. We construct aninfinite class of regular solutions with varying dilaton, and non-zero 3-formfluxes. Our solutions may be viewed as the fully back-reacted geometries of$AdS_5 \times S^5$ (or more generally, Janus) doped with D5 and/or NS5 branes.The solutions are parametrized by the choice of an arbitrary genus $g$hyper-elliptic Riemann surface $\Sigma $ with boundary, all of whose branchpoints are restricted to lie on a line. For genus 0, the Janus solution with 16supersymmetries and 6 real parameters is recovered; its topology coincides withthat of $AdS_5 \times S^5$. The genus $g\geq 1$ solutions are parametrized by atotal of $4g+6$ real numbers, $2g-1$ of which are the real moduli of $\Sigma$.The solutions have $2g+2$ asymptotic $AdS_5 \times S^5$ regions, $g$three-spheres with RR 3-form charge, and another $g$ with NSNS 3-form charge.Collapse of consecutive branch points of $\Sigma $ yields singularities whichcorrespond to D5 and NS5 branes in the probe limit. It is argued that theAdS/CFT dual gauge theory to each of our solutions consists of a2+1-dimensional planar interface on which terminate $2g+2$ half-Minkowski3+1-dimensional space-time $\mathcal{N}=4$ super-Yang-Mills theories.Generally, the $\\mathcal{N}=4$ theory in each Minkowski half-space-time mayhave an independent value of the gauge coupling, and the interface may supportvarious operators, whose interface couplings are further free parameters of thedual gauge theory.
label: human

text: This paper constructs the general local solutions of Type IIB supergravity that preserve sixteen supersymmetries and are invariant under the symmetry group $SO(2,3) \times SO(3) \times SO(3)$. The geometry of these solutions is expressed as a warped product of $AdS_4 \times S^2 \times S^2$ over a two-dimensional Riemann surface $\Sigma$ with a boundary. We demonstrate that the BPS equations are fully integrable, reducing the problem to the determination of two harmonic functions that satisfy specific regularity and boundary conditions. Building on previous results, we explicitly derive flux solutions that incorporate non-constant axion-dilaton profiles and active 3-form and 5-form field strengths. A central focus of this work is the derivation of multi-Janus solutions, which represent multiple $AdS_5 \times S^5$ vacua connected via a complex system of interfaces. These exact solutions provide the gravitational framework necessary for exploring the holographic properties of $(1+2)$-dimensional interfaces in $\mathcal{N}=4$ super-Yang-Mills theory.
label: llm

text: We consider power allocation algorithms for fixed-rate transmission overNakagami-m non-ergodic block-fading channels with perfect transmitter andreceiver channel state information and discrete input signal constellationsunder both short- and long-term power constraints. Optimal power allocationschemes are shown to be direct applications of previous results in theliterature. We show that the SNR exponent of the optimal short-term scheme isgiven by the Singleton bound. We also illustrate the significant gainsavailable by employing long-term power constraints. Due to the nature of theexpressions involved, the complexity of optimal schemes may be prohibitive forsystem implementation. We propose simple sub-optimal power allocation schemeswhose outage probability performance is very close to the minimum outageprobability obtained by optimal schemes.
label: human

text: In contemporary wireless communication, efficient power allocation is vital for enhancing reliability and throughput in dynamic environments. This study specifically addresses the power allocation problem for non-ergodic block-fading channels where transmissions are restricted to discrete-input constellations. Traditional approaches often rely on Gaussian signaling assumptions, which fail to capture the performance limitations of practical modulation schemes like quadrature amplitude modulation. We develop an optimization framework that minimizes outage probability by accounting for the unique mutual information characteristics of finite-alphabet signals. Comparative analysis reveals that the proposed strategy offers significant gains over standard water-filling techniques, especially in scenarios with low-to-moderate signal-to-noise ratios. These results underscore the importance of constellation-aware power control for achieving high spectral efficiency in delay-constrained wireless.
label: llm

text: A new class of Erbium doped glasses with compositions xNa2O - (60-x)PbCl2 -40P2O5 (x=0, 10, 20 and 30) were fabricated and characterized for opticalproperties. Absorption spectra were analyzed for important Judd-Ofeltparameters from the integrated intensities of various Er3+ glass absorptionbands. Photoluminescence (PL) and its decay behavior studies were carried outfor the transition 4I13/2 -> 4I15/2. A systematic correlation between theJudd-Ofelt parameter {omega}2 and the covalent nature of the glass matrix wasobserved, due to increased role of bridging oxygens in the glass network. ThePL broadness and life times of 4I13/2_> 4I15/2 transition were typically in therange of 40-60nm and 2.13-2.5ms respectively. These glasses broadly showed hightransparency, high refractive index, shorter life times and, most importantly,these glasses were found to be capable of being doped with largerconcentrations of Er3+ (up to 4 wt%). Increase of Er3+ concentration resultedin the increase in PL line-widths with no significant effect of concentrationquenching, indicating that these glasses are suitable for opticalfibre/waveguide amplifiers.
label: human

text: This study investigates the optical and spectroscopic properties of $\text{Er}^{3+}$ doped alkali-chloro phosphate glasses designed for potential application in optical amplifiers. A series of glass samples with varying concentrations of Erbium ions were synthesized using the conventional melt-quenching technique. Structural analysis through X-ray diffraction confirmed the amorphous nature of the prepared glass matrices, while physical parameters such as density and molar volume were systematically evaluated. Optical absorption spectra were utilized to determine Judd-Ofelt intensity parameters, providing critical information regarding the local environment and bond covalency of the $\text{Er}^{3+}$ ions. Photoluminescence spectra recorded under 980 nm excitation revealed a prominent emission band centered at 1.53 $\mu$m, corresponding to the $^4I_{13/2} \to ^4I_{15/2}$ transition. Important laser parameters, including the stimulated emission cross-section and the full-width at half-maximum, were calculated to assess the bandwidth and gain performance of the glasses. The findings demonstrate that these alkali-chloro phosphate glasses possess high thermal stability and excellent radiative properties, making them suitable candidates for C-band telecommunication amplifiers.
label: llm

text: The Stanley lattice, Tamari lattice and Kreweras lattice are three remarkableorders defined on the set of Catalan objects of a given size. These latticesare ordered by inclusion: the Stanley lattice is an extension of the Tamarilattice which is an extension of the Kreweras lattice. The Stanley order can bedefined on the set of Dyck paths of size $n$ as the relation of \emph{beingabove}. Hence, intervals in the Stanley lattice are pairs of non-crossing Dyckpaths. In a former article, the second author defined a bijection $\Phi$between pairs of non-crossing Dyck paths and the realizers of triangulations(or Schnyder woods). We give a simpler description of the bijection $\Phi$.Then, we study the restriction of $\Phi$ to Tamari's and Kreweras' intervals.We prove that $\Phi$ induces a bijection between Tamari intervals and minimalrealizers. This gives a bijection between Tamari intervals and triangulations.We also prove that $\Phi$ induces a bijection between Kreweras intervals andthe (unique) realizers of stack triangulations. Thus, $\Phi$ induces abijection between Kreweras intervals and stack triangulations which are knownto be in bijection with ternary trees.
label: human

text: This paper investigates the deep combinatorial connections between intervals in Catalan structures and the geometric properties of planar triangulations. Specifically, we focus on the lattice of Dyck paths and its associated interval structures, which are frequently enumerated by various Catalan-related sequences. We establish a novel correspondence between these intervals and the set of realizers, also known as Schnyder woods, of specific classes of triangulations. Realizers provide a powerful framework for encoding the barycentric coordinates and the internal connectivity of a planar triangulation. By mapping each interval in the Catalan lattice to a unique realizer, we demonstrate a bijective link that preserves several key structural invariants. Our construction shows that the length and depth of an interval directly correspond to the orientations and degree distributions of the vertices within its associated triangulation. These results provide new insights into the enumeration of planar maps and offer a simplified approach to calculating the cardinality of specific interval families. Ultimately, this work bridges the gap between the order-theoretic properties of Catalan lattices and the topological representation of planar graphs.
label: llm

text: With an aim towards understanding the time-dependence of entanglement entropyin generic quantum field theories, we propose a covariant generalization of theholographic entanglement entropy proposal of hep-th/0603001. Apart fromproviding several examples of possible covariant generalizations, we study aparticular construction based on light-sheets, motivated in similar spirit tothe covariant entropy bound underlying the holographic principle. Inparticular, we argue that the entanglement entropy associated with a specifiedregion on the boundary in the context of the AdS/CFT correspondence is given bythe area of a co-dimension two bulk surface with vanishing expansions of nullgeodesics. We demonstrate our construction with several examples to illustrateits reduction to the holographic entanglement entropy proposal in staticspacetimes. We further show how this proposal may be used to understand thetime evolution of entanglement entropy in a time varying QFT state dual to acollapsing black hole background. Finally, we use our proposal to argue thatthe Euclidean wormhole geometries with multiple boundaries should be regardedas states in a non-interacting but entangled set of QFTs, one associated toeach boundary.
label: human

text: We propose a covariant generalization of the holographic entanglement entropy formula within the framework of the AdS/CFT correspondence. The original Ryu-Takayanagi prescription is restricted to static spacetimes, leaving the entropy of time-dependent boundary states largely unexplored. In our proposal, the entanglement entropy of a boundary subregion is determined by the area of a codimension-two extremal surface in the bulk Lorentzian geometry. This formulation moves beyond the requirement of a preferred time-slice by identifying the appropriate surface through a purely geometric extremization procedure. We demonstrate that this covariant approach reduces to the standard minimal surface prescription in the static limit while maintaining consistency with field theory principles. This construction provides a powerful framework for investigating the dynamical evolution of entanglement and the reconstruction of bulk physics in non-equilibrium systems.
label: llm

text: N-body simulations give us a rough idea of how the shape of a simulatedobject appears in three-dimensional space. From an observational point of viewthis may give us a misleading picture. The faint stars may be the most commonstars in the system but the morphological information obtained by observationsof an object may be dominated by the color properties of the bright stars. Dueto dynamical effects, such as energy equipartition, different masses of starsmay populate different regions in the object. Since stars are evolving in massthe stellar evolution may also influence the dynamics of the system. Hence, ifone is interested in simulating what the morphology will look like through atelescope, one needs to simulate in addition evolving stars and weight them bytheir luminosity. Therefore we need to combine simulations of the dynamicalevolution and a stellar population synthesis at the same time. For thedynamical evolution part we use a parallel version of a direct N-body code,NBODY6++. This code also includes stellar evolution. We link the parametersfrom this stellar evolution routine to the BaSeL 2.0 stellar library. Forisolated clusters we found results assimilable to standard stellar populationsynthesis codes such as the PEGASE code. For clusters in a tidal field we foundthat the integrated colors become relatively bluer due to energy equipartitioneffects. In the time shortly before dissolution of the cluster the stellar M/Lratio becomes lower compared to isolated clusters. We compared the results ofour simulations to integrated spectra of galactic globular clusters. For thecluster NGC 1851 we found good agreement between simulation and observation.For extragalactic clusters in M81 and M31 we looked at medium band spectralenergy distributions and found for some clusters also a good agreement.
label: human

text: The integration of direct N-body dynamical simulations with advanced stellar population synthesis represents a critical advancement in our understanding of galactic evolution. Historically, these two fields have evolved in relative isolation due to the immense computational costs of simulating individual stellar encounters alongside complex chemical evolution. In this paper, we introduce the HYDE-PARC Project (HYbrid Dynamics Evolution and Population Analysis for Realistic Clusters), a comprehensive numerical framework designed to unify these disciplines. By incorporating updated stellar evolution tracks directly into a high-precision N-body integrator, the project tracks the simultaneous evolution of stellar positions and internal physical properties. The primary objective is to investigate how dynamical processes, such as mass segregation and stellar evaporation, influence the integrated photometric signatures of dense star clusters. Our methodology employs a new algorithmic coupling that ensures energy conservation while accounting for the mass loss associated with supernovae and stellar winds. We present a diverse library of simulated clusters, spanning a broad parameter space of initial mass functions, metallicities, and orbital environments. The analysis reveals that dynamical relaxation significantly alters the observable color-magnitude diagrams, often mimicking the effects of age or metallicity gradients. We find that the preferential loss of low-mass stars from cluster outskirts leads to a systematic hardening of the integrated ultraviolet spectrum over several billion years. Additionally, the HYDE-PARC models successfully reproduce the frequency and distribution of exotic objects, such as blue stragglers and cataclysmic variables, resulting from close dynamical encounters. Comparative studies with high-resolution observations of Milky Way globular clusters indicate a high degree of fidelity in our predicted mass-to-light ratios.
label: llm

text: We investigate whether the floating phase (where the correlation length isinfinite and the spin-spin correlation decays algebraically with distance)exists in the temperature($T$) - frustration parameter ($\kappa$) phase diagramof 2D ANNNI model. To identify this phase, we look for the region where (i)finite size effect is prominent and (ii) some relevant physical quantitychanges somewhat sharply and this change becomes sharper as the system sizeincreases. For $\kappa < 0.5 $, the low temperature phase is ferromagnetic andwe study energy and magnetization. For $\kappa > 0.5 $, the low temperaturephase is antiphase and we study energy, layer magnetization, length of domainwalls running along the direction of frustration, number of domain-interceptsthat are of length 2 along the direction of frustration, and the number ofdomain walls that do not touch the upper and/or lower boundary. In agreementwith some previous studies, our final conclusion is that, the floating phaseexists, if at all, only along a line.
label: human

text: The two-dimensional Axial Next-Nearest-Neighbor Ising (ANNNI) model serves as a prototypical system for studying the interplay between frustration and thermal fluctuations in low-dimensional magnetism. This paper investigates the thermodynamic properties and phase transitions of the model, specifically addressing the long-standing debate regarding the existence of an intermediate floating phase. Through the application of extensive Monte Carlo simulations and transfer-matrix calculations, we analyze the spatial correlation functions across a wide range of competition parameters. Our numerical results provide robust evidence for a floating phase characterized by algebraic spin correlations and an incommensurate wave vector that varies continuously with temperature. The identification of this phase clarifies the transition mechanism between commensurate and disordered states, offering significant implications for the understanding of topological orders in frustrated statistical models.
label: llm

text: We present the first calculation of the possible (local) cosmic stringcontribution to the cosmic microwave background polarization spectra fromsimulations of a string network (rather than a stochastic collection ofunconnected string segments). We use field theory simulations of the AbelianHiggs model to represent local U(1) strings, including their radiative decayand microphysics. Relative to previous estimates, our calculations show a shiftin power to larger angular scales, making the chance of a future cosmic stringdetection from the B-mode polarization slightly greater. We explore a futureground-based polarization detector, taking the CLOVER project as our example.In the null hypothesis (that cosmic strings make a zero contribution) we findthat CLOVER should limit the string tension \mu to G\mu<0.12e-6 (where G is thegravitational constant), above which it is likely that a detection would bepossible.
label: human

text: This paper investigates the contribution of a scaling network of cosmic strings to the E-mode and B-mode polarization power spectra of the cosmic microwave background (CMB). Using high-resolution numerical simulations based on the unconnected segment model, we calculate the vector and tensor perturbations generated by string dynamics from the epoch of recombination to the present day. Our analysis reveals that cosmic strings produce a characteristic B-mode signal that peaks at high multipoles ($l > 1000$), providing a distinct signature that differentiates them from primordial gravitational waves. These results are used to establish updated constraints on the cosmic string tension $G\mu$ and to evaluate the potential for upcoming polarimetric surveys to detect these topological defects.
label: llm

text: Affine Toda field theories with a purely transmitting integrable defect areconsidered and the model based on a_2 is analysed in detail. After providing acomplete characterization of the problem in a classical framework, a suitablequantum transmission matrix, able to describe the interaction between anintegrable defect and solitons, is found. Two independent paths are taken toreach the result. One is an investigation of the triangle equations using theS-matrix for the imaginary coupling bulk affine Toda field theories proposed byHollowood, and the other uses a functional integral approach together with abootstrap procedure. Evidence to support the results is collected in variousways: for instance, through the calculation of the transmission factors for thelightest breathers. While previous discoveries within the sine-Gordon modelmotivated this study, there are several new phenomena displayed in the a_2model including intriguing disparities between the classical and the quantumpictures. For example, in the quantum framework, for a specific range of thecoupling constant that excludes a neighbourhood of the classical limit, thereis an unstable bound state.
label: human

text: Affine Toda field theories represent a prominent class of integrable models in two dimensions that allow for the introduction of internal boundary conditions known as defects. This paper investigates the specific properties of purely transmitting defects, which permit the passage of excitations without the occurrence of back-reflection. We employ a Lagrangian framework to derive the defect equations of motion and identify the constraints necessary to ensure the preservation of total integrability. By analyzing the underlying algebraic structure, we construct defect matrices that satisfy the generalized Yang-Baxter equations for various affine algebras. The analysis reveals that these defects act as energy-momentum-conserving interfaces, resulting in a momentum-dependent phase shift for incident solitons. Furthermore, we examine the relationship between the defect's transmission properties and the symmetry-breaking effects of the specific Toda potential. Our results provide a comprehensive classification of purely transmitting defects and enhance the understanding of localized perturbations in integrable quantum field theories.
label: llm

text: It is known that the dependence of the emission-line luminosity of a typicalcloud in the active galactic nuclei broad-line regions (BLRs) upon the incidentflux of ionizing continuum can be nonlinear. We study how this nonlinearity canbe taken into account in estimating the size of the BLR by means of the"reverberation" methods. We show that the BLR size estimates obtained bycross-correlation of emission-line and continuum light curves can be much (upto an order of magnitude) less than the values obtained by reverberationmodelling. This is demonstrated by means of numerical cross-correlation andreverberation experiments with model continuum flares and emission-linetransfer functions and by means of practical reverberation modelling of theobserved optical spectral variability of NGC 4151. The time behaviour of NGC4151 in the H_alpha and H_beta lines is modelled on the basis of theobservational data by Kaspi et al. (1996, ApJ, 470, 336) and the theoreticalBLR model by Shevchenko (1984, Sov. Astron. Lett., 10, 377; 1985, Sov. Astron.Lett., 11, 35). The values of the BLR parameters are estimated that allow tojudge on the size and physical characteristics of the BLR. The small size ofthe BLR, as determined by the cross-correlation method from the data of Kaspiet al. (1996, ApJ, 470, 336), is shown to be an artifact of this method. So,the hypothesis that the BLR size varies in time is not necessitated by theobservational data.
label: human

text: Active galactic nuclei (AGN) serve as fundamental laboratories for studying the co-evolution of supermassive black holes and their host galaxies. Determining the physical dimensions of the broad-line region (BLR) is a critical step in quantifying the mass of the central black hole through virial estimators. Reverberation mapping provides a powerful indirect method for measuring this size by analyzing the time delay between the stochastic continuum and the delayed emission-line response. This study investigates the systematic uncertainties and potential biases associated with various cross-correlation techniques used to estimate these characteristic lags. We employ a series of synthetic light curves to simulate a wide range of observational cadences and signal-to-noise ratios typically encountered in monitoring campaigns. Our analysis focuses on comparing the standard interpolation cross-correlation function with more modern, statistically driven Bayesian approaches. We find that the distribution of recovered lags is highly sensitive to both the assumed geometry of the BLR and the temporal sampling frequency of the data. Specifically, shorter lag estimates tend to be biased toward smaller values when the continuum variability occurs on timescales comparable to the light-travel time across the emitting region. The results indicate that the interplay between the transfer function and the sampling window can introduce significant artificial shifts in the centroid of the cross-correlation function.
label: llm

text: We present a rigorous calculation of the dynamical friction force exerted ona spherical massive perturber moving through an infinite homogenous system offield stars. By calculating the shape and mass of the polarization cloudinduced by the perturber in the background system, which decelerates the motionof the perturber, we recover Chandrasekhar's drag force law with a modifiedCoulomb logarithm. As concrete examples we calculate the drag force exerted ona Plummer sphere or a sphere with the density distribution of a Hernquistprofile. It is shown that the shape of the perturber affects only the exactform of the Coulomb logarithm. The latter converges on small scales, becauseencounters of the test and field stars with impact parameters less than thesize of the massive perturber become inefficient. We confirm this way earlierresults based on the impulse approximation of small angle scatterings.
label: human

text: Dynamical friction represents a fundamental gravitational drag force experienced by massive objects moving through a distribution of smaller background particles. This study investigates the analytical properties of the dynamical friction force specifically exerted on spherical bodies traversing both collisionless and gaseous media. Using a combination of linear response theory and high-resolution numerical simulations, we derive a generalized expression for the drag force that accounts for the finite size of the sphere. Our results demonstrate that the friction force deviates significantly from the classical Chandrasekhar formula when the body’s radius is comparable to the characteristic impact parameter scale. Furthermore, we analyze the impact of varying Mach numbers on the drag coefficient, highlighting distinct behaviors in subsonic and supersonic regimes for extended spherical geometries.
label: llm

text: We study the effect of a close encounter of a passing star on the shape ofthe inner Oort Cloud, using the impulse approximation. The deviation of theperturbed Oort Cloud from sphericity adds angular fluctuations to thebrightness of the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) due to thermal emission bythe comets. An encounter with a solar-mass star at an impact parameter of $1750\au$, as expected based on the abundance and velocity dispersion of stars inthe solar neighborhood, leads to a quadrupole moment in the square of thefractional CMB intensity fluctuation of $C_2 = 4.5 \times 10^{-15}, 6.7 \times10^{-12}, 1.1 \times 10^{-9}$ at $\nu = 30, 353, 545 \GHz$ (these being thefrequency bands of the upcoming Planck satellite). We also quantify thequadrupole spectral distortions produced by the Scattered Disc, which willexist regardless of any perturbation and the subsequent shape of the OortCloud. For comparison, the square fractional temperature fluctuation quadrupolemoment predicted by the current cosmological model is $C_2 = 1.76 \times10^{-10}$, which corresponds to fluctuations in the CMB intensity of $C_2 = 2.9\times 10^{-10}, 6.8 \times 10^{-9}, 1.6 \times 10^{-8}$ at $\nu = 30, 353, 545\GHz$. Finally, we discuss how a measurement of the anisotropic spectraldistortions could be used to constrain the trajectory of the closest stellarfly-by.
label: human

text: The Oort Cloud represents a vast, spherical reservoir of icy planetesimals marking the gravitational boundary of the solar system. While the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) provides a definitive snapshot of the early universe, its signals are subject to various foreground contaminations, including those originating from local solar system structures. This paper investigates the potential imprints that spatial inhomogeneities and distortions within the Oort Cloud may leave on CMB temperature and polarization anisotropies. By employing a comprehensive distribution model for Oort Cloud objects, we quantify the thermal emission and occultation effects that contribute to small-scale fluctuations. Our analysis reveals that these distortions manifest primarily at high multipoles, potentially mimicking primordial non-Gaussianities or interfering with the detection of secondary CMB effects. These findings underscore the necessity of accurate foreground subtraction in future high-resolution CMB experiments to prevent the misinterpretation of local signatures as cosmological signals.
label: llm

text: We here report on the multiwavelength study which led us to theidentification of X-ray source IGR J16194-2810 as a new Symbiotic X-ray Binary(SyXB), that is, a rare type of Low Mass X-ray Binary (LMXB) composed of aM-type giant and a compact object. Using the accurate X-ray position allowed bySwift/XRT data, we pinpointed the optical counterpart, a M2 III star. Besides,the combined use of the spectral information afforded by XRT and INTEGRAL/IBISshows that the 0.5-200 keV spectrum of this source can be described with anabsorbed Comptonization model, usually found in LMXBs and, in particular, inSyXBs. No long-term (days to months) periodicities are detected in the IBISdata. The time coverage afforded by XRT reveals shot-noise variability typicalof accreting Galactic X-ray sources, but is not good enough to explore thepresence of X-ray short-term (seconds to hours) oscillations in detail. Byusing the above information, we infer important parameters for this source suchas its distance (about 3.7 kpc) and X-ray luminosity (about 1.4e35 erg/s in the0.5-200 keV band), and we give a description for this system (typical of SyXBs)in which a compact object (possibly a neutron star) accretes from the wind ofits M-type giant companion. We also draw some comparisons between IGRJ16194-2810 and other sources belonging to this subclass, finding that thisobject resembles SyXBs 4U 1700+24 and 4U 1954+31.
label: human

text: We report on the multi-wavelength identification and characterization of the hard X-ray source IGR J16194-2810. Using a combination of INTEGRAL and Swift/XRT data, we demonstrate that the source exhibits a persistent and relatively stable X-ray luminosity. High-resolution near-infrared spectroscopy of the counterpart reveals the characteristic absorption features of a late-type M-giant star. The presence of hydrogen and helium emission lines in the optical spectrum confirms the existence of a circumstellar environment ionized by a compact object. X-ray spectral modeling indicates a hard emission component, which is typical for a neutron star undergoing wind-fed accretion from a giant companion. These combined observational properties allow us to definitively classify IGR J16194-2810 as a new member of the symbiotic X-ray binary (SyXB) class. This finding expands the limited sample of known SyXBs and offers further insight into the evolution and mass-transfer mechanisms of long-period binary systems.
label: llm

text: In this paper the benefits provided by multi-cell processing of signalstransmitted by mobile terminals which are received via dedicated relayterminals (RTs) are assessed. Unlike previous works, each RT is assumed here tobe capable of full-duplex operation and receives the transmission of adjacentrelay terminals. Focusing on intra-cell TDMA and non-fading channels, asimplified uplink cellular model introduced by Wyner is considered. Thisframework facilitates analytical derivation of the per-cell sum-rate ofmulti-cell and conventional single-cell receivers. In particular, the analysisis based on the observation that the signal received at the base stations canbe interpreted as the outcome of a two-dimensional linear time invariantsystem. Numerical results are provided as well in order to provide furtherinsight into the performance benefits of multi-cell processing with relaying.
label: human

text: This paper investigates the integration of full-duplex (FD) amplify-and-forward (AF) relaying within multi-cell cellular networks employing cooperative base stations (BSs). While FD technology promises to significantly increase spectral efficiency, its practical implementation is often hindered by severe self-interference and complex inter-cell interference in cooperative environments. We propose a robust system model where BSs utilize joint processing techniques to mitigate interference while leveraging the simultaneous transmission and reception capabilities of FD relays. Through rigorous mathematical analysis, we derive closed-form expressions for the outage probability and ergodic capacity to evaluate the system’s performance under various channel conditions. Numerical results demonstrate that the combination of BS cooperation and FD relaying consistently outperforms conventional half-duplex and non-cooperative schemes, even in the presence of residual self-interference.
label: llm

text: Using the matrix product formalism, we define a multi-parameter family ofspin models on one dimensional chains, with nearest and next-nearest neighboranti-ferromagnetic interaction for which exact analytical expressions can befound for its doubly degenerate ground states. The family of Hamiltonians whichwe define, depend on 5 continuous parameters and the Majumdar-Ghosh model is aparticular point in this parameter space. Like the Majumdar-Ghosh model, thedoubly degenerate ground states of our models have a very simple structure,they are the product of entangled states on adjacent sites. In each of thesestates there is a non-zero staggered magnetization, which vanishes when we taketheir translation-invariant combination as the new ground states. At theMajumdar-Ghosh point, these entangled states become the spin-singletspertaining to this model. We will also calculate in closed form the two pointcorrelation functions, both for finite size of the chain and in thethermodynamic limit.
label: human

text: This paper investigates the ground-state properties of a specific class of one-dimensional quantum spin chains. We present a continuous family of Hamiltonians for which the exact dimerized ground states can be analytically determined. These models generalize the well-known Majumdar-Ghosh point by incorporating a wider range of competing exchange interactions and local anisotropies. By utilizing a frustration-free construction, we demonstrate that the wave function remains a product of local singlets across the entire parameter space. We further analyze the spectral gap and the stability of these dimer states against various symmetry-breaking perturbations. Our findings provide a rigorous framework for exploring the boundaries between dimerized and disordered phases in low-dimensional quantum magnetism.
label: llm

text: We present the results of a survey of 45 young (<250 Myr), close (<50 pc)stars with the Simultaneous Differential Imager (SDI) implemented at the VLTand the MMT for the direct detection of extrasolar planets. As part of thesurvey, we observed 54 objects total, of which 45 were close, young stars, 2were somewhat more distant (<150 pc), very young (<10 Myr) stars, 3 were starswith known radial velocity planets, and 4 were older, very nearby (<20 pc)solar analogues. Our SDI devices use a double Wollaston prism and a quad filterto take images simultaneously at 3 wavelengths surrounding the 1.62 um methaneabsorption bandhead found in the spectrum of cool brown dwarfs and gas giantplanets. In our VLT data, we achieved H band contrasts > 10 mag (5 sigma) at aseparation of 0.5" from the primary star on 45% of our targets and H bandcontrasts of > 9 mag at a separation of 0.5'' on 80% of our targets. With thisdegree of attenuation, we should be able to image (5sigma detection) a 5M_{Jup} planet 15 AU from a 70 Myr K1 star at 15 pc or a 5 M_{Jup} planet at 2AU from a 12 Myr M star at 10 pc. We believe that our SDI images are thehighest contrast astronomical images ever made from ground or space for methanerich companions <1'' from their star. For the best 20 of our survey stars, weattained 50% 5 sigma completeness for 6-10 M_Jup planets at semi-major axes of20-40 AU. Thus, our completeness levels are sufficient to significantly testtheoretical planet distributions. From our survey null result, we can rule out(at the 98% confidence/2.0sigma level) a model planet population using a planetdistribution where N(a) $\propto$ constant out to a distance of 45 AU (furthermodel assumptions discussed within).
label: human

text: Direct imaging of extrasolar planets remains a critical frontier for understanding the architecture and formation history of planetary systems at wide orbital separations. We present the results of a high-contrast imaging survey targeting 45 close, young stars to search for substellar and planetary-mass companions. Observations were conducted using the Simultaneous Differential Imaging (SDI) cameras mounted on the Very Large Telescope (VLT) and the Multiple Mirror Telescope (MMT). This specialized technique exploits the methane absorption feature characteristic of cool, giant planets to significantly suppress stellar halo noise and enhance contrast at small angular separations. Despite achieving high sensitivity across the sample, our survey did not result in the definitive detection of any new planetary-mass companions. To quantify our results, we performed rigorous Monte Carlo simulations by injecting synthetic planets into the data to determine our detection limits. These simulations indicate that our survey was sensitive to companions with masses between 2 and 10 Jupiter masses at orbital separations beyond 10 AU for the majority of target stars. The lack of detections allows us to place significant statistical constraints on the frequency of massive exoplanets residing at large semi-major axes. Our analysis suggests that fewer than 10% of young, nearby stars harbor giant planets more massive than 5 Jupiter masses at distances between 20 and 100 AU. Finally, these findings contribute to the growing consensus that massive, wide-orbit planets are relatively rare around solar-type and low-mass stars.
label: llm

text: We determine the masses and decay constants of the pseudoscalar mesons Bs andBc, and also the masses of the vector mesons Bs^* and Bc^*, in quenched latticeQCD with exact chiral symmetry. For 100 gauge configurations generated withsingle-plaquette action at beta = 7.2 on the 32^3 x 60 lattice, we computepoint-to-point quark propagators for 33 quark masses in the range [0.01, 0.85],and measure the time-correlation functions of pseudoscalar and vector mesons.The inverse lattice spacing and the charm quark bare mass are determined usingthe mass and decay constant of eta_c(2980). The bare masses of s and b quarksare chosen such that the masses of the corresponding vector mesons are in goodagreement with phi(1020), and Upsilon(9460) respectively. Our results are:m_{Bs} = 5385(27)(17) MeV, f_{Bs} = 253(8)(7) MeV, m_{Bc} = 6278(6)(4) MeV,f_{Bc} = 489(4)(3) MeV, m_{Bs^*} = 5424(28)(19) MeV, and m_{Bc^*} = 6315(6)(5)MeV.
label: human

text: This study investigates the properties of $B_s$ and $B_c$ mesons using lattice Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD) simulations that preserve exact chiral symmetry. By employing overlap fermions for both light and heavy valence quarks, we circumvent the traditional chiral symmetry breaking effects common in lattice regularizations. We report precise determinations of the ground-state masses and leptonic decay constants for these meson systems, accounting for various systematic uncertainties and discretization effects. These results provide crucial benchmarks for heavy-flavor physics and enhance our understanding of non-perturbative quark dynamics within the Standard Model.
label: llm

text: We present in this paper three dynamic clustering techniques forObject-Oriented Databases (OODBs). The first two, Dynamic, Statistical &Tunable Clustering (DSTC) and StatClust, exploit both comprehensive usagestatistics and the inter-object reference graph. They are quite elaborate.However, they are also complex to implement and induce a high overhead. Thethird clustering technique, called Detection & Reclustering of Objects (DRO),is based on the same principles, but is much simpler to implement. These threeclustering algorithm have been implemented in the Texas persistent object storeand compared in terms of clustering efficiency (i.e., overall performanceincrease) and overhead using the Object Clustering Benchmark (OCB). The resultsobtained showed that DRO induced a lighter overhead while still achievingbetter overall performance.
label: human

text: Dynamic clustering remains a fundamental technique for enhancing the performance of object-oriented databases by grouping frequently accessed objects together. Despite its importance, current research often focuses on increasingly complex algorithms that introduce significant computational overhead and management difficulties. This paper challenges the trend toward complexity, advocating for a return to simpler, more transparent clustering strategies. We introduce a streamlined framework that prioritizes low-cost reorganization and intuitive access patterns over intricate structural heuristics. Through extensive simulations, we demonstrate that these simplified methods provide performance improvements comparable to state-of-the-art complex models while maintaining superior system efficiency. The results suggest that embracing simplicity allows for more predictable and scalable dynamic clustering solutions in real-world database environments.
label: llm

text: Trapping and cooling techniques have become very important for manyfundamental experiments in atomic physics. When applied to highly charged ionsconfined in Penning traps, these procedures are very effective for testingquantum electrodynamics in extreme electromagnetic fields produced by heavyhighly charged ions such as uranium U$^{91+}$. In addition, fundamentalconstants or nuclear ground state properties can be determined with highaccuracy in these simple systems. Finally, by studying a single trappedradioactive ion, its nuclear decay can be studied in detail by observing thedisappearance of the signal of the mother and the appearance of that of thedaughter isotope. Such experiments on highly charged ions at extremely lowenergy will become possible by the HITRAP facility which is currently beingbuilt up at GSI. Also the future Facility for Antiproton and Ion Research(FAIR) will be briefly described which is expected to be operational by 2014.
label: human

text: Highly charged ions (HCIs) provide a unique environment for probing fundamental physics because their bound electrons are subjected to the extreme electromagnetic fields of the nucleus. These systems serve as sensitive laboratories for testing quantum electrodynamics, investigating nuclear size effects, and searching for physics beyond the Standard Model. However, the high temperatures inherent in HCI production methods traditionally limited the precision of experimental measurements. The implementation of advanced cooling techniques, such as sympathetic cooling with laser-cooled ions in cryogenic traps, has successfully overcome these thermal constraints. This article explores the current state of atomic physics experiments involving these cold, trapped HCIs, focusing on recent breakthroughs in high-precision spectroscopy and mass spectrometry. Such innovations are essential for the development of next-generation optical clocks and provide a robust pathway toward observing potential variations in fundamental physical constants.
label: llm

text: Complex evolving systems such as the biosphere, ecosystems and societiesexhibit sudden collapses, for reasons that are only partially understood. Herewe study this phenomenon using a mathematical model of a system that evolvesunder Darwinian selection and exhibits the spontaneous growth, stasis andcollapse of its structure. We find that the typical lifetime of the systemincreases sharply with the diversity of its components or species. We also findthat the prime reason for crashes is a naturally occurring internal fragilityof the system. This fragility is captured in the network organizationalcharacter and is related to a reduced multiplicity of pathways between itscomponents. This work suggests new parameters for understanding the robustnessof evolving molecular networks, ecosystems, societies, and markets.
label: human

text: The relationship between structural heterogeneity and functional resilience remains a central question in the study of complex systems. While previous research often focuses on static topologies, the mechanisms governing stability in networks that evolve over time are less understood. This study employs a dynamic modeling framework to investigate how node and edge diversity influence the persistence of an evolving network under stochastic perturbations. Our results demonstrate that increased diversity among network components consistently enhances global stability by preventing synchronized failure modes. Specifically, we find that a wide range of interaction strengths and node behaviors acts as a buffer, effectively dampening the propagation of localized shocks. These findings suggest that fostering diversity is a critical strategy for designing robust infrastructures and understanding ecological or economic equilibrium.
label: llm

text: We investigate the mass function in the substellar domain down to a fewJupiter masses in the young sigma Orionis open cluster (3+/-2 Ma, d =360^+70_-60 pc). We have performed a deep IJ-band search, covering an area of790 arcmin^2 close to the cluster centre. This survey was complemented with aninfrared follow-up in the HKs- and Spitzer 3.6-8.0 mum-bands. Usingcolour-magnitude diagrams, we have selected 49 candidate cluster members in themagnitude interval 16.1 mag < I < 23.0 mag. Accounting for flux excesses at 8.0mum and previously known spectral features of youth, 30 objects are bona fidecluster members. Four are first identified from our optical-near infrared data.Eleven have most probable masses below the deuterium burning limit and areclassified as planetary-mass object candidates. The slope of the substellarmass spectrum (Delta N / Delta M = a M^-alpha) in the mass interval 0.11 Msol M< 0.006 Msol is alpha = +0.6+/-0.2. Any opacity mass-limit, if these objectsform via fragmentation, may lie below 0.006 Msol. The frequency of sigmaOrionis brown dwarfs with circumsubstellar discs is 47+/-15 %. The continuityin the mass function and in the frequency of discs suggests that very low-massstars and substellar objects, even below the deuterium-burning mass limit, mayshare the same formation mechanism.
label: human

text: We present a comprehensive multi-wavelength photometric study of the young $\sigma$ Orionis open cluster to investigate its substellar and planetary-mass population. Our dataset combines deep optical imaging with near-infrared and Spitzer/IRAC mid-infrared observations across a wide field of view. By utilizing color-magnitude diagrams and spectral energy distribution modeling, we identify numerous new candidate members ranging from low-mass brown dwarfs to objects below the deuterium-burning limit. The inclusion of IRAC photometry allows for the precise identification of circumstellar disks through the detection of mid-infrared excesses. We find that a significant fraction of the substellar population harbors disks, suggesting that the disk-bearing phase is a common feature among very low-mass objects. The derived bolometric luminosities and effective temperatures are compared with the latest evolutionary models to estimate the masses of the candidates. Based on these results, we construct the substellar mass function for the cluster across a mass range spanning approximately 0.1 to 0.006 solar masses. Our analysis reveals that the mass function continues to rise into the planetary-mass regime, which is consistent with previous findings for this star-forming region. The observed distribution provides critical constraints on the efficiency of various formation mechanisms.
label: llm

text: A Suzaku observation of the nucleus of the radio-loud AGN Centaurus A in 2005has yielded a broadband spectrum spanning 0.3 to 250 keV. The net exposuretimes after screening were: 70 ks per X-ray Imaging Spectrometer (XIS) camera,60.8 ks for the Hard X-ray Detector (HXD) PIN, and 17.1 ks for the HXD-GSO. Thehard X-rays are fit by two power-laws of the same slope, absorbed by columns of1.5 and 7 * 10^{23} cm^{-2} respectively. The spectrum is consistent withprevious suggestions that the power-law components are X-ray emission from thesub-pc VLBI jet and from Bondi accretion at the core, but it is also consistentwith a partial covering interpretation. The soft band is dominated by thermalemission from the diffuse plasma and is fit well by a two-temperature VAPECmodel, plus a third power-law component to account for scattered nuclearemission, jet emission, and emission from X-ray Binaries and other pointsources. Narrow fluorescent emission lines from Fe, Si, S, Ar, Ca and Ni aredetected. The Fe K alpha line width yields a 200 light-day lower limit on thedistance from the black hole to the line-emitting gas. Fe, Ca, and S K-shellabsorption edges are detected. Elemental abundances are constrained viaabsorption edge depths and strengths of the fluorescent and diffuse plasmaemission lines. The high metallicity ([Fe/H]=+0.1) of the circumnuclearmaterial suggests that it could not have originated in the relativelymetal-poor outer halo unless enrichment by local star formation has occurred.Relative abundances are consistent with enrichment from Type II and Iasupernovae.
label: human

text: Centaurus A, the nearest radio-loud active galactic nucleus (AGN), provides a unique laboratory for studying the physics of accretion and jet formation. This paper presents a detailed analysis of the nuclear region of Centaurus A based on long-term observations conducted with the Suzaku X-ray satellite. By utilizing the combined bandwidth of the X-ray Imaging Spectrometer (XIS) and the Hard X-ray Detector (HXD), we obtained a high-quality broadband spectrum ranging from 0.5 to 250 keV. The spectrum is characterized by a heavily absorbed power-law component, representing the primary emission from the central engine. We applied complex absorption models to account for the neutral and ionized material along the line of sight, yielding a column density of approximately $10^{23}$ cm⁻². A prominent, narrow iron K$\alpha$ fluorescence line was detected at 6.4 keV, originating from the surrounding cold circumnuclear material. Through precise modeling of the reflection component and the absorption edge, we derived tight constraints on the iron abundance of the accreting gas. Our results indicate that the iron abundance is slightly sub-solar, which contrasts with the super-solar metallicities often reported in the nuclei of radio-quiet Seyfert galaxies. Furthermore, measurements of other alpha-elements suggest a chemical enrichment history that differs significantly from the galactic interstellar medium. These findings offer critical insights into the metal-enrichment processes and the physical state of the obscuring torus in radio-loud active galaxies.
label: llm

text: We apply the technique of parameter-splitting to existing cosmological datasets, to check for a generic failure of dark energy models. Given a dark energyparameter, such as the energy density Omega_Lambda or equation of state w, wesplit it into two meta-parameters with one controlling geometrical distances,and the other controlling the growth of structure. Observational data spanningType Ia Supernovae, the cosmic microwave background (CMB), galaxy clustering,and weak gravitational lensing statistics are fit without requiring the twometa-parameters to be equal. This technique checks for inconsistency betweendifferent data sets, as well as for internal inconsistency within any one dataset (e.g., CMB or lensing statistics) that is sensitive to both geometry andgrowth. We find that the cosmological constant model is consistent with currentdata. Theories of modified gravity generally predict a relation between growthand geometry that is different from that of general relativity.Parameter-splitting can be viewed as a crude way to parametrize the space ofsuch theories. Our analysis of current data already appears to put sharp limitson these theories: assuming a flat universe, current data constrain thedifference Omega_Lambda(geom) - Omega_Lambda(grow) to be -0.0044 +/- 0.0058(68% C.L.); allowing the equation of state w to vary, the difference w(geom) -w(grow) is constrained to be 0.37 +/- 0.37 (68% C.L.). Interestingly, theregion w(grow) > w(geom), which should be generically favored by theories thatslow structure formation relative to general relativity, is quite restricted bydata already. We find w(grow) < -0.80 at 2 sigma. As an example, the best-fitflat Dvali-Gabadadze-Porrati (DGP) model approximated by our parametrizationlies beyond the 3 sigma contour for constraints from all the data sets.
label: human

text: The standard $\Lambda$CDM model, while remarkably successful, faces increasing scrutiny due to persistent tensions between different cosmological datasets. In this paper, we address the fundamental question of whether current observations necessitate the adoption of modified gravity theories or can be adequately explained by sophisticated dark energy models. We develop an empirical consistency test that evaluates the relationship between the universe's expansion history and the growth of large-scale structures. Our methodology employs a combination of the latest Cosmic Microwave Background data, Type Ia Supernovae distance moduli, and Baryon Acoustic Oscillation measurements. By introducing a parameterized framework for both the equation of state and the growth index, we are able to isolate the signatures of gravitational departures from General Relativity. The analysis focuses on identifying whether the observed growth of density perturbations is consistent with the background expansion rate predicted by standard gravity. Our results demonstrate that while some datasets suggest a slight suppression in the growth of structure, these features can often be mimicked by specific quintessence models. Quantitative comparisons using Bayesian inference reveal that modified gravity models do not yet offer a statistically superior fit compared to dynamic dark energy. Furthermore, we find that the uncertainties in current local measurements of the Hubble constant remain a significant factor in discriminating between these theoretical frameworks. We conclude that while modified gravity is not strictly required by current empirical evidence, the door remains open for alternative theories as data precision increases. Looking ahead, next-generation weak lensing and galaxy clustering surveys will provide the definitive evidence needed to confirm or refute the necessity of modifying General Relativity on cosmological scales.
label: llm

text: We present the 2nd version of the Catalogue of Radial Velocities withAstrometric Data (CRVAD-2). This is the result of the cross-identification ofstars from the All-Sky Compiled Catalogue of 2.5 Million Stars (ASCC-2.5) withthe General Catalogue of Radial Velocities and with other recently publishedradial velocity lists and catalogues. The CRVAD-2 includes accurate J2000equatorial coordinates, proper motions and trigonometric parallaxes in theHipparcos system, $B, V$ photometry in the Johnson system, spectral types,radial velocities (RVs), multiplicity and variability flags for 54907 ASCC-2.5stars. We have used the CRVAD-2 for a new determination of mean RVs of 363 openclusters and stellar associations considering their established members fromproper motions and photometry in the ASCC-2.5. For 330 clusters andassociations we compiled previously published mean RVs from the literature,critically reviewed and partly revised them. The resulting Catalogue of RadialVelocities of Open Clusters and Associations (CRVOCA) contains about 460 openclusters and about 60 stellar associations in the Solar neighbourhood. Thesenumbers still represent less than 30% of the total number of about 1820 objectscurrently known in the Galaxy. The mean RVs of young clusters are generallybetter known than those of older ones.
label: human

text: This paper presents the first installment of the astrophysical supplements to the All-Sky Compiled Catalogue (ASCC-2.5), focusing on the homogenization of stellar kinematic data. The primary objective of this work is to provide a comprehensive and unified database of radial velocities for a significant subsample of stars within the catalog. We have compiled and cross-referenced radial velocity measurements from several major ground-based and space-borne surveys to ensure broad sky coverage. As a result, precise radial velocities for approximately 55,000 individual stars have been successfully integrated into the ASCC-2.5 framework. Leveraging this extensive stellar data, we further determined the mean radial velocities for 516 Galactic open clusters and stellar associations. The calculation of these cluster velocities involved a rigorous membership selection process based on both spatial and kinematic consistency. This unified dataset significantly increases the number of open clusters with known three-dimensional velocity vectors, facilitating more detailed dynamical analyses of the Milky Way. Ultimately, these supplements serve as a vital resource for researchers investigating the kinematic structure and evolutionary history of the Galactic disk.
label: llm

text: We introduce an exponential random graph model for networks with a fixeddegree distribution and with a tunable degree-degree correlation. We theninvestigate the nature of a percolation transition in the correlated networkwith the Poisson degree distribution. It is found that negative correlation isirrelevant in that the percolation transition in the disassortative networkbelongs to the same universality class of the uncorrelated network. Positivecorrelation turns out to be relevant. The percolation transition in theassortative network is characterized by the non-diverging mean size of finiteclusters and power-law scalings of the density of the largest cluster and thecluster size distribution in the non-percolating phase as well as at thecritical point. Our results suggest that the unusual type percolationtransition in the growing network models reported recently may be inheritedfrom the assortative degree-degree correlation.
label: human

text: Percolation transitions represent a fundamental phenomenon in network science, determining the structural integrity and connectivity of complex systems. While many studies assume random connectivity, real-world networks often exhibit significant degree-degree correlations where nodes of similar or dissimilar degrees tend to link together. In this work, we investigate the influence of such correlations on the critical properties of the percolation transition using an analytical framework based on the configuration model. Our results demonstrate that assortative mixing—where high-degree nodes prefer to connect to each other—significantly lowers the percolation threshold, enhancing network resilience to random failures. Conversely, disassortative correlations are shown to delay the emergence of a giant component, although they can lead to more abrupt transitions in specific topological regimes. These findings provide crucial insights into how local wiring patterns dictate global phase transitions.
label: llm

text: The overlap Dirac operator in lattice QCD requires the computation of thesign function of a matrix. While this matrix is usually Hermitian, it becomesnon-Hermitian in the presence of a quark chemical potential. We show how theaction of the sign function of a non-Hermitian matrix on an arbitrary vectorcan be computed efficiently on large lattices by an iterative method. A Krylovsubspace approximation based on the Arnoldi algorithm is described for theevaluation of a generic matrix function. The efficiency of the method isspoiled when the matrix has eigenvalues close to a function discontinuity. Thisis cured by adding a small number of critical eigenvectors to the Krylovsubspace, for which we propose two different deflation schemes. The ensuingmodified Arnoldi method is then applied to the sign function, which has adiscontinuity along the imaginary axis. The numerical results clearly show theimproved efficiency of the method. Our modification is particularly effectivewhen the action of the sign function of the same matrix has to be computed manytimes on different vectors, e.g., if the overlap Dirac operator is invertedusing an iterative method.
label: human

text: The sign function of a matrix is a fundamental tool in various computational physics applications, particularly in the formulation of the overlap Dirac operator for lattice fermions. However, when a nonzero chemical potential is introduced, the Dirac operator becomes non-Hermitian, which significantly complicates the numerical evaluation of the sign function. In this work, we present an efficient iterative method specifically designed to compute the sign function of a general non-Hermitian matrix. The proposed algorithm leverages iterative refinement techniques to maintain high precision even as the spectrum of the matrix extends into the complex plane. A detailed theoretical analysis of the convergence characteristics is provided, highlighting the robustness of the method against small eigenvalues. We specifically apply this iterative scheme to the overlap Dirac operator at finite density, where standard Hermitian techniques are no longer applicable. Numerical simulations are conducted across various lattice sizes and chemical potentials to validate the efficiency and scalability of the approach. The results demonstrate that our method achieves a favorable balance between computational speed and the preservation of the Ginsparg-Wilson relation.
label: llm

text: In this study, using the analytical and recurrence relations suggested by theauthors in previous works, the new efficient and reliable program procedure forthe overlap integrals over Slater type orbitals (STOs) is presented. Theproposed procedure guarantees a highly accurate evaluation of the overlapintegrals with arbitrary values of quantum numbers, screening constants andinternuclear distances. It is demonstrated that the computational accuracy ofthe proposed procedure is not only dependent on the efficiency of formulas, ashas been discussed previously, but also on a number of other factors includingthe used program language package and solvent properties. The numerical resultsobtained using the algorithm described in the present work are in a completeagreement with those obtained using the alternative evaluation procedure. Wenotice that the program works without any restrictions and in all range ofintegral parameters.
label: human

text: The accurate evaluation of overlap integrals involving Slater-type orbitals (STOs) remains a fundamental challenge in the development of high-precision quantum chemistry software. This study presents a robust computational framework that utilizes a combination of closed-form analytical expressions and stable recurrence relations to compute these integrals efficiently. By deriving general formulas for multicenter overlaps, we address the numerical instabilities often associated with high principal quantum numbers and disparate orbital exponents. The results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior numerical accuracy across a wide range of geometric configurations while maintaining low computational overhead. Ultimately, this approach provides a reliable foundation for molecular simulations where the physical fidelity of STOs is preferred over traditional Gaussian-type approximations.
label: llm

text: The effective recombination coefficient, alpha_eff, is refined for opticallythin cases. Radiation pressure in Lyman-alpha and HeII Lyman-alpha iscalculated in terms of the number density and the mean free path. Pressureequilibrium between Lyman-alpha clouds and an adiabatically expandinginter-galactic medium is assumed, n_i T_i = n_c T_c. Numerical models ofisothermal and adiabatic expanding Lyman-alpha forest clouds are presented,including evolving UV sources (QSOs), with various turn-on times z_on = 20, 10,and 5, and with q_0 = 1/2 in a matter-dominated Friedmann-Robertson-WalkerUniverse. These models lead to the conclusion that the radiation pressure andQSO turn-on time are significant in determining the range of physical size, D,and neutral hydrogen column density, N(HI), permitted for stable Lyman-alphaforest clouds.  This manuscript was written in 1989 and never submitted for publication.
label: human

text: The Lyman-alpha forest serves as a vital probe of the intergalactic medium and the large-scale structure of the high-redshift universe. However, the dynamical influence of radiation pressure arising from the resonant scattering of Lyman-alpha photons within these neutral hydrogen clouds is often overlooked in standard cosmological models. In this study, we utilize high-resolution hydrodynamic simulations coupled with radiative transfer calculations to quantify how this pressure affects the physical properties of the absorbers. Our results demonstrate that the trapping of Lyman-alpha radiation significantly increases the internal pressure of high-column density systems, counteracting gravitational collapse. This enhanced pressure leads to a measurable expansion of the gas clouds and a subsequent modification of their neutral hydrogen fractions and line widths. Consequently, we argue that incorporating radiation pressure is essential for the precise interpretation of absorption features in quasar spectra and for refining our understanding of.
label: llm

text: We prove that the Neumann, Dirichlet and regularity problems for divergenceform elliptic equations in the half space are well posed in $L_2$ for smallcomplex $L_\infty$ perturbations of a coefficient matrix which is either realsymmetric, of block form or constant. All matrices are assumed to beindependent of the transversal coordinate. We solve the Neumann, Dirichlet andregularity problems through a new boundary operator method which makes use ofoperators in the functional calculus of an underlaying first order Dirac typeoperator. We establish quadratic estimates for this Dirac operator, whichimplies that the associated Hardy projection operators are bounded and dependcontinuously on the coefficient matrix. We also prove that certain transmissionproblems for $k$-forms are well posed for small perturbations of blockmatrices.
label: human

text: This paper investigates the solvability of Dirichlet and Neumann boundary value problems for second-order elliptic equations with complex-valued coefficients. We employ the framework of first-order Dirac-type operators to reformulate these elliptic problems as Cauchy-type evolution equations. Through the application of the $H^\infty$ functional calculus, we establish the existence and uniqueness of solutions within the associated Hardy spaces. This methodology specifically addresses complex perturbations of the coefficients, providing a robust approach to stability for boundary value problems in the non-self-adjoint setting. The results demonstrate that the boundary operators are well-defined and satisfy the necessary estimates to recover classical regularity and Neumann solutions under small complex variations.
label: llm

text: Starting from the Liouville equation, we derive the exact hierarchy ofequations satisfied by the reduced distribution functions of the single speciespoint vortex gas in two dimensions. Considering an expansion of the solution inpowers of 1/N in a proper thermodynamic limit $N\to +\infty$, and neglectingsome collective effects, we derive a kinetic equation satisfied by the smoothvorticity field which is valid at order $O(1/N)$. This equation was obtainedpreviously [P.H. Chavanis, Phys. Rev. E, 64, 026309 (2001)] from a moreabstract projection operator formalism. If we consider axisymmetric flows andmake a markovian approximation, we obtain a simpler kinetic equation which canbe studied in great detail. We discuss the properties of these kineticequations in regard to the $H$-theorem and the convergence (or not) towards thestatistical equilibrium state. We also study the growth of correlations byexplicitly calculating the time evolution of the two-body correlation functionin the linear regime. In a second part of the paper, we consider the relaxationof a test vortex in a bath of field vortices and obtain the Fokker-Planckequation by directly calculating the second (diffusion) and first (drift)moments of the increment of position of the test vortex. A specificity of ourapproach is to obtain general equations, with a clear physical meaning, thatare valid for flows that are not necessarily axisymmetric and that take intoaccount non-Markovian effects. A limitations of our approach, however, is thatit ignores collective effects.
label: human

text: This paper presents a formal derivation of the kinetic equations describing the long-term evolution and relaxation of a system composed of two-dimensional point vortices. The point vortex model serves as a fundamental paradigm for understanding the statistical mechanics of two-dimensional turbulence and geophysical flows. We begin by constructing a hierarchy of equations for the reduced $n$-vortex distribution functions, mirroring the Bogoliubov-Born-Green-Kirkwood-Yvon (BBGKY) approach used in classical gases. In the limit of an infinite number of vortices, the first equation of this hierarchy yields the mean-field Vlasov-like description equivalent to the two-dimensional Euler equation. To investigate the effects of finite-$N$ fluctuations and discreteness, we extend the analysis to include the second-order correlation functions. A systematic closure of the hierarchy is achieved by neglecting three-body correlations and employing a separation of timescales between individual interactions and collective dynamics. This procedure leads to the derivation of a closed kinetic equation that characterizes the slow diffusion of vortices in the presence of fluctuations. The resulting expression shares structural similarities with the Lenard-Balescu equation in plasma physics but is adapted for the unique Hamiltonian structure of point vortices. We rigorously demonstrate that this kinetic equation preserves the fundamental invariants of the motion, including total circulation, energy, and angular momentum. Furthermore, we provide a proof of an H-theorem, indicating that the system evolves towards a state of maximum entropy on a diffusive timescale.
label: llm

text: The origin of the ultrahigh-energy (UHE) cosmic rays (CRs) from the secondknee ($\sim6\times10^{17}$eV) above in the CR spectrum is still unknown.Recently, there has been growing evidence that a peculiar type of supernovae,called hypernovae, are associated with sub-energetic gamma-ray bursts (GRBs),such as SN1998bw/GRB980425 and SN2003lw/GRB031203.
