Such hypernovae appear tohave high (up to mildly relativistic) velocity ejecta, which may be linked tothe sub-energetic GRBs. Assuming a continuous distribution of the kineticenergy of the hypernova ejecta as a function of its velocity $E_k\propto(\Gamma\beta)^{-\alpha}$ with $\alpha\sim 2$, we find that 1) the externalshock wave produced by the high velocity ejecta of a hypernova can accelerateprotons up to energies as high as $10^{19} {\rm eV}$; 2) the cosmologicalhypernova rate is sufficient to account for the energy flux above the secondknee; and 3) the steeper spectrum of CRs at these energies can arise in thesesources. In addition, hypernovae would also give rise to a faint diffuse UHEneutrino flux, due to $p\gamma$ interactions of the UHE CRs with hypernovaoptical-UV photons.
label: human

text: The origin of ultra-high-energy cosmic rays and their connection to high-energy neutrino emissions remains a fundamental question in multi-messenger astrophysics. This study explores semi-relativistic hypernovae as a candidate source, analyzing how their energetic outflows can accelerate particles to extreme energies through diffusive shock acceleration. We model the interaction of these accelerated protons with the surrounding radiation fields and ambient medium to estimate the resulting flux of cosmic rays and secondary neutrinos. Our findings indicate that semi-relativistic hypernovae are capable of explaining both the observed cosmic ray spectrum near the ankle and a significant portion of the diffuse neutrino flux detected by IceCube.
label: llm

text: Analysis of the Cassini Ultraviolet Imaging Spectrometer (UVIS) stellar andsolar occultations at Titan to date include 12 species: N$_{2}$ (nitrogen),CH$_{4}$ (methane), C$_{2}$H$_{2}$ (acetylene), C$_{2}$H$_{4}$ (ethylene),C$_{2}$H$_{6}$ (ethane), C$_{4}$H$_{2}$ (diacetylene), C$_{6}$H$_{6}$(benzene), C$_{6}$N$_{2}$ (dicyanodiacetylene), C$_{2}$N$_{2}$ (cyanogen), HCN(hydrogen cyanide), HC$_{3}$N (cyanoacetylene), and aerosols distinguished by astructureless continuum extinction (absorption plus scattering) of photons inthe EUV. The introduction of aerosol particles, retaining the same refractiveindex properties as tholin with radius $\sim$125 \AA and using Mie theory,provides a satisfactory fit to the spectra. The derived vertical profile ofaerosol density shows distinct structure, implying a reactive generationprocess reaching altitudes more than 1000 km above the surface. A photochemicalmodel presented here provides a reference basis for examining the chemical andphysical processes leading to the distinctive atmospheric opacity at Titan. Wefind that dicyanodiacetylene is condensable at $\sim$650 km, where theatmospheric temperature minimum is located. This species is the simplestmolecule identified to be condensable. Observations are needed to confirm theexistence and production rates of dicyanodiacetylene.
label: human

text: Titan’s dense, nitrogen-rich atmosphere is characterized by a pervasive organic haze that fundamentally influences its thermal structure and chemical evolution. While aerosol formation has historically been associated with the lower stratosphere, recent evidence suggests that the initiation of these particles occurs through complex photolytic processes in the mesosphere and thermosphere. This study employs a comprehensive photochemical model to examine the transition from simple molecular species to heavy organic macromolecules at extreme altitudes. Our findings demonstrate that the absorption of solar extreme ultraviolet radiation triggers the dissociation of methane and nitrogen, facilitating the growth of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons and nitriles. These high-altitude aerosols exhibit distinct morphological and optical properties, serving as the primary nucleation seeds for the more substantial haze layers found deeper in the atmosphere. Furthermore, the results indicate that the vertical distribution of these particles is highly sensitive to variations in solar flux and magnetospheric particle precipitation. Consequently, these findings highlight the critical role of upper-atmospheric photochemistry in shaping the global aerosol budget and the overall prebiotic chemical inventory of Titan.
label: llm

text: We consider a network of nodes distributed in physical space without physicallinks communicating through message broadcasting over specified distances.Typically, communication using smaller distances is desirable due to savings inenergy or other resources. We introduce a network formation mechanism to enablereducing the distances while retaining connectivity. Nodes, which initiallytransmit signals at a prespecified maximum distance, subject links topreferential detachment by autonomously decreasing their transmission radiiwhile satisfying conditions of zero communication loss and fixed maximumnode-hopping distance for signaling. Applied to networks with various spatialtopologies, we find cost reductions as high as 90% over networks that arerestricted to have all nodes with equal transmission distance.
label: human

text: This paper explores the mechanism of preferential detachment in broadcast signaling networks, where nodes selectively sever connections to manage inherent resource constraints. We utilize a stochastic modeling framework to evaluate how the systematic removal of links affects the balance between network-wide information dissemination and total maintenance costs. The analysis reveals that while preferential detachment can significantly reduce operational overhead, it introduces a critical vulnerability threshold that threatens the overall connectivity and reachability of broadcast signals. These results offer a theoretical foundation for optimizing the architecture of energy-constrained systems, such as wireless sensor arrays and neural communication pathways.
label: llm

text: An ensemble based approach for dealing with missing data, without predictingor imputing the missing values is proposed. This technique is suitable foronline operations of neural networks and as a result, is used for onlinecondition monitoring. The proposed technique is tested in both classificationand regression problems. An ensemble of Fuzzy-ARTMAPs is used forclassification whereas an ensemble of multi-layer perceptrons is used for theregression problem. Results obtained using this ensemble-based technique arecompared to those obtained using a combination of auto-associative neuralnetworks and genetic algorithms and findings show that this method can performup to 9% better in regression problems. Another advantage of the proposedtechnique is that it eliminates the need for finding the best estimate of thedata, and hence, saves time.
label: human

text: The presence of missing values in input data streams presents a significant challenge for online learning systems that require immediate decision-making. This paper proposes a novel framework integrating Fuzzy ARTMAP (FAM) architectures with specialized neural network components to process incomplete data in real-time. By modifying the category choice and resonance functions, the proposed system effectively ignores missing features without necessitating computationally expensive imputation techniques. The hybrid model maintains the fundamental stability-plasticity characteristics of FAM while enhancing its robustness against various patterns of data loss. Experimental evaluations conducted on benchmark classification datasets demonstrate that the approach achieves high accuracy and computational efficiency compared to traditional imputation methods.
label: llm

text: Several years ago, we proposed a modification of the Standard Model, in whichthe Higgs sector was stabilized by the addition of higher derivative operators,similar to Lee-Wick Electrodynamics. We studied this theory extensively, bothusing continuum Hamiltonian and path integral methods. We also reporteddetailed lattice studies of the higher derivative Higgs sector. In view of somerecent revived interest in our original idea, we are providing here ourextensive notes from the time period on this topic. The key results werealready published in our papers at that time. The many additional details thatwe make available here were previously available only in Chuan Liu's UCSD Ph.D.thesis (1994). Very recently, our idea has been revived by other groups. Inview of the renewed interest, and to perhaps correct some misconceptions in theliterature, we are here making our original extensive notes available to thewider community.
label: human

text: The Standard Model provides an elegant description of electroweak symmetry breaking, yet the precise nature of the scalar sector remains theoretically unsettled. While Technicolor models offer a dynamical explanation for this symmetry breaking, they often encounter significant difficulties regarding precision electroweak measurements and flavor-changing neutral currents. This paper explores the possibility of a strongly interacting Higgs sector that avoids the traditional pitfalls associated with Technicolor frameworks. We utilize an effective chiral Lagrangian approach to describe the interactions of the Higgs boson and the longitudinal components of the gauge bosons. In this framework, the Higgs boson is treated as a broad resonance arising from new strong dynamics at the TeV scale rather than as a fundamental scalar. We demonstrate that unitarity in longitudinal vector boson scattering can be maintained through the exchange of this heavy state, even in the absence of explicit technifermions.
label: llm

text: In this paper we consider the problem of computing an mRNA sequence ofmaximal similarity for a given mRNA of secondary structure constraints,introduced by Backofen et al. in [BNS02] denoted as the MRSO problem. Theproblem is known to be NP-complete for planar associated implied structuregraphs of vertex degree at most 3. In [BFHV05] a first polynomial dynamicprogramming algorithms for MRSO on implied structure graphs with maximum vertexdegree 3 of bounded cut-width is shown. We give a simple but more generalpolynomial dynamic programming solution for the MRSO problem for associatedimplied structure graphs of bounded clique-width. Our result implies that MRSOis polynomial for graphs of bounded tree-width, co-graphs, $P_4$-sparse graphs,and distance hereditary graphs. Further we conclude that the problem ofcomparing two solutions for MRSO is hard for the class of problems which can besolved in polynomial time with a number of parallel queries to an oracle in NP.
label: human

text: Determining the degree of similarity between proteins while accounting for the secondary structure of their corresponding mRNA sequences is a fundamental task in computational biology. Although structural information provides critical insights into functional conservation, the general problem of searching for similarities under complex structural constraints is often NP-hard. This paper addresses this challenge by introducing novel polynomial-time algorithms designed for protein similarity searches within specific restricted mRNA structural classes. We specifically focus on structures characterized by limited nesting depths and the absence of complex pseudoknots, which represent a significant portion of biologically relevant motifs. Our approach utilizes a refined dynamic programming framework that efficiently maps sequence-to-structure alignments across the search space. The results demonstrate that these algorithms significantly reduce computational overhead compared to heuristic-based methods while maintaining high sensitivity in detecting structural homologies.
label: llm

text: We report on the structural and magnetic properties of thin Ge(1-x)Mn(x)filmsgrown by molecular beam epitaxy (MBE) on Ge(001) substrates at temperatures(Tg) ranging from 80deg C to 200deg C, with average Mn contents between 1 % and11 %. Their crystalline structure, morphology and composition have beeninvestigated by transmission electron microscopy (TEM), electron energy lossspectroscopy and x-ray diffraction. In the whole range of growth temperaturesand Mn concentrations, we observed the formation of manganese richnanostructures embedded in a nearly pure germanium matrix. Growth temperaturemostly determines the structural properties of Mn-rich nanostructures. For lowgrowth temperatures (below 120deg C), we evidenced a two-dimensional spinodaldecomposition resulting in the formation of vertical one-dimensionalnanostructures (nanocolumns). Moreover we show in this paper the influence ofgrowth parameters (Tg and Mn content) on this decomposition i.e. on nanocolumnssize and density. For temperatures higher than 180deg C, we observed theformation of Ge3Mn5 clusters. For intermediate growth temperatures nanocolumnsand nanoclusters coexist. Combining high resolution TEM and superconductingquantum interference device magnetometry, we could evidence at least fourdifferent magnetic phases in Ge(1-x)Mn(x) films: (i) paramagnetic diluted Mnatoms in the germanium matrix, (ii) superparamagnetic and ferromagnetic low-Tcnanocolumns (120 K < Tc < 170 K), (iii) high-Tc nanocolumns (Tc> 400 K) and(iv) Ge3Mn5 clusters.
label: human

text: Structure and magnetism of self-organized Ge(1-x)Mn(x) nano-columns Abstract: 1. The integration of magnetic functionality into Group IV semiconductors represents a pivotal challenge for the development of future spintronic architectures. 2. This paper examines the structural and magnetic properties of $Ge_{1-x}Mn_x$ thin films synthesized on Ge(001) substrates via molecular beam epitaxy. 3. Our results show that growth at moderate temperatures triggers the self-organization of Mn atoms into vertical, Mn-rich nano-columns. 4. High-resolution transmission electron microscopy confirms that these nano-columns are coherent with the germanium matrix and exhibit a distinct crystalline phase. 5. Chemical mapping through energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy reveals a sharp Mn gradient between the columns and the surrounding diluted matrix. 6. Magnetic characterization performed with a superconducting quantum interference device indicates that the films possess a Curie temperature well above 200 K. 7. We demonstrate that the ferromagnetic response is primarily driven by the high local concentration of Mn within the self-organized structures. 8. The magnetic data also suggest a superparamagnetic transition, where the blocking temperature is sensitive to the height and diameter of the columns. 9. Systematic variations in growth parameters prove that the density and size of these columns can be controlled to optimize the magnetic performance. 10. Ultimately, this work provides a roadmap for achieving high-temperature ferromagnetism in silicon-compatible materials through the controlled formation of self-organized nanostructures.
label: llm

text: This works presents results of activation-aided determination of thresholdreaction rates in 92 209Bi, natPb, 197Au, 181Ta, 169Tm, natIn, 93Nb, 64Zn,65Cu, 63Cu, 59Co, 19F, and 12C samples and in 121 27Al samples. All the sampleswere aligned with the proton beam axis inside and outside the demountable 92-cmthick Pb target of 15-cm diameter assembled of 23 4-cm thick discs. The sampleswere placed on 12 target disks to reproduce the long axis distribution ofprotons and neutrons. In June 2006, the target was exposed for 18 hours to a800-MeV proton beam extracted from the ITEP U-10 accelerator. The protonfluence and the proton beam shape were determined using the 27Al(p,x)7Bemonitor reaction. The reaction rates were determined by the directgamma-spectrometry techniques. In total, 1196 gamma-spectra have been measured,and about 1500 reaction rates determined. The measured reaction rates weresimulated by the MCNPX code using the following databases: ENDF/B6 for neutronsbelow 20 MeV, MENDL2 for 20-100 MeV neutrons, and MENDL2P for proton crosssections up to 200 MeV. An acceptable agreement of simulations withexperimental data has been found.
label: human

text: The investigation of spallation processes in heavy metal targets is crucial for the development of advanced accelerator-driven systems and high-flux neutron sources. In this study, we provide detailed measurements of reaction rates induced by a 0.8 GeV proton beam incident on a thick, cylindrical lead target. The experimental configuration utilized various activation foils positioned at multiple depths and radial distances within the target assembly to map the spatial distribution of the secondary particle field. Specific focus was placed on high-energy threshold reactions, which allow for the sensitive detection of high-energy nucleons produced during the intranuclear cascade phase. The resulting yields of several radioisotopes were determined via gamma-ray spectroscopy and compared against theoretical predictions generated by Monte Carlo transport codes. Our findings indicate that the reaction rates exhibit a strong dependence on spatial coordinates, reflecting the attenuation and buildup of the secondary hadron flux. Discrepancies between the experimental data and simulations were observed particularly for reactions with thresholds exceeding 50 MeV, highlighting potential areas for refinement in nuclear model parameters.
label: llm

text: If the binding energy of the pulsar's surface is not so high (the case of aneutron star), both the negative and positive charges will flow out freely fromthe surface of the star. The annular free flow model for $\gamma$-ray emissionof pulsars is suggested in this paper. It is emphasized that: (1). Two kinds ofacceleration regions (annular and core) need to be taken into account. Theannular acceleration region is defined by the magnetic field lines that crossthe null charge surface within the light cylinder. (2). If the potential dropin the annular region of a pulsar is high enough (normally the cases of youngpulsars), charges in both the annular and the core regions could be acceleratedand produce primary gamma-rays. Secondary pairs are generated in both regionsand stream outwards to power the broadband radiations. (3). The potential dropin the annular region grows more rapidly than that in the core region. Theannular acceleration process is a key point to produce wide emission beams asobserved. (4). The advantages of both the polar cap and outer gap models areretained in this model. The geometric properties of the $\gamma$-ray emissionfrom the annular flow is analogous to that presented in a previous work by Qiaoet al., which match the observations well. (5). Since charges with differentsigns leave the pulsar through the annular and the core regions, respectively,the current closure problem can be partially solved.
label: human

text: Pulsars represent some of the most extreme environments in the universe for studying high-energy astrophysical processes. The detection of pulsed $\gamma$-ray emission provides crucial insights into the acceleration of particles within pulsar magnetospheres. Despite decades of study, the exact location and geometry of the acceleration zones remain subjects of significant debate in the community. In this paper, we develop a comprehensive annular gap model to explain the $\gamma$-ray characteristics of both young and millisecond pulsars. The annular gap is defined as the vacuum region located between the open-volume coordinates and the last closed magnetic field lines near the polar cap. We calculate the electrostatic potential by solving the longitudinal electric field equations within this specific three-dimensional geometry. High-energy particles are accelerated along the magnetic field lines until they reach Lorentz factors sufficient for $\gamma$-ray production. We specifically examine curvature radiation as the primary source of emission in the GeV energy range. Our model incorporates a realistic magnetic field geometry, assuming a retarded force-free configuration to better simulate the outer magnetosphere. We perform detailed numerical simulations to generate light curves for a wide range of magnetic inclinations and viewing angles. The results indicate that the annular gap can effectively produce the distinctive double-peaked profiles observed in many $\gamma$-ray pulsars.
label: llm

text: The CALICE collaboration is presently constructing a test hadron calorimeter(HCAL) with 7620 scintillator tiles read out by novel photo-detectors - SiliconPhotomultipliers (SiPMs). This prototype is the first device which uses SiPMson a large scale. We present the design of the HCAL and report on measuredproperties of more than 10 thousand SiPMs. We discuss the SiPM efficiency,gain, cross-talk, and noise rate dependence on bias voltage and temperature,including the spread in these parameters. We analyze the reasons for SiPMrejection and present the results of the long term stability studies. The firstmeasurements of the SiPM radiation hardness are presented. We compareproperties of SiPM with the properties of similar devices, MRS APD and MPPC. Apossibility to make the tiles thinner and to read them out without WLS fibershas been studied.
label: human

text: High-precision calorimetry is essential for the next generation of high-energy physics experiments to accurately reconstruct jet energy and particle flow. Traditional hadron calorimeters often face challenges regarding readout complexity and the integration of large-scale sensor arrays within limited physical spaces. This paper presents the design and performance of a highly granular scintillator tile hadron calorimeter (HCAL) featuring a novel Silicon Photomultiplier (SiPM) readout system. The proposed architecture utilizes surface-mounted SiPMs directly coupled to individual scintillator tiles, eliminating the need for complex wavelength-shifting fibers. We evaluated the prototype using a combination of laboratory bench tests and high-energy particle beams to assess its response stability and signal uniformity. Experimental results demonstrate excellent energy resolution and a highly linear response across a wide range of incident hadron energies.
label: llm

text: A key idea in coding for the broadcast channel (BC) is binning, in which thetransmitter encode information by selecting a codeword from an appropriate bin(the messages are thus the bin indexes). This selection is normally done bysolving an appropriate (possibly difficult) combinatorial problem. Recently ithas been shown that binning for the Blackwell channel --a particular BC-- canbe done by iterative schemes based on Survey Propagation (SP). This method usesdecimation for SP and suffers a complexity of O(n^2). In this paper we proposea new variation of the Belief Propagation (BP) algorithm, named Reinforced BPalgorithm, that turns BP into a solver. Our simulations show that this newalgorithm has complexity O(n log n). Using this new algorithm together with anon-linear coding scheme, we can efficiently achieve rates close to the borderof the capacity region of the Blackwell channel.
label: human

text: The Blackwell channel represents a fundamental model in information theory for studying communication over discrete memoryless channels with specific constraints. However, developing robust encoding strategies that can effectively approach the capacity of such channels remains a significant technical challenge. In this paper, we propose a novel encoding architecture based on Reinforced Belief Propagation (RBP) to enhance transmission reliability. By integrating reinforcement learning principles with traditional message-passing algorithms, the RBP framework dynamically optimizes the mapping of source symbols to channel inputs. We evaluate the performance of our proposed method through extensive simulations, comparing it against standard linear codes and conventional belief propagation decoders. Our results demonstrate that the RBP-based approach significantly reduces the bit error rate while maintaining high computational efficiency in diverse noise environments.
label: llm

text: We use HST/ACS observations of the spiral galaxy M51 in F435W, F555W andF814W to select a large sample of star clusters with accurate effective radiusmeasurements in an area covering the complete disc of M51. We present thedataset and study the radius distribution and relations between radius, colour,arm/interarm region, galactocentric distance, mass and age. We select a sampleof 7698 (F435W), 6846 (F555W) and 5024 (F814W) slightly resolved clusters andderive their effective radii by fitting the spatial profiles with analyticalmodels convolved with the point spread function. The radii of 1284 clusters arestudied in detail. We find cluster radii between 0.5 and ~10 pc, and oneexceptionally large cluster candidate with a radius of 21.6 pc. The medianradius is 2.1 pc. We find 70 clusters in our sample which have coloursconsistent with being old GC candidates and we find 6 new "faint fuzzy"clusters in, or projected onto, the disc of M51. The radius distribution cannot be fitted with a power law, but a log-normal distribution provides areasonable fit to the data. This indicates that shortly after the formation ofthe clusters from a fractal gas, their radii have changed in a non-uniform way.We find an increase in radius with colour as well as a higher fraction ofredder clusters in the interarm regions, suggesting that clusters in spiralarms are more compact. We find a correlation between radius and galactocentricdistance which is considerably weaker than the observed correlation for oldMilky Way GCs. We find weak relations between cluster luminosity and radius,but we do not observe a correlation between cluster mass and radius.
label: human

text: We present a comprehensive study of the star cluster population in the nearby spiral galaxy M51 using high-resolution imaging from the Hubble Space Telescope’s Advanced Camera for Surveys (ACS). Utilizing multi-band observations, we have developed a robust methodology for the identification and characterization of thousands of star cluster candidates across the galactic disk. The identification process involves a combination of morphology-based selection and photometric criteria to effectively separate clusters from individual stars and background contaminants. A key focus of this work is the determination of the physical sizes of these clusters through the measurement of their effective radii ($R_{eff}$). To achieve this, we employ sophisticated point spread function convolution techniques to fit analytic profiles to the observed light distribution of each candidate. We account for the effects of crowding and varying background levels by performing extensive artificial cluster simulations to quantify our detection completeness and measurement biases. The resulting radius distribution is found to peak at approximately 2 to 3 parsecs, aligning with the sizes observed for clusters in the Milky Way and other local spiral galaxies. Our analysis reveals that the distribution of cluster radii is remarkably similar across different regions of M51, regardless of the local star formation rate or gas density. We further investigate the relationship between cluster size and luminosity, finding only a weak correlation between these two fundamental parameters. These findings suggest that the internal structures of star clusters are largely determined by universal formation processes rather than their immediate galactic environment.
label: llm

text: Aims: Today, large ground-based instruments, like VISIR on the VLT, providingdiffraction-limited (about 0.3 arcsec) images in the mid-infrared where strongPAH features appear enable us to see the flaring structure of the disks aroundHerbig Ae stars.  Although great progress has been made in modelling the disk with radiativetransfer models able to reproduce the spectral energy distribution (SED) ofHerbig Ae stars, the constraints brought by images have not been yet fullyexploited. Here, we are interested in checking if these new observationalimaging constraints can be accounted for by predictions based on existingmodels of passive centrally irradiated hydrostatic disks made to fit the SEDsof the Herbig Ae stars.  Methods: The images taken by VISIR in the 8.6 and 11.3 microns aromaticfeatures reveal a large flaring disk around HD97048 inclined to the line ofsight. In order to analyse the spatial distribution of these data, we use adisk model which includes the most up to date understanding of disk structureand physics around Herbig Ae stars with grains in thermal equilibrium inaddition to transiently-heated PAHs.  Results: We compare the observed spatial distribution of the PAH emissionfeature and the adjacent continuum emission with predictions based on existingfull disk models. Both SED and spatial distribution are in very good agreementwith the model predictions for common disk parameters.  Conclusions: We take the general agreement between observations andpredictions as a strong support for the physical pictures underlying our flareddisk model.
label: human

text: The study of protoplanetary disks is fundamental to uncovering the physical mechanisms that drive planet formation around young stars. HD97048, a Herbig Ae/Be star located in the Chamaeleon I cloud, represents a key target for such research due to its bright and spatially extended disk. In this work, we present high-resolution imaging and spectroscopic observations aimed at resolving the inner and outer regions of the disk with unprecedented detail. Our analysis reveals a complex architecture characterized by a series of concentric rings and gaps that extend across the dust continuum. We specifically identify a prominent spiral arm and asymmetrical features that suggest dynamical perturbations within the gas-rich environment. These observed substructures provide compelling evidence of ongoing interactions between the disk material and hidden protoplanetary bodies. By comparing our findings with radiative transfer models, we constrain the dust mass and grain size distribution necessary to produce the observed emission profiles. Ultimately, this closer look at the HD97048 disk provides critical insights into the early stages of planetary system architecture and the diversity of disk morphologies.
label: llm

text: In the 1980's Stallings showed that every finitely generated subgroup of afree group is canonically represented by a finite minimal immersion of abouquet of circles. In terms of the theory of automata, this is a minimalfinite inverse automaton. This allows for the deep algorithmic theory of finiteautomata and finite inverse monoids to be used to answer questions aboutfinitely generated subgroups of free groups.  In this paper we attempt to apply the same methods to other classes ofgroups. A fundamental new problem is that the Stallings folding algorithm mustbe modified to allow for ``sewing'' on relations of non-free groups. We look atthe class of groups that are amalgams of finite groups. It is known that thesegroups are locally quasiconvex and thus all finitely generated subgroups arerepresented by finite automata. We present an algorithm to compute such afinite automaton and use it to solve various algorithmic problems.
label: human

text: This paper investigates the structural properties of subgroups within amalgams of finite groups by utilizing an extension of Stallings' folding techniques. While Stallings' original theory provides a robust framework for analyzing free groups, its application to amalgams requires a sophisticated adaptation to the language of graphs of groups. We develop a specialized machinery for folding morphisms of graphs of groups that are specifically tailored to the local constraints imposed by finite vertex groups. By representing subgroups as immersions of finite graphs of groups, we demonstrate how sequences of elementary foldings can be used to resolve these immersions into a canonical form. This geometric approach yields a constructive algorithm for addressing the membership problem for finitely generated subgroups within these amalgamated products. Furthermore, we characterize the conditions under which a subgroup inherits finiteness properties or exhibits specific quasi-isometry types relative to the parent group.
label: llm

text: Intersecting stacks of supersymmetric fractional branes on the Z_6'orientifold may be used to construct the supersymmetric Standard Model. If a,bare the stacks that generate the SU(3)_{colour} and SU(2)_L gauge particles,then, in order to obtain {\em just} the chiral spectrum of the (supersymmetric)Standard Model (with non-zero Yukawa couplings to the Higgs mutiplets), it isnecessary that the number of intersections a \cap b of the stacks a and b, andthe number of intersections a \cap b' of a with the orientifold image b' of bsatisfy (a \cap b,a \cap b')=(2,1) or (1,2). It is also necessary that there isno matter in symmetric representations of the gauge group, and not too muchmatter in antisymmetric representations, on either stack. Fractional braneshaving all of these properties may be constructed on the Z_6' orientifold. Weconstruct a (four-stack) model with two further stacks, each with just a singlebrane, which has precisely the matter spectrum of the supersymmetric StandardModel, including a single pair of Higgs doublets. However, the gauge group isSU(3)_{\rm colour} x SU(2)_L x U(1)_Y x U(1)_H. Only the Higgs doublets arecharged with respect to U(1)_H.
label: human

text: We investigate the construction of four-dimensional chiral gauge theories from intersecting D6-branes in Type IIA string theory on a specific toroidal background. The study focuses on the $Z_6'$ orientifold, utilizing its unique geometric and algebraic properties to search for realistic particle physics models. By carefully arranging stacks of D6-branes on the underlying torus, we derive a configuration that yields the gauge group and matter content of the Standard Model. Our analysis demonstrates that a three-generation chiral fermion spectrum can be realized, mirroring the known matter content of the observable universe. While the model successfully reproduces the core features of the Minimal Supersymmetric Standard Model, it is characterized as "almost" complete due to specific remaining phenomenological challenges. These discrepancies often involve the presence of additional non-chiral exotics or difficulties in achieving the exact Higgs sector and Yukawa coupling structure required for full consistency. This work provides a significant step forward in string phenomenology by narrowing the gap between formal string constructions and the low-energy physics of the supersymmetric Standard Model.
label: llm

text: We present a simplified chemical and thermal model designed to allowcomputationally efficient study of the thermal evolution of metal-poor gaswithin large numerical simulations. Our main simplification is the neglect ofthe molecular chemistry of the heavy elements. The only molecular chemistryretained within the model is the formation and destruction of molecularhydrogen. Despite this major simplification, the model allows for accuratetreatment of the thermal evolution of the gas within a large volume ofparameter space. It is valid for temperatures 50 < T < 10000 K andmetallicities 0 < Z < 0.1 Z_solar. In gas with a metallicity Z = 0.1 Z_solar,and in the absence of an incident ultraviolet radiation field, it is valid forhydrogen number densities n_H < 500 / t_char cm^-3, where t_char is the size inMyr of the characteristic physical timescale of interest in the problem. If Z<< 0.1 Z_solar, or if a strong ultraviolet radiation field is present, then themodel remains accurate up to significantly higher densities. We also discusssome possible applications of this model.
label: human

text: Understanding the transition from primordial Population III star formation to the modern Population II/I mode requires a detailed analysis of gas cooling at low metallicities. In this first paper of a series, we investigate the chemical and thermal evolution of collapsing gas clouds across a wide range of sub-solar metallicities. We utilize a comprehensive chemical network that includes hydrogen, helium, and trace amounts of carbon and oxygen, alongside their respective molecular and ionic species. At low densities, the thermal evolution is primarily governed by the balance between compressional heating and cooling via fine-structure lines and molecular hydrogen. Our results indicate that the cooling efficiency of $\text{H}_2$ and HD molecules remains dominant at extremely low metallicities, whereas metal-line cooling becomes significant as the enrichment levels increase. We identify a critical metallicity threshold below which the gas cannot cool effectively enough to allow for low-mass fragmentation at early stages of collapse. The presence of dust grains, even in trace amounts.
label: llm

text: We discuss Casimir effect of a massless, minimally coupled scalar field in a6D warped flux compactification model and its implications for the hierarchyand cosmological constant problems, which are longstanding puzzles inphenomenology and cosmology. Due to the scale invariance of the backgroundtheory, the 4D effective theory contains a volume modulus. To stabilize themodulus, we consider one-loop corrections to the effective potential by theCasimir effect. The one-loop effective potential for the volume modulus has aform which is very similar to Coleman-Weinberg potential. We evaluatecoefficients appearing in the effective potential by employing zeta functionregularization and heat kernel analysis. The volume modulus is stabilized forsmaller degrees of warping, below a critical value, which depends on deficitangle of the reference brane. After stabilizing the modulus, it is possible toobtain observed values of the mass ratio between the fundamental energy scalesand a tiny effective cosmological constant (though its sign is negative). Thedegree of warping should be tuned to be close to the critical value, not asseverely as the original fine-tuning.
label: human

text: Higher-dimensional models with warped geometries offer a compelling framework for addressing the hierarchy problem and explaining the fundamental structure of spacetime. In this paper, we investigate the Casimir effect within a six-dimensional warped flux compactification model, focusing on the vacuum energy arising from quantum fluctuations of bulk fields. The background geometry is characterized by an axially symmetric metric where the extra dimensions are compactified in the presence of stabilizing magnetic fluxes. We derive the one-loop effective potential for various bulk fields to determine their specific contributions to the total energy density of the system. Using the zeta-function regularization technique, we provide an analytical expression for the Casimir energy as a function of the warp factor and the flux magnitude. Our results demonstrate that the competition between the flux-induced potential and the Casimir energy can lead to the successful stabilization of the extra-dimensional radii. Furthermore, we analyze the influence of the warping scale on the sign and magnitude of the vacuum energy, identifying regions of parameter space that support a small, positive cosmological constant.
label: llm

text: Covariant density functional theory, which has so far been applied onlywithin the framework of static and time dependent mean field theory is extendedto include Particle-Vibration Coupling (PVC) in a consistent way. Starting froma conventional energy functional we calculate the low-lying collectivevibrations in Relativistic Random Phase Approximation (RRPA) and construct anenergy dependent self-energy for the Dyson equation. The resultingBethe-Salpeter equation in the particle-hole ($ph$) channel is solved in theTime Blocking Approximation (TBA). No additional parameters are used and doublecounting is avoided by a proper subtraction method. The same energy functional,i.e. the same set of coupling constants, generates the Dirac-Hartreesingle-particle spectrum, the static part of the residual $ph$-interaction andthe particle-phonon coupling vertices. Therefore a fully consistent descriptionof nuclear excited states is developed. This method is applied for aninvestigation of damping phenomena in the spherical nuclei with closed shells$^{208}$Pb and $^{132}$Sn. Since the phonon coupling terms enrich the RRPAspectrum with a multitude of $ph\otimes$phonon components a noticeablefragmentation of the giant resonances is found, which is in full agreement withexperimental data and with results of the semi-phenomenologicalnon-relativistic approach.
label: human

text: Covariant density functional theory (CDFT) provides an excellent description of ground-state properties across the nuclear chart. However, the standard mean-field approximation often fails to accurately predict single-particle energy levels and their fragmentation. To address this limitation, we present a comprehensive framework for particle-vibration coupling (PVC) developed within a covariant Lagrangian approach. This model explicitly accounts for the interaction between nucleons and collective vibrations, which are calculated self-consistently using the relativistic random phase approximation. By maintaining theoretical consistency, the same relativistic effective interaction is employed for both the static mean field and the dynamic vibrational modes. Our results indicate that the inclusion of PVC significantly improves the description of single-particle spectra by increasing the level density near the Fermi surface. We specifically examine the fragmentation of single-particle states and the resulting spectroscopic factors in several doubly magic nuclei. The calculated energy levels and fragmentation patterns show a much better agreement with experimental data compared to pure mean-field results. This work establishes the PVC-CDFT framework as a powerful and necessary tool for studying the complex spectroscopic properties of both stable and exotic nuclei.
label: llm

text: The function exp(iwt) describes an oscillating motion. Energy of theoscillator is proportional to the square of w. exp(iwt) is the solution of adifferential equation. We have replaced this differential equation by thecorresponding finite-time difference equation with d as the smallest span oftime. We have, then, symmetrized the equation so that it remains invariantunder the change d going to -d. This symmetric equation has solutions in pairs.The angular speed w is modified to w' or w". w' contains a part with aninteger. w" contains a part with a half-integer. This corresponds to quantummechanical oscillator energy levels. F= a.exp(iwt) describes oscillationbetween -a and +a. If we make w=0, F describes free oscillation between -a and+a. Reciprocal symmetric oscillator, thus, unifies quantum and classicalharmonic oscillators on one hand, and a harmonic oscillator and a free particlein a potential well on the other hand. No quantum mechanical postulates areinvolved.
label: human

text: This paper explores the fundamental theoretical link between classical mechanics and quantum theory through the lens of reciprocal symmetry. By analyzing the structural similarities in oscillatory motion, we propose a unified framework defined as the Classico-Quantum Oscillator. Central to this model is the principle of reciprocity, which establishes a formal mathematical equivalence between position and momentum coordinates across scales. We demonstrate that the inherent symmetries of the harmonic oscillator are not merely formal coincidences but reflect a deep consistency within potential theory. A primary objective of this study is to bridge the conceptual gap between a particle confined in a standard potential well and the periodic dynamics of a harmonic oscillator. Through rigorous derivation, we show that the boundary conditions of a finite potential well can be mapped onto the continuous phase space of an oscillator using reciprocal transformations. This mapping reveals that the energy eigenvalues of both systems converge when viewed through a unified geometric representation of the underlying state.
label: llm

text: The physical characteristics of the Lyman-alpha forest cloud systems arecombined with observations on the baryonic mass density of the Universe andconstraints from primordial nucleosynthesis to set boundary conditions on theIntergalactic Medium (IGM) at the epoch of z=2.5. The Universe is considered aclosed system and allowed to expand adiabatically from the epoch when QSOsfirst ionized the IGM (5 <= z_on <= 20). The average kinetic energy of a gas iscalculated in the region where the gas transitions from relativistic tonon-relativistic behavior. All of the above measurements are then used todetermine the thermal history of the IGM in the redshift range 2.5 <= z <=z_on. The hot IGM is assumed to inverse Compton scatter photons from the CosmicMicrowave Background (CMBR) and consequently distort the CMBR as seen at thepresent epoch. The temperature of the IGM at z=2.5 and the epoch z_on areadjusted, within the constraints defined above, to give the best overallagreement with published data on the temperature of the IGM. We find that themodel of the IGM proposed here does not grossly distort the CMBR, and in factagrees quite closely with the preliminary results from the Cosmic BackgroundExplorer (COBE) satellite. However, our model of the IGM cannot explain theobserved cosmic x ray background.  This paper was originally written in 1990. It was never submitted forpublication.
label: human

text: The hot inter-galactic medium (IGM) plays a critical role in our understanding of the distribution of baryonic matter within the large-scale structure of the universe. As the universe evolved, gravitational collapse and subsequent shock heating transformed much of the diffuse gas into a high-temperature plasma. This hot component of the IGM interacts with the cosmic microwave background (CMB) primarily through the thermal Sunyaev-Zeldovich effect. In this article, we examine the spectral distortions and spatial fluctuations produced by this interaction across various cosmological scales. We utilize high-resolution hydrodynamic simulations to model the pressure profiles of both virialized clusters and the more diffuse warm-hot intergalactic medium. Our analysis quantifies the contribution of this hot gas to the small-scale power spectrum of the CMB, highlighting the necessity of precise foreground separation. The findings suggest that a significant fraction of the "missing baryons" can be traced through the distinctive signatures left on these microwave maps. Furthermore, we demonstrate how cross-correlation studies between CMB data and large-scale structure surveys provide tighter constraints on the thermal history of the universe. We also explore how different feedback mechanisms from active galactic nuclei influence the observable properties of the hot IGM. Ultimately, this study provides a framework for future high-sensitivity observations to map the invisible energetic landscape of the cosmic web.
label: llm

text: Binary microlensing light curves have a variety of morphologies. Many areindistinguishable from point lens light curves. Of those that deviate from thepoint lens form, caustic crossing light curves have tended to dominateidentified binary lens events. Other distinctive signatures of binary lensesinclude significant asymmetry, multiple peaks, and repeating events. We havequantified, using high resolution simulations, the theoretically expectedrelative numbers of each type of binary lens event, based on its measurablecharacteristics. We find that a microlensing survey with current levels ofphotometric uncertainty and sampling should find at least as many non-causticcrossing binary lens events as caustic crossing events; in future surveys withmore sensitive photometry, the contribution of distinctive non-caustic crossingevents will be even greater. To try to explain why caustic crossing lightcurves appear to be so dominant among the published binary lensing events, weinvestigate the influence of several physical effects, including blending,sampling rate, and various binary populations.
label: human

text: Gravitational microlensing by binary systems serves as a powerful diagnostic for characterizing the mass and separation of distant stellar and planetary companions. Much of the existing literature focuses on the high-magnification caustic crossings that produce sharp, recognizable features in observed light curves. However, a significant fraction of binary events exhibit subtle deviations from single-lens behavior that occur entirely outside these caustic boundaries. In this study, we systematically investigate the properties of these "non-caustic" features across a broad range of mass ratios and projected lens separations. We identify specific light curve morphologies, such as broad shoulders and asymmetric dips, that arise from the extended magnification patterns inherent to binary configurations. Our results show that these features can provide critical constraints on the lens geometry even when the source trajectory does not directly intersect a caustic. These findings suggest that a more comprehensive analysis of low-magnification anomalies will significantly improve the parameter estimation and discovery potential of current and future microlensing surveys.
label: llm

text: In the purely affine formulation of gravity, the gravitational field isrepresented by the symmetric part of the Ricci tensor of the affine connection.The classical electromagnetic field can be represented in this formulation bythe second Ricci tensor of the connection. Such a construction is dynamicallyequivalent to the sourceless Einstein-Maxwell equations. We generalize thisconstruction to the case with sources, represented by the derivative of theaffine Lagrangian density with respect to the connection. We show that theMaxwell equations with sources emerge for the simplest affine Lagrangian formatter, while the Einstein and Lorentz equations arise if mass haselectromagnetic origin. We also show that the Maxwell equations replace theunphysical constraint imposed by the projective invariance of purely affineLagrangians that depend explicitly on the connection.
label: human

text: This paper presents a comprehensive framework for the unification of gravitational and electromagnetic interactions through a purely affine geometric structure. Unlike traditional metric-based approaches, the proposed theory derives all physical properties of spacetime solely from the affine connection, treating the metric tensor as a secondary, derived quantity. By applying a variational principle to a general Lagrangian density dependent on the curvature tensor, we obtain a self-consistent set of field equations that govern both fields. It is demonstrated that the antisymmetric part of the Ricci tensor naturally corresponds to the electromagnetic field strength, while the symmetric part recovers the vacuum Einstein equations in the appropriate limit. These results suggest that the fundamental forces of nature may be interpreted as distinct manifestations of a single, underlying affine geometry of spacetime.
label: llm

text: The physical interpretation of the spectral line polarization produced by thejoint action of the Hanle and Zeeman effects offers a unique opportunity toobtain empirical information about hidden aspects of solar and stellarmagnetism. To this end, it is important to achieve a complete understanding ofthe sensitivity of the emergent spectral line polarization to the presence of amagnetic field. Here we present a detailed theoretical investigation on therole of resonance scattering and magnetic fields on the polarization signals ofthe Ba II D1 and D2 lines of the Fraunhofer spectrum, respectively at 4934 \AA\and 4554 \AA. We adopt a three-level model of Ba II, and we take into accountthe hyperfine structure that is shown by the $^{135}$Ba and $^{137}$Baisotopes. Despite of their relatively small abundance (18%), the contributioncoming from these two isotopes is indeed fundamental for the interpretation ofthe polarization signals observed in these lines. We consider an optically thinslab model, through which we can investigate in a rigorous way the essentialphysical mechanisms involved (resonance polarization, Zeeman, Paschen-Back andHanle effects), avoiding complications due to radiative transfer effects. Weassume the slab to be illuminated from below by the photospheric solarcontinuum radiation field, and we investigate the radiation scattered at 90degrees, both in the absence and in the presence of magnetic fields,deterministic and microturbulent. We show in particular the existence of adifferential magnetic sensitivity of the three-peak Q/I profile that isobserved in the D2 line in quiet regions close to the solar limb, which is ofgreat interest for magnetic field diagnostics.
label: human

text: The Ba II D1 and D2 resonance lines are crucial diagnostic features for exploring the magnetic field architecture of the solar atmosphere. Due to their high atomic weight and distinct formation heights, these lines provide a unique window into the thermal and magnetic structure of the lower chromosphere. This paper presents a comprehensive theoretical analysis of the magnetic sensitivity of these Fraunhofer lines, focusing on both the Zeeman and Hanle effects. We utilize non-LTE radiative transfer modeling combined with a realistic atomic model to simulate the emergence of spectropolarimetric signals under various physical conditions. The investigation reveals that the D2 line at 455.4 nm is exceptionally sensitive to the Hanle effect, making it suitable for diagnosing weak, turbulent magnetic fields. Conversely, the D1 line at 493.4 nm demonstrates a clear Zeeman signature that serves as a reliable probe for stronger, organized magnetic flux tubes. By comparing the synthetic profiles with high-resolution solar observations, we quantify the impact of atomic polarization and its subsequent depolarization by magnetic fields. These results underscore the importance of the Ba II doublet as a complementary tool for multi-line spectropolarimetry in modern solar physics.
label: llm

text: Electromechanical coupling is ubiquitous in biological systems with examplesranging from simple piezoelectricity in calcified and connective tissues tovoltage-gated ion channels, energy storage in mitochondria, andelectromechanical activity in cardiac myocytes and outer hair cell stereocilia.Piezoresponse force microscopy (PFM) has originally emerged as a technique tostudy electromechanical phenomena in ferroelectric materials, and in recentyears, has been employed to study a broad range of non-ferroelectric polarmaterials, including piezoelectric biomaterials. At the same time, thetechnique has been extended from ambient to liquid imaging on modelferroelectric systems. Here, we present results on local electromechanicalprobing of several model cellular and biomolecular systems, including insulinand lysozyme amyloid fibrils, breast adenocarcinoma cells, andbacteriorhodopsin in a liquid environment. The specific features of SPMoperation in liquid are delineated and bottlenecks on the route towardsnanometer-resolution electromechanical imaging of biological systems areidentified.
label: human

text: The characterization of electromechanical properties in biological systems is essential for understanding fundamental processes such as cellular signaling and structural mechanics at the nanoscale. However, translating scanning probe techniques like Piezoresponse Force Microscopy to these systems is complicated by the necessity of performing measurements in liquid environments to preserve physiological functionality. This article discusses the technical developments and experimental strategies required to achieve high-resolution electromechanical probing of cells and biomolecules while submerged in aqueous solutions. These advancements provide a critical framework for investigating the local piezoelectric and flexoelectric responses that underpin the functional behavior of living matter.
label: llm

text: In 1999, Iwan Duursma defined the zeta function for a linear code as agenerating function of its Hamming weight enumerator. It can also be definedfor other homogeneous polynomials not corresponding to existing codes. If thehomogeneous polynomial is invariant under the MacWilliams transform, then itszeta function satisfies a functional equation and we can formulate an analogueof the Riemann hypothesis. As far as existing codes are concerned, the Riemannhypothesis is believed to be closely related to the extremal property.  In this article, we show there are abundant polynomials invariant by theMacWilliams transform which satisfy the Riemann hypothesis. The proof iscarried out by explicit construction of such polynomials. To prove the Riemannhypothesis for a certain class of invariant polynomials, we establish ananalogue of the Enestr"om-Kakeya theorem.
label: human

text: The study of polynomials that satisfy a Riemann hypothesis-type property—where all non-trivial zeros lie on a specific critical line—has become a central theme in modern analytic number theory. While the classic Riemann hypothesis remains one of the most significant unsolved problems, recent developments have shifted focus toward constructing and analyzing family-specific approximations via invariant polynomials. This paper investigates the structural properties of a broad class of invariant polynomials that inherit the symmetry required to satisfy a local version of the Riemann hypothesis. We demonstrate the existence of an abundance of such polynomials by leveraging the theory of group invariants and their relationship to the functional equations of L-functions. Specifically, we show that these polynomials arise naturally from the spectral analysis of certain differential operators and possess zeros that are strictly constrained to the critical line $Re(s) = 1/2$.
label: llm

text: The measurement of the scale of the baryon acoustic oscillations (BAO) in thegalaxy power spectrum as a function of redshift is a promising method toconstrain the equation-of-state parameter of the dark energy w. To measure thescale of the BAO precisely, a substantial volume of space must be surveyed. Wetest whether light-cone effects are important and whether the scaling relationsused to compensate for an incorrect reference cosmology are in this casesufficiently accurate. We investigate the degeneracies in the cosmologicalparameters and the benefits of using the two-dimensional anisotropic powerspectrum. Finally, we estimate the uncertainty with which w can be measured byproposed surveys at redshifts of about z=3 and z=1, respectively.  In the simulated survey we find that light-cone effects are small and thatthe simple scaling relations used to correct for the cosmological distortionwork fairly well even for large survey volumes. The analysis of thetwo-dimensional anisotropic power spectra enables an independent determinationto be made of the apparent scale of the BAO, perpendicular and parallel to theline of sight. This is essential for two-parameter w-models, such as theredshift-dependent dark energy model w=w_0+(1-a)w_a. Using Planck priors forthe matter and baryon density and Delta(H_0)=5% for the Hubble constant, weestimate that the BAO measurements of future surveys around z=3 and z=1 will beable to constrain, independently of other cosmological probes, a constant w to~ 12% and ~ 11% (68% c.l.), respectively.
label: human

text: The accelerated expansion of the universe represents a central mystery in modern physics, driving the need for increasingly precise constraints on dark energy. Baryon acoustic oscillations (BAO) serve as a fundamental standard ruler, allowing cosmologists to map the expansion history by measuring the characteristic scale of matter clustering across different epochs. However, traditional power spectrum analyses frequently assume a single effective redshift for a given volume, which may overlook the continuous evolution of cosmic structures along the observer's light cone. This study investigates the advantages of utilizing the (an)isotropic light-cone power spectrum to extract dark energy information from large-scale structure data more accurately. We develop a theoretical model that integrates the time-dependent growth of fluctuations and geometric distortions directly into the power spectrum estimator. Applying this framework to synthetic galaxy catalogs, we evaluate how light-cone effects influence the recovery of the Alcock-Paczynski parameters and the BAO scale. Our analysis reveals that accounting for the light-cone geometry reduces systematic biases and enhances the signal-to-noise ratio of the extracted cosmological parameters. Specifically, we find that the light-cone approach yields significantly tighter constraints on the dark energy equation of state than standard snapshot-based methods. These findings underscore the importance of light-cone modeling for upcoming high-redshift spectroscopic surveys aimed at unraveling the fundamental properties of dark energy.
label: llm

text: We first present chemodynamical simulations to investigate how stellar windsof massive stars influence early dynamical and chemical evolution of formingglobular clusters (GCs). In our numerical models, GCs form inturbulent,high-density giant molecular clouds (GMCs), which are embedded in amassive dark matter halo at high redshifts. We show how high-density, compactstellar systems are formed from GMCs influenced both by physical processesassociated with star formation and by tidal fields of their host halos. We alsoshow that chemical pollution of GC-forming GMCs by stellar winds from massivestars can result in star-to-star abundance inhomogeneities among light elements(e.g., C, N, and O) of stars in GCs. The present model with a canonical initialmass function (IMF) also shows a C-N anticorrelation that stars with smaller[C/Fe] have larger [N/Fe] in a GC. Although these results imply that``self-pollution'' of GC-forming GMCs by stellar winds from massive stars cancause abundance inhomogeneities of GCs, the present models with differentparameters and canonical IMFs can not show N-rich stars with [N/Fe] ~ 0.8observed in some GCs (e.g., NGC 6752). We discuss this apparent failure in thecontext of massive star formation preceding low-mass one within GC-forming GMCs(``bimodal star formation scenario''). We also show that although almost allstars (~97%) show normal He abundances (Y) of ~0.24 some stars later formed inGMCs can have Y as high as ~0.3 in some models. The number fraction of He-richstars with Y >0.26 is however found to be small (~10^-3) for most models.
label: human

text: Globular clusters are among the oldest stellar systems in the universe, providing vital clues about early galactic assembly and the conditions of the primordial interstellar medium. However, the presence of multiple stellar populations with distinct chemical signatures remains a significant puzzle that challenges our understanding of star formation. This paper examines the critical role of massive stars as the primary drivers of chemical enrichment and dynamical evolution during the initial stages of cluster assembly. We analyze how mass loss from fast-rotating massive stars and interacting binary systems contributes to the enriched gas reservoir from which second-generation stars originate. Furthermore, the intense ionizing radiation and mechanical feedback from these massive progenitors significantly influence the gas expulsion process within the young proto-cluster. Through high-resolution hydrodynamic simulations, we investigate how the timing and efficiency of this feedback dictate the final mass and spatial distribution of the stellar populations. Our results demonstrate that massive star feedback is essential for reproducing the observed anticorrelations in light-element abundances, such as the sodium-oxygen trend found in nearly all ancient clusters. We also address the limitations of current models, particularly concerning the mass budget problem and the high initial cluster masses required by evolutionary scenarios. Ultimately, understanding the complex interplay between massive stars and their parental environments is fundamental to deciphering the formation history of the Milky Way’s globular cluster system.
label: llm

text: We present a search for the near infrared spectroscopic signature of theclose orbiting extrasolar giant planet HD 75289b. We obtained ~230 spectra inthe wavelength range 2.18 - 2.19 microns using the Phoenix spectrograph atGemini South. By considering the direct spectrum, derived from irradiated modelatmospheres, we search for the absorption profile signature present in thecombined star and planet light. Since the planetary spectrum is separated fromthe stellar spectrum at most phases, we apply a phase dependent orbital modeland tomographic techniques to search for absorption signatures.  Because the absorption signature lies buried in the noise of a singleexposure we apply a multiline deconvolution to the spectral lines available inorder to boost the effective S/N ratio of the data. The wavelength coverage of80 angstroms is expected to contain ~100 planetary lines, enabling a mean linewith S/N ratio of ~800 to be achieved after deconvolution. We are neverthelessunable to detect the presence of the planet in the data and carry out furthersimulations to show that broader wavelength coverage should enable a planetlike HD 75289b to be detected with 99.9 per cent (4 sigma) confidence. Weinvestigate the sensitivity of our method and estimate detection tolerances formismatches between observed and model planetary atmospheres.
label: human

text: We present the results of a high-resolution spectroscopic search for the short-period giant planet HD 75289b in the near-infrared K-band. Observations were conducted using the Very Large Telescope over several nights to capture the planet near its superior conjunction and maximum radial velocity separation. The analysis focused on identifying molecular absorption or emission lines from the planetary atmosphere by cross-correlating the data with synthetic spectral models. Significant effort was dedicated to the removal of stellar and telluric features, which are several orders of magnitude stronger than the predicted planetary signal. Our search did not yield a direct detection of the planet’s reflected or emitted light at the $3\sigma$ confidence level. We used this non-detection to derive stringent upper limits on the planet’s mass and orbital inclination. The results suggest that the planetary atmosphere may be characterized by high-altitude clouds or a lower-than-expected temperature profile. These findings contribute to the ongoing efforts to refine the observational limits for characterizing hot Jupiter atmospheres via ground-based spectroscopy.
label: llm

text: We constrain blastwave parameters and the circumburst media of a subsample often BeppoSAX Gamma-Ray Bursts. For this sample we derive the values of theinjected electron energy distribution index, p, and the density structure indexof the circumburst medium, k, from simultaneous spectral fits to their X-ray,optical and nIR afterglow data. The spectral fits have been done in count spaceand include the effects of metallicity, and are compared with the previouslyreported optical and X-ray temporal behaviour. Using the blastwave model andsome assumptions which include on-axis viewing and standard jet structure,constant blastwave energy and no evolution of the microphysical parameters, wefind a mean value of p for the sample as a whole of 2.04 +0.02/-0.03. Astatistical analysis of the distribution demonstrates that the p values in thissample are inconsistent with a single universal value for p at the 3-sigmalevel or greater, which has significant implications for particle accelerationmodels. This approach provides us with a measured distribution of circumburstdensity structures rather than considering only the cases of k=0 (homogeneous)and k=2 (wind-like). We find five GRBs for which k can be well constrained, andin four of these cases the circumburst medium is clearly wind-like. The fifthsource has a value of 0<k<1, consistent with a homogeneous circumburst medium.
label: human

text: Gamma-ray burst (GRB) afterglows serve as critical diagnostics for understanding the microphysics of relativistic shocks and the density structure of the environments where these bursts occur. In this second installment of a series, we perform an extensive broadband temporal and spectral analysis of a diverse sample of GRB afterglows to derive their fundamental physical parameters. A primary objective of this work is to characterize the statistical distribution of the electron power-law index, $p$, to test the universality of shock acceleration theories. Our results reveal that $p$ exhibits a significant spread across the population, with a mean value that aligns with theoretical expectations for diffusive shock acceleration while allowing for individual variation. We also investigate the spatial configuration of the circumburst medium by comparing the observational fit quality for constant-density and wind-stratified environments. The analysis indicates a notable diversity in environment types, suggesting that GRB progenitors may emerge from a wider range of stellar evolutionary paths than previously assumed. These environmental findings offer important constraints on the mass-loss history of the progenitor stars and the density scales of their surrounding gaseous envelopes. Ultimately, this study enhances our global understanding of GRB blastwave evolution and provides a robust framework for interpreting multi-wavelength data from future high-energy transient surveys.
label: llm

text: We report the conjectures on the three-dimensional (3D) Ising model on simpleorthorhombic lattices, together with the details of calculations for a putativeexact solution. Two conjectures, an additional rotation in the fourth curled-updimension and the weight factors on the eigenvectors, are proposed to serve asa boundary condition to deal with the topologic problem of the 3D Ising model.The partition function of the 3D simple orthorhombic Ising model is evaluatedby spinor analysis, by employing these conjectures. Based on the validity ofthe conjectures, the critical temperature of the simple orthorhombic Isinglattices could be determined by the relation of KK* = KK' + KK'' + K'K'' orsinh 2K sinh 2(K' + K'' + K'K''/K) = 1. For a simple cubic Ising lattice, thecritical point is putatively determined to locate exactly at the golden ratioxc = exp(-2Kc) = (sq(5) - 1)/2, as derived from K* = 3K or sinh 2K sinh 6K = 1.If the conjectures would be true, the specific heat of the simple orthorhombicIsing system would show a logarithmic singularity at the critical point of thephase transition. The spontaneous magnetization and the spin correlationfunctions of the simple orthorhombic Ising ferromagnet are derived explicitly.The putative critical exponents derived explicitly for the simple orthorhombicIsing lattices are alpha = 0, beta = 3/8, gamma = 5/4, delta = 13/3, eta = 1/8and nu = 2/3, showing the universality behavior and satisfying the scalinglaws. The cooperative phenomena near the critical point are studied and theresults obtained based on the conjectures are compared with those of theapproximation methods and the experimental findings. The 3D to 2D crossoverphenomenon differs with the 2D to 1D crossover phenomenon and there is agradual crossover of the exponents from the 3D values to the 2D ones.
label: human

text: The search for an exact analytical solution to the three-dimensional (3D) Ising model remains one of the most significant challenges in statistical physics. This paper presents a series of conjectures aimed at providing an exact solution for the 3D simple orthorhombic Ising lattice. By introducing a generalized algebraic framework, we explore the transfer matrix approach within the context of non-commutative geometry and topological considerations. We specifically address the constraints imposed by the crossing of world-lines, proposing that these topological knots can be resolved through specific mathematical transformations. Based on these conjectures, we derive the partition function and the corresponding critical temperatures for orthorhombic lattices with anisotropic interaction constants. The results are shown to reduce correctly to the known 2D Onsager solution and are consistent with previously proposed conjectures for the isotropic simple cubic case. These findings offer a potential pathway toward a rigorous mathematical proof and provide deeper insight into the universal nature of phase transitions in three dimensions.
label: llm

text: Single-particle excitation spectra of the two-dimensional Hubbard model onthe square lattice near half filling and at zero temperature are investigatedon the basis of the self-consistent projection operator method. The methodguarantees a high accuracy of the spectra with high energy and high momentumresolutions. It takes into account long-range intersite correlations as well asthe strong on-site correlations. Effects of nonlocal excitations are clarifiedby comparing the results with those of the single-site approximation. Thecalculated spectra verify the quantum Monte-Carlo results for finitetemperatures. The spectra at the Fermi level yield a hole-like Fermi surface inthe underdoped region and an electron-like Fermi surface in the overdopedregion. From a numerical analysis of the momentum dependent effective mass andself-energy, it is concluded that a marginal Fermi-liquid like state persistseven at finite doping concentrations in the strongly correlated region becausea van Hove singularity is pinned to the Fermi surface. It is also found that akink structure appears in the quasiparticle energy band in the same region. Thekink is shown to be caused by a mixing between the quasiparticle band and anexcitation band with strong short-range antiferromagnetic correlations. Theseresults suggest an explanation for some of the unusual properties of the normalstate in high-$T_{\rm c}$ cuprates.

text: The two-dimensional (2D) Hubbard model remains a fundamental framework for understanding the complex physics of strongly correlated electron systems and high-temperature superconductivity. Despite significant progress in the field, the precise nature of nonlocal excitation spectra in the doped regime remains a subject of intense theoretical debate. In this work, we systematically investigate the evolution of the momentum-resolved spectral function and collective excitations using advanced numerical cluster methods. Our analysis focuses on the transition from the Mott insulating state to the overdoped metallic phase, emphasizing the critical role of spatial correlations. We find that nonlocal effects significantly modify the quasiparticle dispersion, leading to the emergence of pronounced Fermi arcs in the underdoped regime. The calculated spectra reveal a clear separation between coherent and incoherent excitations, which is found to be strongly dependent on the specific doping level. Furthermore, we demonstrate that short-range antiferromagnetic correlations persist well into the doped phase, manifesting as distinct peak structures in the spin-excitation sector. These results provide a theoretical basis that is in excellent qualitative agreement with recent angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) data observed in copper-oxide materials. Our findings suggest that the interplay between local Hubbard interactions and nonlocal fluctuations is essential for capturing the pseudogap phenomenon accurately.

text: We calculate the nuclear matrix elements of the neutrinoless double beta($0\nu\beta\beta$) decays of $^{76}$Ge and $^{82}$Se for the light-neutrinoexchange mechanism. The nuclear wave functions are obtained by using realistictwo-body forces within the proton-neutron quasiparticle random-phaseapproximation (pnQRPA). We include the effects that come from the finite sizeof a nucleon, from the higher-order terms of nucleonic weak currents, and fromthe nucleon-nucleon short-range correlations. Most importantly, we improve onthe presently available calculations by replacing the rudimentary Jastrowshort-range correlations by the more advanced unitary correlation operatormethod (UCOM). The UCOM corrected matrix elements turn out to be notably largerin magnitude than the Jastrow corrected ones. This has drastic consequences forthe detectability of $0\nu\beta\beta$ decay in the present and future doublebeta experiments.

text: The search for neutrinoless double beta decay ($0\nu\beta\beta$) remains a primary frontier in particle physics for determining the Majorana nature and absolute mass scale of neutrinos. However, the accurate extraction of neutrino properties from experimental half-life limits is currently hindered by significant theoretical uncertainties in nuclear matrix elements (NMEs). This study presents an improved treatment of short-range correlations (SRC) based on a more rigorous implementation of nucleon-nucleon interactions at small distances. This refined framework is applied to calculate the NMEs for the key experimental candidates $^{76}$Ge and $^{82}$Se using a self-consistent nuclear structure approach. Our results indicate that the inclusion of modernized SRC schemes leads to a systematic shift in the matrix elements compared to traditional phenomenological parameterizations. Consequently, these findings offer a more robust theoretical foundation for interpreting data from next-generation $0\nu\beta\beta$ experiments.

text:
Multicriticality of the gonihedric model in 2+1 dimensions is investigatednumerically. The gonihedric model is a fully frustrated Ising magnet with thefinely tuned plaquette-type (four-body and plaquette-diagonal) interactions,which cancel out the domain-wall surface tension. Because thequantum-mechanical fluctuation along the imaginary-time direction is simplyferromagnetic, the criticality of the (2+1)-dimensional gonihedric model shouldbe an anisotropic one; that is, the respective critical indices of real-space(\perp) and imaginary-time (\parallel) sectors do not coincide. Extending theparameter space to control the domain-wall surface tension, we analyze thecriticality in terms of the crossover (multicritical) scaling theory. By meansof the numerical diagonalization for the clusters with N\le 28 spins, weobtained the correlation-length critical indices(
u_\perp,
