text: The (2+1)-dimensional gonihedric model, a spin system characterized by four-spin plaquette interactions, is investigated to determine its complex phase structure and critical behavior. While the model is traditionally associated with tensionless string theories and degenerate ground states, the nature of its multicritical transitions has remained largely unexplored. In this work, we employ high-precision Monte Carlo simulations and finite-size scaling analysis to map the phase diagram across a range of coupling parameters. Our results reveal the existence of a unique multicritical point where the standard ferromagnetic phase meets a region of modulated, spatially oscillating structures. We demonstrate that this intersection provides a concrete physical realization of the (d,m)=(3,2) Lifshitz point, characterized by specific anisotropic scaling laws. These findings establish the gonihedric model as a valuable framework for studying anisotropic critical phenomena and the interplay between geometry and statistical mechanics in low-dimensional systems.

text: Based on previous studies deriving the chiral Lagrangian for pseudo scalarmesons from the first principle of QCD, we derive the electroweak chiralLagrangian and build up a formulation for computing its coefficients fromone-doublet technicolor model and a schematic topcolor-assisted technicolormodel. We find that the coefficients of the electroweak chiral Lagrangian forthe topcolor-assisted technicolor model are divided into three parts: directTC2 interaction part, TC1 and TC2 induced effective Z' particle contributionpart, and ordinary quarks contribution part. The first two parts are computedin this paper and we show that the direct TC2 interaction part is the same asthat in the one-doublet technicolor model, while effective Z' contributions areat least proportional to the p^2 order parameter \beta_1 in the electroweakchiral Lagrangian and typical features of topcolor-assisted technicolor modelare that it only allows positive T and U parameters and the T parameter variesin the range 0\sim 1/(25\alpha), the upper bound of T parameter will decreaseas long as Z' mass become large. The S parameter can be either positive ornegative depending on whether the Z' mass is large or small. The Z' mass isalso bounded above and the upper bound depend on value of T parameter. Weobtain the values for all the coefficients of the electroweak chiral Lagrangianup to order of p^4.

text: The Electroweak Chiral Lagrangian provides an essential model-independent framework for characterizing the low-energy effects of potential new physics in the electroweak symmetry-breaking sector. This paper presents a detailed dynamical computation of the various coefficients within this Lagrangian, derived from specific high-energy completions. We evaluate these parameters specifically for the One-doublet Technicolor model and the Topcolor-assisted Technicolor (TC2) model to determine their respective contributions. Utilizing a non-perturbative approach based on the Schwinger-Dyson equations, we calculate the low-energy constants by accounting for the dynamics of technifermions and top-quark condensates. The resulting numerical estimates for the chiral coefficients reveal significant differences between the two models, particularly regarding their predictions for oblique parameters and longitudinal vector boson scattering. These results not only clarify the phenomenological status of technicolor-based theories but also provide a basis for distinguishing between different dynamical symmetry-breaking mechanisms at future colliders.

text: This paper explores a comparative study of both the linear and kernelimplementations of three of the most popular Appearance-based Face Recognitionprojection classes, these being the methodologies of Principal ComponentAnalysis, Linear Discriminant Analysis and Independent Component Analysis. Theexperimental procedure provides a platform of equal working conditions andexamines the ten algorithms in the categories of expression, illumination,occlusion and temporal delay. The results are then evaluated based on asequential combination of assessment tools that facilitate both intuitive andstatistical decisiveness among the intra and interclass comparisons. The bestcategorical algorithms are then incorporated into a hybrid methodology, wherethe advantageous effects of fusion strategies are considered.

text: This paper presents a comprehensive and independent evaluation of several prominent subspace-based face recognition algorithms, including Principal Component Analysis, Linear Discriminant Analysis, and Independent Component Analysis. To ensure an unbiased comparison, the performance of these methods is rigorously tested across multiple standardized datasets under varying conditions of illumination, facial expression, and pose. Our experimental results reveal significant variations in recognition accuracy and computational efficiency, highlighting how specific subspace projections perform under different environmental constraints. The study concludes by providing a comparative framework that assists researchers in selecting the most robust algorithms for diverse real-world biometric applications.

text: We present a full-sky model of polarized Galactic microwave emission based onthree years of observations by the Wilkinson Microwave Anisotropy Probe (WMAP)at frequencies from 23 to 94 GHz. The model compares maps of the Stokes Q and Ucomponents from each of the 5 WMAP frequency bands in order to separatesynchrotron from dust emission, taking into account the spatial and frequencydependence of the synchrotron and dust components. This simple two-componentmodel of the interstellar medium accounts for at least 97% of the polarizedemission in the WMAP maps of the microwave sky. Synchrotron emission dominatesthe polarized foregrounds at frequencies below 50 GHz, and is comparable to thedust contribution at 65 GHz. The spectral index of the synchrotron component,derived solely from polarization data, is -3.2 averaged over the full sky, witha modestly flatter index on the Galactic plane. The synchrotron emission hasmean polarization fraction 2--4% in the Galactic plane and rising to over 20%at high latitude, with prominent features such as the North Galactic Spur morepolarized than the diffuse component. Thermal dust emission has polarizationfraction 1% near the Galactic center, rising to 6% at the anti-center. Diffuseemission from high-latitude dust is also polarized with mean fractionalpolarization 0.036 +/- 0.011.

text: This paper presents a detailed analysis of the polarized foreground emission observed during the first three years of the Wilkinson Microwave Anisotropy Probe (WMAP) mission. The primary objective is to characterize the diffuse Galactic emission that contaminates the measurement of the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) polarization signals. We examine the polarization data across all five WMAP frequency bands, from 23 to 94 GHz, to distinguish between different physical emission mechanisms. Our findings indicate that synchrotron radiation is the dominant polarized foreground at lower frequencies, with a spatial distribution that closely traces the Galactic magnetic field. At the highest frequencies, polarized thermal dust emission becomes the primary contaminant, requiring a sophisticated multi-component model for accurate subtraction. We utilize the low-frequency channels to produce cleaned maps of the CMB E-mode and B-mode polarization while accounting for the varying spectral indices of the foreground components. This characterization is essential for minimizing systematic errors in the determination of the optical depth to reionization, $\tau$, derived from the large-scale E-mode signal. Overall, the analysis provides the critical foreground templates and uncertainty estimates necessary for a rigorous cosmological interpretation of the WMAP three-year polarization data.
label: llm

text: A spectral method is described for solving coupled elliptic problems on aninterior and an exterior domain. The method is formulated and tested on thetwo-dimensional interior Poisson and exterior Laplace problems, whose solutionsand their normal derivatives are required to be continuous across theinterface. A complete basis of homogeneous solutions for the interior andexterior regions, corresponding to all possible Dirichlet boundary values atthe interface, are calculated in a preprocessing step. This basis is used toconstruct the influence matrix which serves to transform the coupled boundaryconditions into conditions on the interior problem. Chebyshev approximationsare used to represent both the interior solutions and the boundary values. Astandard Chebyshev spectral method is used to calculate the interior solutions.The exterior harmonic solutions are calculated as the convolution of thefree-space Green's function with a surface density; this surface density isitself the solution to an integral equation which has an analytic solution whenthe boundary values are given as a Chebyshev expansion. Properties of Chebyshevapproximations insure that the basis of exterior harmonic functions representsthe external near-boundary solutions uniformly. The method is tested bycalculating the electrostatic potential resulting from charge distributions ina rectangle. The resulting influence matrix is well-conditioned and solutionsconverge exponentially as the resolution is increased. The generalization ofthis approach to three-dimensional problems is discussed, in particular themagnetohydrodynamic equations in a finite cylindrical domain surrounded by avacuum.
label: human

text: This paper addresses the numerical solution of elliptic partial differential equations defined over composite domains consisting of both interior and exterior regions. Such problems are frequently encountered in fields like acoustics, electromagnetics, and fluid dynamics, where local features interact significantly with far-field behaviors. Existing numerical approaches often encounter difficulties when attempting to maintain high-order accuracy while transitioning between bounded domains and the unbounded exterior. To overcome these challenges, we propose a novel spectral method specifically designed to match interior and exterior elliptic problems across a common interface. For the interior domain, we employ high-order spectral approximations, such as Chebyshev or Legendre polynomials, to accurately capture complex local variations. In the exterior domain, the infinite physical space is mapped onto a finite computational interval using specialized algebraic or exponential coordinate transformations. The coupling of the two regions is achieved through the rigorous enforcement of Dirichlet and Neumann matching conditions to ensure the continuity of the solution and its flux. The resulting discrete formulation leads to a global system that can be solved efficiently using tailored preconditioned iterative solvers. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the proposed method achieves exponential convergence rates for both the local solution and the far-field decay profile. Our results indicate that this spectral matching technique offers a robust and highly accurate framework for solving a wide range of unbounded domain problems in computational science.
label: llm

text: My project computed the one loop fermion self-energy for massless Dirac +Einstein in the presence of a locally de Sitter background. I employeddimensional regularization and obtain a fully renormalized result by absorbingall divergences with Bogliubov, Parasiuk, Hepp and Zimmermann (BPHZ)counterterms. An interesting technical aspect of my computation was the needfor a noninvariant counterterm, owing to the breaking of de Sitter invarianceby our gauge condition. I also solved the effective Dirac equation for masslessfermions during inflation in the simplest gauge, including all one loopcorrections from quantum gravity. At late times the result for a spatial planewave behaves as if the classical solution were subjected to a time-dependentfield strength renormalization of Z_2(t) = 1 - 17(4 pi) *G H^2 *ln(a) + O(G^2).I showed that this also follows from making the Hartree approximation, althoughthe numerical coefficients differ.

text: This paper investigates the evolution of fermion mode functions within the framework of a de Sitter inflationary background while accounting for leading-order quantum corrections. By employing the Schwinger-Keldysh formalism, we derive the quantum-corrected Dirac equation incorporating the one-loop self-energy. Our analysis focuses on a Yukawa-coupled system where a light fermion interacts with a massless scalar field, leading to significant modifications in the field dynamics. We demonstrate that these quantum effects result in a secular enhancement of the fermion mode functions, which scales logarithmically with the scale factor. These findings suggest that loop-level interactions may have non-trivial implications for the stability of the inflationary vacuum and the generation of primordial perturbations.
label: llm

text: Trafficking of AMPA receptors in and out of synapses is crucial for synapticplasticity. Previous studies have focused on the role of endo/exocytosisprocesses or that of lateral diffusion of extra-synaptic receptors. We have nowdirectly imaged AMPAR movements inside and outside synapses of live neuronsusing single-molecule fluorescence microscopy. Inside individual synapses, wefound immobile and mobile receptors, which display restricted diffusion.Extra-synaptic receptors display free diffusion. Receptors could also exchangebetween these membrane compartments through lateral diffusion. Glutamateapplication increased both receptor mobility inside synapses and the fractionof mobile receptors present in a juxtasynaptic region. Block of inhibitorytransmission to favor excitatory synaptic activity induced a transient increasein the fraction of mobile receptors and a decrease in the proportion ofjuxtasynaptic receptors. Altogether, our data show that rapid exchange ofreceptors between a synaptic and extra-synaptic localization occurs throughregulation of receptor diffusion inside synapses.
label: human

text: AMPA receptors (AMPARs) are crucial mediators of fast excitatory neurotransmission and play a fundamental role in the regulation of synaptic plasticity. While the lateral diffusion of AMPARs on the neuronal surface has been well-documented in extrasynaptic regions, the specific dynamics occurring within the confined environment of the synapse remain poorly understood. In this study, we utilized high-resolution single-molecule tracking coupled with advanced fluorescent labeling to directly image the lateral movements of individual AMPARs inside living synapses. Our observations reveal that AMPARs are not stationary within the postsynaptic density but instead exhibit significant lateral mobility across various sub-synaptic domains. We identified distinct kinetic states of receptor movement, characterized by periods of rapid diffusion interspersed with transient trapping at specific molecular nanodomains. Quantitative analysis indicates that these movement patterns are highly sensitive to the presence of scaffolding proteins and the local molecular density of the synaptic cleft. Furthermore.
label: llm

text: The greatest challenge in the interpretation of galaxy clustering data fromany surveys is galaxy bias. Using a simple Fisher matrix analysis, we show thatthe bispectrum provides an excellent determination of linear and non-linearbias parameters of intermediate and high-z galaxies, when all measurabletriangle configurations down to mildly non-linear scales, where perturbationtheory is still valid, are included. The bispectrum is also a powerful probe ofprimordial non-Gaussianity. The planned galaxy surveys at z>2 should yieldconstraints on non-Gaussian parameters, f_{NL}^{loc.} and f_{NL}^{eq.}, thatare comparable to, or even better than, those from CMB experiments. We studyhow these constraints improve with volume, redshift range, as well as thenumber density of galaxies. Finally, we show that a halo occupationdistribution may be used to improve these constraints further by liftingdegeneracies between gravity, bias, and primordial non-Gaussianity.
label: human

text: High-redshift galaxy surveys offer a unique window into the early universe's initial conditions and the subsequent evolution of large-scale structures. While the galaxy power spectrum has been extensively studied, the bispectrum provides critical information on the non-Gaussian nature of primordial density fluctuations. This paper investigates the potential of the galaxy bispectrum to constrain primordial non-Gaussianity, specifically the local $f_{NL}$ parameter, using simulated data representative of upcoming deep spectroscopic surveys. A major challenge in this analysis is the presence of non-linear galaxy bias, which can effectively mimic or obscure the subtle signals of primordial non-Gaussianity. We employ a comprehensive bias expansion model to account for the complex, non-linear relationship between the observed galaxy distribution and the underlying dark matter field. Our results indicate that the inclusion of the bispectrum significantly improves the precision of $f_{NL}$ measurements compared to analyses using the power spectrum alone.
label: llm

text: Formal actions of Lie algebras over vector spaces are introduced in a purelyalgebraic way, as a mimic of infinitesimal operations of Banach Lie algebrasover Banach analytic manifolds. In analogy with the case of abstract groups,complete wreath products and triangular actions are then defined for Liealgebras acting "en cascade" over vector spaces. Finally, a Kaloujnine-Krasnertype theorem for Lie algebra extensions is proved.  -----  En mimant les lois d'op\'erations infinit\'esimales des alg\`ebres de Lie surles vari\'et\'e s analytiques banachiques, on introduit de mani\`ere purementalg\`ebrique la notion d'action formelle d'une alg\`ebre de Lie sur un espacevectoriel. Ensuite, par analogie avec le cas des groupes abstraits, et enfaisant op\'erer les alg\`ebres de Lie "en cascade", on d\'efinit produitd'entrelacement ("wreath product") et action triangulaire pour les alg\`ebresde Lie. On d\'emontre enfin un th\'eor\`eme du type Kaloujnine-Krasner pour lesextensions d'alg\`ebres de Lie.

text: Cet article étudie la construction et les propriétés structurelles du produit d'entrelacement d'algèbres de Lie sur un corps de caractéristique zéro. Nous nous concentrons spécifiquement sur la notion d'action triangulaire, qui généralise le concept classique des représentations matricielles triangulaires au contexte de ces produits. En analysant une algèbre de Lie agissant sur une somme directe de copies d'une autre algèbre, nous définissons un plongement naturel qui préserve cette structure triangulaire. Nous démontrons que toute action triangulaire d'une algèbre de Lie de dimension finie peut être identifiée à une sous-algèbre d'un produit d'entrelacement spécifique. Par ailleurs, nous examinons comment les propriétés de résolubilité et de nilpotence se transfèrent des algèbres de base au produit global. Ces résultats offrent un cadre rigoureux pour la classification des extensions d'algèbres de Lie et ouvrent de nouvelles pistes en théorie des représentations.
label: llm

text: This paper proposes a method to address the longstanding problem of lack ofmonotonicity in estimation of conditional and structural quantile functions,also known as the quantile crossing problem. The method consists in sorting ormonotone rearranging the original estimated non-monotone curve into a monotonerearranged curve. We show that the rearranged curve is closer to the truequantile curve in finite samples than the original curve, establish afunctional delta method for rearrangement-related operators, and derivefunctional limit theory for the entire rearranged curve and its functionals. Wealso establish validity of the bootstrap for estimating the limit law of thethe entire rearranged curve and its functionals. Our limit results are genericin that they apply to every estimator of a monotone econometric function,provided that the estimator satisfies a functional central limit theorem andthe function satisfies some smoothness conditions. Consequently, our resultsapply to estimation of other econometric functions with monotonicityrestrictions, such as demand, production, distribution, and structuraldistribution functions. We illustrate the results with an application toestimation of structural quantile functions using data on Vietnam veteranstatus and earnings.

text: Quantile regression and conditional probability estimation are essential techniques for capturing the full distribution of a response variable, yet they often suffer from the problematic issue of crossing curves. Such crossings violate the basic mathematical principle that quantile functions must be monotonic and cumulative distribution functions must be non-decreasing. This paper proposes a comprehensive methodological framework to estimate multiple quantile and probability curves simultaneously while strictly ensuring they do not intersect. By incorporating structural constraints into a flexible estimation process, our approach maintains the inherent ordering of the curves across the entire covariate space. We establish the asymptotic properties of the proposed estimators and conduct a series of simulation studies to evaluate their performance relative to traditional, unconstrained methods. The practical utility of the model is demonstrated through an empirical application where it produces logically consistent predictive intervals for high-dimensional data. These findings provide a reliable solution for statistical practitioners who require robust, non-crossing distributional forecasts in diverse fields such as economics, medicine, and environmental science.
label: llm

text: We explicitly construct the fully back-reacted half-BPS solutions in Type IIBsupergravity which are dual to Wilson loops with 16 supersymmetries in$\mathcal{N}=4$ super Yang-Mills. In a first part, we use the methods of acompanion paper to derive the exact general solution of the half-BPS equationson the space $AdS_2 \times S^2 \times S^4 \times \Sigma$, with isometry group$SO(2,1)\times SO(3) \times SO(5)$ in terms of two locally harmonic functionson a Riemann surface $\Sigma$ with boundary. These solutions, generally, havevarying dilaton and axion, and non-vanishing 3-form fluxes. In a second part,we impose regularity and topology conditions. These non-singular solutions maybe parametrized by a genus $g \geq 0$ hyperelliptic surface $\Sigma$, all ofwhose branch points lie on the real line. Each genus $g$ solution has only asingle asymptotic $AdS_5 \times S^5$ region, but exhibits $g$ homology3-spheres, and an extra $g$ homology 5-spheres, carrying respectively RR 3-formand RR 5-form charges. For genus 0, we recover $AdS_5 \times S^5$ with 3 freeparameters, while for genus $g \geq 1$, the solution has $2g+5$ freeparameters. The genus 1 case is studied in detail. Numerical analysis is usedto show that the solutions are regular throughout the $g=1$ parameter space.Collapse of a branch cut on $\Sigma$ subtending either a homology 3-sphere or ahomology 5-sphere is non-singular and yields the genus $g-1$ solution. Thisbehavior is precisely expected of a proper dual to a Wilson loop in gaugetheory.
label: human

text: The study of Wilson loop operators provides a fundamental window into the non-perturbative structure of gauge theories and their gravitational duals within the AdS/CFT correspondence. In this paper, we investigate the systematic construction of gravity duals for half-BPS Wilson loops in $\mathcal{N}=4$ supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory. We focus on the correspondence between these gauge-invariant operators and specific configurations of branes and strings in type IIB supergravity. The dual description depends crucially on the representation of the gauge group, where small representations correspond to probe strings and large representations require fully back-reacted geometries. For representations with rank comparable to the number of colors, we construct explicit "bubbling" solutions that preserve half of the maximal supersymmetry. The analysis involves solving the Killing spinor equations for the background geometry, which is constrained by the $SO(3) \times SO(5)$ symmetry of the Wilson loop configuration. We demonstrate that these geometries emerge as smooth deformations of the $AdS_5 \times S^5$ vacuum that satisfy specific boundary conditions. The holographic expectation values are computed by evaluating the regularized on-shell action of the corresponding supergravity solutions. Our findings show precise agreement with exact results derived from supersymmetric localization in the dual field theory, particularly for the circular Wilson loop. Finally, these results further solidify the holographic dictionary and provide new insights into the interplay between geometry and representation theory in string theory.
label: llm

text: To examine the evolution of giant molecular clouds in the stream of a hotplasma we performed two-dimensional hydrodynamical simulations that take fullaccount of self-gravity, heating and cooling effects and heat conduction byelectrons. We use the thermal conductivity of a fully ionized hydrogen plasmaproposed by Spitzer and a saturated heat flux according to Cowie & McKee inregions where the mean free path of the electrons is large compared to thetemperature scaleheight. Significant structural and evolutionary differencesoccur between simulations with and without heat conduction. Dense clouds inpure dynamical models experience dynamical destruction by Kelvin-Helmholtz (KH)instability. In static models heat conduction leads to evaporation of suchclouds. Heat conduction acting on clouds in a gas stream smooths out steeptemperature and density gradients at the edge of the cloud because theconduction timescale is shorter than the cooling timescale. This diminishes thevelocity gradient between the streaming plasma and the cloud, so that thetimescale for the onset of KH instabilities increases, and the surface of thecloud becomes less susceptible to KH instabilities. The stabilisation effect ofheat conduction against KH instability is more pronounced for smaller and lessmassive clouds. As in the static case more realistic cloud conditions allowheat conduction to transfer hot material onto the cloud's surface and to mixthe accreted gas deeper into the cloud.
label: human

text: The interaction between cool interstellar clouds and a surrounding hot, streaming plasma is a fundamental process driving the evolution of the multi-phase interstellar medium. Understanding how these clouds survive or disperse in high-temperature environments is crucial for accurately modeling galactic winds and global star formation rates. This study investigates the magnetohydrodynamic evolution of a spherical cloud subjected to a supersonic plasma wind, specifically incorporating the effects of classical and saturated heat conduction. Using high-resolution numerical simulations, we analyze the competitive roles of hydrodynamic instabilities and thermal evaporation in determining the cloud's lifetime and structural integrity. Our results indicate that heat conduction initially smooths the cloud boundaries, which effectively delays the onset of disruptive Kelvin-Helmholtz instabilities. However, at later stages, the increased thermal pressure gradient at the interface accelerates mass loss through a combination of ablation and conductive evaporation. Compared to purely adiabatic models, the inclusion of heat conduction leads to a more rapid expansion and eventual fragmentation of the cloud into smaller, less dense filaments. These findings suggest that thermal conduction significantly reduces the survival time of dense clumps within galactic halos and the intra-cluster medium. Ultimately, this work highlights the necessity of including thermal transport mechanisms in large-scale gas dynamics simulations to accurately represent the lifecycle of interstellar matter.
label: llm

text: We use the Barnard 68 dark globule as a test case for a spherically symmetricPDR model exposed to low-UV radiation fields. With a roughly sphericalmorphology and an accurately determined density profile, Barnard 68 is idealfor this purpose. The processes governing the energy balance in the cloudsurface are studied in detail. We compare the spherically symmetric PDR modelby Stoerzer, Stutzki & Sternberg (1996) to observations of the three lowestrotational transitions of 12CO, 13CO J = 2-1 and J = 3-2 as well as the [CI]3P_1-3P_0 fine structure transition. We study the role of Polycyclic AromaticHydrocarbons (PAHs) in the chemical network of the PDR model and consider theimpact of depletion as well as of a variation of the external FUV field. Wefind it difficult to simultaneously model the observed 12CO and 13CO emission.The 12CO and [CI] emission can be explained by a PDR model with a external FUVfield of 1-0.75 chi_0, but this model fails to reproduce the observed 13CO by afactor of ~2. Adding PAHs to the chemical network increases the [CI] emissionby 50% in our model but makes [CII] very faint. CO depletion only slightlyreduces the 12CO and 13CO line intensity (by <10% and <20%, respectively).Predictions for the [CII] 2P_3/2-2P_1/2, [CI] 3P_2-3P_1 and 12CO J= 5-4 and 4-3transitions are presented. This allows a test of our model with futureobservations (APEX, NANTEN2, HERSCHEL, SOFIA).
label: human

text: Barnard 68 is a prototypical isolated starless globule characterized by its well-defined structure and relative proximity to Earth. Despite its appearance as a quiescent dark cloud, the outer layers of the globule are significantly influenced by the ambient interstellar radiation field. In this study, we perform detailed Photon Dominated Region (PDR) modeling to characterize the physical and chemical state of the cloud’s interface with its environment. The density structure is represented by a pressure-confined Bonnor-Ebert sphere, consistent with high-resolution dust extinction maps. Using a sophisticated numerical PDR code, we simulate the penetration of far-ultraviolet radiation and the resulting heating and cooling balances throughout the globule. Our model accounts for a range of incident radiation field strengths and varying cosmic ray ionization rates to find the best fit for observed molecular abundances. Results indicate a significant temperature gradient from the warm outer shell to the cryogenic interior, which governs the transition from ionized to neutral atomic and molecular species. We demonstrate that the predicted intensities of atomic carbon and carbon monoxide lines align closely with available submillimeter spectroscopic observations. These findings suggest that PDR physics are essential for accurately determining the thermal stability and eventual collapse potential of such pre-stellar cores.
label: llm

text: The analytic asymptotic expressions for the Casimir free energy, pressure andentropy at low temperature in the configuration of one metal and one dielectricplate are obtained. For this purpose we develop the perturbation theory in asmall parameter proportional to the product of the separation between theplates and the temperature. This is done using both the simplified model of anideal metal and of a dielectric with constant dielectric permittivity and forthe realistic case of the metal and dielectric with frequency-dependentdielectric permittivities. The analytic expressions for all related physicalquantities at high temperature are also provided. The obtained analytic resultsare compared with numerical computations and good agreement is found. Wedemonstrate for the first time that the Lifshitz theory, when applied to theconfiguration of metal-dielectric, satisfies the requirements of thermodynamicsif the static dielectric permittivity of a dielectric plate is finite. If it isinfinitely large, the Lifshitz formula is shown to violate the Nernst heattheorem. The implications of these results for the thermal quantum field theoryin Matsubara formulation and for the recent measurements of the Casimir forcebetween metal and semiconductor surfaces are discussed.
label: human

text: The thermal Casimir force represents a fundamental fluctuation-induced interaction that becomes increasingly significant at the micro- and nano-scales. Calculating this force between a metal and a dielectric presents unique theoretical challenges due to the disparate electromagnetic responses of the two materials. In this paper, we develop a comprehensive analytic approach to determine the Casimir pressure for this hybrid configuration using the Lifshitz theory framework. By employing the Matsubara summation technique, we derive explicit asymptotic expressions for the interaction energy across various temperature regimes and separation distances. We specifically examine the influence of the Drude and plasma models on the metallic response to highlight how dissipation affects the resulting thermal force. The analysis reveals that the dielectric properties of the second plate significantly modulate the classical limit of the force, leading to non-trivial temperature dependencies. Our results provide closed-form solutions that offer physical insight into the interplay between conductivity and polarizability, which is often obscured in purely numerical studies. These findings are essential for the precise design of microelectromechanical systems where thermal fluctuations can influence structural stability.
label: llm

text: The estimation of missing input vector elements in real time processingapplications requires a system that possesses the knowledge of certaincharacteristics such as correlations between variables, which are inherent inthe input space. Computational intelligence techniques and maximum likelihoodtechniques do possess such characteristics and as a result are important forimputation of missing data. This paper compares two approaches to the problemof missing data estimation. The first technique is based on the current stateof the art approach to this problem, that being the use of Maximum Likelihood(ML) and Expectation Maximisation (EM. The second approach is the use of asystem based on auto-associative neural networks and the Genetic Algorithm asdiscussed by Adbella and Marwala3. The estimation ability of both of thesetechniques is compared, based on three datasets and conclusions are made.
label: human

text: Missing data represents a persistent obstacle in data science, often compromising the integrity and predictive power of statistical models. This research investigates the comparative performance of Neural Networks and the Expectation Maximisation (EM) algorithm in addressing various patterns of data incompleteness. We simulate multiple scenarios involving missing completely at random (MCAR) and missing at random (MAR) data to rigorously test the robustness of each method. The evaluation criteria include mean squared error of the imputations, preservation of variance, and overall computational overhead. Findings reveal that while EM remains highly effective for linear dependencies, Neural Networks demonstrate a significant advantage in capturing high-dimensional, non-linear patterns within the data. The study concludes that the choice between these techniques should be guided by the complexity of the dataset and the specific requirements of the downstream analysis.
label: llm

text: We present here a detailed study of the behaviour of a three dimensionalBrownian motor based on cold atoms in a double optical lattice [P. Sjolund etal., Phys. Rev. Lett. 96, 190602 (2006)]. This includes both experiments andnumerical simulations of a Brownian particle. The potentials used are spatiallyand temporally symmetric, but combined spatiotemporal symmetry is broken byphase shifts and asymmetric transfer rates between potentials. The diffusion ofatoms in the optical lattices is rectified and controlled both in direction andspeed along three dimensions. We explore a large range of experimentalparameters, where irradiances and detunings of the optical lattice lights arevaried within the dissipative regime. Induced drift velocities in the order ofone atomic recoil velocity have been achieved.
label: human

text: Brownian motors represent a fundamental class of systems capable of extracting useful work from random thermal fluctuations in out-of-equilibrium environments. While directed transport has been extensively investigated in one and two dimensions, the characterisation of a fully three-dimensional (3D) Brownian motor in an optical lattice remains a significant challenge. This study provides a comprehensive analysis of the transport properties of cold atoms within a 3D periodic potential designed to break spatial symmetry. By employing a configuration of four interfering laser beams, we create an asymmetric lattice structure that facilitates the rectification of stochastic motion in all spatial directions. The dynamics of the system are explored using semi-classical Monte Carlo simulations that account for the complex interplay between laser cooling and diffusive heating.
label: llm

text: We investigate some fundamental features of a class of non-linearrelativistic lagrangian field theories with kinetic self-coupling. We focus ourattention upon theories admitting static, spherically symmetric solutions inthree space dimensions which are finite-energy and stable. We determine generalconditions for the existence and stability of these non-topological solitonsolutions. In particular, we perform a linear stability analysis that goesbeyond the usual Derrick-like criteria. On the basis of these considerations weobtain a complete characterization of the soliton-supporting members of theaforementioned class of non-linear field theories. We then classify the familyof soliton-supporting theories according to the central and asymptoticbehaviors of the soliton field, and provide illustrative explicit examples ofmodels belonging to each of the corresponding sub-families. In the present workwe restrict most of our considerations to one and many-components scalarmodels. We show that in these cases the finite-energy static sphericallysymmetric solutions are stable against charge-preserving perturbations,provided that the vacuum energy of the model vanishes and the energy density ispositive definite. We also discuss briefly the extension of the presentapproach to models involving other types of fields, but a detailed study ofthis more general scenario will be addressed in a separate publication.
label: human

text: Non-topological solitons, such as Q-balls, represent stable localized configurations of field energy protected by a conserved global charge. While traditional models rely primarily on nonlinear self-interactions within the scalar potential to ensure stability, the role of derivative self-couplings remains a significant area for theoretical expansion. In this paper, we investigate the existence and properties of stationary non-topological solitons in field theories characterized by non-standard kinetic terms. We consider a complex scalar field Lagrangian where the kinetic sector includes higher-order corrections that depend on the square of the field gradients. Our analysis demonstrates that these kinetic interactions can significantly alter the classical stability regions and the internal structure of the resulting soliton solutions. Through numerical integration of the nonlinear field equations, we identify a new class of configurations that emerge even when the scalar potential lacks the typical features required for soliton formation. We further apply the Vakhitov-Kolokolov stability criterion to determine the specific parameter space where these kinetic solitons are immune to small perturbations. The results indicate that kinetic self-coupling can facilitate the formation of more compact and massive configurations compared to those driven solely by potential interactions. Ultimately, this work provides a broader framework for understanding how derivative interactions influence the dynamics of extended objects in high-energy physics and.
label: llm

text: An operator theoretic approach to orthogonal rational functions on the unitcircle with poles in its exterior is presented in this paper. This approach isbased on the identification of a suitable matrix representation of themultiplication operator associated with the corresponding orthogonalitymeasure. Two different alternatives are discussed, depending whether we use forthe matrix representation the standard basis of orthogonal rational functions,or a new one with poles alternatively located in the exterior and the interiorof the unit circle. The corresponding representations are linear fractionaltransformations with matrix coefficients acting respectively on Hessenberg andfive-diagonal unitary matrices.  In consequence, the orthogonality measure can be recovered from the spectralmeasure of an infinite unitary matrix depending uniquely on the poles and theparameters of the recurrence relation for the orthogonal rational functions.Besides, the zeros of the orthogonal and para-orthogonal rational functions areidentified as the eigenvalues of matrix linear fractional transformations offinite Hessenberg and five-diagonal matrices.  As an application of this operator approach, we obtain new relations betweenthe support of the orthogonality measure and the location of the poles andparameters of the recurrence relation, generalizing to the rational case knownresults for orthogonal polynomials on the unit circle.  Finally, we extend these results to orthogonal polynomials on the real linewith poles in the lower half plane.
label: human

text: Traditional spectral methods based on orthogonal polynomials often exhibit slow convergence when applied to functions containing singularities or sharp boundary layers. To overcome these limitations, this paper develops a robust framework for spectral methods utilizing orthogonal rational functions as the primary basis. We derive new recurrence relations and specialized quadrature rules that facilitate the efficient evaluation of these rational expansions. Furthermore, a novel transformation algorithm is introduced to accelerate the conversion between expansion coefficients and physical space representations. Theoretical analysis demonstrates that the proposed method maintains exponential convergence rates, provided that the pole locations are appropriately chosen to match the function’s behavior. Numerical experiments on several differential equations illustrate that this rational approach significantly outperforms standard Chebyshev and Legendre methods in terms of accuracy. Ultimately, our results suggest that orthogonal rational functions provide a powerful and flexible alternative for high-precision scientific computing in complex domains.
label: llm

text: Past work has shown that ions can pass through a membrane more readily in onedirection than the other. We demonstrate here in a model and an experiment thatfor a mixture of small and large particles such asymmetric diffusion can arisesolely from an asymmetry in the geometry of the pores of the membrane. Ourdeterministic simulation considers a two-dimensional gas of elastic disks oftwo sizes diffusing through a membrane, and our laboratory experiment examinesthe diffusion of glass beads of two sizes through a metal membrane. In bothexperiment and simulation, the membrane is permeable only to the smallerparticles, and the asymmetric pores lead to an asymmetry in the diffusion ratesof these particles. The presence of even a small percentage of large particlescan clog a membrane, preventing passage of the small particles in one directionwhile permitting free flow of the small particles in the other direction. Thepurely geometric kinetic constraints may play a role in common biologicalcontexts such as membrane ion channels.
label: human

text: Diffusion processes in confined environments are fundamental to a wide range of physical and biological systems. In this paper, we investigate how specific geometric configurations can induce asymmetric diffusion behaviors in otherwise isotropic particles. By applying a generalized Fick-Jacobs approach, we model particle transport through complex channels with varying cross-sectional profiles and broken spatial symmetry. Our results demonstrate that structural asymmetries in the bounding walls lead to preferential directionality and non-uniform diffusion coefficients across the longitudinal axis. We find that these effects are primarily driven by the emergence of entropic barriers that rectify Brownian motion without the requirement of external force fields. These findings provide a robust theoretical basis for designing novel microfluidic devices capable of passive particle separation and targeted molecular sorting.
label: llm

text: We classify Lagrangian subcategories of the representation category of atwisted quantum double of a finite group. In view of results of 0704.0195v2this gives a complete description of all braided tensor equivalent pairs oftwisted quantum doubles of finite groups. We also establish a canonicalbijection between Lagrangian subcategories of the representation category of atwisted quantum double of a finite group G and module categories over thecategory of twisted G-graded vector spaces such that the dual tensor categoryis pointed. This can be viewed as a quantum version of V. Drinfeld'scharacterization of homogeneous spaces of a Poisson-Lie group in terms ofLagrangian subalgebras of the double of its Lie bialgebra. As a consequence, weobtain that two group-theoretical fusion categories are weakly Moritaequivalent if and only if their centers are equivalent as braided tensorcategories.
label: human

text: This paper investigates the classification of braided tensor equivalences between the representation categories of twisted quantum doubles of finite groups. We specifically explore the pivotal role played by Lagrangian subcategories in determining the modular properties and categorical symmetries of these structures. By employing the theory of Lagrangian induction, we provide a concrete description of the conditions under which two twisted quantum doubles are braided tensor equivalent. Our analysis includes a detailed characterization of how these equivalences act on the set of Lagrangian subcategories within the associated modular categories. These results enhance the understanding of the relationship between group-theoretical data and the structural invariants of fusion categories.
label: llm

text: Red supergiant stars represent a key phase in the evolution of massive stars.Recent radiative hydrodynamic simulations suggest that their atmospheres may bethe location of large-scale convective motions. As supergiant convection isexpected to generate supersonic motions and shocks, we seek constraints onthese atmospheric motions and their possible relation with mass-loss rates. Wepresent high-resolution, visible spectroscopy of a sample of red supergiants(spectral type M I) and analyse them with a tomographic technique. We observesteep velocity gradients, characterising both upward and downward supersonicmotions, which are time variable on time scales of a few hundred days. Theseconvective motions will generate turbulent pressure, which will stronglydecrease the effective gravity. We suggest that this decrease, combined withradiative pressure on molecular lines, initiate the mass loss in red supergiantstars.
label: human

text: Red supergiant stars (RSGs) represent a critical phase of massive star evolution, characterized by substantial mass-loss rates that determine their ultimate fate as supernovae. Despite their significance, the underlying physical mechanisms that initiate and sustain these powerful outflows remain incompletely understood. This paper examines the role of complex atmospheric dynamics, specifically focusing on the interactions between large-scale convection, stellar pulsations, and shock wave propagation. Our results indicate that these dynamical processes significantly increase the atmospheric scale height, facilitating the formation of molecules and dust at relatively low altitudes. The subsequent radiation pressure exerted on these newly formed dust grains serves as a primary driver for accelerating the stellar wind into the interstellar medium. By clarifying the link between internal turbulence and mass ejection, this work enhances our theoretical framework for the evolution and chemical enrichment of the galaxy.
label: llm

text: It is shown that the the interference of above-threshold electron de Brogliewaves, generated by an intense laser pulse at a metal surface yields attosecondelectron pulses. This inerference is an analogon of the superposition of highharmonics generated from rare gas atoms, resulting in trains of attosecondlight pulses.Owing to the inherent kinematic dispersion, the propagation ofattosecond de Broglie waves in vacuum is very different from that of attosecondlight pulses, which propagate without changing shape. Above the metal surfacethere are "collaps bands" and "revival layers" of the electron current even atmacroscopic distances. In the range of parameters considered, the maximum valueof the current densities of such ultrashort electron pulses has been estimatedto be of order of couple of tenths of milliamps per square centimeters.
label: human

text: The generation of attosecond electron pulses represents a critical frontier in ultrafast science, enabling the direct observation of electronic motion in atoms and molecules at their natural timescales. Here, we propose a method to synthesize these ultrashort pulses by exploiting the coherent interference of multiple above-threshold de Broglie waves produced in a strong laser field. Our analysis reveals that the phase-locked superposition of these wave components leads to the formation of highly localized electron wave packets with temporal durations reaching the sub-femtosecond regime. These findings provide a robust theoretical framework for developing next-generation electron sources, opening new avenues for high-resolution ultrafast electron diffraction and microscopy.
label: llm

text: The interaction of the electromagnetic field with a two dimensional plasmasheet intended to describe the pi-electrons of a carbon nano-tube or a $C_{60}$molecule is investigated. By integrating out first the displacement field ofthe plasma or first the electromagnetic field different representations forquantities like the Casimir energy are derived which are shown to be consistentwith one another. Starting from the covariant gauge for the electromagneticfield it is shown that the matching conditions to which the presence of theplasma sheet can be reduced are different from the commonly used ones. Thedifference in the treatments does not show up in the Casimir force between twoparallel sheets, but it is present in the Casimir-Polder force between a chargeor a neutral atom and a sheet. At once, since the plasma sheet is aregularization of the conductor boundary conditions, this sheds light on thedifference in physics found earlier in the realization of conductor boundaryconditions as 'thin' or 'thick' boundary conditions inPhys.Rev.D70(2004)085010.
label: human

text: This paper investigates the electromagnetic interaction between a point charge and a two-dimensional thin plasma sheet. We employ a linear response formalism based on the hydrodynamic model to derive the induced potential and the resulting forces acting on the charge. The analysis specifically accounts for the effects of surface plasmon excitations and the spatial dispersion of the plasma electrons within the sheet. Our results demonstrate that the interaction energy and the stopping power exhibit a strong dependence on both the charge's distance from the sheet and its velocity relative to the plasma's characteristic frequencies. These findings provide theoretical insights into the dynamics of charged particles near low-dimensional plasma structures, offering potential applications in nanotechnology and beam physics.
label: llm

text: We investigate the behavior of a circuit QED device when the resonator isinitially populated with a mesoscopic coherent field. The strong couplingbetween the cavity and the qubit produces an entangled state involvingmesoscopic quasi-pointer states with respect to cavity dissipation. The overlapof the associated field components results in collapse and revivals for theRabi oscillation. Although qubit relaxation and dephasing do not preserve thesestates, a simple analytical description of the dissipative dynamics of thecircuit QED device including cavity relaxation as well as qubit dissipation isobtained from the Monte-Carlo approach. Explicit predictions for thespontaneous and induced Rabi oscillation signals are derived and sucessfullycompared with exact calculations. We show that these interesting effects couldbe observed with a 10 photon field in forthcoming circuit QED experiments.
label: human

text: Circuit quantum electrodynamics provides a versatile platform for exploring the interaction between light and matter at the fundamental quantum level. However, as these systems scale towards the mesoscopic regime, the interplay between coherent drives and environmental dissipation becomes increasingly complex and difficult to model. In this work, we investigate the dissipative dynamics of a multi-photon circuit-QED system by employing a systematic expansion of the Lindblad master equation. Our analysis reveals the emergence of non-equilibrium phase transitions and bistable behavior that are uniquely driven by the mesoscopic nature of the cavity field. We further demonstrate that quantum fluctuations significantly alter the switching rates between these metastable states, departing from purely classical predictions. These findings provide crucial insights into the stability and control of high-power superconducting circuits, offering a pathway for developing robust quantum-classical interfaces.
label: llm

text: New HI images from the VLA Galactic Plane Survey (VGPS) show clear absorptionfeatures associated with the supernova remnant (SNR) G18.8+0.3. High-resolution$^{13}$CO images reveal that molecular clouds overlap the radio filaments ofG18.8+0.3. The $^{13}$CO emission spectrum over the full velocity range in thedirection of G18.8+0.3 shows two molecular components with highbrightness-temperatureand three molecular components with lowbrightness-temperature, all with respective HI absorption. This implies thatthese clouds are in front of G18.8+0.3. In the HI images, the highest velocityabsorption feature seen against the continuum image of G18.8+0.3 is at 129 kms$^{-1}$, which corresponds to the tangent point in this direction. This yieldsa lower distance limit of 6.9 kpc for G18.8+0.3. Absence of absorption atnegative velocities gives an upper distance limit of 15 kpc. The broadenedprofile at 20$\pm$5 km s$^{-1}$ in the $^{13}$CO emission spectra is a strongindicator of a possible SNR/CO cloud interaction. Thus, G18.8+0.3 is likely tobe at the distance of about 12 kpc. The upper mass limit and mean density ofthe giant CO cloud at 20$\pm$5 km s$^{-1}$ are \sim 6 \times 10^{5} M_{\odot}and \sim 2 \times 10^{2} cm^{-3}. We find an atomic hydrogen column density infront of G18.8+0.3 of $N_{HI}$ \sim 2 \times 10^{22} cm^{-2}. The ROSAT PSPCobservations show a diffuse X-ray enhancement apparently associated with partof the radio shell of G18.8+0.3. Assuming an association, the unabsorbed fluxis 2.2 \times10^{-12} erg cm^{-2} s^{-1}, suggesting an intrinsic luminosity of3.6 \times 10^{34} erg s^{-1} for G18.8+0.3.
label: human

text: Supernova remnants (SNRs) serve as critical laboratories for studying the feedback processes between stellar explosions and the surrounding interstellar medium. In this study, we present a detailed multi-wavelength investigation of the SNR G18.8+0.3, utilizing high-resolution radio and X-ray observations. Radio continuum data reveal a complex, multi-shell morphology characterized by enhanced emission along the northern and eastern boundaries. The presence of nearby molecular gas was assessed through CO line emission surveys, which indicate a dense environment surrounding the remnant. Spatial correlations between the radio filaments and the edges of adjacent molecular clouds suggest a direct physical interaction. Specifically, we identified significant CO line broadening at the interface, providing kinematic evidence for shock-cloud impact. Archival X-ray observations from *Chandra* and *XMM-Newton* were re-analyzed to characterize the high-energy emission originating from the remnant's interior. The X-ray spectra are best fitted by a thermal plasma model, indicating temperatures consistent with a shock wave propagating through a dense medium. Localized regions of non-thermal X-ray emission were also detected, potentially pointing toward sites of efficient cosmic ray acceleration. Our analysis suggests that the expansion of the shock wave is significantly inhibited in regions where it encounters the high-density molecular material. This interaction explains the observed brightness asymmetries in both the radio and X-ray bands across the remnant's shell. Furthermore, we provide revised estimates for the distance and age of G18.
label: llm

text: Theory of magnetic deflagration (avalanches) in crystals of molecular magnetshas been developed. The phenomenon resembles the burning of a chemicalsubstance, with the Zeeman energy playing the role of the chemical energy.Non-destructive reversible character of magnetic deflagration, as well as thepossibility to continuously tune the flammability of the crystal by changingthe magnetic field, makes molecular magnets an attractive toy system for adetailed study of the burning process. Besides simplicity, new features, ascompared to the chemical burning, include possibility of quantum decay ofmetastable spin states and strong temperature dependence of the heat capacityand thermal conductivity. We obtain analytical and numerical solutions forcriteria of the ignition of magnetic deflagration, and compute the ignitionrate and the speed of the developed deflagration front.
label: human

text: This paper develops a comprehensive theoretical framework for magnetic deflagration, describing the subsonic propagation of a magnetization reversal front in single-molecule magnets. The mechanism is driven by the release of Zeeman energy during spin transitions, which provides the thermal energy necessary to overcome magnetic anisotropy barriers in adjacent regions of the crystal. By analyzing the coupled nonlinear dynamics of heat diffusion and spin relaxation, we derive analytical expressions for the flame velocity and determine the conditions for the stability of the front. Our findings provide a quantitative basis for understanding experimental observations in materials such as $\text{Mn}_{12}$-acetate and offer insights into the control of rapid magnetic switching processes.
label: llm

text: We present the mid-infrared spectrum, obtained with the Spitzer InfraredSpectrograph (IRS), of HD 98800, a quadruple star system located in the10-Myr-old TW Hydrae association. It has a known mid-infrared excess thatarises from a circumbinary disk around the B components of the system. The IRSspectrum confirms that the disk around HD 98800 B displays no excess emissionbelow about 5.5 micron, implying an optically thick disk wall at 5.9 AU and aninner, cleared-out region; however, some optically thin dust, consisting mainlyof 3-micron-sized silicate dust grains, orbits the binary in a ring between 1.5and 2 AU. The peculiar structure and apparent lack of gas in the HD 98800 Bdisk suggests that this system is likely already at the debris disks stage,with a tidally truncated circumbinary disk of larger dust particles and aninner, second-generation dust ring, possibly held up by the resonances of aplanet. The unusually large infrared excess can be explained by gravitationalperturbations of the Aa+Ab pair puffing up the outer dust ring and causingfrequent collisions among the larger particles.
label: human

text: HD 98800 is a unique quadruple star system in the TW Hydrae Association that hosts a prominent circumbinary disk around its B component. This study characterizes the 10-Myr-old disk, which displays the classic signatures of a transition disk with a significant central cavity. High-resolution observations reveal that the inner regions are depleted of small dust grains, while the outer disk remains massive and relatively cool. The presence of this large clearing suggests that dynamical clearing by the central binary stars or the early formation of giant protoplanets is actively shaping the system. These findings provide critical insights into the longevity and evolution of transition disks in complex multiple-star environments during the primary stages of planetesimal growth.
label: llm

text: This paper presents a geometric description of Lagrangian and Hamiltoniansystems on Lie affgebroids subject to affine nonholonomic constraints. Wedefine the notion of nonholonomically constrained system, and characterizeregularity conditions that guarantee that the dynamics of the system can beobtained as a suitable projection of the unconstrained dynamics. It is shownthat one can define an almost aff-Poisson bracket on the constraint AV-bundle,which plays a prominent role in the description of nonholonomic dynamics.Moreover, these developments give a general description of nonholonomic systemsand the unified treatment permits to study nonholonomic systems after or beforereduction in the same framework. Also, it is not necessary to distinguishbetween linear or affine constraints and the methods are valid for explicitlytime-dependent systems.
label: human

text: This paper proposes a general geometric framework for nonholonomic mechanics by developing the theory of nonholonomic systems on Lie affgebroids. This approach generalizes previous formulations based on Lie algebroids and tangent bundles, providing a more flexible description that accommodates affine constraints and time-dependent structures. We provide a rigorous derivation of the equations of motion by applying a generalized d’Alembert-Lagrange principle adapted to the specific bundle geometry of the affgebroid. The resulting framework establishes a unified setting that encompasses several known models in constrained dynamics and facilitates the further study of symmetries and reduction in nonholonomic systems.
label: llm

text: There is a large literature devoted to the problem of finding an optimal(min-cost) prefix-free code with an unequal letter-cost encoding alphabet ofsize. While there is no known polynomial time algorithm for solving itoptimally there are many good heuristics that all provide additive errors tooptimal. The additive error in these algorithms usually depends linearly uponthe largest encoding letter size.  This paper was motivated by the problem of finding optimal codes when theencoding alphabet is infinite. Because the largest letter cost is infinite, theprevious analyses could give infinite error bounds. We provide a new algorithmthat works with infinite encoding alphabets. When restricted to the finitealphabet case, our algorithm often provides better error bounds than the bestprevious ones known.
label: human

text: This paper investigates the construction of optimal prefix-free codes in scenarios where the encoding alphabet consists of letters with distinct, unequal costs. Although standard Huffman coding provides an efficient solution for uniform costs, the unequal cost variant presents a significantly more complex optimization challenge that has remained a focus of information theory for decades. Current state-of-the-art algorithms often face limitations in scalability or precision when applied to large source alphabets or diverse cost ratios. To address these challenges, we propose several novel algorithms that optimize the search space through advanced geometric interpretations and refined dynamic programming techniques. In addition to these algorithmic improvements, we present a more precise theoretical analysis of the code redundancy, establishing tighter bounds than those found in previous literature.
label: llm

text: The optimization of the pressure angle in a cam-follower transmission isreported in this paper. This transmission is based on Slide-o-Cam, a cammechanism with multiple rollers mounted on a common translating follower. Thedesign of Slide-o-Cam, a transmission intended to produce a sliding motion froma turning drive, or vice versa, was reported elsewhere. This transmissionprovides pure-rolling motion, thereby reducing the friction of rack-and-pinionsand linear drives. The pressure angle is a suitable performance index for thistransmission because it determines the amount of force transmitted to the loadvs. that transmitted to the machine frame. Two alternative design strategiesare studied, namely, (i) increase the number of lobes on each cam or (ii)increase the number of cams. This device is intended to replace the currentball-screws in Orthoglide, a three-DOF parallel robot for the production oftranslational motions, currently under development at Ecole Centrale de Nantesfor machining applications.
label: human

text: The Slide-o-Cam transmission represents an innovative mechanical solution for achieving high-load motion conversion with minimal friction and backlash. Despite its advantages, the design process is often complicated by the intricate geometric relationships between the cam profile and the sliding followers. This paper outlines a comprehensive set of design strategies aimed at optimizing the kinematic performance and structural integrity of Slide-o-Cam systems. First, we establish a robust mathematical framework for synthesizing the conjugate cam profiles to ensure constant transmission ratios and smooth motion profiles. Furthermore, specific attention is given to the reduction of contact stresses through the implementation of non-standard pressure angle adjustments. Computational simulations are utilized to validate these strategies, demonstrating a significant reduction in sliding friction and wear compared to traditional cam designs. The results indicate that the proposed methodologies effectively enhance the power density and operational lifespan of the transmission unit.
label: llm

text: We propose that the CP violating phase in the CKM mixing matrix is identicalto the CP phases responsible for the spontaneous CP violation in the Higgspotential. A specific multi-Higgs model with Peccei-Quinn (PQ) symmetry isconstructed to realize this idea. The CP violating phase does not vanish whenall Higgs masses become large. There are flavor changing neutral current (FCNC)interactions mediated by neutral Higgs bosons at the tree level. However,unlike general multi-Higgs models, the FCNC Yukawa couplings are fixed in termsof the quark masses and CKM mixing angles. Implications for meson-anti-mesonmixing, including recent data on $D-\bar D$ mixing, and neutron electric dipolemoment (EDM) are studied. We find that the neutral Higgs boson masses can be atthe order of one hundred GeV. The neutron EDM can be close to the presentexperimental upper bound.
label: human

text: In the Standard Model of particle physics, CP violation is parameterized by a single irreducible phase in the Cabibbo-Kobayashi-Maskawa (CKM) matrix. Despite its empirical success, the fundamental origin of this complex phase remains one of the most significant mysteries in flavor physics. This paper explores the possibility that the CKM phase is not an explicit parameter but arises instead from the vacuum expectation value of a hidden scalar sector. We construct a theoretical model featuring a multi-Higgs doublet structure where CP is an exact symmetry of the underlying Lagrangian. Through the mechanism of spontaneous CP violation, the scalar potential develops a complex minimum that breaks the symmetry during the electroweak phase transition. We demonstrate how this spontaneous phase is successfully communicated to the quark sector, effectively generating the observed CKM phase $\delta_{13}$ through Yukawa interactions.
label: llm

text: The mechanism of carbon nanotube (CNT) nucleation and growth has been amystery for over 15 years. Prior models have attempted the extension of olderclassical transport mechanisms. In July 2000, a more detailed and accuratenonclassical, relativistic mechanism was formulated considering the detaileddynamics of the electronics of spin and orbital rehybridization between thecarbon and catalyst via novel mesoscopic phenomena and quantum dynamics.Ferromagnetic carbon was demonstrated. Here, quantum (Hall) effects andrelativistic effects of intense many body spin-orbital interactions for novelorbital rehybridization dynamics (Little Effect) are proposed in this newdynamical magnetic mechanism. This dynamic ferromagnetic mechanism is proven byimposing dynamic and static magnetic fields during CNT syntheses and observingthe different influence of these external magnetic environments on thecatalyzing spin currents and spin waves and the resulting CNT formation.
label: human

text: This paper investigates the fundamental physical mechanisms underlying the nucleation and growth of carbon nanotubes (CNTs) by examining the synergy between magnetism and quantum transport. We employ a theoretical framework that integrates dynamical ferromagnetic fluctuations with quantum Hall phenomena to model the initial stages of carbon atom self-assembly on catalyst surfaces. The analysis reveals that relativistic effects, arising from the Dirac-like electronic structure of carbon precursors, significantly modify the energy barriers and electronic density of states during tube formation. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the interplay between these relativistic corrections and the Quantum Hall effect dictates the structural stability and chirality of the burgeoning nanotubes under high-energy synthesis conditions. These findings offer a novel perspective on how magnetic and quantum field interactions can be leveraged to achieve precise control over the growth of high-performance carbon nanostructures.
label: llm

text: To simulate the transient enhanced diffusion near the surface or interface, aset of equations describing the impurity diffusion and quasichemical reactionsof dopant atoms and point defects in ion-implanted layers is proposed andanalyzed. The diffusion equations obtained take into account different chargestates of mobile or immobile species and drift the mobile species in thebuilt-in electric field and field of elastic stresses. The absorption ofself-interstitials on the surface and drift of the defects due to elasticstresses result in the nonuniform distributions of point defects. It was shownanalytically and by means of numerical calculations that consideration of thenonuniform defect distributions enables one to explain the phenomenon of"uphill" impurity diffusion near the surface during annealing of ion-implantedlayers. The performed calculations of the boron concentration profile afterannealing of a shallow implanted layer agree well with the experimental dataconfirming the efficiency of the proposed equations.
label: human

text: Transient enhanced diffusion (TED) remains a critical challenge in the precise fabrication of shallow junctions for advanced semiconductor devices. As ion-implantation depths continue to scale down, traditional diffusion models frequently fail to capture the intricate interactions between point defects and dopant atoms near the surface. This paper introduces a comprehensive set of analytical equations specifically formulated to describe the kinetics of TED in shallow implanted layers. The proposed model incorporates the depth-dependent evolution of interstitial clusters and accounts for the role of the surface as a dominant sink for excess defects. Validation against experimental data confirms that these equations offer significantly improved predictive accuracy for dopant profiles, providing a robust framework for optimizing sub-micron process flows.
label: llm

text: A characteristic feature of thermalized non-equilibrated matter is that, inspite of energy relaxation--equilibration, a phase memory of the way themany-body system was excited remains. As an example, we analyze data on astrong forward peaking of thermal proton yield in the Bi($\gamma$,p)photonuclear reaction. New analysis shows that the phase relaxation inhighly-excited heavy nuclei can be 8 orders of magnitude or even much longerthan the energy relaxation. We argue that thermalized non-equilibrated matterresembles a high temperature superconducting state in quantum many-bodysystems. We briefly present results on the time-dependent correlation functionof the many-particle density fluctuations for such a superconducting state. Itshould be of interest to experimentally search for manifestations ofthermalized non-equilibrated matter in many-body mesoscopic systems andnanostructures.
label: human

text: Understanding the emergence of macroscopic quantum phenomena in out-of-equilibrium conditions remains a central challenge in modern condensed matter physics. Traditional theories of superconductivity often rely on equilibrium assumptions that may not fully capture the complex dynamics of high-temperature phases in strongly correlated systems. This paper explores the theoretical existence of thermalized non-equilibrated matter as a novel regime for sustaining superconducting correlations at significantly elevated temperatures. Utilizing advanced quantum many-body simulations and a non-equilibrium Green’s function approach, we analyze the intricate interplay between rapid energy redistribution and electron pairing symmetry. Our results demonstrate that these transiently thermalized states can effectively suppress phase fluctuations, thereby facilitating a robust superconducting state that exceeds conventional critical temperature limits.
label: llm

text: In previous work done by us and coworkers, we have been able to construct alocal, non-Abelian gauge invariant action with a mass parameter, based on thenonlocal gauge invariant mass dimension two operator F1/D^2F. Therenormalizability of the resulting action was proven to all orders ofperturbation theory, in the class of linear covariant gauges. We also discussedthe perturbative equivalence of the model with ordinary massless Yang-Millsgauge theories when the mass is identically zero. Furthermore, we pointed outthe existence of a BRST symmetry with corresponding nilpotent charge. In thispaper, we study the issue of unitarity of this massive gauge model. Firstly, weprovide a short review how to discuss the unitarity making use of the BRSTcharge. Afterwards we make a detailed study of the most general version of ouraction, and we come to the conclusion that the model is not unitary, as we areunable to remove all the negative norm states from the physical spectrum in aconsistent way.
label: human

text: The introduction of mass terms into non-Abelian gauge theories typically compromises gauge invariance, leading to significant theoretical hurdles in the construction of renormalizable models. This paper performs a comprehensive unitarity analysis of a specific non-Abelian action that maintains local gauge symmetry while incorporating a fundamental mass parameter. We utilize a generalized Stueckelberg-like mechanism to ensure that the Lagrangian remains invariant under local transformations despite the presence of this mass term. The propagator for the gauge field is meticulously derived in a general class of gauges, allowing for a detailed examination of the pole structure and the identification of physical degrees of freedom. By applying the Cutkosky cutting rules and investigating the optical theorem, we demonstrate that all residues at the poles corresponding to physical states remain positive-definite. Our findings confirm that non-physical modes, such as longitudinal components and Faddeev-Popov ghosts, decouple from the S-matrix, thereby ensuring the preservation of unitarity at the tree and one-loop levels.
label: llm

text: Image and video quality in Long Range Observation Systems (LOROS) suffer fromatmospheric turbulence that causes small neighbourhoods in image frames tochaotically move in different directions and substantially hampers visualanalysis of such image and video sequences. The paper presents a real-timealgorithm for perfecting turbulence degraded videos by means of stabilizationand resolution enhancement. The latter is achieved by exploiting the turbulentmotion. The algorithm involves generation of a reference frame and estimation,for each incoming video frame, of a local image displacement map with respectto the reference frame; segmentation of the displacement map into two classes:stationary and moving objects and resolution enhancement of stationary objects,while preserving real motion. Experiments with synthetic and real-lifesequences have shown that the enhanced videos, generated in real time, exhibitsubstantially better resolution and complete stabilization for stationaryobjects while retaining real motion.
label: human

text: Atmospheric turbulence significantly degrades long-range video quality by introducing dynamic geometric distortions and space-variant blur. This paper presents a novel real-time framework designed to restore turbulent videos through the integrated application of image stabilization and super-resolution techniques. The proposed method utilizes an efficient motion estimation algorithm to compensate for turbulent fluctuations, effectively stabilizing the frame sequence while suppressing temporal jitter. Subsequently, a fast multi-frame super-resolution module is employed to reconstruct high-frequency details and mitigate the effects of atmospheric blurring. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach achieves superior visual clarity and structural integrity while maintaining the computational efficiency necessary for live video processing applications.
label: llm

text: The differing M_bh-Luminosity relations presented in McLure & Dunlop, Marconi& Hunt and Erwin et al. have been investigated. A number of issues have beenidentified and addressed in each of these studies, including but not limitedto: the removal of a dependency on the Hubble constant; a correction for dustattenuation in the bulges of disc galaxies; the identification of lenticulargalaxies previously treated as elliptical galaxies; and application of the same(Y|X) regression analysis. These adjustments result in relations which nowpredict similar black hole masses. The optimal K-band relation islog(M_bh/M_sun) = -0.37(+/-0.04)[M_K +24] + 8.29(+/-0.08), with a total (notintrinsic) scatter in log M_bh equal to 0.33 dex. This level of scatter issimilar to the value of 0.34 dex from the M_bh-sigma relation of Tremaine etal. and compares favourably with the value of 0.31 dex from the M_bh-n relationof Graham & Driver. Using different photometric data, consistent relations inthe B- and R-band are also provided, although we do note that the small (N=13)R-band sample used by Erwin et al. is found here to have a slope of-0.30(+/-0.06) and a total scatter of 0.31 dex.
