Performing a symmetricalregression on the larger K-band sample gives a slope of -0.40, implying M_bh ~L^{1.00}. Implications for galaxy-black hole coevolution, in terms of drymergers, are briefly discussed, as are predictions for intermediate mass blackholes. Finally, as previously noted by Tundo et al., a potential bias in thegalaxy sample used to define the M_bh-L relations is shown and a correctiveformula provided.
label: human

text: The fundamental connection between supermassive black holes (SMBHs) and their host galaxies remains a cornerstone of modern extragalactic astrophysics. Among the various scaling relations identified, the correlation between black hole mass ($M_{BH}$) and the luminosity of the host galactic spheroid ($L_{sph}$) provides critical insights into their joint evolution. This study investigates the empirical parameters of the $M_{BH}–L_{sph}$ relation using an updated sample of galaxies with reliable dynamical black hole mass measurements. We utilize high-resolution imaging from the Hubble Space Telescope to perform precise multi-component decomposition of host galaxy profiles. By isolating the bulge component from disks and bars, we minimize systematic uncertainties in determining the total spheroid luminosity across different Hubble types. Our analysis confirms a tight power-law relationship between these two physical quantities spanning several orders of magnitude. The derived slope of the relation suggests that $M_{BH}$ scales almost linearly with luminosity in the near-infrared bands, albeit with a slight dependence on the specific wavelength observed. When compared to the $M_{BH}–\sigma$ relation, the luminosity-based correlation exhibits a marginally higher intrinsic scatter but remains a robust predictor for black hole masses in distant systems. We observe significant deviations in the relation for low-mass dwarf galaxies and high-redshift quasars, hinting at different evolutionary paths for these specific populations. These findings support the theoretical framework of "co-evolution," where self-regulated accretion and active galactic nucleus feedback govern the growth of both components.
label: llm

text: There is currently much interest in the possible presence ofintermediate-mass black holes in the cores of globular clusters. Based ontheoretical arguments and simulation results it has previously been suggestedthat a large core radius -- or particularly a large ratio of the core radius tohalf-mass radius -- is a promising indicator for finding such a black hole in astar cluster. In this study N-body models of 100000 stars with and withoutprimordial binaries are used to investigate the long-term structural evolutionof star clusters. Importantly, the simulation data is analysed using the sameprocesses by which structural parameters are extracted from observed starclusters. This gives a ratio of the core and half-mass (or half-light) radiithat is directly comparable to the Galactic globular cluster sample. As aresult, it is shown that the ratios observed for the bulk of this sample can beexplained without the need for an intermediate-mass black hole. Furthermore, itis possible that clusters with large core to half-light radius ratios harbour ablack-hole binary (comprised of stellar mass black holes) rather than a singlemassive black hole. This work does not rule out the existence ofintermediate-mass black holes in the cores of at least some star clusters.
label: human

text: The search for intermediate-mass black holes (IMBHs) in the centers of dense star clusters remains a pivotal objective in modern stellar dynamics. Previous studies have suggested that an expanded ratio of the core radius to the half-mass radius ($r_c/r_h$) serves as a reliable morphological signature of a central IMBH. However, the robustness of this diagnostic remains a subject of debate, as various dynamical processes can influence cluster structure. In this work, we use high-resolution N-body simulations to investigate the evolution of the $r_c/r_h$ ratio in clusters with and without central black holes. Our results demonstrate that internal factors, such as primordial binary fractions and mass-loss through stellar evolution, can significantly inflate the core radius independently. We find that clusters lacking an IMBH can achieve $r_c/r_h$ values comparable to those containing a black hole, particularly during certain dynamical phases. These findings suggest that a high core-to-half-mass radius ratio is not a unique indicator of an IMBH and must be interpreted with caution. We conclude that multi-wavelength observations and detailed kinematic modeling are necessary to distinguish between black hole signatures and standard dynamical relaxation.
label: llm

text: We study the influence of cooperative effects such as superradiance andsubradiance, on the scattering properties of dilute atomic gases. We show thatcooperative effects lead to an effective potential between pairs of atoms thatdecays like $1/r$. In the case of superradiance, this potential is attractivefor close enough atoms and can be interpreted as a coherent mesoscopic effect.We consider a model of multiple scattering of a photon among superradiant pairsand calculate the elastic mean free path and the group velocity. We study firstthe case of a scalar wave which allows to obtain and to understand basicfeatures of cooperative effects and multiple scattering. We then turn to thegeneral problem of a vector wave. In both cases, we obtain qualitativelysimilar results and derive, for the case of a scalar wave, analytic expressionsof the elastic mean free path and of the group velocity for an arbitrary (nearresonance) detuning.
label: human

text: This paper investigates the complex interplay between collective superradiant emission and the multiple scattering of photons within dense atomic gases. While Dicke superradiance is traditionally defined for sub-wavelength volumes, its behavior in extended, disordered media presents unique challenges for understanding light-matter interactions. We employ a microscopic approach based on the coupled dipole model to simulate the temporal evolution of light within ensembles of varying optical depths. Our analysis reveals that multiple scattering processes can both facilitate and suppress cooperative effects, depending on the spatial density and the detuning of the incident field. We further identify a transition regime where the signature of superradiant decay is fundamentally reshaped by diffusive photon transport and radiation trapping. These results contribute to a deeper understanding of collective optics in cold atoms, with significant implications for quantum memories and the development of light-based quantum technologies.
label: llm

text: Hard processes leading to high transverse momentum hadron production arecalculable in perturbative Quantum Chromodynamics (pQCD) for proton-protoncollisions. In heavy-ion collisions, such processes occur as well, and due to aseparation of scales are calculable on the level of the production of high p_Tpartons. These subsequently interact with the medium which originates fromsemi-hard and soft processes in the same collision before they hadronize. Thepresence of the medium thus modifies the momentum spectrum of outgoing partonsand thus hard hadrons. The idea of jet tomography is to study this modificationin order to learn about the medium density distribution. While this is acompelling idea, its practical application encounters some difficulties. Inthis paper, the capability of various observables to provide tomographicinformation about the medium is discussed and compared.
label: human

text: The study of high-energy nuclear collisions provides unique insights into the properties of the Quark-Gluon Plasma (QGP) through the lens of parton interactions. While hard probes are known to be sensitive to the density of the medium, extracting detailed spatial and temporal information remains a significant challenge in current experimental paradigms. This paper examines the prospects of performing medium tomography by analyzing the interaction between hard partonic processes and the surrounding soft bulk medium. We utilize integrated simulations that couple jet energy loss models with relativistic hydrodynamic expansions to track energy deposition across varying space-time coordinates. Our analysis shows that specific jet observables, such as azimuthal anisotropy and momentum imbalance, are highly sensitive to the initial geometry and expansion rates of the soft background.
label: llm

text: The aim of the KArlsruhe TRItium Neutrino experiment KATRIN is thedetermination of the absolute neutrino mass scale down to 0.2 eV, withessentially smaller model dependence than from cosmology and neutrinolessdouble beta decay. For this purpose, the integral electron energy spectrum ismeasured close to the endpoint of molecular tritium beta decay. The endpoint,together with the neutrino mass, should be fitted from the KATRIN data as afree parameter. The right-handed couplings change the electron energy spectrumclose to the endpoint, therefore they have some effect also to the preciseneutrino mass determination. The statistical calculations show that, using theendpoint as a free parameter, the unaccounted right-handed couplingsconstrained by many beta decay experiments can change the fitted neutrino massvalue, relative to the true neutrino mass, by not larger than about 5-10 %.Using, incorrectly, the endpoint as a fixed input parameter, the above changeof the neutrino mass can be much larger, order of 100 %, and for some cases itcan happen that for large true neutrino mass value the fitted neutrino masssquared is negative. Publications using fixed endpoint and presenting largeright-handed coupling effects to the neutrino mass determination are notrelevant for the KATRIN experiment.
label: human

text: The KArlsruhe TRItium Neutrino (KATRIN) experiment is the primary direct measurement endeavor focused on determining the effective electron anti-neutrino mass via high-precision spectroscopy of tritium beta decay. In addition to its primary objective, the experiment provides a sensitive platform to probe physics beyond the Standard Model, particularly through the investigation of right-handed weak currents. This study evaluates the projected sensitivity of KATRIN to the neutrino mass scale while accounting for the potential presence of right-handed current contributions in the decay kinematics. By analyzing the differential energy spectrum of the decay electrons, we quantify how these exotic couplings could influence the spectral shape near the endpoint and potentially bias the neutrino mass determination. Our results indicate that KATRIN can set stringent, model-independent limits on right-handed currents, offering a complementary approach to searches conducted in high-energy collider experiments. These findings highlight the versatility of the KATRIN apparatus as a dual-purpose tool for both establishing the neutrino mass scale and testing the fundamental symmetries of the electroweak interaction.
label: llm

text: The non-existence of asymptotically flat, neutral black holes andasymptotically flat, charged black holes in the Maxwell electrodynamics, withnon-trivial scalar field has been proved for a large class of scalar-tensortheories. The no-scalar-hair theorems, however, do not apply in the case ofnon-linear electrodynamics. In the present work numerical solutions describingcharged black holes coupled to Born-Infeld type non-linear electrodynamics inscalar-tensor theories of gravity with massless scalar field are found. Thecausal structure and properties of the solutions are studied, and a comparisonbetween these solutions and the corresponding solutions in the GeneralRelativity is made. The presence of the scalar field leads to a much moresimple causal structure. The present class of black holes has a single,non-degenerate horizon, i.e., its causal structure resembles that of theSchwarzschild black hole.
label: human

text: This paper investigates a novel class of stationary, spherically symmetric black hole solutions within scalar-tensor gravity theories coupled to Born-Infeld nonlinear electrodynamics. By incorporating the Born-Infeld framework, we aim to address the limitations of standard Maxwellian electromagnetism, specifically regarding the divergent self-energy of point-like charges. We derive the field equations for the coupled system and obtain analytical solutions that describe black holes characterized by their mass, scalar charge, and Born-Infeld parameter. The analysis reveals that the presence of the scalar field and nonlinear electrodynamics significantly modifies the horizon structure and the asymptotic behavior of the metric compared to traditional Reissner-Nordström black holes. Furthermore, we examine the thermodynamic properties of these solutions, evaluating parameters such as the Hawking temperature, entropy, and heat capacity to determine their local stability.
label: llm

text: The design of a mechanical transmission taking into account the transmittedforces is reported in this paper. This transmission is based on Slide-o-Cam, acam mechanism with multiple rollers mounted on a common translating follower.The design of Slide-o-Cam, a transmission intended to produce a sliding motionfrom a turning drive, or vice versa, was reported elsewhere. This transmissionprovides pure-rolling motion, thereby reducing the friction of rack-and-pinionsand linear drives. The pressure angle is a relevant performance index for thistransmission because it determines the amount of force transmitted to the loadvs. that transmitted to the machine frame. To assess the transmissioncapability of the mechanism, the Hertz formula is introduced to calculate thestresses on the rollers and on the cams. The final transmission is intended toreplace the current ball-screws in the Orthoglide, a three-DOF parallel robotfor the production of translational motions, currently under development formachining applications at Ecole Centrale de Nantes.
label: human

text: Prismatic drives are essential components in modern robotic systems, providing the precise linear motion required for various industrial and research applications. However, traditional designs often suffer from high frictional losses and limited payload capacities, necessitating the development of more efficient mechanical architectures. This paper presents a comprehensive optimization study of a novel prismatic drive mechanism utilizing a unique rolling-element configuration. Using a multi-objective genetic algorithm coupled with finite element analysis, the structural parameters were iteratively refined to maximize mechanical advantage while minimizing overall mass. The optimized design demonstrates a 22% improvement in the power-to-weight ratio and a significant reduction in parasitic friction compared to conventional linear guides. Detailed experimental validation confirms that the drive maintains high positional accuracy and thermal stability even under varying load conditions. These findings offer a robust foundation for the implementation of advanced linear actuators in high-precision aerospace and medical robotics.
label: llm

text: We present the observations of a weak MgII absorption system detected atz~0.452 in the UVES high resolution spectrum of the QSO HE0001-2340. The weakerof the two MgII components forming the system shows associated absorptions dueto SiI, CaI and FeI observed for the first time in a QSO spectrum. Weinvestigate the nature of this absorber by comparing its properties with thoseof different classes of absorbers (weak MgII, Damped Ly-alpha systems and localinterstellar clouds) and reproducing its ionization conditions withphotoionization models. The observed absorber belongs to the class of weak MgIIsystems on the basis of its equivalent width, however the relative strength ofcommonly observed transitions deviates significantly from those of the abovementioned absorbers. A rough estimate of the probability to cross such a systemwith a QSO line of sight is P~0.03. The presence of rare neutral transitionssuggests that the cloud is shielded by a large amount of neutral hydrogen. Adetailed comparison of the observed column densities with the averageproperties of damped Ly-alpha systems and local interstellar cold clouds shows,in particular, deficient MgII/MgI and CaII/CaI ratios in our cloud. The resultsof photoionization models indicate that the cloud could be ionized by the UVbackground. However, a simple model of a single cloud with uniform densitycannot reproduce the observed ionic abundance ratios, suggesting a more complexdensity structure for the absorber. Supposing that ionization corrections arenegligible, the most puzzling result is the underabundance of magnesium withrespect to iron which is hard to explain both with nucleosynthesis and withdifferential dust depletion. [Abridged]
label: human

text: Quasar absorption line spectroscopy provides a unique tool for probing the physical conditions of the diffuse interstellar and circumgalactic medium across cosmic time. We present the detailed analysis of a unique absorption system at $z \approx 0.45$ identified through a weak Mg II doublet in the spectrum of a distant quasar. High-resolution spectroscopic observations reveal a complex velocity structure characterized by remarkably narrow line profiles, indicating an extremely low kinetic temperature within the gas. The most significant finding of this study is the first-ever detection of the neutral species Si I, Ca I, and Fe I within a quasar absorber. These rare neutral transitions are typically suppressed by the ambient ionizing radiation, suggesting that this cloud consists of high-density, self-shielded material. The measured column densities of these species allow for a precise determination of the ionization state and the thermal properties of the absorbing medium. Our chemical analysis reveals that the cloud is characterized by a low metallicity, significantly below solar values, despite its high neutral fraction. The presence of such cold, metal-poor gas suggests a reservoir of primitive material that has not yet undergone significant chemical enrichment or mixing with the galactic interstellar medium. Furthermore, the ratio of neutral to ionized species indicates that the cloud is likely shielded from the external ultraviolet background by high local column densities. This discovery challenges current models of gas accretion, which often predict higher metallicities for dense, neutral gas clumps at intermediate redshifts. Future high-resolution surveys will be essential to determine the frequency and role of these cold, metal-poor clouds in the broader context of galaxy evolution.
label: llm

text: We use strongly coupled lattice QED with two flavors of massless staggeredfermions to model the physics of pions in two-flavor massless QCD. Our modelhas the right chiral symmetries and can be studied efficiently with clusteralgorithms. In particular we can tune the strength of the QCD anomaly and thusstudy its effects on the chiral phase transition. Our study confirms the widelyaccepted view point that the chiral phase transition is first order in theabsence of the anomaly. Turning on the anomaly weakens the transition and turnsit second order at a critical anomaly strength. The anomaly strength at thetricritical point is characterized using $r = (M_{\eta'}-M_{\pi})/\rho_{\eta'}$where $M_{\eta'}, M_{\pi}$ are the screening masses of the anomalous andregular pions and $\rho_{\eta'}$ is the mass-scale that governs the low energyfluctuations of the anomalous symmetry. We estimate that $r \sim 7 $ in ourmodel. This suggests that a strong anomaly at the two-flavor QCD chiral phasetransition is necessary to wash out the first order transition.
label: human

text: The nature of the chiral phase transition in two-flavor Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD) remains a fundamental problem in the study of strongly interacting matter. A critical factor in determining the order of this transition is the behavior of the $U(1)_A$ axial anomaly near the pseudo-critical temperature. In this work, we employ an effective field theory framework to analyze the sensitivity of the chiral transition to the strength of the anomalous symmetry breaking. We specifically investigate how the partial restoration of $U(1)_A$ symmetry influences the thermodynamic potential and the resulting order parameter fluctuations. Our analysis reveals that a persistent anomaly at high temperatures favors a first-order phase transition, whereas a rapidly vanishing anomaly supports a continuous second-order transition or crossover. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the magnitude of the anomaly directly affects the position of the critical endpoint in the temperature-density phase diagram. These results are compared with current lattice QCD data to constrain the parameters of the effective potential and the topological susceptibility.
label: llm

text: In nuclear chiral perturbation theory (ChPT), an operator is defined in aspace with a cutoff which may be varied within a certain range. The operatorruns as a result of the variation of the cutoff [renormalization group (RG)running]. In order for ChPT to be useful, the operator should run in a wayconsistent with the counting rule; that is, the running of chiral counter termshave to be of natural size. We vary the cutoff using the Wilsonianrenormalization group (WRG) equation, and examine this consistency. As anexample, we study the s-wave pion production operator for NN\to d pi, derivedin ChPT. We demonstrate that the WRG running does not generate anychiral-symmetry-violating (CSV) interaction, provided that we start with anoperator which does not contain a CSV term. We analytically show how thecounter terms are generated in the WRG running in case of the infinitesimalcutoff reduction. Based on the analytic result, we argue a range of the cutoffvariation for which the running of the counter terms is of natural size. Then,we numerically confirm this.
label: human

text: In the framework of chiral effective field theory, the systematic expansion of operators relies heavily on a well-defined power counting scheme to ensure the convergence of the nuclear Hamiltonian and current operators. However, a critical requirement for the robustness of this theory is that the renormalization group (RG) evolution of these operators must remain consistent with their assigned chiral orders. This study investigates this consistency by focusing specifically on the chiral pion production operator, which is essential for describing electroweak processes in few-nucleon systems. We perform a detailed analysis of the scale dependence of the low-energy constants associated with the pion production operator at various orders in the chiral expansion. By deriving the renormalization group equations for these operators, we track how their strengths evolve as the renormalization scale changes across the typical range of the effective theory. Our calculations demonstrate that the running of the leading-order and next-to-leading-order terms does not violate the underlying hierarchy established by the chiral counting rule.
label: llm

text: We review the decomposition method of stock return cross-correlations,presented previously for studying the dependence of the correlation coefficienton the resolution of data (Epps effect). Through a toy model of randomwalk/Brownian motion and memoryless renewal process (i.e. Poisson pointprocess) of observation times we show that in case of analytical treatability,by decomposing the correlations we get the exact result for the frequencydependence. We also demonstrate that our approach produces reasonable fittingof the dependence of correlations on the data resolution in case of empiricaldata. Our results indicate that the Epps phenomenon is a product of the finitetime decay of lagged correlations of high resolution data, which does not scalewith activity. The characteristic time is due to a human time scale, the timeneeded to react to news.
label: human

text: The Epps effect describes the empirical observation that the cross-correlation between asset returns tends to decrease as the sampling frequency increases. Despite its significance in high-frequency finance, developing a robust mathematical framework to quantify this scale-dependent decay remains a complex task. This paper introduces a novel modeling approach that utilizes asynchronous stochastic processes to simulate the interaction between irregularly spaced trade arrivals. By incorporating lead-lag relationships and microstructure noise, the proposed model provides a mechanistic explanation for the observed loss of correlation at ultra-high frequencies. Numerical experiments and empirical validations demonstrate that our framework accurately reproduces the Epps effect across diverse asset classes and market conditions. These findings offer valuable insights for risk estimation and the design of high-frequency trading strategies that rely on accurate correlation matrices.
label: llm

text: Significant alignment and signed-intensity anomalies of local features of thecosmic microwave background (CMB) are detected on the three-year WMAP data,through a decomposition of the signal with steerable wavelets on the sphere.Firstly, an alignment analysis identifies two mean preferred planes in the sky,both with normal axes close to the CMB dipole axis. The first plane is definedby the directions toward which local CMB features are anomalously aligned. Amean preferred axis is also identified in this plane, located very close to theecliptic poles axis. The second plane is defined by the directions anomalouslyavoided by local CMB features. This alignment anomaly provides further insighton recent results (Wiaux et al. 2006). Secondly, a signed-intensity analysisidentifies three mean preferred directions in the southern galactic hemispherewith anomalously high or low temperature of local CMB features: a cold spotessentially identified with a known cold spot (Vielva et al. 2004), a secondcold spot lying very close to the southern end of the CMB dipole axis, and ahot spot lying close to the southern end of the ecliptic poles axis. In bothanalyses, the anomalies are observed at wavelet scales corresponding to angularsizes around 10 degress on the celestial sphere, with global significancelevels around 1%. Further investigation reveals that the alignment andsigned-intensity anomalies are only very partially related. Instrumental noise,foreground emissions, as well as some form of other systematics, are stronglyrejected as possible origins of the detections. An explanation might still beenvisaged in terms of a global violation of the isotropy of the Universe,inducing an intrinsic statistical anisotropy of the CMB.
label: human

text: Observations of the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) by the Wilkinson Microwave Anisotropy Probe (WMAP) have provided unprecedented constraints on the fundamental parameters of the universe. However, several statistical features at large angular scales appear to deviate significantly from the expectations of the standard inflationary $\Lambda$CDM model. This study specifically investigates the reported alignment of the low-order multipoles, focusing on the relationship between the quadrupole and the octopole moments. We perform a comprehensive analysis of the WMAP temperature maps to characterize the spatial distribution of power across the celestial sphere. Our results confirm that the preferred axes of the quadrupole and octopole are remarkably close to each other, a phenomenon often referred to in the literature as the "Axis of Evil." In addition to this directional alignment, we examine signed-intensity anomalies that suggest a pronounced hemispherical asymmetry in the distribution of temperature fluctuations. By utilizing various statistical estimators, we quantify the probability of such alignments occurring within a random, Gaussian, and isotropic ensemble. The analysis incorporates data from multiple WMAP releases and utilizes different foreground cleaning techniques to ensure the robustness of the detected signals. We find that the alignment of the $l=2$ and $l=3$ modes remains statistically significant regardless of the specific galactic mask applied during processing. Furthermore, the signed-intensity distribution indicates a notable lack of power in the northern ecliptic hemisphere compared to the southern hemisphere. These anomalies raise important questions regarding the global topology of the universe or potential residual systematic effects in the data reduction process.
label: llm

text: Recently [J. Haro and E. Elizalde, Phys. Rev. Lett. {\bf 97}, 130401 (2006)],a Hamiltonian formulation has been introduced in order to address somelongstanding severe problems associated with the physical description of thedynamical Casimir effect at all times while the mirrors are moving. Here wepresent the complete calculation providing precise details, in particular, ofthe regularization procedure, which is decisive for the correct derivation ofphysically meaningful quantities. A basic difference when comparing with theresults previously obtained by other authors is the fact that the motion forcederived in our approach contains a reactive term --proportional to the mirrors'acceleration. This is of the essence in order to obtain particles with apositive energy all the time during the oscillation of the mirrors --whilealways satisfying the energy conservation law. A careful analysis of theinterrelations among the different results previously obtained in theliterature is then carried out. For simplicity, the specific case of a neutralscalar field in one dimension, with one or two partially transmitting mirrors(a fundamental proviso for the regularization issue) is considered in moredetail, but our general method is shown to be generalizable, without essentialproblems (Sect. 2 of this paper), to fields of any kind in two and higherdimensions.
label: human

text: The Dynamical Casimir Effect (DCE) represents a fundamental quantum mechanical phenomenon where moving boundaries or time-varying media convert vacuum fluctuations into real photons. Despite its theoretical significance, existing Hamiltonian descriptions of the DCE often face challenges regarding gauge invariance and the precise definition of instantaneous energy. This paper presents a physically sound Hamiltonian formulation for the DCE that rigorously addresses the non-trivial coupling between field modes and time-dependent boundaries. By employing a systematic canonical transformation, we map the system with moving walls onto a fixed-boundary domain governed by a time-dependent effective potential. We demonstrate that this approach ensures the resulting Hamiltonian corresponds directly to the physical energy of the electromagnetic field, avoiding common ambiguities in the choice of a time-dependent basis. The derivation accounts for the non-local effects inherent in quantum field theories under external constraints, ensuring mathematical consistency across various reference frames. Our results indicate that certain previously ignored terms in standard perturbative expansions are essential for maintaining the unitary evolution of the quantum state. Furthermore, the proposed framework allows for a clearer interpretation of the particle creation rate during non-adiabatic boundary oscillations.
label: llm

text: One proposed method for finding terrestrial planets around nearby stars is touse two spacecraft--a telescope and a specially shaped occulter that isspecifically designed to prevent all but a tiny fraction of the starlight fromdiffracting into the telescope. As the cost and observing cadence for such amission will be driven largely by the separation between the two spacecraft, itis critically important to design an occulter that can meet the observing goalswhile flying as close to the telescope as possible. In this paper, we explorethis tradeoff between separation and occulter diameter. More specifically, wepresent a method for designing the shape of the outer edge of an occulter thatis as small as possible and gives a shadow that is deep enough and large enoughfor a 4m telescope to survey the habitable zones of many stars for Earth-likeplanets. In particular, we show that in order for a 4m telescope to detect inbroadband visible light a planet 0.06 arcseconds from a star shining $10^{10}$times brighter than the planet requires a specially-shaped occulter 50m indiameter positioned about $72,000$ km in front of the telescope.
label: human

text: The direct observation of Earth-like extrasolar planets is fundamentally limited by the extreme contrast between the host star and its orbiting companions. To address this challenge, we examine the use of an external occulter, or starshade, positioned thousands of kilometers from a space telescope to suppress stellar diffraction. This paper presents a rigorous mathematical framework for optimizing occulter shapes to achieve deep shadow levels across a broad range of wavelengths while minimizing the physical dimensions of the shade. Our numerical simulations demonstrate that specific apodized petal designs can successfully reduce starlight by ten orders of magnitude within the telescope's field of view. These optimized designs provide a feasible path for future space-based missions to characterize the atmospheres of terrestrial planets and search for signs of habitability.
label: llm

text: Unparticles as suggested recently by Georgi have surprising phenomenologicalimplications, distinctive from any other new physics that we know of. But theymust interact very feebly with ordinary matter to have avoided detection thusfar. We determine how feebly they can interact with the electron, using theprecisely measured quantities in QED: the electron g-2 and the bounds oninvisible and exotic positronium decays. The most stringent bound comes frominvisible ortho-positronium decays: the effective energy scale entering thevector unparticle-electron interaction must exceed 4 x 10^5 TeV for a scalingdimension 3/2 of the vector unparticle. The lower bounds on scales for otherunparticles range from a few tens to a few hundreds TeV. This makes thedetection of unparticles challenging in low energy electron systems.
label: human

text: This study investigates the phenomenological implications of unparticle physics by examining its potential interactions with electrons. We derive new constraints on the coupling constants between unparticle operators and the electron sector across a range of scaling dimensions. By utilizing the highly precise experimental data for the electron anomalous magnetic moment ($g-2$), we establish upper limits on scalar, pseudoscalar, and vector unparticle couplings. Furthermore, we analyze the impact of unparticle exchange on the decay rates and lifetimes of orthopositronium and parapositronium. The resulting bounds are shown to vary significantly depending on the unparticle scale $\Lambda_U$ and the non-integral scaling dimension $d_U$. Our findings provide a comprehensive framework for restricting unparticle models and offer insights into the sensitivity of low-energy precision experiments to scale-invariant sectors.
label: llm

text: Max-product belief propagation is a local, iterative algorithm to find themode/MAP estimate of a probability distribution. While it has been successfullyemployed in a wide variety of applications, there are relatively fewtheoretical guarantees of convergence and correctness for general loopy graphsthat may have many short cycles. Of these, even fewer provide exact ``necessaryand sufficient'' characterizations.  In this paper we investigate the problem of using max-product to find themaximum weight matching in an arbitrary graph with edge weights. This is doneby first constructing a probability distribution whose mode corresponds to theoptimal matching, and then running max-product. Weighted matching can also beposed as an integer program, for which there is an LP relaxation. Thisrelaxation is not always tight. In this paper we show that \begin{enumerate}\item If the LP relaxation is tight, then max-product always converges, andthat too to the correct answer. \item If the LP relaxation is loose, thenmax-product does not converge. \end{enumerate} This provides an exact,data-dependent characterization of max-product performance, and a preciseconnection to LP relaxation, which is a well-studied optimization technique.Also, since LP relaxation is known to be tight for bipartite graphs, ourresults generalize other recent results on using max-product to find weightedmatchings in bipartite graphs.
label: human

text: Maximum weight matching (MWM) is a fundamental problem in combinatorial optimization with wide-ranging applications in network science, resource allocation, and bioinformatics. Traditionally, this problem is solved using centralized algorithms or by examining the linear programming (LP) relaxation of the matching polytope. Alternatively, the Max-Product belief propagation algorithm offers a distributed message-passing framework for estimating MWM in various graph structures. While the equivalence between the LP relaxation and Max-Product convergence is well-established for bipartite graphs, its behavior in general graphs remains a complex area of study due to the presence of odd cycles. This paper rigorously investigates the relationship between the fixed points of the Max-Product algorithm and the optimal solutions of the fractional matching LP in arbitrary non-bipartite graphs. We prove that if the LP relaxation has a unique optimum, the Max-Product algorithm converges to this solution, even when the optimum is non-integral. Our analysis demonstrates that the algorithm effectively reconstructs the structure of the fractional matching by accounting for the specific constraints imposed by the graph's topology. By utilizing a computation tree approach, we show that the messages in the Max-Product scheme directly reflect the dual variables of the corresponding LP relaxation. These results provide a unified theoretical bridge between local message-passing dynamics and global optimization via convex relaxation.
label: llm

text: We show that, based on the critical state model for flux-line pinning in hardsuperconductors, one can assess the magnetic moment relaxation induced by theoscillations of a perpendicular magnetic field. Our theory follows a recentproposal of using phenomenological 2D modeling for the description of crossedfield dynamics in high-T$_c$ superconductors [{\tt arXiv:cond-mat/0703330}].  Stationary regimes with either saturation to metastable configurations, orcomplete decay to the thermodynamic equilibrium are obtained. The transitionbetween both types of response is related to the disappearance of a flux freecore within the sample. As a common feature, a step-like dependence in the timerelaxation is predicted for both cases. The theory may be applied to long barsof arbitrary and non homogeneous cross section, under in-plane magnetic fieldprocesses.
label: human

text: This study presents a comprehensive critical state analysis of type-II superconductors subjected to the interaction of orthogonal magnetic flux components. While standard models typically address unidirectional fields, the presence of perpendicular flux lines introduces complex phenomena such as flux-cutting and cross-flow. We utilize a vector critical state framework to model the spatial distribution of current densities and magnetic induction within the pinned superconducting medium. The numerical results reveal how the interplay between transverse and longitudinal fields alters the penetration depth and the evolution of the critical current density. Furthermore, the analysis quantifies the influence of pinning strength on the hysteretic behavior observed during multi-axial magnetic field cycling. Ultimately, these results provide a theoretical foundation for improving the stability and efficiency of superconducting devices operating in complex electromagnetic environments.
label: llm

text: Flow-induced instabilities are relevant for the storage and dynamics ofmagnetic fields in stellar convection zones and possibly also in otherastrophysical contexts. We continue the study started in the first paper ofthis series by considering the stability properties of longitudinal flows alongmagnetic flux tubes. A linear stability analysis was carried out to determinecriteria for the onset of instability in the framework of the approximation ofthin magnetic flux tubes. In the non-dissipative case, we find Kelvin-Helmholtzinstability for flow velocities exceeding a critical speed that depends on theAlfv{\'e}n speed and on the ratio of the internal and external densities.Inclusion of a friction term proportional to the relative transverse velocityleads to a friction-driven instability connected with backward (or negativeenergy) waves. We discuss the physical nature of this instability. In the caseof a stratified external medium, the Kelvin-Helmholtz instability and thefriction-driven instability can set in for flow speeds significantly lower thanthe Alfv{\'e}n speed. Dissipative effects can excite flow-driven instabilitybelow the thresholds for the Kelvin-Helmholtz and the undulatory (Parker-type)instabilities. This may be important for magnetic flux storage in stellarconvection zones and for the stability of astrophysical jets.
label: human

text: This paper investigates the stability of magnetic flux tubes in the presence of steady longitudinal flows within a magnetohydrodynamic framework. Building upon the analysis of transverse motions in the first part of this series, we examine how field-aligned plasma motion modifies the dynamic response of the tube. Using a linearized approach for an incompressible plasma, we derive a comprehensive dispersion relation to describe the behavior of various oscillation modes. We specifically analyze the influence of flow shear and magnetic field strength on the onset of instability for both surface and body waves. The results demonstrate that longitudinal flows can induce Kelvin-Helmholtz instabilities when the relative velocity between the tube and its environment exceeds a threshold determined by the Alfvën speed. Additionally, the study reveals that the presence of flow significantly alters the phase speeds and growth rates of the fundamental kink and sausage modes. These theoretical insights are particularly relevant for understanding the evolution of solar features such as spicules and photospheric flux tubes where high-speed flows are frequently observed. Our findings suggest that longitudinal mass transport serves as a critical mechanism for energy dissipation and wave-mode coupling in magnetized stellar atmospheres.
label: llm

text: We report discovery of a compact object at high Galactic latitude. The objectwas initially identified as a ROSAT All-Sky Survey Bright Source Catalog X-raysource, 1RXS J141256.0+792204, statistically likely to possess a high X-ray tooptical flux ratio. Further observations using {\em  Swift}, Gemini-North, and the Chandra X-ray Observatory refined the sourceposition and confirmed the absence of any optical counterpart to an X-ray tooptical flux ratio of F_X/F_V > 8700 (3 sigma). Interpretation of 1RXSJ141256.0+792204 -- which we have dubbed Calvera -- as a typical X-ray-dimisolated neutron star would place it at z ~ 5.1 kpc above the Galactic disk --in the Galactic halo -- implying that it either has an extreme space velocity(v_z >~ 5100 km s-1) or has failed to cool according to theoreticalpredictions. Interpretations as a persistent anomalous X-ray pulsar, or a``compact central object'' present conflicts with these classes' typicalproperties. We conclude the properties of Calvera are most consistent withthose of a nearby (80 to 260 pc) radio pulsar, similar to the radio millisecondpulsars of 47 Tuc, with further observations required to confirm thisclassification. If it is a millisecond pulsar, it has an X-ray flux equal tothe X-ray brightest millisecond pulsar (and so is tied for highest flux); isthe closest northern hemisphere millisecond pulsar; and is potentially theclosest known millisecond pulsar in the sky, making it an interesting targetfor X-ray-study, a radio pulsar timing array, and LIGO.
label: human

text: The identification of isolated compact objects remains a significant challenge in modern astrophysics due to their inherent low luminosity and lack of binary interactions. In this study, we report the discovery of a candidate isolated compact object located at a high Galactic latitude, identified through a multi-wavelength analysis of deep optical and infrared survey data. Detailed photometric observations indicate a complete lack of a detectable stellar companion, suggesting that the object is truly solitary rather than part of a binary system. Follow-up spectroscopy reveals a nearly featureless continuum, a property consistent with the thermal emission of a cooling neutron star or a quiescent stellar-mass black hole. High-precision proper motion measurements demonstrate that the object possesses a high tangential velocity, likely originating from a supernova-induced kick that ejected it from the Galactic plane. This discovery provides a rare opportunity to investigate the physical properties and cooling models of degenerate matter in a low-background environment far from the Galactic disk. Ultimately, this finding highlights the efficacy of modern wide-field surveys in uncovering a significant but previously hidden population of compact remnants inhabiting the Galactic halo.
label: llm

text: The author studied the growth of the amplitude in a Mathieu-like equationwith multiplicative white noise. The approximate value of the exponent at theextremum on parametric resonance regions was obtained theoretically byintroducing the width of time interval, and the exponents were calculatednumerically by solving the stochastic differential equations by a symplecticnumerical method. The Mathieu-like equation contains a parameter $\alpha$ thatis determined by the intensity of noise and the strength of the couplingbetween the variable and the noise. The value of $\alpha$ was restricted not tobe negative without loss of generality. It was shown that the exponentdecreases with $\alpha$, reaches a minimum and increases after that. It wasalso found that the exponent as a function of $\alpha$ has only one minimum at$\alpha \neq 0$ on parametric resonance regions of $\alpha = 0$. This minimumvalue is obtained theoretically and numerically. The existence of the minimumat $\alpha \neq 0$ indicates the suppression of the growth by multiplicativewhite noise.
label: human

text: Parametric resonance is a well-known physical phenomenon characterized by the exponential growth of oscillations when system parameters are periodically modulated. While traditional studies focus on the amplification of motion, the presence of stochastic perturbations can significantly alter these dynamics. This paper investigates the influence of multiplicative white noise on the stability and growth rates of a standard parametric resonant system. Using the framework of stochastic differential equations, we model the system as a Mathieu-type oscillator subject to random fluctuations in its restoring force. Our analysis demonstrates that multiplicative white noise can effectively suppress the exponential growth typically observed within the instability regions of the resonance map. By calculating the top Lyapunov exponent, we determine the specific threshold of noise intensity required to induce stochastic stabilization. The results reveal that this stabilizing effect depends critically on the relationship between the noise strength and the deterministic excitation amplitude.
label: llm

text: Open questions from Sarovar and Milburn (2006 J.Phys. A: Math. Gen. 39 8487)are answered. Sarovar and Milburn derived a convenient upper bound for theFisher information of a one-parameter quantum channel. They showed that forquasi-classical models their bound is achievable and they gave a necessary andsufficient condition for positive operator-valued measures (POVMs) attainingthis bound. They asked (i) whether their bound is attainable more generally,(ii) whether explicit expressions for optimal POVMs can be derived from theattainability condition. We show that the symmetric logarithmic derivative(SLD) quantum information is less than or equal to the SM bound, i.e.\$H(\theta) \leq C_{\Upsilon}(\theta)$ and we find conditions for equality. Asthe Fisher information is less than or equal to the SLD quantum information,i.e. $F_M(\theta) \leq H(\theta)$, we can deduce when equality holds in$F_M(\theta) \leq C_{\Upsilon}(\theta)$. Equality does not hold for allchannels. As a consequence, the attainability condition cannot be used to testfor optimal POVMs for all channels. These results are extended tomulti-parameter channels.
label: human

text: The characterization of information transmission rates over quantum channels remains a fundamental challenge in quantum information theory. While the Holevo capacity provides a limit for classical information, its practical evaluation is often hindered by the complex non-additive nature of quantum states. This paper presents an in-depth analysis of a novel, computationally convenient information bound designed for general quantum channels. The proposed bound is derived using a combination of entropic inequalities and the structural properties of the channel's Choi-Jamiołkowski representation. Unlike traditional measures that require exhaustive optimization over multi-copy inputs, this metric focuses on single-letter expressions to ensure mathematical tractability. We rigorously demonstrate the essential properties of this bound, including its continuity and its specific behavior under channel composition. Numerical simulations are conducted across various standard models, such as depolarizing, phase-damping, and amplitude-damping channels. The results indicate that our bound provides a tighter approximation than previously established upper bounds, particularly in several high-noise regimes.
label: llm

text: We give a detailed critical discussion of the properties of Wilsonianeffective actions, defined by integrating out all modes above a given scale$\mu$. In particular, we provide a precise and relatively convenientprescription how to implement the infrared cutoff $\mu$ in any loop integralthat is manifestly Lorentz invariant and also preserves global linearsymmetries such as e.g. supersymmetry. We discuss the issue of gauge invarianceof effective actions in general and in particular when using background fieldgauge. Our prescription for the IR cutoff (as any such prescription) breaks thegauge symmetry. Using our prescription, we have explicitly computed, at oneloop, many terms of the Wilsonian effective action for general gauge theories,involving bosonic and fermionic matter fields of arbitrary masses and inarbitrary representations, exhibiting the non-gauge invariant (as well as thegauge invariant) terms. However, for supersymmetric gauge theories allnon-gauge invariant terms cancel within each supermultiplet. This is strongevidence that in supersymmetric gauge theories this indeed defines a Lorentz,susy and gauge invariant Wilsonian effective action. As a byproduct, we obtainthe explicit one-loop Wilsonian couplings for all higher-derivative terms $FD^{2n}F$ in the effective action of arbitrary supersymmetric gauge theories.
label: human

text: The tension between the Wilsonian approach to renormalization and the preservation of gauge invariance remains a central challenge in quantum field theory. By construction, the Wilsonian effective action is defined by integrating out high-energy modes above a certain cutoff scale, a procedure that typically lacks a gauge-invariant regulator. This paper provides a critical discussion of the inherent non-gauge invariance of these effective actions, with a specific focus on both standard and supersymmetric gauge theories. We examine how the presence of a momentum cutoff explicitly breaks the underlying symmetry, leading to the emergence of non-invariant terms in the effective Lagrangian. Through the framework of the Exact Renormalization Group, we analyze the modified Slavnov-Taylor identities that govern the evolution of the theory across different energy scales. In the supersymmetric case, the interplay between the cutoff and the algebra of supercharges introduces additional complexities that further complicate the realization of manifest symmetry. We argue that while the Wilsonian action is technically non-invariant, it must satisfy specific consistency conditions to ensure the recovery of physical gauge symmetry in the infrared limit. A detailed critique is offered regarding the various regularization schemes employed to mitigate these issues, highlighting their respective advantages and fundamental limitations.
label: llm

text: Several stars orbit around a black hole candidate of mass $3.7\times 10^6$M$_{\odot}$, in the region of the Galactic Center (GC). Looking for GeneralRelativistic (GR) periastron shifts is limited by the existence of a stellarcluster around the black hole that would modify the orbits due to classicaleffects that might mask the GR effect. Only if one knows the cluster parameters(its mass and core radius) it is possible to unequivocally deduce the GReffects expected and then test them. In this paper it is shown that theobservation of the proper motion of Sgr A$^*$, $v_{Sgr A^*} = (0.4\pm 0.9)$ kms$^{-1}$ (\citealt{reid2004}), could help us to constrain the clusterparameters significantly and that future measurements of the periastron shiftsfor at least three stars may adequately determine the cluster parameters andthe mass of the black hole.
label: human

text: Sagittarius A* (Sgr A*) serves as a premier natural laboratory for investigating the complex interplay between a supermassive black hole and its immediate stellar environment. This study utilizes high-precision monitoring of stellar orbits to simultaneously constrain the fundamental parameters of the central black hole and the surrounding nuclear star cluster. By integrating multi-wavelength astrometric data, we provide refined estimates for the black hole’s mass and distance while characterizing the density profile of the surrounding stellar distribution. These findings underscore the importance of Sgr A* in testing general relativity and improving our understanding of the co-evolution between central compact objects and galactic nuclei.
label: llm

text: We consider a diffusion model with limit cycle reaction functions, in thepresence of convection. We select a set of functions derived from a realisticreaction model: the Schnakenberg equations. This resultant form isunsymmetrical. We find a transformation which maps the irregular equations intomodel form. Next we transform the dependent variables into polar form. Fromhere, a travelling wave analysis is performed on the radial variable. Resultsare complex, but we make some simple estimates.  We carry out numerical experiments to test our analysis. An initial `knock'starts the propagation of pattern. The speed of the travelling wave is notquite as expected. We investigate further. The system demonstrates distinctlydifferent behaviour to the left and the right. We explain how this phenomenonoccurs by examining the underlying behaviour.
label: human

text: This study explores the emergence and stability of limit cycles within dissipative systems subjected to significant convective transport. While temporal oscillations are well-understood in homogeneous environments, the introduction of a velocity field complicates the underlying bifurcations and spatial symmetry. We employ a travelling wave framework to transform the governing partial differential equations into a system of nonlinear ordinary differential equations. This coordinate transformation allows for a detailed investigation of periodic solutions in the moving frame of reference. By utilizing Poincaré-Bendixson theory and center manifold reduction, we identify the critical parameters governing the transition to oscillatory behavior. Particular attention is paid to the Peclet number and its role in determining the frequency and amplitude of the resultant limit cycles.
label: llm

text: A free zero-range process (FRZP) is a simple stochastic process describingthe dynamics of a gas of particles hopping between neighboring nodes of anetwork. We discuss three different cases of increasing complexity: (a) FZRP ona rigid geometry where the network is fixed during the process, (b) FZRP on arandom graph chosen from a given ensemble of networks, (c) FZRP on a dynamicalnetwork whose topology continuously changes during the process in a way whichdepends on the current distribution of particles. The case (a) provides a verysimple realization of the phenomenon of condensation which manifests as theappearance of a condensate of particles on the node with maximal degree. Thecase (b) is very interesting since the averaging over typical ensembles ofgraphs acts as a kind of homogenization of the system which makes all nodesidentical from the point of view of the FZRP. In the case (c), the distributionof particles and the dynamics of network are coupled to each other. Thestrength of this coupling depends on the ratio of two time scales: for changesof the topology and of the FZRP. We will discuss a specific example of thattype of interaction and show that it leads to an interesting phase diagram.
label: human

text: Zero-range processes (ZRP) serve as a fundamental framework for studying mass transport and condensation phenomena in non-equilibrium statistical mechanics. In this paper, we investigate the dynamics of free zero-range processes specifically situated on complex network topologies. We employ a mean-field approach to derive the steady-state properties of the system across various graph structures, ranging from regular lattices to scale-free networks. Our analysis reveals that the "free" nature of the jump rates leads to unique scaling behaviors that diverge from standard interacting models. We demonstrate that the heterogeneity of the network degree distribution plays a critical role in determining the phase transition and the onset of particle condensation. Furthermore, we identify the specific conditions under which a macroscopic fraction of particles accumulates at high-degree nodes, effectively acting as condensation centers. These results provide new insights into how topological constraints influence the collective behavior and spatial distribution of non-interacting stochastic agents.
label: llm

text: Low energy supersymmetric models provide a solution to the hierarchy problemand also have the necessary ingredients to solve two of the most outstandingissues in cosmology: the origin of dark matter and baryonic matter. One of themost attractive features of this framework is that the relevant physicalprocesses are related to interactions at the weak scale and therefore may betested in collider experiments in the near future. This is true for the MinimalSupersymmetric Standard Model (MSSM) as well as for its extension with theaddition of one singlet chiral superfield, the so-called nMSSM. It has beenrecently shown that within the nMSSM an elegant solution to both the problem ofbaryogenesis and dark matter may be found, that relies mostly on the mixing ofthe singlet sector with the Higgs sector of the theory. In this work we reviewthe nMSSM model constraints from cosmology and present the associated colliderphenomenology at the LHC and the ILC. We show that the ILC will efficientlyprobe the neutralino, chargino and Higgs sectors, allowing to confrontcosmological observations with computations based on collider measurements. Wealso investigate the prospects for a direct detection of dark matter and theconstraints imposed by the current bounds of the electron electric dipolemoment in this model.
label: human

text: The Nearly-Minimal Supersymmetric Standard Model (nMSSM) provides a natural solution to the $\mu$-problem of the MSSM by introducing a singlet superfield without the cosmological domain wall issues often associated with the NMSSM. In this framework, we perform a comprehensive analysis of the model’s parameter space, considering both the singlet-extended Higgs sector and the neutralino dark matter sector. We investigate the impact of current LHC data on the Higgs mass and coupling measurements, highlighting the regions where the singlet-like state can stay hidden or provide small deviations. Our study further explores the production and decay signatures of light neutralinos and charginos at current and future colliders to identify potential signals of new physics. On the cosmological front, we evaluate the thermal relic density of the lightest neutralino, identifying the dominant annihilation channels that satisfy observed abundances. Furthermore, we contrast these findings with the latest results from dark matter direct detection experiments, which impose stringent bounds on the singlino-higgsino mixing. Ultimately, we demonstrate that the nMSSM offers a rich phenomenology that bridges the gap between high-energy collider searches and astrophysical observations.
label: llm

text: We present a Regge-plus-resonance (RPR) description of the p(e,e'K^+)Yprocesses (Y=\Lambda,\Sigma^0) in the resonance region. The backgroundcontributions to the RPR amplitude are constrained by the high-energy p(\gamma,K^+)Y data. As a result, the number of free model parameters in the resonanceregion is considerably reduced compared to typical effective-Lagrangianapproaches. We compare a selection of RPR model variants, originallyconstructed to describe $KY$ photoproduction, with the world electroproductiondatabase. The electromagnetic form factors of the intermediate N^*s and$\Delta^*s are computed in the Bonn constituent-quark model. With this input,we find a reasonable description of the p(e,e'K^+)Y data without adding orreadjusting any parameters. It is demonstrated that the electroproductionresponse functions are extremely useful for fine-tuning both the background andresonant contributions to the reaction dynamics.
label: human

text: This study investigates the electroproduction of $K^+\Lambda$ and $K^+\Sigma^0$ from the proton using a hybrid Regge-plus-resonance (RPR) framework. The background contribution is described by the exchange of $K$ and $K^*$ Regge trajectories in the $t$-channel, which ensures the correct high-energy behavior and minimizes the number of free parameters. To account for the structure in the resonance region, a selection of $s$-channel nucleon resonances is incorporated into the scattering amplitude. We determine the model parameters by performing a global fit to a comprehensive set of world data covering a wide range of center-of-mass energies and photon virtuality. The results demonstrate that the RPR approach provides a consistent and unified description of both photoproduction and electroproduction observables. Particular emphasis is placed on investigating the $Q^2$ dependence of the cross sections and the sensitivity of the results to specific $N^*$ states.
label: llm

text: In this paper we present large-scale correlated calculations of linearoptical absorption spectrum of oligo-acenes containing up to seven benzenerings. For the calculations we used the Pariser-Parr-Pople (P-P-P) Hamiltonian,along with the configuration interaction (CI) technique at various levels suchas the full CI (FCI), the quadruple CI (QCI) and multi-referencesingles-doubles CI (MRSDCI). The role of Coulomb parameters used in the P-P-PHamiltonian was examined by considering standard Ohno parameters, as well as ascreened set of parameters. A detailed analysis of the many-body character ofthe important excited states contributing to the linear absorption has alsobeen performed. The results of our calculations have been compared extensivelywith the theoretical work of other authors, as well as with the experiments.
label: human

text: This study presents a comprehensive theoretical investigation into the linear optical absorption spectra and the nature of low-lying excited states in an extensive series of polyacenes. The electronic structures are modeled using the semi-empirical Pariser-Parr-Pople Hamiltonian, which rigorously accounts for long-range electron-electron correlations through high-level configuration interaction techniques. Our results demonstrate that these correlation effects are fundamental in accurately determining the energy positions and oscillator strengths of the primary singlet and triplet transitions across the acene series. We systematically track the evolution of the optical gap as the molecular length increases, identifying a consistent redshift and the emergence of specific many-body features in the spectra. These findings provide a systematic understanding of the excited-state manifolds in organic semiconductors and offer essential benchmarks for the development.
label: llm

text: Recent experimental data for the complete wetting behavior of pure 4He and of3He-4He mixtures exposed to solid substrates show that there is a change of thecorresponding film thicknesses L upon approaching thermodynamically thelambda-transition and the tricritical end point, respectively, which can beattributed to critical Casimir forces f_C. We calculate the scaling functionsvartheta of f_C within models representing the corresponding universalityclasses. For the mixtures our analysis provides an understanding of the richbehavior of vartheta deduced from the experimental data and predicts thecrossover behavior between the tricritical point and the lambda-transition ofpure 4He which are connected by a line of critical points. The formation of a'soft-mode' phase within the wetting films gives rise to a pronounced maximumof f_C below the tricritical point as observed experimentally. Near thetricritical point we find logarithmic corrections ~L^(-3)(ln L)^(1/2) for theleading behavior of vartheta dominating the contributions from the backgrounddispersion forces.
label: human

text: The critical Casimir effect arises from the confinement of long-range order-parameter fluctuations between surfaces, leading to a force that significantly alters the properties of thin liquid films. This study investigates the influence of this effect on the wetting behavior and stability of superfluid $^4\text{He}$ films near the $\lambda$-transition. By applying finite-size scaling theory, we analyze how the confinement of critical fluctuations results in a temperature-dependent force that modifies the film’s equilibrium thickness. Our results demonstrate that this force leads to a characteristic thinning of the superfluid film, which follows universal scaling functions predicted for the XY universality class. These findings provide a precise theoretical framework for interpreting experimental measurements and enhance our understanding of fluctuation-induced forces in quantum fluids.
label: llm

text: Experiments in coherent nuclear and electron magnetic resonance, and opticalspectroscopy correspond to control of quantum mechanical ensembles, guidingthem from initial to final target states by unitary transformations. Thecontrol inputs (pulse sequences) that accomplish these unitary transformationsshould take as little time as possible so as to minimize the effects ofrelaxation and decoherence and to optimize the sensitivity of the experiments.Here we give efficient syntheses of various unitary transformations on Isingspin chains of arbitrary length. The efficient realization of the unitarytransformations presented here is obtained by computing geodesics on a sphereunder a special metric. We show that contrary to the conventional belief, it ispossible to propagate a spin order along an Ising spin chain with couplingstrength J (in units of Hz), significantly faster than 1/(2J) per step. Themethods presented here are expected to be useful for immediate and futureapplications involving control of spin dynamics in coherent spectroscopy andquantum information processing.
label: human

text: The efficient creation and transport of order in quantum systems are essential for the development of scalable quantum technologies. This study utilizes the framework of information geometry to identify geodesics that represent time-optimal trajectories for generating correlations within Ising spin chains. We demonstrate how these optimal paths facilitate the rapid propagation of magnetic order by dynamically modulating exchange interactions and transverse fields. Numerical simulations reveal that our geodesic-based protocols achieve high state fidelity while significantly reducing the preparation time compared to standard adiabatic protocols. These results establish a geometric foundation for optimizing many-body dynamics, offering new insights into the limits of state manipulation in strongly correlated systems.
label: llm

text: Two different approaches to calculate the fusion rules of the c_{p,1} seriesof logarithmic conformal field theories are discussed. Both are based on themodular transformation properties of a basis of chiral vacuum torus amplitudes,which contains the characters of the irreducible representations. One of theseis an extension, which we develop here for a non-semisimple generalisation ofthe Verlinde formula introduced by Fuchs et al., to include fusion productswith indecomposable representations. The other uses the Verlinde formula in itsusual form and gets the fusion coefficients in the limit, in which the basis oftorus amplitudes degenerates to the linear dependent set of characters ofirreducible and indecomposable representations. We discuss the effects, whichthis linear dependence has on any result for fusion rules, which are calculatedfrom these character's modular transformation properties. We show that the twopresented methods are equivalent. Furthermore we calculate explicit BPZ-likeexpressions for the resulting fusion rules for all p larger than 2.
label: human

text: Logarithmic conformal field theories (LCFTs) represent an important generalization of standard models, characterized by the non-diagonalizable action of the Virasoro generator $L_0$. Among these, the $c_{p,1}$ series serves as a fundamental class of models for investigating the structural properties of non-semi-simple representations. In this work, we investigate the existence and properties of Verlinde-like formulas that relate modular transformation matrices to the fusion coefficients of the theory. We specifically address the challenges posed by the presence of both irreducible and projective modules, which leads to a more complex fusion algebra than that of rational CFTs. By employing generalized characters and considering the modular behavior of the associated vacuum blocks, we derive explicit expressions for the fusion of various representation types. Our results demonstrate that these Verlinde-like formulas accurately reproduce the fusion rules obtained through alternative algebraic methods, such as the Nahm algorithm. Ultimately, this study clarifies the interplay between modularity and fusion in $c_{p.
label: llm

text: Soil bulk density affects water storage, water and nutrient movement, andplant root activity in the soil profile. Its measurement is difficult in fieldconditions. Vibration-induced conductivity fluctuation was investigated toquantify soil bulk density with possible field applications in the future. TheAC electrical conductivity of soil was measured using a pair of blade-likeelectrodes while exposing the soil to periodic vibration. The blades werepositioned longitudinally and transversally to the direction of the inducedvibration to enable the calculation of a normalized index. The normalized indexwas expected to provide data independent from the vibration strength and toreduce the effect of soil salinity and water content. The experiment wasconducted on natural and salinized fine sand at two moisture conditions andfour bulk densities. The blade-shaped electrodes improved electrode-soilcontact compared to cylindrical electrodes, and thereby, reduced measurementnoise. Simulations on a simplified resistor lattice indicate that thetransversal effect increases as soil bulk density decreases. Measurement of drysand showed a negative correlation between the normalized conductivityfluctuation and soil bulk density for both longitudinal and transversalsettings. The decrease in the transversal signal was smaller than expected. Thewet natural and salinized soils performed very similarly as hypothesized, buttheir normalized VICOF response was not significant to bulk density changes.
label: human

text: Soil bulk density (SBD) is a fundamental physical property that significantly influences soil aeration, water retention, and root penetration in agricultural and geotechnical contexts. Traditional methods for determining SBD, such as the core sampling technique, are often destructive, labor-intensive, and unsuitable for rapid, large-scale field assessments. This study proposes a novel sensing approach based on vibration-induced conductivity fluctuation (VICF) to estimate SBD in a non-destructive and efficient manner. The underlying principle relies on the fact that controlled mechanical vibrations cause periodic changes in the contact resistance between soil particles, which manifests as measurable fluctuations in the bulk electrical conductivity. To test this hypothesis, a specialized experimental apparatus was developed, incorporating a high-precision impedance analyzer and a calibrated electromagnetic vibrator. Controlled laboratory experiments were conducted on various soil textures at different moisture contents to evaluate the consistency and robustness of the VICF signal. It was observed that the amplitude of the conductivity fluctuation decreases as the soil becomes more compacted due to the increased stability of particle-to-particle contacts. Statistical analysis revealed a strong inverse correlation between the standardized variance of the conductivity signal and the measured soil bulk density across all samples. Calibration models were subsequently established, demonstrating that the specific vibration frequency and amplitude are critical parameters for optimizing measurement sensitivity.
label: llm

text: We propose a gravitational dual of ``single-sector'' models of supersymmetrybreaking which contain no messenger sector and naturally explain the scale ofsupersymmetry breaking and the fermion mass hierarchy. In five dimensions thesemodels can be given a simple interpretation. Inspired by flux-backgroundsolutions of type IIB supergravity, a metric background that deviates fromAdS_5 in the IR breaks supersymmetry, while the fermion mass hierarchy resultsfrom the wavefunction overlap of bulk fermions with a UV-confined Higgs field.The first and second generation squarks and sleptons, which are localized nearthe IR brane, directly feel the supersymmetry breaking and obtain masses oforder 10 TeV. These are interpreted as composite states of the dual 4D theory.The gauginos and third generation squarks and sleptons are elementary statesthat obtain soft masses of order 1 TeV at the loop level via direct gaugemediation. This particle spectrum leads to distinctive signatures at the LHC,similar to the usual gauge mediation with a neutralino NLSP that decayspromptly to a gravitino LSP, but with lower event rates. Nevertheless we showthat with 1-10 fb^{-1} of LHC data "single-sector" models can easily bedetected above background and distinguished from conventional gravity and gaugemediation.
label: human

text: This paper investigates single-sector models of supersymmetry breaking where the Standard Model fields and the supersymmetry-breaking sector are integrated within the same strongly coupled dynamics. To address the computational challenges inherent in such strong coupling, we construct a five-dimensional gravity dual based on the AdS/CFT correspondence. We derive the mass spectrum of the superpartners by analyzing the holographic profile of the fields and calculating the resulting soft terms. Our results indicate a distinct hierarchy of masses, characterized by relatively heavy scalars and a light gravitino, which distinguishes this framework from traditional hidden-sector scenarios. We then perform a detailed phenomenological study of these models at the Large Hadron Collider, focusing on specific signatures such as multijet events and missing transverse energy. Ultimately, we demonstrate that this single-sector approach provides a viable solution to the flavor problem while remaining testable through upcoming experimental data at the LHC.
label: llm

text: We identify plain evaporation of ions as the fundamental loss mechanism outof a multipole ion trap. Using thermalized negative Cl- ions we find that theevaporative loss rate is proportional to a Boltzmann factor. This thermodynamicdescription sheds new light on the dynamics of particles in time-varyingconfining potentials. It specifically allows us to extract the effective depthof the ion trap as the activation energy for evaporation. As a function of therf amplitude we find two distinct regimes related to the stability of motion ofthe trapped ions. For low amplitudes the entire trap allows for stable motionand the trap depth increases with the rf field. For larger rf amplitudes,however, rapid energy transfer from the field to the ion motion can occur atlarge trap radii, which leads to a reduction of the effective trapping volume.In this regime the trap depth decreases again with increasing rf amplitude. Wegive an analytical parameterization of the trap depth for various multipoletraps that allows predictions of the most favorable trapping conditions.
label: human

text: This study investigates the evaporation kinetics of anions stored in a multipole radiofrequency (rf) ion trap under the influence of buffer gas cooling. Multipole traps provide a large field-free region, making them ideal for studying cold ion-molecule reactions and high-resolution spectroscopy. However, the stability of the stored ion cloud is fundamentally limited by the escape of ions over the effective potential barriers of the trap. We present a systematic analysis of ion loss rates as a function of the trapping potential depth and the temperature of the helium buffer gas. Experimental observations are compared with a theoretical model that describes the evaporation process as a thermally activated escape mechanism. Our results demonstrate that the evaporation rate follows an exponential dependence on the ratio between the trap depth and the mean kinetic energy of the ions. We also examine the influence of rf heating on the effective temperature of the anions, which can lead to enhanced evaporation even at low nominal buffer gas temperatures. These findings provide critical insights for optimizing ion storage times and interpreting temperature-dependent data in multipole trap experiments.
label: llm

text: We present a study of the distribution of AGN in clusters of galaxies with auniformly selected, spectroscopically complete sample of 35 AGN in eightclusters at z = 0.06 to 0.31.
