This hybrid neuro-fuzzy framework offers a promising solution for reliable fault diagnosis in structural health monitoring of cylindrical components.
label: llm

text: The precise determination of the arrival direction of cosmic rays is afundamental prerequisite for the search for sources or the study of theiranisotropies on the sky. One of the most important aspects to achieve anoptimal measurement of these directions is to properly take into account themeasurement uncertainties in the estimation procedure. In this article wepresent a model for the uncertainties associated with the time measurements inthe Auger surface detector array. We show that this model represents well themeasurement uncertainties and therefore provides the basis for an optimaldetermination of the arrival direction. With this model and a description ofthe shower front geometry it is possible to estimate, on an event by eventbasis, the uncertainty associated with the determination of the arrivaldirections of the cosmic rays.
label: human

text: The precise determination of the arrival directions of ultra-high-energy cosmic rays is essential for investigating potential sources and large-scale anisotropies in their distribution. Accurate reconstruction of these directions relies heavily on the timing information provided by the surface detector array of the Pierre Auger Observatory, where uncertainties in individual station time measurements must be properly accounted for in the fitting procedure. This work introduces an empirical model for the time uncertainties in the water-Cherenkov detectors, incorporating contributions from particle arrival fluctuations, signal size, and detector response characteristics. The model is validated against real data from extensive air showers, demonstrating good agreement across a range of signal strengths and zenith angles. By enabling a more optimal weighting of timing data.
label: llm

text: We present a simple implementation of the dynamical mean-field theoryapproach to the electronic structure of strongly correlated materials. Thisimplementation achieves full self-consistency over the charge density, takinginto account correlation-induced changes to the total charge density andeffective Kohn-Sham Hamiltonian. A linear muffin-tin orbital basis-set is used,and the charge density is computed from moments of the many bodymomentum-distribution matrix. The calculation of the total energy is alsoconsidered, with a proper treatment of high-frequency tails of the Green'sfunction and self-energy. The method is illustrated on two materials withwell-localized 4f electrons, insulating cerium sesquioxide Ce2O3 and thegamma-phase of metallic cerium, using the Hubbard-I approximation to thedynamical mean-field self-energy. The momentum-integrated spectral function andmomentum-resolved dispersion of the Hubbard bands are calculated, as well asthe volume-dependence of the total energy. We show that full self-consistencyover the charge density, taking into account its modification by strongcorrelations, can be important for the computation of both thermodynamical andspectral properties, particularly in the case of the oxide material.
label: human

text: We present a straightforward implementation of dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT) for the electronic structure of strongly correlated materials, achieving full self-consistency over the charge density within the linear muffin-tin orbital (LMTO) framework. This approach accounts for correlation-induced modifications to the total charge density and the effective Kohn-Sham Hamiltonian by expressing the charge density through moments of the k-dependent many-body momentum-distribution matrix. The method is applied to two cerium-based systems with well-localized 4f electrons: the insulating cerium sesquioxide Ce₂O₃ and the γ-phase of metallic cerium, using the Hubbard-I approximation as the DMFT impurity solver. Momentum-integrated spectral functions and k-resolved dispersions of the Hubbard bands are computed, along with the volume dependence of the total energy. Results demonstrate that incorporating full charge self-consistency significantly influences both spectral and thermodynamical properties. This effect proves particularly pronounced in the oxide material Ce₂O₃, where correlation-driven charge redistribution plays a crucial role. The proposed implementation offers a computationally efficient route to more accurate descriptions of strongly correlated systems compared to one-shot or partially self-consistent schemes.
label: llm

text: Rigorous computer simulations of propagating electromagnetic fields havebecome an important tool for optical metrology and optics design ofnanostructured components. As has been shown in previous benchmarks some of thepresently used methods suffer from low convergence rates and/or low accuracy ofthe results and exhibit very long computation times which makes application toextended 2D layout patterns impractical. We address 3D simulation tasks byusing a finite-element solver which has been shown to be superior to competingmethods by several orders of magnitude in accuracy and computational time fortypical microlithography simulations. We report on the current status of thesolver, incorporating higher order edge elements, adaptive refinement methods,and fast solution algorithms. Further, we investigate the performance of thesolver in the 3D simulation project of light diffraction off an alternatingphase-shift contact-hole mask.
label: human

text: Rigorous numerical simulations of electromagnetic fields in nanostructures are essential for advancing optical metrology and designing nano-optical devices. However, many existing methods exhibit slow convergence, limited accuracy, or excessive computational demands, rendering them unsuitable for complex three-dimensional problems. This study employs the time-harmonic finite-element method to perform accurate 3D simulations of electromagnetic wave propagation and scattering in nanostructures. The approach incorporates higher-order vectorial edge elements, adaptive mesh refinement, and efficient iterative solvers to achieve superior performance. Results demonstrate high convergence rates and reduced computation times, enabling practical application to challenging nanostructures such as those in microlithography and photonics.
label: llm

text: A release of multicolor broad band (BVRI) photometry for a subsample of 44isolated spirals drawn from the Catalogue of Isolated Galaxies (CIG) ispresented. Total magnitudes and colors at various circular apertures, as wellas some global structural/morphological parameters are estimated. Morphology isreevaluated through optical and sharp/filtered R band images, (B-I) color indexmaps, and archive near-IR JHK images from the Two-Micron Survey. The CASstructural parameters (Concentration, Asymmetry, and Clumpiness) werecalculated from the images in each one of the bands. The fraction of galaxieswith well identified optical/near-IR bars (SB) is 63%, while a 17% more showsevidence of weak or suspected bars (SAB). The sample average value of themaximum bar ellipticity is 0.4. Half of the galaxies in the sample shows rings.We identify two candidates for isolated galaxies with disturbed morphology. Thestructural CAS parameters change with the observed band, and the tendenciesthey follow with the morphological type and global color are more evident inthe redder bands. In any band, the major difference between our isolatedspirals and a sample of interacting spirals is revealed in the A-S plane. Adeep and uniformly observed sample of isolated galaxies is intended for variouspurposes including (i) comparative studies of environmental effects, (ii)confronting model predictions of galaxy evolution and (iii) evaluating thechange of galaxy properties with redshift.
label: human

text: We present multicolor broadband BVRI surface photometry for a sample of isolated spiral galaxies selected from the Catalogue of Isolated Galaxies (CIG). Deep CCD imaging in the B, V, R, and I bands was obtained to derive accurate surface brightness profiles, isophotal parameters, and geometric profiles including ellipticity and position angle. Total magnitudes and integrated colors within various circular apertures were calculated for each galaxy, providing a homogeneous photometric database. Exponential disk components were fitted to the surface brightness profiles in all four bands to determine disk scale lengths and central surface brightnesses. A systematic decrease in disk scale length from B to I band was observed in the majority of the sample, consistent with the presence of negative color gradients in isolated disks. Color profiles reveal radial variations indicative of inside-out disk formation and different stellar population distributions. Structural parameters such as concentration, asymmetry, and clumpiness were measured to characterize the morphological properties of these galaxies. The results show that isolated spirals generally exhibit regular and symmetric structures with minimal evidence of recent gravitational perturbations. Comparison with previous studies confirms the reliability of the derived photometric parameters within the estimated uncertainties. These data provide a valuable reference for investigating the role of environment in spiral galaxy evolution by serving as a control sample for interacting systems.
label: llm

text: Solar coronal mass ejections (CMEs) show a large variety in their kinematicproperties. CMEs originating in active regions and accompanied by strong flaresare usually faster and accelerated more impulsively than CMEs associated withfilament eruptions outside active regions and weak flares. It has been proposedmore than two decades ago that there are two separate types of CMEs, fast(impulsive) CMEs and slow (gradual) CMEs. However, this concept may not bevalid, since the large data sets acquired in recent years do not show twodistinct peaks in the CME velocity distribution and reveal that both fast andslow CMEs can be accompanied by both weak and strong flares. We presentnumerical simulations which confirm our earlier analytical result that aflux-rope CME model permits describing fast and slow CMEs in a unified manner.We consider a force-free coronal magnetic flux rope embedded in the potentialfield of model bipolar and quadrupolar active regions. The eruption is drivenby the torus instability which occurs if the field overlying the flux ropedecreases sufficiently rapidly with height. The acceleration profile depends onthe steepness of this field decrease, corresponding to fast CMEs for rapiddecrease, as is typical of active regions, and to slow CMEs for gentledecrease, as is typical of the quiet Sun. Complex (quadrupolar) active regionslead to the fastest CMEs.
label: human

text: Coronal mass ejections (CMEs) exhibit a wide range of kinematics, with fast CMEs typically originating from active regions and slow CMEs from quieter solar environments. This study employs three-dimensional magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) numerical simulations to investigate the dynamics of both fast and slow CMEs within a unified flux-rope framework. A force-free magnetic flux rope is embedded in potential magnetic field configurations representing bipolar and quadrupolar active regions, as well as quieter coronal structures. The overlying coronal magnetic field strength and its radial decay rate are varied to model different source region characteristics. Simulations reveal that a rapid decrease in the overlying field strength with height, characteristic of complex active regions, leads to impulsive accelerations and fast CMEs. In contrast, a gentler field decay, typical of quiet-Sun regions, results in gradual accelerations and slow CMEs. The eruption dynamics are governed primarily by the torus instability, where the decay index of the external field determines the onset and profile of the acceleration. These results confirm that fast and slow CMEs can be described uniformly through variations in the background magnetic field topology, without requiring distinct initiation mechanisms. The simulated CMEs reproduce observed kinematic profiles and highlight the role of magnetic reconfiguration in driving the eruptions.
label: llm

text: We investigate the dynamical properties of asymmetric nuclear matter at lowdensity. The occurrence of new instabilities, that lead the system to adynamical fragment formation, is illustrated, discussing in particular thecharge symmetry dependence of the structure of the most important unstablemodes. We observe that instabilities are reduced by charge asymmetry, leadingto larger size and time scales in the fragmentation process. Configurationswith less asymmetric fragments surrounded by a more asymmetric gas arefavoured. Interesting variances with respect to a pure thermodynamicalprediction are revealed, that can be checked experimentally. All these featuresare deeply related to the structure of the symmetry term in the nuclearEquation of State (EOS) and could be used to extract information on the lowdensity part of the EOS.
label: human

text: We investigate the spinodal decomposition process in low-density asymmetric nuclear matter, where mechanical instabilities drive the system toward a liquid-gas phase separation. At subsaturation densities, the presence of isospin asymmetry modifies the instability region, leading to a single dominant isoscalar-like unstable mode that favors density fluctuations over pure isovector ones. This instability directs the phase separation toward restoring isospin symmetry in the denser (liquid) phase while enhancing asymmetry in the rarer (gas) phase, a phenomenon known as isospin fractionation or distillation. The growth rates of unstable modes and the resulting cluster sizes are influenced by the nuclear symmetry energy, which plays a critical role in determining the boundaries of the spinodal region. Quantum statistical effects further shift dominant wavelengths and amplify fluctuations, particularly at lower temperatures.
label: llm

text: Crosslinks and molecular motors play an important role in the organization ofcytoskeletal filament networks. Here we incorporate the effect of crosslinksinto our model of polar motor-filament organization [Phys. Rev. E {\bf 71},050901 (2005)], through suppressing the relative sliding of filaments in thecourse of motor-mediated alignment. We show that this modification leads to anontrivial macroscopic behavior, namely the oriented state exhibits atransverse instability in contrast to the isotropic instability that occurswithout crosslinks. This transverse instability leads to the formation of denseextended bundles of oriented filaments, similar to recently observed structuresin actomyosin. This model also can be applied to situations with two oppositelydirected motor species or motors with different processing speeds.
label: human

text: Active cytoskeletal networks, composed of polar filaments and molecular motors, exhibit emergent self-organization driven by motor activity. Crosslinking proteins play a critical role in modulating this process by influencing filament connectivity and alignment. In motor-mediated systems, passive crosslinks enhance network rigidity, facilitating the transmission of motor-generated forces across larger scales. At low crosslink densities, motors promote extensile stresses and filament sliding, leading to disordered or expansive configurations. Higher crosslink concentrations enable buckling and polarity sorting, transitioning the network toward contractile states with bundled structures. Computational and in vitro studies reveal that crosslink density qualitatively alters motor-driven deformation modes, from extensile to contractile.
label: llm

text: We investigate non-perturbative features of a three-dimensional Abelian Higgsmodel with singly- and doubly-charged scalar fields coupled to a single compactAbelian gauge field. The model is pretending to describe various planar systemsof strongly correlated electrons such as high-Tc superconductivity in theoverdoped regime and exotic materials possessing excitations withfractionalized quantum numbers. The complicated phase structure of the model isstudied thoroughly using numerical tools and analytical arguments. In thethree-dimensional space of coupling parameters we identify the Fermi liquid,the spin gap, the superconductor and the strange metallic phases. The behaviorof three kinds of topological defects -- holon and spinon vortices andmonopoles - is explored in various phases. We also observe a new effect, thestrong enhancement of the phase transition strength reflected in a lower orderof the transition: at sufficiently strong gauge coupling the two second orderphase transitions -- corresponding to spinon-pair and holon condensation lines- join partially in the phase diagram and become a first order phase transitionin that region. The last observation may have an analogue in QuantumChromodynamics at non-zero temperature and finite baryon density. We argue thatat sufficiently large baryon density the finite-temperature transition betweenthe (3-flavor paired) color superconducting phase and the quark-gluon plasmaphases should be much stronger compared with the transition between 2-flavorpaired and 3-flavor paired superconducting phases.
label: human

text: We investigate nonperturbative features of a three-dimensional compact Abelian Higgs model featuring singly and doubly charged scalar fields coupled to a single Abelian gauge field. This model serves as an effective description for planar systems of strongly correlated electrons, including high-temperature superconductivity in the overdoped regime and materials exhibiting fractionalized excitations such as spinons and holons. The phase structure is explored using a combination of numerical Monte Carlo simulations and analytical arguments. The phase diagram reveals multiple regions corresponding to distinct condensates: holon condensation, spinon-pair condensation, and coexisting phases. At weak gauge couplings, the transitions associated with these condensates are second-order. However, at sufficiently strong gauge couplings, the two second-order transition lines partially merge, resulting in a segment of first-order phase transition. This strengthening of the transition order reflects enhanced nonperturbative effects mediated by the gauge field. Finally, we discuss potential analogies to quantum chromodynamics at finite baryon density, where similar gauge-mediated mechanisms may intensify the transition between color-superconducting phases and the quark-gluon plasma.
label: llm

text: The well known FPU phenomenon (lack of attainment of equipartition of themode--energies at low energies, for some exceptional initial data) suggeststhat the FPU model does not have the mixing property at low energies. We givenumerical indications that this is actually the case. This we show by computingorbits for sets of initial data of full measure, sampled out from themicrocanonical ensemble by standard Montecarlo techniques. Mixing is tested bylooking at the decay of the autocorrelations of the mode--energies, and it isfound that the high--frequency modes have autocorrelations that tend instead topositive values. Indications are given that such a nonmixing property survivesin the thermodynamic limit. It is left as an open problem whether mixingobtains within time--scales much longer than the presently available ones.
label: human

text: The well-known Fermi-Pasta-Ulam (FPU) phenomenon, originally observed for exceptional initial excitations of low-frequency modes, consists in the lack of equipartition among normal mode energies at low specific energies. This work investigates whether an analogous phenomenon persists for generic initial data, sampled from the Gibbs measure at low temperature, rather than special excitations of zero measure. Numerical simulations are performed on the FPU-β model with a large number of oscillators, averaging the time evolution of mode energies over many initial conditions. The results reveal a persistent sharing of energy primarily among lower-frequency modes, with higher modes remaining weakly excited on observable timescales. This behavior indicates the presence of a metastable state and suggests that the system lacks strong mixing properties in the low-energy regime.
label: llm

text: We revisit the model of a system made up of a Brownian quantum oscillatorunder the influence of an external classical force and linearly coupled to anenvironment made up of many quantum oscillators at zero or finite temperature.We show that the HPZ master equation for the reduced density matrix derivedearlier [B.L. Hu, J.P. Paz, Y. Zhang, Phys. Rev. D 45, 2843 (1992)] withcoefficients obtained from solutions of integro-differential equations canassume closed functional forms for a fairly general class of spectral densitiesof the environment at arbitrary temperature and coupling strength. As anillustration of these new results we solve the corresponding master equationand calculate, among other physical quantities, the uncertainty function whoselate time behavior can be obtained fully. This produces a formula forinvestigating the standard quantum limit which is central to addressing manytheoretical issues in macroscopic quantum phenomena and experimental concernsrelated to low temperature precision measurements. We find that any initialstate always settles down to a Gaussian density matrix whose covariance isdetermined by the thermal reservoir and whose mean is determined by theexternal force. For more general spectra we show that the solution of themaster equation can be reduced to solving for the motion of a classicalparametric oscillator with parametric frequency determined by the unsolved formaster equation coefficients. States in these systems experience evolution thatis parametrically similar to the simpler evolution explicitly determined for inthe case of Laurent-series spectra.
label: human

text: We revisit the quantum Brownian motion of a harmonic oscillator subjected to an external classical force and linearly coupled to a general bath of harmonic oscillators at arbitrary temperature. The exact Hu-Paz-Zhang (HPZ) master equation for the reduced density matrix, originally derived with time-dependent coefficients from integro-differential equations, is shown to admit closed functional forms for a broad class of environmental spectral densities. These closed forms hold independently of temperature and coupling strength, extending prior results limited to specific cases. The inclusion of an external force introduces a driving term that shifts the mean position without altering the dissipative or diffusive coefficients. We derive explicit solutions for the time evolution of the reduced density matrix, revealing that arbitrary initial states evolve toward a Gaussian form in the long-time limit. The equilibrium covariance matrix is fully determined by the thermal fluctuations of the bath, satisfying the quantum fluctuation-dissipation theorem. The mean values of position and momentum follow classical trajectories driven by the external force, damped by the environment. For certain spectral densities, the master equation coefficients are obtained analytically via contour integration, yielding exact expressions for renormalization, dissipation, and diffusion terms. These solutions provide insight into macroscopic quantum phenomena, including the quantum limit of precision measurements and decoherence processes under driven conditions.
label: llm

text: This paper investigates the use of evolutionary optimisation techniques toregister a template with a scene image. An error function is created to measurethe correspondence of the template to the image. The problem presented here isto optimise the horizontal, vertical and scaling parameters that register thetemplate with the scene. The Genetic Algorithm, Simulated Annealing andParticle Swarm Optimisations are compared to a Nelder-Mead Simplex optimisationwith starting points chosen in a pre-processing stage. The paper investigatesthe precision and accuracy of each method and shows that all four methodsperform favourably for image registration. SA is the most precise, GA is themost accurate. PSO is a good mix of both and the Simplex method returns localminima the most. A pre-processing stage should be investigated for theevolutionary methods in order to improve performance. Discrete versions of theoptimisation methods should be investigated to further improve computationalperformance.
label: human

text: Template-based image registration involves aligning a predefined template image with a target scene image by optimizing transformation parameters to maximize correspondence. Traditional optimization methods often struggle with multimodal fitness landscapes and local optima in such registration tasks. Evolutionary optimization techniques offer robust global search capabilities, making them suitable for addressing these challenges. This study explores the application of evolutionary methods, including Genetic Algorithms (GA), Simulated Annealing (SA), and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), to template-based registration. An error function based on pixel intensity differences is employed as the fitness metric to evaluate alignment quality. The optimization focuses on key parameters such as horizontal translation, vertical translation, and uniform scaling. Comparisons are made with the classical Nelder-Mead Simplex method, which uses pre-processed initial points for local refinement. Experimental evaluations demonstrate that all tested methods achieve favorable registration performance on various image pairs.
label: llm

text: We describe our software package Block Locally Optimal PreconditionedEigenvalue Xolvers (BLOPEX) publicly released recently. BLOPEX is available asa stand-alone serial library, as an external package to PETSc (``Portable,Extensible Toolkit for Scientific Computation'', a general purpose suite oftools for the scalable solution of partial differential equations and relatedproblems developed by Argonne National Laboratory), and is also built into {\ithypre} (``High Performance Preconditioners'', scalable linear solvers packagedeveloped by Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory). The present BLOPEXrelease includes only one solver--the Locally Optimal Block PreconditionedConjugate Gradient (LOBPCG) method for symmetric eigenvalue problems. {\ithypre} provides users with advanced high-quality parallel preconditioners forlinear systems, in particular, with domain decomposition and multigridpreconditioners. With BLOPEX, the same preconditioners can now be efficientlyused for symmetric eigenvalue problems. PETSc facilitates the integration ofindependently developed application modules with strict attention to componentinteroperability, and makes BLOPEX extremely easy to compile and use withpreconditioners that are available via PETSc. We present the LOBPCG algorithmin BLOPEX for {\it hypre} and PETSc. We demonstrate numerically the scalabilityof BLOPEX by testing it on a number of distributed and shared memory parallelsystems, including a Beowulf system, SUN Fire 880, an AMD dual-core Opteronworkstation, and IBM BlueGene/L supercomputer, using PETSc domain decompositionand {\it hypre} multigrid preconditioning. We test BLOPEX on a model problem,the standard 7-point finite-difference approximation of the 3-D Laplacian, withthe problem size in the range $10^5-10^8$.
label: human

text: This paper introduces Block Locally Optimal Preconditioned Eigenvalue Xolvers (BLOPEX), a software package designed for solving large-scale symmetric eigenvalue problems using preconditioned iterative methods. BLOPEX is available in multiple forms: as a stand-alone serial library, as an external package integrated with PETSc, and built directly into the hypre library. The core solver implemented in the current release is the Locally Optimal Block Preconditioned Conjugate Gradient (LOBPCG) method, which is particularly effective for computing extreme eigenpairs of symmetric positive definite generalized eigenvalue problems. The integration with hypre enables the direct reuse of its high-quality parallel multigrid and domain decomposition preconditioners, originally developed for linear systems, now applied efficiently to eigenvalue computations. Similarly, the PETSc interface leverages PETSc's modular design to facilitate seamless interoperability with a wide range of existing preconditioners and parallel computing tools. The abstract implementation of LOBPCG in BLOPEX allows for flexible deployment across different software environments through user-supplied operator interfaces. Numerical experiments demonstrate the scalability of BLOPEX on various parallel architectures, including shared-memory systems and distributed clusters. Tests on a model problem—the 7-point finite-difference discretization of the 3D Laplacian with problem sizes ranging from 10^5 to 10^8 degrees of freedom—confirm strong scaling when using hypre multigrid and PETSc domain decomposition preconditioning. Overall, BLOPEX provides a robust and efficient framework for preconditioned eigensolving in high-performance scientific computing applications.
label: llm

text: Electron acceleration in high Mach number perpendicular shocks isinvestigated through two-dimensional electrostatic particle-in-cell (PIC)simulation. We simulate the shock foot region by modeling particles thatconsist of three components such as incident protons and electrons andreflected protons in the initial state which satisfies the Buneman instabilitycondition. In contrast to previous one-dimensional simulations in which strongsurfing acceleration is realized, we find that surfing acceleration does notoccur in two-dimensional simulation. This is because excited electrostaticpotentials have a two-dimensional structure that makes electron trappingimpossible. Thus, the surfing acceleration does not work either in itself or asan injection mechanism for the diffusive shock acceleration. We briefly discussimplications of the present results on the electron heating and acceleration byshocks in supernova remnants.
label: human

text: Electron acceleration in high Mach number perpendicular collisionless shocks is investigated using a two-dimensional electrostatic particle-in-cell (PIC) simulation focused on the shock foot region. The simulation initializes particles comprising incident protons and electrons along with reflected protons, establishing conditions conducive to the Buneman instability. In contrast to prior one-dimensional simulations where robust electron surfing acceleration was observed, the two-dimensional setup reveals no significant surfing acceleration of electrons. This absence arises because the excited electrostatic potentials develop a complex two-dimensional structure. Such multidimensional potential configurations prevent effective long-term trapping of electrons within the wave structures. Consequently, electron surfing acceleration proves ineffective both as a standalone mechanism and as a potential injection process for subsequent diffusive shock acceleration in realistic multidimensional shock environments.
label: llm

text: As the dimensionality is reduced, the world becomes more and moreinteresting; novel and fascinating phenomena show up which call forunderstanding. Physics in one dimension is a fascinating topic for theory andexperiment: for the former often a simplification, for the latter always achallenge. Various ways will be demonstrated how one-dimensional structures canbe achieved in reality. In particular organic conductors could establishthemselves as model systems for the investigation of the physics in reduceddimensions.  In the metallic state of a one-dimensional solid, Fermi-liquid theory breaksdown and spin and charge degrees of freedom become separated. But the metallicphase is not stable in one dimension: as the temperature is reduced, theelectronic charge and spin tend to arrange themselves in an ordered fashion dueto strong correlations. The competition of the different interactions isresponsible for which broken-symmetry ground state is eventually realized in aspecific compound and which drives the system towards an insulating state.  Here we review the various ordering phenomena and how they can be identifiedby dielectric and optic measurements.
label: human

text: One-dimensional solids exhibit fascinating electronic properties due to reduced dimensionality, where strong electron correlations and electron-phonon interactions play dominant roles. In these systems, the metallic phase is inherently unstable at low temperatures, leading to various broken-symmetry ground states. Charge-ordering phenomena arise from the tendency of electrons to arrange in periodic patterns, often driven by Coulomb repulsion or nesting of the Fermi surface. A key example is the charge density wave (CDW), originating from the Peierls instability, where a periodic lattice distortion opens a gap at the Fermi level, stabilizing an insulating state. In contrast, charge ordering in correlated systems, such as quarter-filled organic conductors, results from short-range Coulomb interactions localizing charges on specific sites, forming patterns like Wigner crystals or stripes. These mechanisms can compete or coexist, with the dominant one determined by the balance of electron-electron repulsion, electron-phonon coupling, and bandwidth. Optical and dielectric spectroscopy provide powerful tools to distinguish CDW from pure charge-ordered states, revealing differences in gap formation and collective excitations.
label: llm

text: We propose a new field-theoretic framework for formulating thenon-relativistic quantum mechanics of D particles in a Fock space of U(N)Yang-Mills theories with all different N in a unified way. D-particle fieldoperators, creating and annihilating a D particle and hence changing N one byone, are defined. The base space of these D-particle fields is a (complex)vector space of infinite dimensions. The gauge invariance of Yang-Mills quantummechanics is reinterpreted as a quantum-statistical symmetry, which is takeninto account by setting up a novel algebraic and projective structure in theformalism. Ordinary physical observables of Yang-Mills theory, obeying thestandard algebra, are expressed as bilinear forms of the D-particle fields.Together with the open-closed string duality, our new formulation suggests atrinity of three different but mutually dual viewpoints in string theory.
label: human

text: We propose a novel field-theoretic framework to describe the non-relativistic quantum mechanics of D-particles (D0-branes) within a unified Fock space that incorporates U(N) Yang-Mills theories for all values of N simultaneously. D-particle field operators are introduced, which create or annihilate individual D-particles, thereby dynamically changing the rank N of the gauge group by unity. These fields are defined over an infinite-dimensional complex vector space as their base manifold. The inherent gauge invariance of Yang-Mills quantum mechanics is reinterpreted as a quantum-statistical symmetry, accommodated through a specialized algebraic and projective structure in the formalism. Finally, standard physical observables of the Yang-Mills theory, satisfying conventional algebraic relations, are constructed as bilinear expressions in terms of these D-particle fields.
label: llm

text: From several points of view it is strongly suggested that the currentuniverse is unstable and will ultimately decay to one that is exactlysupersymmetric (susy). The possibility that atoms and molecules form in thisfuture universe requires that the degenerate electron/selectron mass isnon-zero and hence that electroweak symmetry breaking (EWSB) survives the phasetransition to exact susy. However, the minimal supersymmetric standard model(MSSM) and several of its extensions have no EWSB in the susy limit. Among theextended higgs models that have been discussed one stands out in this regard.The higgs sector that is revealed at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) willtherefore have implications for the future universe. We also address thequestion as to whether the transition to the exact susy phase with EWSB isexothermic.
label: human

text: Extended Higgs models, incorporating additional scalar fields beyond the Standard Model doublet, give rise to richer vacuum landscapes characterized by multiple minima and complex potential structures. These extended sectors can modify the renormalization group evolution of the Higgs quartic coupling, potentially resolving the vacuum metastability issue present in the Standard Model by stabilizing the potential up to high scales. In the context of the string theory landscape or multiverse scenarios, the distribution of vacua in such models influences statistical predictions for observable parameters, favoring regions where the electroweak scale is anthropically suitable. The implications include altered patterns of electroweak symmetry breaking, additional phase transitions, and constraints on new physics scales from vacuum selection mechanisms.
label: llm

text: [Abridged] We have been exploring a spectroscopic unification for all knowntypes of broad line emitting AGN. The 4D Eigenvector 1 (4DE1) parameter spaceshows promise as a unification capable of organizing quasar diversity on asequence primarily governed by Eddington ratio. This paper considers the roleof CIV 1549 measures with special emphasis on the CIV 1549 line shift as aprincipal 4DE1 diagnostic. We use HST archival spectra for 130 sources with S/Nhigh enough to permit reliable CIV 1549 broad component (BC) measures. We finda CIV 1549 BC profile blueshift that is strongly concentrated among (largelyradio-quiet: RQ) sources with FWHM(H beta BC) < 4000 km/s (which we callPopulation A). Narrow line Seyfert 1 (NLSy1, with FWHM H beta < 2000 km/s)sources belong to this population but do not emerge as a distinct class. Thesystematic blueshift, widely interpreted as arising in a disk wind/outflow, isnot observed in broader lined AGN which we call Population B. We find newcorrelations between FWHM(CIV 1549 BC) and CIV 1549 line shift as well as theequivalent width of CIV 1549. They are seen only in Pop. A sources. CIV 1549measures enhance the apparent dichotomy at FWHM(Hbeta BC) approx. 4000 \kms\(Sulentic et al. 2000) suggesting that it has more significance in the contextof Broad Line Region structure than the more commonly discussed RL vs. RQdichotomy. Black hole masses computed from FWHM CIV 1549 BC for about 80 AGNindicate that the CIV 1549 width is a poor virial estimator. Comparison of massestimates derived from Hbeta BC and CIV 1549 reveals that the latter showdifferent and nonlinear offsets for population A and B sources. A significantnumber of sources also show narrow line CIV 1549 emission. We present a recipefor CIV 1549 narrow component extraction.
label: human

text: The four-dimensional Eigenvector 1 (4DE1) parameter space provides a powerful framework for organizing the spectroscopic diversity observed in broad-line active galactic nuclei (AGN). This space is primarily driven by the Eddington ratio, with secondary contributions from source orientation effects. Key optical parameters in 4DE1 include the full width at half maximum (FWHM) of the broad Hβ emission line and the strength of the optical Fe II emission blend relative to Hβ (R_FeII). The high-ionization C IV λ1549 emission line has emerged as a critical ultraviolet diagnostic within this context. This study utilizes high signal-to-noise Hubble Space Telescope (HST) archival spectra of 130 AGN to measure reliable broad component properties of C IV λ1549. Systematic blueshifts in the C IV λ1549 broad profile are predominantly found in sources with FWHM(Hβ) < 4000 km s⁻¹, designated as Population A. Population A sources are largely radio-quiet and include narrow-line Seyfert 1 galaxies, though the latter do not form a distinct subclass. No significant blueshifts are observed in broader-lined sources (FWHM(Hβ) > 4000 km s⁻¹), termed Population B, which encompass most radio-loud AGN. These blueshifts are interpreted as signatures of disk winds or outflows driven by high accretion rates. New correlations are identified between the FWHM of the C IV λ1549 broad component and its line shift amplitude. Additional correlations involve the equivalent width of C IV λ1549 and other 4DE1 parameters. Population A sources exhibit stronger correlations, consistent with higher Eddington ratios promoting outflow activity. The dichotomy between Populations A and B appears more fundamental to broad-line region structure than the traditional radio-loud versus radio-quiet classification.
label: llm

text: We present deep polarimetric observations at 1420 MHz of the European LargeArea ISO Survey North 1 region (ELAIS N1) as part of the Dominion RadioAstrophysical Observatory Planck Deep Fields project. By combining closelyspaced aperture synthesis fields, we image a region of 7.43 square degrees to amaximum sensitivity in Stokes Q and U of 78 microJy/beam, and detect 786compact sources in Stokes I. Of these, 83 exhibit polarized emission. We findthat the differential source counts (log N - log p) for polarized sources arenearly constant down to p > 500 microJy, and that these faint polarized radiosources are more highly polarized than the strong source population. The medianfractional polarization is (4.8 +/- 0.7)% for polarized sources with Stokes Iflux density between 1 and 30 mJy; approximately three times larger thansources with I > 100 mJy. The majority of the polarized sources have beenidentified with galaxies in the Spitzer Wide Area Infrared Extragalactic Survey(SWIRE) image of ELAIS N1. Most of the galaxies occupy regions in the IRAC5.8/3.6 micron vs. 8.0/4.5 micron color-color diagram associated with dustyAGNs, or with ellipticals with an aging stellar population. A few host galaxieshave colors that suggests significant PAH emission in the near-infrared. Asmall fraction, 12%, of the polarized sources are not detected in the SWIREdata. None of the polarized sources in our sample appears to be associated withan actively star-forming galaxy.
label: human

text: We present deep polarimetric observations at 1420 MHz of the European Large Area ISO Survey North 1 region (ELAIS N1) as part of the Dominion Radio Astrophysical Observatory Planck Deep Fields project. By combining closely spaced aperture synthesis fields, we image a region of 7.43 square degrees to a maximum sensitivity in Stokes Q and U of 78 μJy beam⁻¹. In total intensity (Stokes I), we detect 786 compact sources across the surveyed area. Of these, 83 sources exhibit significant polarized emission above the detection threshold. The differential source counts for polarized flux density remain nearly constant down to polarized intensities greater than 500 μJy. Faint polarized sources display higher fractional polarization compared to brighter ones. The median fractional polarization reaches 4.8% ± 0.7% for sources with Stokes I flux densities between 1 and 30 mJy. This value is approximately three times higher than that observed for sources exceeding 100 mJy in total intensity. Most polarized sources are optically identified with galaxies cataloged in the Spitzer Wide-Area Infrared Extragalactic Survey (SWIRE) of the ELAIS N1 field. None of the polarized sources in the sample show associations with actively star-forming galaxies.
label: llm

text: In any attempt to build a quantum theory of gravity, a central issue is tounravel the structure of space-time at the smallest scale. Of particularrelevance is the possible definition of coordinate functions within the theoryand the study of their algebraic properties, such as non-commutativity. Here weapproach this issue from the perspective of loop quantum gravity and thepicture of quantum geometry that the formalism offers. In particular, as weargue here, this emerging picture has two main elements: i) The nature of thequantum geometry at Planck scale is one-dimensional, polymeric with quantizedgeometrical quantities and; ii) Appropriately defined operators correspondingto coordinates by means of intrinsic, relational, constructions becomenon-commuting. This particular feature of the operators, that operationallylocalize points on space, gives rise to an emerging geometry that is also, in aprecise sense, fuzzy.
label: human

text: In quantum gravity theories, understanding the microstructure of spacetime at Planck scales is crucial, particularly through the potential definition of coordinate operators and their algebraic relations, including non-commutativity. This work explores the quantum geometry emerging in loop quantum gravity, where spatial structure is described by spin network states leading to discrete, "loopy" features. We construct operators intended to localize points in space and analyze their properties within the kinematical Hilbert space. These operators exhibit characteristics that prevent sharp localization, resulting in an inherent uncertainty. Consequently, the emergent quantum geometry is not only discrete but also fuzzy in a precise operational sense, with implications for the classical limit and semiclassical states.
label: llm

text: Several years ago, it was pointed out that the U-spin-related decays$B_d\to\pi^+\pi^-$, $B_s\to K^+K^-$ and $B_d\to\pi^\mp K^\pm$, $B_s\to \pi^\pmK^\mp$ offer interesting strategies for the extraction of the angle gamma ofthe unitarity triangle. Using the first results from the Tevatron on the $B_s$decays and the B-factory data on $B_{u,d}$ modes, we compare the determinationsof gamma from both strategies, study the sensitivity on U-spin-breakingeffects, discuss the resolution of discrete ambiguities, predict observablesthat were not yet measured but will be accessible at LHCb, explore theextraction of the width difference $\Delta\Gamma_s$ from untagged $B_s\toK^+K^-$ rates, and address the impact of new physics. The data for the$B_d\to\pi^+\pi^-$, $B_s\to K^+K^-$ system favour the BaBar measurement ofdirect CP violation in $B_d\to\pi^+\pi^-$, which will be used in the numericalanalysis, and result in a fortunate situation, yielding$\gamma=(66.6^{+4.3+4.0}_{-5.0-3.0})^\circ$, where the latter errors correspondto a generous estimate of U-spin-breaking effects. On the other hand, the$B_d\to\pi^\mp K^\pm$, $B_s\to \pi^\pm K^\mp$ analysis leaves us with$26^\circ\leq\gamma\leq70^\circ$, and points to a value of the $B_s\to \pi^\pmK^\mp$ branching ratio that is larger than the current Tevatron result. Animportant further step will be the measurement of mixing-induced CP violationin $B_s\to K^+K^-$, which will also allow us to extract the $B^0_s$--$\barB^0_s$ mixing phase unambiguously with the help of $B_s\to J/\psi \phi$ at theLHC. Finally, the measurement of direct CP violation in $B_s\to K^+K^-$ willmake the full exploitation of the physics potential of the $B_{s,d}\to \pi\pi,\pi K, KK$ modes possible.
label: human

text: The charmless hadronic decays of $B_{s}$ and $B_{d}$ mesons into $\pi\pi$, $\pi K$, and $KK$ final states provide a rich laboratory for probing CP violation and extracting the CKM angle $\gamma$ through U-spin symmetry relations. These modes, particularly the pairs $B_d\to\pi^+\pi^-$ with $B_s\to K^+K^-$ and $B_d\to\pi^\mp K^\pm$ with $B_s\to\pi^\pm K^\mp$, allow complementary strategies to determine $\gamma$ while controlling penguin contributions. Recent high-precision measurements from LHCb have significantly improved branching ratios and CP asymmetries, largely resolving earlier tensions such as the "$\pi K$ puzzle" and aligning observables closer to Standard Model expectations. U-spin-breaking effects remain moderate, enabling robust extractions of $\gamma$ with reduced theoretical uncertainties. Time-dependent analyses of $B_s\to K^+K^-$ have yielded precise determinations of the $B_s$ mixing phase and mixing-induced CP violation. Future data from LHCb upgrades and Belle II are expected to further constrain potential new physics contributions in electroweak penguins and refine the full exploitation of these channels for CKM metrology.
label: llm
